akron/0.summary: Council took up a Washington County Housing Authority housing project over several meetings, including special housing meetings in August and September, a water review request under the subdivision title, and a proposed MOU with the Housing Authority dated 9/8/26. On Aug. 10 it considered Resolution 26.09 to create an expedited review process for qualified affordable housing projects under Proposition 123.

akron/1.title: Settlement with Town Manager and acting manager appointment
akron/1.summary: Council reaffirmed Braden Piel as Acting Town Manager on Aug. 3. On Aug. 18 it was to discuss in executive session and possibly act on a settlement with the Town Manager. The agendas do not state the terms or the outcome.

akron/2.title: Sewer and water system improvement loan hearings
akron/2.summary: Council scheduled public hearings on Sept. 14 for the Water Pollution Control Revolving Fund (sanitary sewer collection system replacement) and the Drinking Water Revolving Fund (water system improvements). Dannah Koeniger of GMS presented both.

akron/3.title: Veregy West energy performance contract
akron/3.summary: Council considered approving an energy performance contract with Veregy West LLC on Aug. 3. The agenda gives no cost or scope details.

akron/4.title: Title 14 Planning and Zoning rewrite (Ordinance 614)
akron/4.summary: Ordinance 614, adopting a new Title 14 on planning and zoning, had its first reading on Sept. 14.

akron/5.title: Scott hangar lease at the airport (Ordinance 613)
akron/5.summary: Ordinance 613 approving a hangar lease to Scott had first reading on Aug. 3 and second reading on Sept. 14.

akron/6.title: 2027 budget review
akron/6.summary: Council scheduled its 2027 budget review for Oct. 12.

akron/7.title: Vacant trustee seat and coordinated election
akron/7.summary: Council was to appoint a successor to fill Ms. Benson's trustee seat on Aug. 18. On Aug. 3 it considered a coordinated election agreement with Washington County (Resolution 26.08).

akron/8.title: Lindsie Grass special animal permit
akron/8.summary: Council considered a special animal permit for Lindsie Grass on Aug. 3 and again on Sept. 14.

arapahoe-county/9.summary: The Board of Health considered a resolution to establish the existing state code as the local standard for pools and start a stakeholder process for local aquatic rules, possibly based on the CDC Model Aquatic Health Code. It does not itself adopt new fees or licensing.

arapahoe-county/11.summary: Staff warned that the state plans to cover 60% of a reduction in allocation tied to the Payment Error Rate, leaving counties to cover the rest, and discussed how county human services could lower errors. Commissioners also reviewed state and federal legislative priorities and 2026 ballot measures.

archuleta-county/0.title: Archuleta County Comprehensive Plan update
archuleta-county/0.summary: Consultant HRGreen is updating the county Comprehensive Plan, including the Strategic Growth and Water Supply chapters. At the Oct. 22 Planning Commission meeting, members asked about outreach (only one public meeting planned before the draft) and state deadlines, and a resident urged the plan to focus on growth and housing costs.

archuleta-county/1.title: Housing Action Plan
archuleta-county/1.summary: The multijurisdictional housing coordinator, Jeff Sams, is scheduled to brief on the Housing Action Plan at the Aug. 24 and Sept. 28 meetings. Habitat for Humanity's Infill in Trails project also received a county letter of support for an Enterprise Zone contribution.

archuleta-county/2.title: Septic (OWTS) regulation changes and property line setbacks
archuleta-county/2.summary: The Board of Health continued discussing on-site wastewater treatment system rules, including reducing property line setbacks of less than 10 feet. A Water Quality Manager presentation was held Aug. 27.

archuleta-county/3.title: Planning Commission land use cases: rezonings, B&B and agritourism campground
archuleta-county/3.summary: The Planning Commission is handling the Cloman Blvd administrative rezoning, the Brock rezone at 760 River Forrest Drive, a bed and breakfast conditional use permit at 78 W Golf Place, and the Cerulean Skies agritourism campground request, which had been tabled in July.
archuleta-county/3.where: Cloman Blvd; 760 River Forrest Drive; 78 W Golf Place

archuleta-county/4.title: 2027 draft budget and budget-to-actual review
archuleta-county/4.summary: Officials scheduled discussion of the draft 2027 budget on Sept. 28 and a budget-to-actual update at the Oct. 26 work session.

archuleta-county/5.title: Lot consolidations and un-consolidation resolutions
archuleta-county/5.summary: Commissioners were asked to approve resolutions to consolidate lots in Pagosa in the Pines Unit 2 and Lake Pagosa Park, and to reverse a consolidation of Lot 26X in Continental Estates 2.
archuleta-county/5.where: Pagosa in the Pines, Lake Pagosa Park, Continental Estates 2

archuleta-county/6.title: Medical director contract amendment with Axis Health
archuleta-county/6.summary: The board was asked to ratify the director's signature on an amendment to the medical director contract with Axis Health Services.

archuleta-county/7.title: Marijuana business license application
archuleta-county/7.summary: A marijuana business license application, with operating and license fees, was on the Oct. 6 agenda.

arriba/0.title: Wastewater permit compliance and facility study
arriba/0.summary: Arriba is working with GMS Inc on an engineering study of its wastewater facility under new state permit rules, with half the costs covered by DOLA grants (a $16,428.06 reimbursement; $19,250 in invoices paid in July 2026). The facility has had BOD and ammonia violations, flooding and infiltration problems, and board members are looking at cheaper alternatives to evaporative ponds. In September 2026 CDPHE let the Town revert to its old permit compliance; the permit expires in 2027.
arriba/0.where: Town wastewater facility and sewer lines

arriba/1.title: RV park sewer and water rates
arriba/1.summary: Residents, notably Beverly Langley, have complained that campgrounds like Big Ben's RV Park use more water and sewer than they pay for. In January 2026 the board raised the monthly RV sewer rate per hookup (a $2 increase from $5 was moved after a $10 motion failed for lack of a second), and the RV park's heavy use has affected BOD levels at the wastewater pond. Residents asked again in August and September 2026 for a rate review.

arriba/2.title: Base water rate increase
arriba/2.summary: To stay in compliance with its drinking water loan covenant, the Town adopted a resolution raising the in-town and out-of-town base water rates by $5.50, to $55.00. It takes effect August 1, 2026.

arriba/3.title: Mandatory trash service ordinance and Rob's Trash Service contract
arriba/3.summary: The board negotiated a contract with Rob's Trash Service and adopted an ordinance requiring every occupied residential household to have trash service, with an option for residents to use their own approved 3-yard dumpster emptied monthly for $45. The contract can be renegotiated at the end of 2026.

arriba/4.title: 2026 budget and mill levy cut
arriba/4.summary: After a public hearing, the board adopted the 2026 budget and a 2025 supplemental sewer fund budget, which raised sewer spending from $116,940 to $229,440 for wastewater permit costs. The mill levy was certified at 14.509, down from 25.948, to stay under the property tax revenue limit.

arriba/5.title: Sales tax ballot question for 2026
arriba/5.summary: The board placed a question on the 2026 ballot asking voters to let the Town keep 2025 sales tax revenue above its estimate. The Town had estimated $14,000 but projected about $30,000. The 2026 election will be by mail ballot.

arriba/6.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption (Ordinance 159)
arriba/6.summary: The state-required wildfire code was tabled for months over concerns about enforcement, with the Town Clerk as code official. In July 2026 the board adopted Ordinance 159 adopting the 2025 Wildfire Resiliency Code, after discussing its effect on residents' insurance rates and a state affidavit requirement.

arriba/7.title: Time capsule event and park improvements
arriba/7.summary: The Town held a July 4, 2026 time capsule event funded by a $7,500 grant and a $2,500 tourism grant, with a beer garden on the park basketball court. Volunteers painted the park building. A $2,500 donation from Big Ben's RV Park and Conservation Trust funds are earmarked for a park sprinkler system that staff and volunteers plan to install.

arriba/8.title: Pine Street drainage and speeding on College and Lincoln Avenues
arriba/8.summary: Resident Beverly Langley reported rainwater from Pine Street flooding her house, and the board agreed to a ditch on the west side of Pine Street. Residents also raised truck speeding, and the board discussed speed bumps on College Ave and Lincoln Ave, plus a missing stop sign at Grant and Lincoln.
arriba/8.where: Pine Street, College Ave, Lincoln Ave, Grant St

arriba/9.title: RV and manufactured home permits
arriba/9.summary: The board approved a manufactured home permit at 521 Lincoln Ave and an RV permit for Troy McCue at 214 Main Street. The board decided under the RV ordinance that no tap fee applies, only the permit fee and backhoe use.

arriba/10.title: Hooved animals ordinance (Ordinance 113)
arriba/10.summary: A request to allow hooved animals in Town or on lots over 5 acres was considered in July 2026. The board agreed not to change Ordinance 113, which bans them except by variance for 4-H.

arvada/0.title: Data center moratorium
arvada/0.summary: Council discussed on Aug 11 a temporary moratorium on new data center applications, citing water, energy and land-use concerns and moratoriums adopted by neighboring jurisdictions. On Sept 15 an ordinance (CB26-029) authorizing a moratorium on primary-use data center applications was introduced, with a public hearing set for Oct 6.

arvada/1.title: City Water Treatment Plant annexation and rezoning at 6809 SH 93
arvada/1.summary: The city is annexing two parcels (17.885 and 9.016 acres, 25.257 total) at 6809 SH 93 for a new water treatment plant, rezoning from Jefferson County PD to city Open Space, with major modifications and a height exception. Planning Commission heard it Aug 5 with public comment emailed in; Council set hearings for Oct 6.

arvada/2.title: 2027 water, wastewater and stormwater rates
arvada/2.summary: Council held workshops on draft 2027 utility rate scenarios to close infrastructure funding gaps. Rate ordinances CB26-032 and CB26-033 were set for hearing Oct 20. A proposed drought water surcharge (CB26-018) was pulled and may return in spring 2027.

arvada/3.title: 2027-2028 city budget and mill levy
arvada/3.summary: The City Manager proposed a 2027-2028 budget with 2027 appropriations of $412,447,446 and a pay plan; 32 new positions were requested. Budget, mill levy and pay plan resolutions were scheduled for hearing Oct 20.

arvada/4.title: Hibernia Gold Strike Apartments, 240 units
arvada/4.summary: A conditional use permit is requested for a five-story, 240-unit apartment building with a small coffee shop on 3.47 acres at 4800 W 60th Ave. About 20 residents attended the neighborhood meeting. Council first reading was Oct 20 with a hearing set for Nov 17.

arvada/5.title: Paid parking in Olde Town
arvada/5.summary: Council study session on a decade of parking demand pressure in Olde Town and options for paid, metered parking under the Strategic Reinvestment Plan. Staff reviewed studies from 2010, 2016 and 2025 and stakeholder feedback.

arvada/6.title: Proposition 123 housing commitments and zoning changes
arvada/6.summary: Planning Commission considered zoning text amendments tied to Prop 123, an ordinance revising the residential land use table was introduced, and Council took up a commitment to Prop 123 obligations for 2027-2029. The Housing Advisory Committee also worked on housing strategy.

arvada/7.title: Comprehensive Plan update
arvada/7.summary: Phase 1 of the Comprehensive Plan update with consultant Metta Urban Design is complete, with Phase 2 starting and adoption targeted for Q3 2027. Presentations covered housing attainability and growth patterns.

arvada/8.title: Residency rules for registered sex offenders
arvada/8.summary: Council held a workshop on a possible ordinance restricting where registered sex offenders may live. Legal asked for direction on who it would cover and distance limits, recommending no further than 1,000 feet.

arvada/9.title: City Attorney leadership change and ethics matters
arvada/9.summary: Council discussed next steps on pending ethics investigations and held personnel sessions. It approved amendments to employment agreements for the City Attorney, Municipal Judge and City Manager, and an interim City Attorney contract with Nora Steenson.

arvada/10.title: Gold Strike Park redevelopment contract
arvada/10.summary: Council considered a construction agreement with Arrow-J Landscape and Design for redeveloping Gold Strike Park, not to exceed $9,596,751.06.

arvada/11.title: Scenic Heights West Metropolitan District service plan
arvada/11.summary: Council held a public hearing on a resolution approving the proposed service plan for the Scenic Heights West Metropolitan District.

arvada/12.title: Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan update
arvada/12.summary: Staff presented a plan to update the 2016 Parks Master Plan, including a gap analysis, timeline and public engagement approach, and asked Council to authorize the update.

arvada/13.title: Wildfire early detection system and Navigation Center funding
arvada/13.summary: Council considered an agreement with the Arvada Urban Renewal Authority for up to $300,000 to create a wildfire early detection system, and an intergovernmental agreement on operating funding for the Navigation Center.

arvada/14.title: Olde Town Social liquor show cause hearing
arvada/14.summary: The Liquor Licensing Authority considered a show cause order against Olde Town Social at 5610 Yukon Street over a June 25, 2026 incident. A proposed settlement included a liquor education class and a fine.

aspen/0.title: Conner Park performance stage and amplified music
aspen/0.summary: Neighbors and nearby churches told Council they worry amplified music at the Conner Park performance deck will disturb the quiet park and the Armory Hall redevelopment, and asked Council to reconsider its approval. Council scheduled a Conner Park stage discussion for a September 22 work session.

aspen/1.title: Charter amendment ordinances (Ordinance #17) and election options
aspen/1.summary: Council moved two proposed ordinances amending the Home Rule Charter to second reading on August 11 so the public could speak on both options. At the August 25 hearing, staff said a runoff has significant issues outlined in a memo, and a council member was uncomfortable moving forward without more outreach.

aspen/2.title: Affordable housing fee-in-lieu and housing credits
aspen/2.summary: Council considered Q2 fee-in-lieu requests for several properties, including 1335 Riverside Drive and 807 McSkimming Road. A five-year fee-in-lieu study update went to Council on September 14 and to Planning & Zoning on October 7. Council also discussed the Affordable Housing Credits program and previewed the APCHA 2027 budget request.

aspen/3.title: Local fee deferral program for qualified locals (Ordinance #11)
aspen/3.summary: Planning & Zoning reviewed a recommendation on Ordinance #11, a program deferring city fees for qualified locals. The hearing was held August 19 and continued September 2.

aspen/4.title: 121-123 East Hyman Avenue special review
aspen/4.summary: Planning & Zoning held three hearings (August 5, September 2, October 21) on a special review for the 121 and 123 East Hyman Avenue project, with a reduced application and public comment from Good Thunder Condos residents.

aspen/5.title: Entrance to Aspen / CO 82 reevaluation
aspen/5.summary: The city is reevaluating the CO 82 entrance with a refined preferred alternative. Historic Preservation Commission discussed mitigation of effects on historic resources, and an info update was amended at Council's request.

aspen/6.title: Drought, Stage Three water restrictions and water supply
aspen/6.summary: With low flows and wildfires nearby, the city reported on a regional drought response using Ruedi Reservoir water and continued Stage Three water restrictions. Council also discussed buying Twin Lakes water right shares and met with the Ruedi Water and Power Authority.

aspen/7.title: Water treatment facility improvements and bond question
aspen/7.summary: Council considered an early work package amendment and a Holy Cross Electric contract and easements for the water treatment facility improvements, and a resolution supporting a water treatment plan bond question on the ballot.

aspen/8.title: 2027 city budget work sessions
aspen/8.summary: Council held four budget work sessions in October covering fund overviews, capital, supplemental requests and fees, and wrap-up, along with ACRA and CORE budget presentations. A Community Development fee update and consultant report were also discussed.

aspen/9.title: E-bikes and e-motos on trails
aspen/9.summary: A resident asked Council to align valley-wide rules on e-bikes and e-motos, with licensing and a minimum age of 16. The mayor said locals no longer feel comfortable on the Rio Grande Trail and that the issue is being taken seriously.

aspen/10.title: Armory Hall redevelopment
aspen/10.summary: Council approved Change Order #4 for builders risk on the Armory Hall project with Shaw Construction and received an interior update on the project.

aspen/11.title: Short-term rental program guideline amendments
aspen/11.summary: Staff reported forthcoming amendments to the short-term rental program guidelines.

aspen/12.title: Golf clubhouse area master plan
aspen/12.summary: Council reviewed a concept design for the golf clubhouse and campus master plan and received a follow-up report.

aurora/0.title: Data center moratorium and new data center rules
aurora/0.summary: Council adopted a moratorium on development applications that include a data center, directed staff to write data center regulations, and worked through development standards and a zoning use table change for data centers, ending in a public hearing in October.

aurora/1.title: Water rules on evaporative cooling, turf and water features
aurora/1.summary: Council passed Aurora Water ordinances on evaporative cooling and limits on new turf and ornamental water features, and set 2027 water rates and fees.

aurora/2.title: 2027 budget deliberations
aurora/2.summary: Council spent a day going department by department through the 2027 budget, service fees, pay tables and improvement district budgets.

aurora/3.title: Homeless services funding and the Regional Navigation Campus
aurora/3.summary: Council funded outdoor renovations at the Aurora Regional Navigation Campus and reviewed a slate of homeless services grant recommendations for emergency shelter, rapid rehousing and rental help.

aurora/4.title: Nine Mile Station redevelopment
aurora/4.summary: The Aurora Urban Renewal Authority amended the Point Crossing agreement and approved a redevelopment agreement for the Tempo at Nine Mile Station apartments.

aurora/5.title: Affordable housing ground lease with Mercy Housing
aurora/5.summary: Council approved a ground lease with Mercy Housing for an affordable housing project and assigned the city's private activity bonds to the Aurora Housing Authority.

aurora/6.title: Socioeconomic sales and services impact permit
aurora/6.summary: Council introduced an ordinance requiring an impact permit for certain sales and services businesses.

aurora/7.title: Support for Proposition 308
aurora/7.summary: Council took up a resolution supporting state ballot Proposition 308.

aurora/8.title: Oil and gas lease and advisory board
aurora/8.summary: Council considered an oil and gas lease and filled seats on the Oil and Gas Advisory Committee.

aurora/9.title: Police and fire union contracts
aurora/9.summary: Council approved 2027-2028 collective bargaining agreements with the firefighters' and police unions.

aurora/10.title: Regis Jesuit High comprehensive plan change
aurora/10.summary: Council held a public hearing on changing the comprehensive plan map for land near Regis Jesuit High north of East Arapahoe Road.
aurora/10.where: E Arapahoe Rd & S Olathe St

avon/0.title: Flock license plate reader cameras and petition to end the contract
avon/0.summary: Residents repeatedly urged Council to end the Town's contract with Flock Safety's automated license plate reader cameras, citing privacy concerns and a petition that grew from 1,544 to over 1,900 signatures. Town Manager Eric Heil said the agreement has not been renewed and is under review, including contract terms and data security. Council discussion is scheduled for October 6, 2026.

avon/1.title: Avon Whitewater Park and Bob the Bridge area improvements
avon/1.summary: Residents asked Council to improve the Bob the Bridge area and the Avon Whitewater Park, including adding a standing river wave. Other speakers raised low-water conditions limiting river access and an approved but unfunded skate park.
avon/1.where: Avon Whitewater Park / Bob the Bridge

avon/2.title: Community housing: fast track scheduling policy and deed restrictions
avon/2.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-07 adopting a fast track priority scheduling policy for community housing projects. A resident supported the deed restriction requirement, and another asked for more neighborhood input on a recent community housing project. The Town Manager said public hearings would offer further comment opportunities.

avon/3.title: Short-term rental licenses and unrestricted rental eligibility in new developments
avon/3.summary: A resident raised concerns about short-term rental licenses and the approval of additional residential developments with unrestricted short-term rental eligibility.

avon/4.title: Pedestrian crossing safety on Avon Road near Highway 6
avon/4.summary: A resident asked for flashing pedestrian beacons on both sides of Avon Road near Highway 6 after his father was struck and nearly hit at the crosswalks. He noted beacons exist along Highway 6 near Avon Road.

avon/5.title: Piedmont Apartments trash, wildlife and code enforcement
avon/5.summary: Residents raised trash management and code enforcement problems at the Piedmont Apartments. Deputy Chief Cosper reported police had received 27 calls about trash and wildlife.

avon/6.title: Lot B (The Summit) redevelopment and tree removal
avon/6.summary: A resident asked about trees that could be affected by future redevelopment of Lot B (The Summit), and staff said some would be removed during redevelopment and excavation. Council also handled a notice of award for heat recovery system expansion design tied to Lot B.

avon/7.title: Tax increment agreements with Urban Renewal and Downtown Development Authorities
avon/7.summary: Council approved intergovernmental agreements (Resolutions 26-08 and 26-09) on remitting tax increment with the Avon Urban Renewal Authority and the Avon Downtown Development Authority.

avon/8.title: Capital project awards: West Beaver Creek bridge, Rec Center aquatics, bus stop
avon/8.summary: Council issued notices of award for West Beaver Creek Blvd Bridge rehab construction, Rec Center aquatic renovation design, and a Lettuce Patch Early Learning Center bus stop.
avon/8.where: West Beaver Creek Blvd; Rec Center; Lettuce Patch Early Learning Center

avon/9.title: Clogged culvert and culvert maintenance
avon/9.summary: A resident thanked the Town for clearing a clogged culvert and asked for continued monitoring and maintenance of culverts.

basalt/0.title: Shared Public Works and Police facility and 0.5% sales tax on November ballot
basalt/0.summary: The Town plans a roughly $25 million shared Public Works and Police facility on the town-owned lot at the end of East Valley Road by Highway 82, recently annexed. Voters will be asked in November for a 0.5% sales tax with a 20-year sunset; the Town has also applied for a USDA loan and is considering selling the current police condo and the Annex site to offset costs.

basalt/1.title: 218 E. Valley Road (Movieland site) Residence Inn hotel
basalt/1.summary: Planning and Zoning has heard repeated hearings on a 93-key Residence Inn by Marriott with three deed-restricted affordable units at the former Movieland site, including PUD, site plan and annexation agreement amendments. Draft conditions restrict the use to the approved hotel, and the matter went to Town Council with a site visit on Sept. 22.

basalt/2.title: Jadwin/Black Mountain development and annexation
basalt/2.summary: Council continued the second reading of an ordinance approving 64 dwelling units and 12 short-term rental cabins, with annexation and initial zoning of the property at 431 Emma Road.

basalt/3.title: Town-owned affordable housing: BCC units, Certificates of Participation and Parcel 9
basalt/3.summary: The Town closed on six deed-restricted units in the BCC project on Aug. 5 (contracted at $2.38 million) and is setting rents for them. Ordinance 21 would finance the purchase through Certificates of Participation. The Finance Committee is also reviewing the pro-forma for the Parcel 9 (Pitchview, rugby field) project.

basalt/4.title: 2027 budget and town finances
basalt/4.summary: Council held a budget work session Sept. 17 and received the proposed 2027 budget Sept. 22. Mid-year results show revenue tracking well, but cash generated in the first half of 2026 was about $450,000 versus $2.2 million a year earlier, and a state grant for Two Rivers Road was deferred to 2027.

basalt/5.title: Short-term rental rules and fees
basalt/5.summary: A resident asked Council to exempt on-site hosted primary residents who rent a spare room from the commercial fees and 60-day cap in Ordinance 3 of 2025. Council scheduled a work session on STR regulatory fees for Oct. 22.

basalt/6.title: Tobacco tax increase request
basalt/6.summary: Residents urged Council to refer a tobacco tax increase to the ballot, noting Basalt's $2 per pack cigarette tax is below the $4 rate in Pitkin and Eagle counties and neighboring towns.

basalt/7.title: Zoning, annexation and subdivision code rewrite
basalt/7.summary: Planning and Zoning is reviewing a reorganized Chapters 15, 16 and 17 (annexation, zoning, subdivision) prepared with Design Workshop. The hearing was continued to Oct. 20 for a recommendation, then goes to Town Council.

basalt/8.title: Midland Avenue streetlights and snow removal
basalt/8.summary: Residents complained that the new catenary streetlights on Midland provide inadequate light, and staff say they are at maximum output and being worked on with the contractor. Public Works also presented options for snow removal on the new streetscape, including contracted service.

basalt/9.title: Police coordination with ICE
basalt/9.summary: A speaker at the Aug. 11 Council meeting raised barring local police from coordinating with ICE absent a judicial warrant tied to a criminal case.

basalt/10.title: Cliff's Hillside Park design and trail wayfinding funding
basalt/10.summary: The Parks committee reviewed the 90% design of Cliff's Hillside Park. It also discussed a wayfinding sign funding request to Mid-Valley Trails/RFTA, which missed the 2027 budget cycle, and plans to hear from Roaring Fork Outdoor Volunteers and RFMBA.

basalt/11.title: Green Team: building benchmarking, grants and leaf blower rules
basalt/11.summary: The Green Team heard that a regional IMPACT Accelerator Grant award topped $4 million, and discussed building benchmarking with CORE and its funding sources. Staff asked for ideas to extend the 2025 ban on combustion leaf blowers on town property to a wider area.

berthoud/0.title: Data center moratorium and land use rules
berthoud/0.summary: After trustees asked on Aug 25 for a discussion of a data center moratorium, the Board on Sept 22 approved Emergency Ordinance 1391 temporarily suspending acceptance, processing and approval of large data center applications. Discussion focused on the size threshold for a "large" facility. A Sept 29 work session was set to develop a technical memo and possible code amendments covering noise, heat and water, with noise consulting budgeted for 2027.

berthoud/1.title: Mountain Vista Park cost reduction and bond financing
berthoud/1.summary: The Board reviewed cost reductions and financing for Mountain Vista Park on July 28, and a resident spoke in favor of a bond to finance it on Aug 11. A park design change order was on the Sept 8 consent agenda, and the Board has been drafting ballot language for the Nov 3, 2026 election, with concern that it clearly say taxes would not increase.

berthoud/2.title: Berthoud Arboretum design reductions
berthoud/2.summary: Trustees discussed reductions to the Arboretum park project, asking about lighting, utilities, trees, trails, sponsorship and grants. The Berthoud Historical Society spoke in support of the project. Staff were authorized to finalize a revised construction contract, and an Arboretum Design Reduction Contract came back on Aug 25.

berthoud/3.title: Tundra Flats rezoning and master plan denied
berthoud/3.summary: On July 28 the Board adopted Resolution 2026-18 and Ordinance 1387 denying the Tundra Flats Neighborhood Master Plan and the rezoning from Planned Unit Development to Neighborhood Commercial.

berthoud/4.title: Legacy Park final plat, development agreement and water dedication
berthoud/4.summary: The Planning Commission approved the Legacy Park Final Plat on Sept 10, and the Board held a hearing on Sept 8 on the development agreement and revised vesting, including phasing and improvement guarantees. A water dedication agreement with Legacy Park Inc. was on the Oct 13 agenda. The silos on the site will be removed because of asbestos.
berthoud/4.where: South of Mountain Avenue, east of Meadowlark Drive, west of S. Berthoud Parkway

berthoud/5.title: Boards and commissions ordinance 1388
berthoud/5.summary: The Board adopted Ordinance 1388 on Aug 11, consolidating rules for town boards and commissions into new Municipal Code Section 4.9. Trustee Murphy's amendment requires each board to review it in October and update its bylaws. Advisory committees have since been discussing it and recruiting members.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Recreation, and Trails Committee

berthoud/6.title: Wildfire resiliency code and wildland-urban interface
berthoud/6.summary: A hearing on adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code (Ordinance 1389) was continued on Sept 8 and set for Oct 13. A cooperative agreement with the Berthoud Fire Protection District for administering and enforcing the code is also pending.

berthoud/7.title: Heron Lakes Marina Neighborhood Master Plan
berthoud/7.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on Sept 10 on the Heron Lakes Marina Neighborhood Master Plan and sent a recommendation to the Board of Trustees.

berthoud/8.title: Land Use Code rewrite of Chapter 30
berthoud/8.summary: Staff are proposing amendments to Chapter 30 covering impact fees, annexation, zoning, flood mitigation and more. The Planning Commission hears them Oct 22 and the Trustees on Nov 10.

berthoud/9.title: Affordable housing fee waivers and Ordinance 1355
berthoud/9.summary: The Board considered a Habitat for Humanity request to waive development fees under Ordinance 1355 for new homes at 772 and discussed expanding affordable housing incentives. The Planning Commission also planned a housing work session with the regional housing director.

berthoud/10.title: Public Art Master Plan
berthoud/10.summary: The Planning Commission recommended approval of the Public Art Master Plan, and Resolution 2026-28 adopting it was set for the Board on Oct 13.

berthoud/11.title: Water projects: treatment plant study and water shares
berthoud/11.summary: The Board was to award a contract for a Water Treatment Plant preliminary engineering study on Oct 13. On Aug 25 it considered contracts to purchase Loveland Lake and Ditch water shares and a lease amendment with Northern Water.

berthoud/12.title: Historic preservation: water tower sign and survey grants
berthoud/12.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission received funding for an interpretive sign at the elevated water tank and is pursuing a survey plan grant from History Colorado. Residents asked the Board on Sept 22 to support historic preservation.

berthoud/13.title: Welch Avenue and 9th Street road improvements
berthoud/13.summary: On Sept 22 the Board approved a request for proposals for design of Welch Avenue roadway and drainage improvements. An update on 9th Street crossing improvements was given Sept 8.

black-hawk/0.title: Water supply expansion: Four Mile Gulch Well #6 and residents' water concerns
black-hawk/0.summary: Council approved a contract in May for Four Mile Gulch Well #6 near Dory Hill Road, to be drilled 1,000 feet deep. At the Sept. 9 meeting, residents of unincorporated Black Hawk (including Aspen Springs and Chalet Park) asked the city to pause additional wells and study harm to neighbors' water. The city is also pursuing an Army Corps of Engineers permit for a reservoir, and approved a reimbursement agreement (CB12) for the permit review costs.
black-hawk/0.where: Four Mile Gulch / Dory Hill Road

black-hawk/1.title: Education Enhancement Tax and possible Gilpin County sales tax
black-hawk/1.summary: Black Hawk's 1.5% Education Enhancement Tax, which has raised over $10 million for the Gilpin school since 2009, would automatically end if county voters approve a countywide sales tax. The county is considering such a tax for the November 2026 ballot. Council discussed it in February and March and adopted Resolution 17-2026 reaffirming the tax's self-terminating conditions.

black-hawk/2.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adopted
black-hawk/2.summary: Council adopted the 2025 Wildfire Resiliency Code by reference into the municipal code (CB3) after a March 25 public hearing, passing 5-1. In July the city manager also issued an administrative order imposing fire restrictions.

black-hawk/3.title: Vacant land sale agreement (Resolution 48-2026) and Central City roadway traffic dispute
black-hawk/3.summary: Resolution 48-2026, a vacant land sale agreement, was repeatedly continued from August into September. Discussion at the Aug. 12 meeting touched on Central City's roadway permitting process and the traffic study behind it.

black-hawk/4.title: Gregory Hill land purchase and property deals
black-hawk/4.summary: Council approved a contract to buy land on Gregory Hill in June and accepted conveyance of property in July. A boundary line agreement involving Oregory Street was approved in January.

black-hawk/5.title: Highway 119 storm culvert repairs
black-hawk/5.summary: After a hole opened in Highway 119 at Gregory Street from a failed culvert, council approved an agreement with Insituform Technologies (C & L Water Solutions) to reline two storm culverts under the highway.

black-hawk/6.title: City capital projects: Bobtail Mine, Ballard House, Red Dolly electrical, storage sheds
black-hawk/6.summary: Council approved a $949,307 change order for Bobtail Mine Improvements Phase 2. It also awarded bids for the Red Dolly Casino electrical service relocation, storage sheds, and the Ballard House renovation with Barn Shed addition (Roche Constructors). An ordinance (CB10) changed the approval process for city capital projects.

black-hawk/7.title: Police chief and city manager transitions
black-hawk/7.summary: Police Chief Moriarty retired after a 31-year career, and Ely Reyes became the new chief in July. Council approved an employment agreement for Lance Hillis as city manager, effective May 2, after personnel discussions about the prior manager.

black-hawk/8.title: Fee schedule update and 2025 audit
black-hawk/8.summary: Council approved an amended fee schedule in June that aligns commercial electrical fees with state fees and changes SAFEbuilt's rate to consultant fees. It also accepted the 2025 audit.

black-hawk/9.title: Rick Thomas Distillery trademark license and water fee waiver
black-hawk/9.summary: Council approved a trademark license agreement with Rick Thomas Distillery and extended a waiver of water fees for one more year for the distillery on Lot 7 of the Black Hawk Park Subdivision.

black-hawk/10.title: Historic preservation: Lace House designation and survey work
black-hawk/10.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission scheduled the Lace House designation for 2026 and worked on intensive survey properties. Council accepted the reconnaissance survey and a five-year work plan in August to meet Certified Local Government requirements.

black-hawk/11.title: Proposed resolution on natural gas Initiative 177 and energy diversification
black-hawk/11.summary: On Sept. 9 the mayor said he wanted to draft a resolution supporting Initiative 177, on the right to purchase and sell natural gas. Council also took up Resolution 53-2026 encouraging diversification of the city's local economy.

blue-river/0.title: Short-term rental caps, zones and moratorium exceptions
blue-river/0.summary: The Board has been working through a new short-term rental policy: a six-zone framework with license caps by zone, a draft ordinance effective Jan. 1, 2027, and licensing set to begin May 1, 2027. Ordinances 2026-10, 2026-11 and 2026-12 would let some owners hurt by the moratorium (Ordinance 2026-03) apply, with a Nov. 1, 2026 application deadline, and change renewal and enforcement processes. Residents urged enforcement against unlicensed operators and fair treatment for recent buyers.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/1.title: Transition Zone District lot size and setback rules (Ordinance 2026-06 and 2026-07)
blue-river/1.summary: The Board held a hearing on Ordinance 2026-06, which sets minimum lot size, lot width and setbacks in the Transition Zone District. Ordinance 2026-07 would put a Development Code in effect Oct. 1, 2026, on the condition that 2026-06 is in effect. Discussion covered consistency with R-1 standards and wetland and topography limits.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/2.title: Proposed 2027 budget and town finances
blue-river/2.summary: The Board was scheduled to hear a presentation and discuss the proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 20. Financial reports show a 10.459 mill levy after a temporary credit, and 2026 general property tax is projected at about $930,583.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/3.title: Porch, deck and roof project at 6871 Highway 9 and wildfire code review
blue-river/3.summary: The Planning Commission found the application incomplete in August because it lacked wildfire-code measurements, a current survey and parking and second-access information on Highway 9. In September it found the revised materials adequate and approved the application. The Town Attorney advised on how far the Highway 9 Access Control Plan applies to minor projects.

blue-river/4.title: 1253 Indiana Creek Road residence: height, garages and carriage house
blue-river/4.summary: The Commission held a pre-application session on a proposed home. Topics were the 35-foot height limit, whether recessed garage entrances count as basement entries, the 25% garage area limit, two separate living areas and a carriage house. The applicant was asked for revised exhibits showing existing and proposed grades.

blue-river/5.title: Sewer and septic concerns along Blue River Road
blue-river/5.summary: Residents raised aging septic systems and environmental concerns on Blue River Road. They asked the Town to explore grants, financing and partnerships for future sewer infrastructure.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/6.title: Goose Pasture Tarn boat dock rules repealed
blue-river/6.summary: The Board considered Resolution 2026-10, repealing Resolution 13-05, which set rules and permits for private boat docks at Goose Pasture Tarn. The Town Attorney gave background and the Board moved to adopt it.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/7.title: Speeding and traffic calming on Indiana Creek Road
blue-river/7.summary: Residents raised speeding on Indiana Creek Road and asked for traffic-calming measures.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/8.title: Summit School District mill levy override presentation (Measure 4A)
blue-river/8.summary: District representatives presented Ballot Measure 4A, a local mill levy override raising up to $5.9 million a year, and the statewide Proposition NN. About 76% of the 4A money would go to staff pay, and the district cited turnover and cost of living.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/9.title: Summit County Hazard Mitigation Plan 2026 adoption
blue-river/9.summary: The Board was to consider Resolution 2026-13 adopting the Summit County Hazard Mitigation Plan 2026.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

blue-river/10.title: Board policy on agenda item placement
blue-river/10.summary: Trustees discussed a draft bylaw policy setting a clear process for bringing items before the Board and supported moving it forward for formal consideration.

sources.body: Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees
Regular Meeting of the Board of Trustees

boone/0.title: Water treatment facility project, startup and draws
boone/0.summary: The town's new water treatment facility moved from operator training in March to startup in early May, with monthly construction draws and a 2-year warranty. By August, a leak in the GreenSands room and a problem with the chlorine pumps still needed investigation, and a council member asked for an itemized breakdown of the draw.

boone/1.title: Water and sewer billing procedure ordinance and tap fee ordinance
boone/1.summary: Council has spent months drafting ordinances on water bill dates and on water and sewer tap fees. The tap fee ordinance was accepted in June and signed and posted in July. The billing ordinance is on hold while Section 9 on landlord and tenant responsibilities is reworded; it was to be posted for 10 days and finalized Oct. 14. A late, reconnect and disconnect fee discussion was also on the June agenda.

boone/2.title: Fire protection IGA with Edison Fire Protection District
boone/2.summary: Council reviewed an intergovernmental agreement, contract and lease agreements with the Edison fire district for the town's fire department. Council voted to accept the IGA on April 15 and adopted a resolution approving the IGA and contracts on May 7.

boone/3.title: Building code enforcement and Southern Colorado Building Department ordinances
boone/3.summary: Council discussed adopting Pueblo codes for code enforcement and noted that ordinances tied to the Pueblo regional building department need updating. The department's attorney is working on revisions, and the department was to attend the Sept. 16 meeting. Council planned to review and finalize the ordinances and an amended IGA on Oct. 14.

boone/4.title: Safe water notice and drinking water quality
boone/4.summary: The state health department lifted a bottled water advisory, and the town sent copies of the letter to all residents. Residents later questioned the safe water notice, and they were pointed to test results online. Council also discussed the 2025 drinking water quality report and a lead line survey and notices.

boone/5.title: Refuse rate increase
boone/5.summary: The trash fee was set to rise 3% per the hauling contract. Council approved a resolution on the refuse rate increase in July and all members signed it in August.

boone/6.title: Town park, playground equipment and mower
boone/6.summary: After sprinkler heads were damaged during mowing, 8 were replaced and council approved buying a new mower. Council discussed that the playground needs new equipment, and the fire chief suggested USDA or GOCO grants. A re-dedication of the park memorial for the 250th anniversary was also on the June agenda.

boone/7.title: Utility billing system and payment processing
boone/7.summary: The town worked to set up online card and ACH payments for utility bills; merchant account and payment applications were approved by April. In June it decided to keep using Waterworks, and found that SIPA can process payments.

boone/8.title: Town administrator appointment and sewage disposal regulations
boone/8.summary: Council approved a resolution appointing a town administrator in August and re-signed it in September. A sewer tap request for Kevin Garcia and a proposed resolution establishing sewage disposal regulations were on the Oct. 14 agenda.

boone/9.title: Town internet switch from CenturyLink to Starlink
boone/9.summary: Council discussed changing from CenturyLink to Starlink at a flat $280 monthly fee for 1 TB of usage.

boulder-county/0.title: Data center and detention center land use code amendments
boulder-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled on Oct. 21 to consider text amendments to the county Land Use Code defining data centers (DC-26-0003) and detention centers (DC-26-0004) and setting where and at what scale they may be allowed in unincorporated Boulder County. The commission's action is a recommendation to the commissioners.

boulder-county/1.title: 2027 Boulder County budget
boulder-county/1.summary: The county presented the 2027 recommended budget in departmental sessions in October, held a Superior town hall on it Aug. 18, and took public testimony at an Oct. 22 hearing. Budget adoption is set for Dec. 8. Work sessions also covered general fund reduction recommendations and an efficiencies project.

boulder-county/2.title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan major update
boulder-county/2.summary: The Planning Commission and then the commissioners conditionally approved the ten-year major update to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan, including Rural Lands text amendments. A resolution formally approving it followed Oct. 13.

Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/3.title: Ballot measure to expand the Board of Commissioners from 3 to 5
boulder-county/3.summary: The commissioners adopted Resolution 2026-056 setting ballot titles for an initiative petition to increase the board from 3 to 5 members on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot. The clerk found the petition sufficient. In October the board also considered county positions on 2026 ballot measures.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/4.title: Eldorado Springs wastewater plant debt ballot question
boulder-county/4.summary: Sitting as the Eldorado Springs Public Improvement District board, the commissioners referred a multi-year debt authorization to the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot. It would pay for wastewater treatment plant improvements required by the state health department.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/5.title: Riverside Cabins Lodge special review revocation
boulder-county/5.summary: Staff recommended revoking the special review approval (SU-23-0013) for violating conditions. The commissioners declined to revoke and continued the hearing to Jan. 7, 2027, so the applicants can finish the work and meet conditions. Lyons Fire Protection District staff took part.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/6.title: Longmont 1st & Main urban renewal tax increment agreement
boulder-county/6.summary: The county considered a tax increment financing agreement with the Longmont Urban Renewal Authority for redevelopment of the 1st & Main corridor. The project includes a regional transit center, environmental cleanup and public infrastructure.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/7.title: Housing Authority annual plan and homelessness funding
boulder-county/7.summary: The commissioners held hearings on and approved the Boulder County Housing Authority 2027 Annual Plan and Moving to Work supplement, then approved submission. They also pursued state homelessness grants of $300,000 and $571,306 for youth housing, reallocated funds to Family Bridge Housing, and awarded $1,084,000 for Willoughby Corner Phases II and III in Lafayette.

boulder-county/8.title: Apahapa LLC boundary line adjustment appeal, Flagstaff Road
boulder-county/8.summary: The commissioners heard an appeal of a director's determination on a boundary line adjustment between parcels at 6808 and 7022 Flagstaff Road, which also denied recognition of 6808 Flagstaff as a parcel. They tabled the hearing to Dec. 3 and took no comment because of time.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/9.title: Osterholm-DiGiulian ADU denial
boulder-county/9.summary: After an executive session with county attorneys, the commissioners denied the application for a family care accessory dwelling unit and a 165-square-foot addition. A resolution of denial followed Sept. 15. No one commented at the hearing.

Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/10.title: Mental and behavioral health tax school funding
boulder-county/10.summary: The county approved $800,000 contracts each with Boulder Valley and St. Vrain Valley school districts from the 1B Mental and Behavioral Health Tax, including Wellness Centers at six BVSD high schools. A tax advisory committee and bylaws were also discussed.
boulder-county/10.where: Boulder Valley and St. Vrain Valley school districts

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting
Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/11.title: Xcel easements for 120th Street shoulder reconstruction
boulder-county/11.summary: Xcel proposed acquiring three permanent easements over about 1.38 acres of the Liley, Roberts (Simi) and Thompson (Tommy) open space properties for the 120th Street shoulder reconstruction. The commissioners held a hearing, and a funding agreement for 120th Street multimodal improvements was also approved.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/12.title: Wildfire mitigation grants and fire restrictions
boulder-county/12.summary: The county approved strategic fuels mitigation funding: $191,350 for Superior's grazing program and $990,262.88 for The Watershed Center's Conifer Hill work. It also added $30K for wildfire awareness advertising and lifted Stage 1 fire restrictions in the mountain area on Oct. 15.

boulder-county/13.title: Eldora Resort cell tower
boulder-county/13.summary: The commissioners conditionally approved a 100-foot macro-cell tower, proposed with Verizon Wireless, on a 46-acre forestry-zoned parcel at Eldora Resort. A resolution followed on Oct. 13.

Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/14.title: Erie Parkway road renaming
boulder-county/14.summary: The commissioners conditionally approved the Town of Erie's request to rename a section of Isabelle Road between US 287 and N. 109th Street as Erie Parkway.
boulder-county/14.where: Isabelle Road, US 287 to N. 109th Street

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder-county/15.title: Tucker Complex interim management and Zero Waste Plan
boulder-county/15.summary: A work session covered an interim management proposal for the Tucker Complex open space and a Zero Waste Plan update on fees and composting. Grading code amendments were also approved.

Board of County Commissioners - Regular Meeting

boulder/0.title: November ballot measures
boulder/0.summary: Council put several questions on the November 3 ballot, including general obligation bonds for recreation and safety projects, a vacancy excise tax on homes occupied 183 days a year or less, a charter right for firefighters to bargain collectively, and a wildfire resilience measure for open space.

boulder/1.title: Boulder Downtown Development Authority
boulder/1.summary: Council moved to ask downtown voters whether to form a Downtown Development Authority that could use tax increment financing for downtown projects.

boulder/2.title: Wildfire resilience and home hardening
boulder/2.summary: Council worked on a wildfire home hardening hub and a review of every city wildfire program as a council priority project, alongside the open space wildfire ballot measure.

boulder/3.title: Local minimum wage increase
boulder/3.summary: Council held the second reading of an ordinance setting Boulder's local minimum wage.

boulder/4.title: 2027 budget
boulder/4.summary: Council held a study session on the 2027 recommended budget and then adopted budgets and mill levies for the downtown, University Hill and Boulder Junction improvement districts.
boulder/4.where: Citywide, Downtown, University Hill, Boulder Junction

boulder/5.title: Eminent domain for the 30th Street projects
boulder/5.summary: Council introduced ordinances allowing the city to buy or condemn land for the North 30th Street project and the South 30th Street multimodal improvements.

boulder/6.title: Annexation of Cherryvale Road and McSorley Lane properties
boulder/6.summary: Council took up a petition to annex about 5.4 acres at 1275 Cherryvale Rd. and 5995 McSorley Ln. with rural residential zoning, setting a public hearing for November 12.

boulder/7.title: Affordable housing bonds for Boulder Housing Partners and Harvest34
boulder/7.summary: Council assigned $7.3 million in private activity bonds to Boulder Housing Partners for permanently affordable rentals and cleared housing revenue bonds for the Harvest34 project.

boulder/8.title: Arapahoe Avenue rezoning and Naropa campus redevelopment
boulder/8.summary: Council introduced a rezoning of 3.7 acres at 2106 and 2130 Arapahoe Avenue to high-density residential, vacated part of Marine Street, and reviewed a site plan to redevelop the Naropa campus.

boulder/9.title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan update
boulder/9.summary: Council introduced the ordinance adopting the 2025 major ten-year update to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan.

boulder/10.title: Power reliability and resilience forum
boulder/10.summary: Council held a community forum on power reliability and resilience, a council priority project, and reviewed a concept plan to expand Xcel Energy's service center at 2655 N. 63rd Street.

boulder/11.title: Civic Area East Bookend redevelopment
boulder/11.summary: Council discussed a request for proposals for a development partner on the east end of the Civic Area.

boulder/12.title: Marijuana and liquor licensing changes
boulder/12.summary: Council updated the medical and recreational marijuana code and created expanded permits and a tax for spirits manufacturers.

boulder/13.title: Pedicab licenses
boulder/13.summary: Council created licenses and fees for pedicab companies and drivers.

boulder/14.title: Frasier senior campus expansion
boulder/14.summary: Council reviewed a site review amendment for Frasier to build a 55-foot, four-story, 96-unit independent living building with underground parking.

boulder/15.title: Landmark designations at 1004 Lincoln Place and 844-850 12th Street
boulder/15.summary: Council designated two properties as individual landmarks.

breckenridge/0.title: Flock license plate reader cameras and contract renewal
breckenridge/0.summary: Residents told Council they are concerned about Flock license plate cameras, citing broad data-use rights, lack of oversight and unclear camera placement, and asked for better communication ahead of the contract renewal in March 2027. Council scheduled an automated license plate reader program presentation for its Oct. 13 budget retreat.

breckenridge/1.title: Comprehensive Plan underutilized parcels and workforce housing density
breckenridge/1.summary: The Planning Commission is reviewing maps of underutilized parcels, including Park Avenue corridor sites, the Breckenridge Elementary parcel and the North Gold Rush lot, as potential housing sites under state comp plan rules. Staff recommended workforce housing densities such as 30 units per acre on the Park Avenue corridor, and commissioners raised concerns about views from Carter Park and historic district limits. Council also toured Riverwalk Center for the plan.
breckenridge/1.where: Park Avenue corridor, Carter Park, Breckenridge Elementary parcel, North Gold Rush lot

breckenridge/2.title: Workforce housing: Housing Helps, Stables Village, Runway Neighborhood and Trails at Berlin Placer
breckenridge/2.summary: Council reviewed workforce housing progress including the sale of Stables Village units, a possible phase two of the Runway Neighborhood, and the 2027 Workforce Housing Fund. Residents praised the Housing Helps program and urged continued funding, and Council went into executive session on water service and bond money for the Trails at Berlin Placer development.

breckenridge/3.title: Proposed special district and Village/Vail Resorts tax structure
breckenridge/3.summary: Council held a legal executive session on the process for a special district request in light of a proposed district being discussed in the community. A resident at the Aug. 11 meeting called the proposal a land grab by the Village and Vail Resorts with an unfair tax structure.

breckenridge/4.title: Wildfire mitigation and exterior fire suppression permit moratorium
breckenridge/4.summary: Council considered Resolution No. 14 imposing a temporary moratorium on permits for exterior fire suppression systems.

breckenridge/5.title: Water restrictions, Gary Roberts plant and French Gulch treatment
breckenridge/5.summary: Council received water restrictions updates and planned a site tour and update on the Gary Roberts Water Treatment Plant. Staff also reported on optimizing the Wellington-Oro/French Gulch treatment plant for cadmium and zinc ahead of a 2029 Water Quality Control Commission hearing.
breckenridge/5.where: Gary Roberts Water Treatment Plant; French Gulch

breckenridge/6.title: Quandary Trailhead, Little Daisy and Tiger Road trail projects
breckenridge/6.summary: The Open Space commission worked on a trails prioritization matrix including a Tiger Road rec path and heard from riders seeking downhill trails near Little Mountain. It also covered Quandary trailhead design, with the Town pledging $400,000 to a grant match, and Little Daisy Open Space trail naming.
breckenridge/6.where: Quandary Peak trailhead; Little Daisy Open Space; Tiger Road

breckenridge/7.title: Aspen Alley seasonal shuttle and parking management
breckenridge/7.summary: A free shuttle funded by a transit grant, along with police patrols and citations, was used to manage parking at Aspen Alley. Staff reported strong compliance and expect continued grant funding.

breckenridge/8.title: Delivery zone permits and traffic code changes
breckenridge/8.summary: Council took up Council Bill 9 updating the delivery zone program, clarifying eligibility and time limits, updating fees, setting enforcement penalties and confirming the Police Chief's authority to designate permits.

breckenridge/9.title: Mamba Trust retaining wall variance at 219 Glen Eagle Loop
breckenridge/9.summary: The Planning Commission heard a variance request to let part of an unpermitted retaining wall remain outside the platted disturbance envelope; staff said about 75 feet would otherwise need removal. The owner's architect presented in support.

breckenridge/10.title: City Market fuel center at 430 N. Park Avenue
breckenridge/10.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled preliminary hearings on a proposed City Market #430 fuel center (PL-2026-0171).

breckenridge/11.title: Little Red Schoolhouse expansion
breckenridge/11.summary: The Planning Commission held a work session and then a town project hearing on the proposed Little Red Schoolhouse expansion.

breckenridge/12.title: 2027 budget, capital plan and certificates of participation refunding
breckenridge/12.summary: Council held a work session on cash flow and capital improvements, and a Oct. 13 budget retreat. It approved refunding the Series 2016 certificates of participation, with $4.6 million outstanding, if savings justify costs.

breckenridge/13.title: Permit parking shortages for workers and residents
breckenridge/13.summary: A resident said permit holders often cannot find parking, and suggested gated permit lots, towing enforcement and expanding permitted parking into the South Gondola lots or the parking structure.

breckenridge/14.title: Arts and Culture Master Plan and arts funding requests
breckenridge/14.summary: A consultant's community engagement report drawing 650+ participants went to Council, and residents asked for skate park, Arts District and TEDx Breckenridge funding in the plan.

breckenridge/15.title: Strong Future ballot measure and Summit School District mill levy
breckenridge/15.summary: Council considered resolutions supporting the Strong Future ballot measure and Measure 4A, the school district mill levy override, and held an executive session on negotiations with the school district.

brighton/0.title: Data center moratorium (180 days)
brighton/0.summary: Council took up an ordinance pausing acceptance, processing or approval of permits, licenses, zoning or other land use applications where a data center is a proposed use, for 180 days. It was introduced Oct. 6 and returned Oct. 20 for final consideration in an amended version.

brighton/1.title: North 40th Avenue roadway construction and 27J agreement
brighton/1.summary: Council reviewed the North 40th Avenue construction project in a July study session, then considered a construction contract of about $2.7 million and an intergovernmental agreement with School District 27J covering a regional detention pond, easements and maintenance.

brighton/2.title: Bromley Park PUD amendments (38th and 39th)
brighton/2.summary: Council considered the Bromley Park Planned Unit Development 38th Amendment near the I-76 frontage road and North 60th Avenue, heard Aug. and Oct., then took it up as an ordinance Oct. 20. A 39th Amendment covering about 5.92 acres near Bromley Business Parkway and the BNSF railroad was also on the Oct. 20 agenda.
brighton/2.where: I-76 frontage road and North 60th Avenue; Bromley Business Parkway

brighton/3.title: Case Farms zoning change to R-2 and open space
brighton/3.summary: Council held a public hearing and first reading on rezoning about 232 acres of the Case Farms PUD to R-2 and open space and parks, with the ordinance returning Sept. 1. The Planning Commission had already acted and neighbors were notified.

brighton/4.title: 2027-2028 budget, mill levy and fees
brighton/4.summary: Council reviewed proposed 2027 and 2028 budgets and a Q2 2026 financial update in August, discussed the 2027 rate and fee proposal in September, and the October agenda lists the 2027 budget, mill levy and fees. A third amendment to the 2026 budget was also heard Oct. 6.

brighton/5.title: Water system: bond refunding, chemicals and well contamination lawsuit
brighton/5.summary: Council moved to refund the 2016 water revenue bonds with Series 2026 refunding bonds, awarded water treatment chemical price agreements to Univar and PVS DX, and approved filing an amended complaint adding defendants over contamination of a city drinking water well.

brighton/6.title: Land Use and Development Code amendments
brighton/6.summary: Council worked on several code changes: temporary sign regulations, Articles 1 and 11 on administration, Article 10 and floodplain amendments to Section 10.02, and parks and open space amendments.

brighton/7.title: City-owned Bridge Street property and Comprehensive Plan update
brighton/7.summary: Council studied land use scenarios for city-owned property on Bridge Street and reviewed the 80% draft of the Comprehensive Plan update.

brighton/8.title: Prairie Center Metropolitan District No. 7 service plan amendment
brighton/8.summary: Council held a public hearing on a second amendment to the service plan for Prairie Center Metropolitan District No. 7.

brighton/9.title: Lupton Meadows reservoir and Cherry Meadows pond work
brighton/9.summary: Council discussed Cherry Meadows pond maintenance and the Lupton Meadows reservoir design, and approved a change order with Engineering Analytics for the reservoir design project. A Thornton agreement was also presented.

brighton/10.title: JAG grant for police technology (Flock)
brighton/10.summary: Council reviewed and then approved accepting an Edward Byrne Memorial JAG grant and authorized the police chief to sign grant agreements. Presentation materials reference Flock.

brighton/11.title: Board and commission appointment policy changes
brighton/11.summary: Council revised its policy on interviewing and appointing members of city boards and commissions, and also moved to change Sustainability Board membership.

broomfield/0.title: Broomfield Town Square site plan revocation and show-cause notice
broomfield/0.summary: On Sept. 22 Councilmembers Twiss and Peterson asked Council to consider starting a revocation hearing for the Broomfield Town Square Site Development Plan. On Oct. 13 Council took up a Notice to Show Cause (Resolution 2026-133) on the project.

broomfield/1.title: 2026 revised and 2027 operating and capital budgets
broomfield/1.summary: Council reviewed the economic and fiscal update, draft budgets and long range financial plan, held department budget presentations in September, and scheduled an Oct. 13 public hearing on the 2027 budgets. The Library Advisory Board was told the 2027 library budget is flat, with concern that it could erode over the longer term.

broomfield/2.title: Affordable housing: Prop 123 opt-in, expedited review and inclusionary housing
broomfield/2.summary: Council discussed opting in to the next Proposition 123 cycle with DOLA and creating an expedited review process for affordable housing, then took up the Cycle 2 opt-in resolution on Sept. 22. Staff also updated Council on the housing needs assessment and the status of an inclusionary housing ordinance, and the Housing Alliance gave its annual update.

broomfield/3.title: Transit-oriented communities density rules (HB24-1313) and development review
broomfield/3.summary: At an Aug. 3 study session Council reviewed the development review process and sought direction on complying with state transit-oriented communities law. That law requires increased density and administrative review for qualifying properties near transit.

broomfield/4.title: November 2026 ballot: lodging tax and Xcel franchise
broomfield/4.summary: Council referred a lodging tax question to the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot and later considered resolutions supporting Ballot Item 1A (lodging tax) and 1B (Broomfield-Xcel franchise agreement). Council also approved election IGAs for the November general election and considered a district attorney term-limits ballot question.

broomfield/5.title: Protecting outdoor recreation facilities in site plan amendments
broomfield/5.summary: Ordinance 2305 would require a public hearing for site development plan amendments that reduce or eliminate outdoor recreation facilities. It had first reading Aug. 25 and second reading Sept. 22.

broomfield/6.title: Northlands PUD amendment for hospital building height and parking
broomfield/6.summary: Council considered a Northlands PUD amendment to change building height and parking requirements for hospital and medical office uses (Resolution 2026-95).

broomfield/7.title: Fiscal impact review criteria for rezonings and PUDs
broomfield/7.summary: Ordinance 2306 adds fiscal impact review criteria for rezonings, PUD plans and amendments, and use by special review. It had second reading and a public hearing on July 28.

broomfield/8.title: Electric vehicle charging rules and fees
broomfield/8.summary: Council set a fee structure for EV charging stations on city property and held second reading of an ordinance making EV charging a primary permitted use in non-residential districts.

broomfield/9.title: Electronic bike enforcement ordinance
broomfield/9.summary: Council heard first reading of Ordinance 2311 on electronic bike enforcement on Aug. 25.

broomfield/10.title: Rail district station narrative for Front Range Passenger Rail
broomfield/10.summary: Council considered resolutions on a rail district station narrative for joint service and Front Range Passenger Rail. Councilmember Ward also asked for a study session on regional transportation authorities.

broomfield/11.title: Palisade Park Chipotle plat and site plan
broomfield/11.summary: Council and the Broomfield Urban Renewal Authority held public hearings on the final plat and site development plan for a Chipotle at Palisade Park.

broomfield/12.title: Nordstrom Silo landmark nomination
broomfield/12.summary: Council considered a landmark nomination for the Nordstrom Silo (Resolution 2026-111) on Sept. 22.

broomfield/13.title: Enterprise utility ordinance
broomfield/13.summary: Ordinance 2308, establishing an enterprise utility, had first reading on Oct. 13, and Council also considered the Mile High Water license.

buena-vista/0.title: Short-term rental cap and Ordinance 2026-14/2026-16
buena-vista/0.summary: The Board held a July 28 work session on a cap on short-term rentals, then took up Ordinance 2026-14 on Aug 11 and Aug 25. A follow-up Ordinance 2026-16 amending the same article of Chapter 6 was on the Sept 22 agenda. A letter from "The Alliance" was part of the July 28 packet.

buena-vista/1.title: R-2 OT zone: allowing duplexes and small multifamily (The Crossing)
buena-vista/1.summary: Residents including The Crossing developer Paul Andrews asked the Planning & Zoning Commission to amend R-2 OT zoning to allow small multifamily and attached townhomes for lower-priced housing. On Aug 19 commissioners discussed party walls, 3-foot side setbacks, articulation, and possibly requiring a special use permit for larger lots. Staff were to bring code amendments back, with a formal amendment on the Nov 4 agenda and Historic Preservation Commission feedback on over/under duplexes requested.
buena-vista/1.where: R-2 OT zone, including The Crossing

sources.body: Planning and Zoning Commission - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)
Planning and Zoning Commission - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/2.title: Boys & Girls Club facility at 710 Cedar Street
buena-vista/2.summary: The Planning & Zoning Commission held a public hearing on the major site plan for a new Boys & Girls Club facility on a 0.729-acre town-owned lot. A neighbor wrote in support with a question about Cedar Street parking. The Board of Trustees also considered a second amendment to the ground lease and assignment of the lease to Great Futures BV, Inc.

buena-vista/3.title: 2027 Town budget and fee schedule
buena-vista/3.summary: Treasurer Phillip Puckett presented the preliminary 2027 budget, followed by department head and advisory board presentations and public hearings on Sept 8, Sept 22 and Oct 13. The Board also reviewed a draft 2027 fee schedule, and a well project was included for consideration.

sources.body: Board of Trustees - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/4.title: Water rate study and water efficiency planning
buena-vista/4.summary: Swiftwater Solutions is updating the town utility rate study, with technical memos on 10-year financial planning before the Water Advisory Board. The Urban Land Institute presented on water efficiency in local development and landscaping, and the town is working on a water conservation plan.

buena-vista/5.title: Housing needs assessment and Proposition 123 commitments
buena-vista/5.summary: Buena Vista is part of a regional Housing Needs Assessment with Chaffee County and Salida, due to the state by end of 2026. The Board was asked to adopt a regional Proposition 123 memorandum of understanding and the town's affordable housing commitment for 2027-2029.

buena-vista/6.title: Data center moratorium discussion
buena-vista/6.summary: The Planning & Zoning Commission scheduled a general discussion of a data center moratorium for its Oct 21 meeting.

sources.body: Planning and Zoning Commission - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/7.title: Transportation Master Plan
buena-vista/7.summary: KLJ Engineering introduced the Transportation Master Plan to the Planning & Zoning Commission and then updated the Board. Public priorities include safe crossings of major roads and the railroad, paved multimodal trails, and a parking strategy.

buena-vista/8.title: Rustic Haven cohousing site plan
buena-vista/8.summary: The Planning & Zoning Commission heard the major site plan for Rustic Haven, a 2.2-acre property converting existing cabins (11 units) into cohousing with homeownership at a range of price points. Staff required a water audit, and a neighbor raised concerns about fencing and livestock along an access easement.

buena-vista/9.title: Cottonwood Lake dam and spillway, and Park-n-Ride IGA with CDOT
buena-vista/9.summary: The Board considered bids and funding for the Cottonwood Lake Dam and Spillway project through the Upper Arkansas Water Conservancy District. It also considered an agreement with the state to build a Park-n-Ride on U.S. Highway 24.

buena-vista/10.title: South Main PUD development agreement amendment
buena-vista/10.summary: The Board considered Resolution 2026-55 approving a first amendment to the amended and restated development agreement for the South Main PUD.

buena-vista/11.title: Wildfire resiliency code, fire district inclusion and Ballot Issue 6A
buena-vista/11.summary: The Board held a hearing on local amendments to the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code (Ordinance 2026-15). It later considered a resolution supporting Ballot Issue 6A to include all town property in the Chaffee County Fire Protection District.

sources.body: Board of Trustees - Agendas & Minutes (Packets below)

buena-vista/12.title: Law enforcement agreements with Chaffee County Sheriff
buena-vista/12.summary: The Board considered agreements for a regional tactical response team and for law enforcement mutual aid with the Sheriff's Office. It also considered ending the town's participation in a prior collective special response agreement. The Sheriff's Co-Response Program also gave an update.

buena-vista/13.title: Airport projects and Aspen closure planning
buena-vista/13.summary: The Airport Advisory Board tracked the AWOS weather system bids, which came in higher than expected but ended within funding after the state added money. It also discussed a safety plan, ground lease resolutions, prairie dog hazards, a fuel tank coating problem, and preparing for the 2027 Aspen airport closure.

buena-vista/14.title: Historic buildings: the Pearl and St. Rose of Lima roof
buena-vista/14.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission approved a roof replacement at the historic St. Rose of Lima church building with recommendations including a closer shingle match. Staff reported on stabilizing the Pearl building and expect the town to step away by year end.
buena-vista/14.where: 343 St. Rose of Lima building; the Pearl

buena-vista/15.title: Sangre de Cristo Electric tree permit and town tree work
buena-vista/15.summary: Sangre de Cristo Electric Association's contractor is inventorying trees along its primary lines for pruning and removal, and requested a right-of-way tree work permit presented to the Board on Sept 8. The Tree Advisory Board is also planning its 2026 pruning and removal project.

burlington/0.title: Proposed 2027 city budget
burlington/0.summary: City staff and department heads were scheduled to present the proposed 2027 budget to the City Council at the Oct. 26 meeting. The presenters included the city administrator, police, activities, treasurer, Old Town and economic development.

burlington/1.title: City administrator executive search
burlington/1.summary: The City Council scheduled a closed-door session on a personnel matter about the search for a city administrator. No outcome is stated in the documents.

burlington/2.title: Our Hometown Charitable Foundation fundraiser at The Midway Theater
burlington/2.summary: Council was asked to consider a special events permit for a fundraising event by Our Hometown Charitable Foundation on Saturday, Nov. 21. The event would be at The Midway Theater, 446 14th St.

campo/0.title: Triangle Bikeway East Design alignment and opposition
campo/0.summary: The TCC and Executive Board were asked to endorse a technical alignment for the Triangle Bikeway East Design Project to carry forward to 30% design. At the November 2025 board meeting, a resident spoke against the project, citing mining regulations, zoning and active lawsuits on the property.
campo/0.where: Triangle Bikeway East corridor, Wake County

campo/1.title: Capital Boulevard/US 1 North (U-5307) project and tolling
campo/1.summary: The board discussed accelerating the Capital Blvd./US 1 North project, including its earlier action authorizing tolling. The 2055 transportation plan was recommended for approval subject to removing U-5307 as a tolled project. An outside speaker praised NCDOT and CAMPO for speeding it up.
campo/1.where: Capital Boulevard / US 1 North, Raleigh area

campo/2.title: 2055 Metropolitan Transportation Plan adoption
campo/2.summary: The Executive Board approved the draft 2055 MTP/CTP project list in November 2025 and held public hearings, with final adoption planned for February 2026. A resident at the January hearing called the plan good and asked that safety be emphasized.

campo/3.title: Wake Transit Plan 2035, Bus Plan and annual work plans
campo/3.summary: CAMPO committees reviewed the Recommended 2035 Wake Transit Plan, which aims for routes running 365 days a year, plus quarterly amendments and the FY 2027 Wake Transit Work Plan. The board approved a Wake Bus Plan 2035 contract with Nelson\Nygaard, and a public hearing on the FY 2027 work plan was held in May 2026. A vehicle rental tax revenue footnote was debated.

campo/4.title: Triangle Mobility Hub preferred alternative
campo/4.summary: GoTriangle sought approval of the Locally Preferred Alternative for the Triangle Mobility Hub. After a public hearing where comments generally supported the project, the Executive Board moved to approve it in June 2026. The Triangle West board approved it the day before.

campo/5.title: Project cost estimates and delivery deadline for NCDOT-funded projects
campo/5.summary: NCDOT now requires a certified cost estimate (CSCE) for prioritized projects, with a September 30, 2027 target for all projects. CAMPO has 27 projects needing plans, and officials tracked Division 4 and 5 projects such as the Western Boulevard tunnel and NC 42. The chair asked for more frequent updates.

campo/6.title: Local roads and greenways funding (LAPP) including Crabtree Creek Greenway
