campo/6.summary: Raleigh requested additional funding for the Crabtree Creek Greenway at Lassiter Mill, requiring a 50/50 match, with bids due February 10, 2026. The FFY 2027 LAPP funded 19 submitted projects, including Rolesville, Holly Springs Road and Smith Creek Greenway, and planning began for the FFY 2028 call for projects in August 2026.
campo/6.where: Crabtree Creek Greenway at Lassiter Mill, Raleigh; other Wake County sites

campo/7.title: Bonus allocation projects and TIP amendments (NC 540, RDU interchange)
campo/7.summary: The board selected 16 NC 540 bonus allocation projects, including a new two-lane Neuse River bridge and the Benson Road and Poole Road work, and added them in TIP Amendment #3. The amendment also added an RDU-funded interchange at Aviation Boulevard and National Park, and removed a Cary trails project. Amendment #4 had a hearing in August 2026.
campo/7.where: Johnston and Wake counties; Aviation Blvd at National Park Drive, RDU

campo/8.title: NCDOT resurfacing and safety improvements in Johnston County
campo/8.summary: NCDOT Division 5 briefed the TCC on resurfacing, bridge replacements and the Angier Bypass (scheduled April 2028). CAMPO staff asked whether local funds could widen FY 2028 resurfacing projects to add intersection improvements, and were told it was possible but timing was unclear.

campo/9.title: Regional Transit Technology Plan
campo/9.summary: The TCC and Executive Board approved the Regional Transit Technology Plan as a guiding document for future technology investment, covering real-time passenger information, integrated payments and open data. No public comments were received.

canon-city/0.title: Community pool ballot question and sales tax IGA with the Recreation and Park District
canon-city/0.summary: Council and the Cañon City Area Recreation and Park District worked on ballot language and a revised pool project, including Resolution 12 asking voters to let the city retain previously collected 0.30% pool sales and use tax and continue collecting it. An intergovernmental agreement caps bonds at $18 million and says that if the 2026 question fails, collection of the tax ends.

canon-city/1.title: Royal Gorge Lease Agreement termination and Royal Gorge Mountain Park
canon-city/1.summary: Council held closed-session discussions on negotiation strategy about terminating the Royal Gorge Lease Agreement with Royal Gorge Company of Colorado. Council also took up a grant application for Royal Gorge Mountain Park (Resolution 13, removed from the Oct. 5 agenda), and a trails committee discussed the South Rim Trail.

sources.body: Royal Gorge Mountain Park Trails Committee

canon-city/2.title: Water supply, drought response, rates and bulk water policy
canon-city/2.summary: Council and the Water Committee discussed water quality, water bills and availability during the drought, including which tier of the shortage response plan to adopt. The committee also reviewed a bulk water kiosk policy and a proposed 7% water rate increase, and a special July 9 meeting dealt with water restrictions.

canon-city/3.title: 2027 city budget and budget workshops
canon-city/3.summary: Staff planned the 2027 budget through committee workshops covering police, parks improvement, stormwater and raw water, and discussed using 2026 underspending for critical needs. A public hearing on the 2027 budget was held Oct. 21, showing taxes of about $18.5 million and funds for streets, water, stormwater, the 3rd Street Connector and the pool tax.

sources.body: Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee
Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee
Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee
Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee
Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee
Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee

canon-city/4.title: 2A streets program and pavement plans
canon-city/4.summary: Staff reported 40 road projects completed under the voter-approved 1% 2A sales tax, which now runs through 2036. Contracts were awarded for N 9th Street segments ($2.14M and $4.83M), and 2027 projects include S 12th, College Ave and Harding Ave. Staff also recommended continuing magnesium chloride on gravel roads and updating the Pavement Management Plan in 2028. Council also took up an ordinance amending 2A tax code sections.

sources.body: Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee

canon-city/5.title: Public plaza and parking design options with bids near $940K–$971K
canon-city/5.summary: Council weighed two design options for a public parking and plaza site: the bid design, with low bids of $939,559.78 (Gordon Construction) and $971,290.03 (IS West), or a cheaper concept without stage and restrooms that needs $57–94K more design work and likely stormwater features. Funds are 100% city dollars budgeted in 2026 and proposed for 2027.

canon-city/6.title: City attorney resignation and search
canon-city/6.summary: Council discussed next steps after the city attorney's resignation, and committees were formed to study the city attorney relationship and to search for a replacement.

canon-city/7.title: Police impound lot fence variances at 161 Justice Center Road
canon-city/7.summary: The Board of Adjustment heard a request for four variances from fence standards to allow a 6-foot galvanized chain link security fence around the expanded police impound lot on a 3.99-acre site. Staff had received no public comment as of Sept. 30.

canon-city/8.title: Police compensation, retention and equipment
canon-city/8.summary: The finance committee took up compensation and retention for Cañon City Police, and council approved a police vehicle lease addendum with U.S. Bancorp (Ordinance 11) and bought handguns and ammunition.

sources.body: Finance, Budget, and Public Works Committee

canon-city/9.title: Ditch and culvert maintenance ordinance
canon-city/9.summary: Council considered code language defining culverts, ditches and obstructions and making property owners responsible for maintaining private culverts and stormwater-only ditches and keeping them free of obstruction.

canon-city/10.title: Downtown urban renewal grants
canon-city/10.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority reviewed a Building Systems Grant for 320 Main Street, pre-budget discussion of URA grants, and a special project grant application for 111 N. Cottonwood.

canon-city/11.title: Sales tax on food for home consumption (Sally's Bakery)
canon-city/11.summary: The Economic Development Committee heard a presentation from Ken Rief on whether city sales tax should apply to food for home consumption, prompted by Sally's Bakery.

canon-city/12.title: Public restroom design recommendations
canon-city/12.summary: The Public Safety and Quality of Life Committee reviewed recommendations for public restrooms, including local metal-frame construction, preventing gutter clogging with trash and needles, and police opening/closing.

sources.body: Public Safety and Quality of Life Committee

canon-city/13.title: Saving Places 'On the Road' conference bid and 2027 historic preservation budget
canon-city/13.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission formed a committee and worked on an application to host Colorado Preservation Inc.'s Saving Places 'On the Road' conference for 2028. It also approved a $5,400 2027 budget, planned an archaeology workshop, and wrote a letter on proposed Section 106 changes.

castle-pines/0.title: Annexation Policy and charter amendment requiring voter approval for annexations
castle-pines/0.summary: Council adopted an Annexation Policy (Resolution 26-49) on Aug. 25 after continuing it from Aug. 11, with a minor wording addition. It also passed Resolution 26-53 opposing a citizen-initiated charter amendment on the ballot that would require voter approval for certain large annexations. The Chamber of Commerce spoke against the ballot measure, and a resident asked for a timeline of public meetings in the annexation process.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/1.title: Site Improvement Plan zoning amendment (Ordinance 26-06)
castle-pines/1.summary: Council amended Section 27 (Site Improvement Plan) of the zoning ordinance, with first reading Aug. 11 and a public hearing and second reading Aug. 25. A speaker said comprehensive plan elements should be left in and asked for a holistic review and an amendment, while another supported the ordinance as clear and predictable.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/2.title: Happy Canyon Road/I-25 interchange funding and engineering
castle-pines/2.summary: Council took up several agreements for the Happy Canyon interchange project: an amendment to the CDOT design-phase funding IGA, an IGA with Douglas County, a first amendment to the Alfred Benesch engineering agreement, a Benesch construction-management agreement for Phase 1, and a Stanton constructability and cost-estimating amendment.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/3.title: 2027 city budget and strategic projects
castle-pines/3.summary: Council discussed 2027-2029 strategic projects in August, and the City Manager presented the proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 20. It includes a Road Solutions Plan, Spring Tributary stormwater work at Lagae Road, an open-air pavilion, a second parks foreman, a Trails Master Plan update, and lodging and admissions tax research. Projections assume 104 new home permits, a 36% drop in construction use tax in 2027, and a 28% decrease in some development revenue from 2026.

castle-pines/4.title: Transfer of recreation properties between the City and Castle Pines North Metro District
castle-pines/4.summary: Ordinances 26-08 and 26-09 convey recreation properties from the metro district to the city and certain tracts of land to Castle Pines North Metropolitan District under an existing intergovernmental agreement. They had first reading Sept. 22 and public hearings on second reading Oct. 13.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting
City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/5.title: Soaring Hawk Park phasing and park and trail projects
castle-pines/5.summary: The Parks and Recreation Advisory Board discussed Soaring Hawk Park Phase 1 and its phasing from August through October, plus a Coyote Ridge Park renovation update. Staff also proposed trail signage across 35 trail segments, including kiosks, directional signs and mile markers, with three options weighing budget and look and feel.
castle-pines/5.where: Soaring Hawk Park, Coyote Ridge Park and city trails

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting
Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting
Parks and Recreation Advisory Board Meeting

castle-pines/6.title: Canyonside Preliminary Plan amendment
castle-pines/6.summary: Council held a public hearing on Resolution 26-62 approving the Canyonside Preliminary Plan No. 1, 2nd Amendment (case PFP-2026-001), with staff and applicant presentations.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/7.title: Expedited review for affordable housing (Proposition 123)
castle-pines/7.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-63 adopting an expedited review process for qualified affordable housing developments as part of the city's Proposition 123 commitment.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/8.title: Campaign finance ordinance (Ordinance 26-07)
castle-pines/8.summary: Council reviewed Ordinance 26-07 amending Article 1 of Chapter 2 of the municipal code on campaign finance, with a study session overview and first reading on Sept. 22.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/9.title: Council redistricting (Ordinance 26-10)
castle-pines/9.summary: Council considered an ordinance amending the boundaries of the city's three districts.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/10.title: Coffee shop location and Castle Pines Parkway
castle-pines/10.summary: A resident said she opposes the location of a coffee shop on Castle Pines Parkway and wants the roadway opened.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

castle-pines/11.title: Snow removal contract with Designscapes
castle-pines/11.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-55 approving a professional services agreement with Designscapes for 2026-2027 snow removal, with an updated bid schedule.

sources.body: City Council Study Session and Regular Meeting

centennial/0.title: Elevation Volleyball Annexation and initial zoning
centennial/0.summary: Council took up annexation of the Elevation Volleyball property: first reading of the annexation and initial zoning ordinances (2026-O-11 and 2026-O-12) on Sept. 15, then a Planning Commission review of zoning from Arapahoe County mixed use, and public hearings with findings of fact set for Oct. 6. An annexation petition resolution (2026-R-23) was also on the Aug. 18 agenda.

centennial/1.title: Rezoning north of East Fremont Avenue and east of Potomac Street to light industry
centennial/1.summary: Ordinance 2026-O-14 would rezone property north of E. Fremont Ave. and east of Potomac St. from PUD to Employment Center – Light Industry 50 (EC-LI-50). It went to Planning Commission Aug. 26, first reading Sept. 1, and a public hearing Sept. 15 (Case RZONE-26-00001).
centennial/1.where: North of E. Fremont Ave. and east of Potomac St.

centennial/2.title: 2027/2028 biennial budget
centennial/2.summary: The Budget Committee and Council held work sessions on revenues and fund balance, a Sept. 11 review of the proposed 2027/2028 budget, and workshops on the City Manager's proposed budget Oct. 12 and 13.

centennial/3.title: Sales and use tax rate increase and election
centennial/3.summary: On Aug. 11 Council considered an intergovernmental agreement with an election official and a resolution on authorization to increase the sales and use tax rate (Resolutions 2026-R-25 and 2026-R-26). The documents don't state the outcome.

centennial/4.title: Opting out of the state graywater program
centennial/4.summary: Ordinance 2026-O-15 would opt Centennial out of the state graywater program and prohibit graywater treatment works and graywater use. First reading was Sept. 1 with a hearing on Sept. 15.

centennial/5.title: Land Development Code amendments and industrial/business park regulation
centennial/5.summary: Council study session on Oct. 6 and Planning Commission on Oct. 14 discussed proposed Land Development Code amendments and legislative zoning opportunities. A Sept. 15 special meeting was held for legal advice on regulating industrial and business park uses.

centennial/6.title: General Improvement District fee and cost analysis
centennial/6.summary: The Budget Committee reviewed a fee and cost analysis for General Improvement Districts on Aug. 6. The documents give no details.

centennial/7.title: Westray Business Improvement District 2027 operating plan and budget
centennial/7.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-R-32 approving the Westray Business Improvement District's 2027 operating plan and budget on Oct. 20.

centennial/8.title: Livable Streets residential collectors next phase
centennial/8.summary: Council had a discussion item on the next phase of the Livable Streets program for residential collector streets on Oct. 20.

centennial/9.title: Cisco's All In One Auto Repair conditional use
centennial/9.summary: Planning Commission considered a resolution approving a conditional use for Cisco's All In One Auto Repair on Sept. 9.

center/0.title: Water fund loan from Light & Power: repay or extend
center/0.summary: The water fund borrowed from the Light & Power fund in 2021 when it was running negative, and the Board must decide whether to extend the loan or pay it back. The interest on it is about $25,000 for the water fund, and the Water Department is still in the same financial position. A resolution is needed.

center/1.title: 2026 budget workshops and December budget hearing
center/1.summary: The Council held a budget workshop on Oct. 27-28, with another set for Nov. 18 at 6 p.m. and the budget hearing on Dec. 16. A resident, Bill McClure, asked whether the full budget will be available at the hearing and asked for a five-year goal-setting plan on a future agenda.

center/2.title: Affordable housing contract and Brownstein legal review
center/2.summary: The Brownstein contract is funded through an LPC grant and covers legal review of the Affordable Housing contract. A Housing Authority Board seat is also open, and Ann Cunningham asked to be appointed.

center/3.title: Pathway Project legal representation (Healy Law Office)
center/3.summary: The Council discussed a change to the agreement with Healy Law Office, the Town's attorneys on the Pathway Project, after the attorney who handled it moved on. Splitting the work between two firms would mean two separate bills, so the Town wants a single agreement.

center/4.title: Contract and license confusion with Colorado Post
center/4.summary: Council discussed a contract the Town signed, which new information from Colorado Post may void in part. The Town asked for the contract and not the other party, and the Town is asking Post to let it keep the license. The Town feels it was in good standing, and the Board needs to resolve the confusion.

chaffee-county/0.title: Corrigan Rezone in Garfield (Hwy 50)
chaffee-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission heard a request to rezone several parcels at 22420 and 22435 Hwy 50 in the historic Garfield townsite from Residential Rural to Mixed Use Rural so they can apply for commercial lodging. Staff described it as remediation of a land use code violation; neighbors raised spot zoning, noise, unpermitted structures, septic and fire concerns, while the owner said he wants to help with housing. The matter went to a Commissioners public hearing on October 20.

chaffee-county/1.title: River Village Mobile Home Park rehabilitation and housing grants
chaffee-county/1.summary: The County agreed to act as applicant and fiscal sponsor for a DOLA Division of Housing asbestos-removal grant, with Chaffee Housing Trust implementing rehabilitation of units at River Village Mobile Home Park. Commissioners also took up a $25,000 reimbursement to the Housing Trust from the lodging tax reallocation fund for planning and building fees at the park.

chaffee-county/2.title: Airport land lease, 2027 budget and projects
chaffee-county/2.summary: The airport advisory board discussed a new land lease at length, with members of the Plumb family commenting. The 2027 airport budget includes old fuel farm removal (about $48,000 eligible for grant funding), a well, a master drainage plan and Taxiway A rehabilitation design; the new fuel farm and Taxiway A extension projects are nearly closed out.

chaffee-county/3.title: 2027 county budget hearings
chaffee-county/3.summary: Commissioners scheduled budget hearings in late August and a Sheriff's Office budget hearing in September. The Fair Committee presented its FY27 request, the Conservation Trust Fund 2027 budget was discussed, and the 2027 tourism budget was on the tourism board agenda.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/4.title: Wildfire response, forest health and Common Ground grants
chaffee-county/4.summary: The Common Ground advisory committee reviewed grants including year 3 of 4 for the National Forest Foundation's Sawatch Range Restoration Project, Hands for Lands, and a no-cost extension to 2027 for the Williams and Hamm Ditch project. The county also supported local fire districts' state wildfire mitigation grant applications and updated its community wildfire protection plan, while the Willow Fire burned nearby in Lake County.

chaffee-county/5.title: Salida Mountain Trails grants and GOCO/CYCA application
chaffee-county/5.summary: Commissioners backed a county GOCO/CYCA application for Conservation Service Corps trail maintenance with Colorado Youth Corps, serving as fiscal sponsor. They also ratified a letter of support for Salida Mountain Trails' Colorado Parks and Wildlife non-motorized trails grant with Buena Vista Single Track.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/6.title: Opposition to Colorado Parks and Wildlife water court case 2026CW3107
chaffee-county/6.summary: The commissioners ratified a statement of opposition to a water court application to change water rights held by Colorado Parks and Wildlife and the Wildlife Commission. Separately, they discussed helping people who rely on a water supply at Monarch-area lodging get water restored.

chaffee-county/7.title: Post-event review of The Meadows concert
chaffee-county/7.summary: A public hearing on the post-event review of the August concert at The Meadows was set for October 20; vendor permits for the event were reviewed by public health.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/8.title: Planned developments and affordable housing planning
chaffee-county/8.summary: The Planning Commission held a training session on planned developments, including density bonuses for public benefit and affordable housing requirements for projects over 10 units, and scheduled an affordable housing work session. Commissioners also received regular updates from the Chaffee Housing Authority and Housing Trust.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/9.title: 15099 County Road 350 wetland setback reduction
chaffee-county/9.summary: The Planning Commission put a request to reduce the wetland setback at 15099 County Road 350 on its August 18 agenda.

chaffee-county/10.title: Landfill waste audit and equipment
chaffee-county/10.summary: Commissioners heard a landfill waste audit presentation, approved a purchase agreement with John Deere for a landfill compactor, and accepted a Colorado Energy Office Local IMPACT Accelerator grant for waste diversion and facility energy improvements.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

chaffee-county/11.title: Chaffee County archery range lease with Colorado Parks and Wildlife
chaffee-county/11.summary: Commissioners approved entering a ground lease with CPW for CPW to manage the Chaffee County Archery Range, directing staff to finalize terms.

chaffee-county/12.title: EMS medical director and regional tactical agreement
chaffee-county/12.summary: Commissioners approved a services agreement with Dr. Michael Mandrell as contracted EMS Medical Director and an intergovernmental agreement with Buena Vista for a regional tactical team. The 911 board also approved a Motorola console replacement and a 2026 budget amendment.

chaffee-county/13.title: Electric vehicle fleet study and transmission discussion
chaffee-county/13.summary: A CSU fellow presented on converting county vehicles to electric, including costs, grants and Colorado Charge Ahead. The Colorado Electric Transmission Authority was scheduled to meet with commissioners on September 14.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday
Board of Commissioners Work Session - 1st Monday

chaffee-county/14.title: Public Health reports on completed gun violence prevention grant and safe firearm storage outreach
chaffee-county/14.summary: In the Public Health report in the August 10, 2026 work session materials, staff said the Gun Violence Prevention (GVP) grant has been completed. They noted local firearm retailers were already being approached by multiple initiatives, causing outreach fatigue. The grant's required safe firearm storage messaging did not always match local perspectives.

sources.body: Board of Commissioners Work Session - 2nd Monday

cherry-hills-village/0.title: 2027 budget and temporary 0-mill property tax holiday
cherry-hills-village/0.summary: The draft 2027 budget cuts the Village property tax mill levy to 0 for 2027, about $8.5 million in relief (roughly $4M General Fund and $4.5M Parks Fund), or about $3,800 for the average homeowner. The levy could be restored starting in 2028. Council held a study session on Oct. 20 and a public hearing and first reading of the budget ordinance is scheduled; the draft also adds a Planner I position and a placeholder 10% compensation increase.

cherry-hills-village/1.title: Ballot Question 2C and home rule authority over zoning
cherry-hills-village/1.summary: Council approved Resolution 29 supporting Ballot Question 2C, a Charter amendment referred to voters on Nov. 3, 2026, affirming the city's home rule authority over zoning and land use. Council asked for stronger language challenging state land use legislation framed as a statewide concern, and approved the resolution subject to an added whereas clause.

cherry-hills-village/2.title: Opposition to Ballot Issue 7A (Front Range Passenger Rail District tax)
cherry-hills-village/2.summary: Council considered Resolution 30 opposing Ballot Issue 7A, a Front Range Passenger Rail District tax increase on the November ballot. Council's objection focused on how the district was structured for taxing purposes, and it noted a planned stop near Santa Fe in unincorporated Jefferson County.

cherry-hills-village/3.title: Legislative rezoning, lot frontage and Master Plan sustainability
cherry-hills-village/3.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission scheduled a study session on legislative rezoning and lot frontage. It also discussed Master Plan sustainability goals such as electric police and public works vehicles, electronic permitting, and roadside drainage concerns on steeper streets such as South Holly Street. Land use discussions were deferred partly because of a lawsuit filed by Northglenn over state legislation.

cherry-hills-village/4.title: Parks, Trails & Recreation 2027 work plan
cherry-hills-village/4.summary: The commission drafted its 2027 work plan, adding a Trail Passport Program, Parks & Trails Visioning with safety improvements, a Recreation Reimbursement Program, park signage, e-bike/e-moto rules and possible bike lane improvements on Colorado, Quincy and Mansfield. A member raised concerns about people being hit in crosswalks at the High Line Canal. Council also has potential expansion of municipal parks on its agenda.
cherry-hills-village/4.where: High Line Canal, Volunteer Park, Colorado/Quincy/Mansfield

cherry-hills-village/5.title: Art Commission Day of the Dead exhibit and Oct. 24 family event
cherry-hills-village/5.summary: Council approved an art loan of eight calaveras and bases, not to exceed $10,000. The Art Commission planned a free family event on Oct. 24 from 2 to 4 p.m. with food, crafts, a guitarist and possibly an author or storyteller, within about $4,800 of remaining budget.

cherry-hills-village/6.title: Art Commission 2027 work plan, sculpture-on-loan and logo color
cherry-hills-village/6.summary: The commission is shaping its 2027 work plan and deciding whether to start a 2027 Sculpture-on-Loan project brief, with about $4,687.50 available and $5,000 anticipated in 2027. It is also discussing a brighter cherry-red logo and a Snow Plow Painting Program with the elementary school.

cherry-hills-village/7.title: Wireless infrastructure regulation
cherry-hills-village/7.summary: The City Attorney told Council that the city has limited authority to regulate wireless infrastructure up to fifty feet tall.

cheyenne-county/0.title: PRCA rodeo contracts and Sunday night Cowboy Church approval
cheyenne-county/0.summary: The City Council agenda for October 26, 2026 includes contracts for approval for the PRCA rodeo and approval of a Sunday night Cowboy Church. The agenda gives no amounts, dates or other details.

clear-creek-county/0.title: Lodging tax increase ballot question (Resolution R-26-55)
clear-creek-county/0.summary: The commissioners considered Resolution R-26-55 to send voters a question on raising the county's lodging tax. The funds would go to road maintenance, public safety, childcare and housing for the tourism sector. The question would go to unincorporated areas and the municipalities except Georgetown. The Sept. 1 agenda also lists a work session on the Tourism Bureau website and messaging.

clear-creek-county/1.title: Open fire ban ordinance (Ordinance No. 20) and wildfire preparedness
clear-creek-county/1.summary: The board held a second-reading public hearing on Ordinance No. 20, which would repeal and replace Ordinance No. 16 and set new rules for banning open fires. A Public Safety Power Shutoff presentation and the 2026 wildfire mitigation plan were also on the Aug. 18 agenda. A Wildfire Preparedness Workshop is set for Aug. 26 at the Dumont Fire Station.

clear-creek-county/2.title: 2026 budget check-in and 2027 budget process
clear-creek-county/2.summary: The commissioners reviewed the 2026 budget and began the 2027 budget process. A 2027 proposed budget workshop was scheduled for Oct. 20. Staff requests, including restoring a full-time Deputy Clerk position, are part of the discussion.

clear-creek-county/3.title: I-70 Floyd Hill and CDOT requirements (Condition 9)
clear-creek-county/3.summary: The board scheduled work sessions on CDOT reporting for the I-70 Floyd Hill project. It also planned to discuss CDOT requirements for Condition 9.

clear-creek-county/4.title: Alvarado Open Space Park and Glass Memorial
clear-creek-county/4.summary: The Open Space Commission and commissioners have been following the Alvarado Open Space Park concept and next steps for the Glass Memorial there. Land use review approvals for the Saxon Mountain/Alvarado area and the Waldorf Basin/Stevens area were also on the agenda.

clear-creek-county/5.title: Waldorf inholding purchase by Georgetown and Open Space rules
clear-creek-county/5.summary: The Open Space Commission planned a closed session on a property interest in Parcel 2091-034-00-645 involving the Town of Georgetown. A memo covers Georgetown's purchase of the Waldorf inholding. The commission also began a first discussion of updating its rules and regulations, using Jeffco Open Space park regulations as a reference.

clear-creek-county/6.title: Housing: Prop 123 agreement and Housing Action Plan
clear-creek-county/6.summary: The county considered a letter of commitment to the Clear Creek Regional Housing Authority's Housing Action Plan. It also considered an intergovernmental agreement on shared Proposition 123 affordable housing credits.

clear-creek-county/7.title: Parking on county roads to access open space
clear-creek-county/7.summary: The commissioners scheduled a discussion on parking on county roads used to reach open space and other recreational lands. A related Open Space Commission item concerns legal questions about adding a gate to an access road.

clear-creek-county/8.title: Public road easements from the U.S. Forest Service
clear-creek-county/8.summary: The board considered accepting public road easements from the U.S. Forest Service for Little Bear Creek Road, Raven Ridge Road, Van Eden Road, Morrison Lane, South Spring Gulch Road and Sinton Road.
clear-creek-county/8.where: Little Bear Creek, Raven Ridge, Van Eden, Morrison Ln, South Spring Gulch and Sinton roads

clear-creek-county/9.title: Emergency services improvement district and Fire Authority board nominations
clear-creek-county/9.summary: The board acted as the Emergency Services General Improvement District to nominate Bruce Hohne to the Clear Creek Fire Authority board. The matter appeared on the Oct. 6 and Oct. 20 agendas.

clear-creek-county/10.title: Public health agreements with Jefferson and Arapahoe counties
clear-creek-county/10.summary: The board rescinded and re-approved agreements with Jefferson County Public Health for referral clinical services. It did the same for clinician preceptor services with Arapahoe County Public Health.

clear-creek-county/11.title: Motorcycle noise/pictures public comment
clear-creek-county/11.summary: A resident submitted written public comment with motorcycle pictures for the Aug. 18 meeting. The documents do not state the underlying concern.

colorado-springs/0.title: Project Taurus data center appeal
colorado-springs/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a 15-hour hearing on Project Taurus, a data center development at 1565 High Tech Way (Corporate Ridge Filing No. 1, Lot 4). Appellants challenged the administrative approval of its development plan major modification, and City Council set a special meeting for September 17 at the Pikes Peak Center, with public comment capped at 120 speakers. Planning staff advised commissioners not to discuss the project because next steps are uncertain.

colorado-springs/1.title: Kettle Creek annexation, zoning, metro district and garage setback adjustment
colorado-springs/1.summary: Council took up annexation of 19.88 acres northeast of Kettle Creek Road and Old Ranch Road, along with its zoning. On August 25 it approved the Kettle Creek Metropolitan District service plan on the consent calendar. A separate adjustment to the street-loaded garage setback for the Unit B product at 2060 Old Ranch Road is moving through the Planning Commission. Public comments were included in the annexation packet.
colorado-springs/1.where: Old Ranch Road and Kettle Creek Road

colorado-springs/2.title: 501 N Wahsatch Ave residential conversion adjustment
colorado-springs/2.summary: The owner seeks a Development Standards Adjustment to allow 13.33 dwelling units per acre so an existing commercial building can be converted to residential. Neighbors raised concerns about parking and about losing commercial use. Staff found the request met all criteria. The owner has six parking spaces and said he would join a residential permit-parking program. The item was pulled from the Planning Commission consent calendar for discussion.

colorado-springs/3.title: Homelessness response and the ban on sleeping in vehicles
colorado-springs/3.summary: Council heard the Homelessness Response Action Plan and an update on enforcement of the ordinance banning living in cars, including the Safe Parking program model. Councilmember Donelson asked whether the Chief Housing and Homelessness Officer role should be split in two. An earlier briefing covered the Clean and Safe downtown program, which includes a $400,000 Business Improvement District allocation for cleaning and landscaping.

colorado-springs/4.title: 2027 city budget and revenue outlook
colorado-springs/4.summary: Council reviewed a financial report showing revenue running above 2026 budget, with discussion of retail marijuana tax funding for police and fire and of employee turnover. A supplemental appropriation would eliminate the November furlough day. Council also held a 2027 Budget Work Session on October 15.

colorado-springs/5.title: 2027 budgets, mill levies and operating plans for BIDs, DDA and GIDs
colorado-springs/5.summary: Council scheduled resolutions approving 2027 operating plans for many Business Improvement Districts, the Pikes Peak Regional Building Department budget and general business license fees. It also set mill levies and budgets for the Downtown Development Authority, Briargate GID (4.409 mills) and Marketplace at Austin Bluffs GID (50 mills).

colorado-springs/6.title: Sale of Meadows Park and Wilson Ranch Park property interest
colorado-springs/6.summary: Council went into closed executive session to get legal advice and give negotiating instructions on the sale of Meadows Park Community Center. A later closed session covered a property interest in part of Wilson Ranch Park and sales tax refunds for construction projects.

colorado-springs/7.title: Lowell redevelopment rezoning at East Las Animas Street
colorado-springs/7.summary: A rezone of 1.20 acres at 202, 251 and 252 East Las Animas Street would raise allowed density from 15 to 184 dwelling units per acre, with 950 square feet of commercial space and 65-foot building height. The proposal also modifies the approved Lowell land use plan. Public comment is in the Planning Commission packet.

colorado-springs/8.title: Height allowances for accessory dwelling units
colorado-springs/8.summary: A proposed ordinance would change the Unified Development Code on height allowances for accessory dwelling units. It moved from Planning Commission review to a City Council work session on October 26.

colorado-springs/9.title: Terra Mesa Metropolitan District service plan
colorado-springs/9.summary: Council considered a service plan for the Terra Mesa Metropolitan District covering 42 acres at Research Parkway, including financing of public improvements.

colorado-springs/10.title: Banning Lewis Ranch Village B2 rezoning
colorado-springs/10.summary: Council advanced on first reading a rezoning of land near Tamlin Road and the Dublin Boulevard and Banning Lewis Parkway intersection, to a planned development zone with 3.5-7.99 dwelling units per acre and a 35-foot height limit. A public hearing date was set, and public comment was included in the packet.
colorado-springs/10.where: Tamlin Road near Dublin Blvd and Banning Lewis Parkway

colorado-springs/11.title: Wagner Equipment rezoning at East Platte Avenue and Wooten Road
colorado-springs/11.summary: A 22.37-acre rezone and land use plan southeast of East Platte Avenue and Wooten Road, in the Towne East area, moved from Planning Commission to a Council first reading, with a public hearing set for October 27.
colorado-springs/11.where: East Platte Avenue and Wooten Road

colorado-springs/12.title: Business licensing code rewrite
colorado-springs/12.summary: Council repealed and reordained the city's business license, sales of goods and services, and adult use business codes (Ordinances 26-52, 26-53 and 26-54). A resolution setting general business license fees followed in October.

colorado-springs/13.title: Colorado Springs Utilities bond issues
colorado-springs/13.summary: Council advanced ordinances to refund outstanding utilities system revenue bonds and to issue new Series 2026A tax-exempt and 2026B taxable improvement revenue bonds. The improvement bonds came back for second reading in October.

colorado-springs/14.title: Historic preservation ordinance update and board changes
colorado-springs/14.summary: Staff said updating the historic preservation ordinance is overdue. The board discussed a possible landmarking component, website improvements, a possible meeting time change, and a new chair and vice chair.

columbine-valley/0.title: E-bike and e-scooter ordinance
columbine-valley/0.summary: Trustees raised concerns about electric bikes in January, and in April the police chief described the current approach to e-bikes and e-scooters. The Board directed staff to draft an ordinance. A resident spoke in support in June, and the mayor later reported positive support for it.

columbine-valley/1.title: Platte Canyon Road sidewalk project
columbine-valley/1.summary: The Board approved extra spending on the sidewalk in June. In August a required design change was discussed and the Trustees directed staff to proceed. In September staff said the sidewalk would not proceed because the design had changed too much.

columbine-valley/2.title: 2027 Town Budget
columbine-valley/2.summary: Staff presented a first draft of the 2027 budget in September, including several special projects and initiatives. A second draft and a required public hearing were scheduled for the October and November meetings. A long-range financial forecast was also presented in August.

columbine-valley/3.title: Housing Needs Assessment
columbine-valley/3.summary: The town is conducting a Housing Needs Assessment. A community survey is underway and staff expects the response to exceed the 20% target. A first draft was scheduled for the October 20 meeting.

columbine-valley/4.title: Annexation of 8 Hunter Run
columbine-valley/4.summary: The Board approved Resolution #14 in August concerning the annexation of 8 Hunter Run. Trustee Bill #11 on the annexation was set for a public hearing on October 20. Earlier, the town had also discussed an HOA about annexing into the town.

columbine-valley/5.title: Pickleball noise and Columbine Country Club development
columbine-valley/5.summary: A resident at 7 Fairway raised concerns about pickleball noise and asked the Trustees to act before future development of the Columbine Country Club Villas. Pickleball discussions came up again in May.

columbine-valley/6.title: Fee schedule and permit fees
columbine-valley/6.summary: The Board approved Resolution #13 in August adopting a town-wide fee schedule. Trustee Bill #9 on permit fees was on the October 20 agenda.

columbine-valley/7.title: Jake brake ordinance
columbine-valley/7.summary: Trustee Bill #8 on engine compression (Jake) brakes passed first reading in July and second reading in August.

columbine-valley/8.title: Smoking and vaping ban in Town Park
columbine-valley/8.summary: Trustee Bill #4 prohibiting smoking and vaping in the Town Park passed first reading in March and second reading in April.

columbine-valley/9.title: Building and fire code updates
columbine-valley/9.summary: The Board adopted updated building codes in November 2025 and the 2024 Fire Code in June 2026 after a public hearing. A Building Commissioner ordinance was tabled indefinitely in March. Land use and zoning updates (Trustee Bill #10) were set for a November hearing.

columbine-valley/10.title: Graffiti in Platte Canyon Road culvert
columbine-valley/10.summary: The Town took steps to mitigate graffiti in a culvert under Platte Canyon Road, and updates continued into April.

commerce-city/0.title: Data center moratorium and study
commerce-city/0.summary: Council took up a request to schedule a data center topic for a study session and a possible moratorium ordinance. The Environmental Policy and Innovation Commission is researching data centers and has a recommendation on its October agenda. Public feedback was encouraged.

commerce-city/1.title: Reunion Filing 39 final plat (Oakwood Homes)
commerce-city/1.summary: Oakwood Homes asked for approval of a final plat creating 84 lots and six tracts in the Reunion PUD near Chambers Road and Heartland Drive. The Planning Commission heard it September 1, and a Council resolution approving the plat was set for a public hearing October 19. Written public comment and an applicant response are in the packet.
commerce-city/1.where: Reunion PUD, Chambers Road and Heartland Drive

commerce-city/2.title: Shamrock Foods rezoning at 5199 Ivy Street
commerce-city/2.summary: Shamrock Foods requested rezoning from I-2 to I-3 heavy industrial, plus a conditional use permit involving food oil, at 5199 Ivy Street. The Planning Commission heard it August 4 and Council had the rezoning ordinance on first reading October 5, with second reading set for November 16.
commerce-city/2.where: 5199 Ivy Street, East 52nd Avenue and Ivy Street

commerce-city/3.title: Annexations: Moreno Salas, Third Creek East, South Platte Crossing Phase 2, and enclaves
commerce-city/3.summary: Council considered several annexations: Moreno Salas at East 81st and Quebec, a property near Tower Road, Third Creek East, and South Platte Crossing Phase 2. A September 28 session also covered annexing surrounded enclaves.
commerce-city/3.where: East 81st Avenue and Quebec Street; Tower Road; other sites

commerce-city/4.title: 2027 budget, mill levies and improvement districts
commerce-city/4.summary: Council and the Urban Renewal Authority held preliminary 2027 budget sessions, and the E-470 and Northern Infrastructure improvement districts reviewed mill levy options. Public hearings to adopt the 2027 budgets and set the tax levy were scheduled for October 19.

sources.body: E-470 Commercial Area General Improvement District
E-470 Residential Area General Improvement District
E-470 Commercial Area General Improvement District
E-470 Residential Area General Improvement District

commerce-city/5.title: Oil and gas development north of the city
commerce-city/5.summary: A community open house on the Cord oil and gas development plan was held, and Chevron hosted a meeting on proposed oil and gas development north of the city. Council also set a study session request with Suncor.

sources.body: City Council Notice of Potential Quorum

commerce-city/6.title: Land Development Code rezoning and amendments
commerce-city/6.summary: The city is revising its 2025 Land Development Code, including a legislative rezoning project with proposed zoning maps, Ordinance 2795 and Tier 2 amendments. Public comment was included in packets and a joint study session was set for October 6.

commerce-city/7.title: Hogan Property PUD amendment
commerce-city/7.summary: Council took up an ordinance on second reading amending the Hogan Property PUD to consolidate development standards and expand the boundary at 15955 E 101st Way, covering 16.82 acres. Written public comment was submitted.

commerce-city/8.title: Chambers Road widening and road impact fees
commerce-city/8.summary: Council considered moving road impact fee funds to Phase I road widening projects, awarded a contract for work at Chambers Road and Heartland Drive, and set a project update for October 12.

commerce-city/9.title: Housing Action Plan and Commerce City Housing Authority
commerce-city/9.summary: Council reviewed Commerce City Housing Authority projects and affordable housing developed, and a consultant presented a Housing Action Plan to Council and Planning Commission.

commerce-city/10.title: Crown Enterprises development plan at 10251 Newark Street
commerce-city/10.summary: A development plan amendment for the Crown Enterprises property was continued to a later date set by staff.

commerce-city/11.title: Municipal court, noise and code enforcement ordinances
commerce-city/11.summary: Court staff presented draft ordinances on jury trials and compliance and enforcement, and Council discussed options for the municipal noise ordinance. Ordinances 2806 and 2807 were on the October 19 agenda.

commerce-city/12.title: Public art and Police substation art
commerce-city/12.summary: The Arts & Culture Commission discussed art for the new police substation, 96th Avenue public art, Second Creek Farm Park and the golf course.
commerce-city/12.where: 96th Avenue; Second Creek Farm Park; police substation

commerce-city/13.title: Police mobile command unit purchase
commerce-city/13.summary: Council considered a budget ordinance (2796) to buy a mobile command unit from the SACFD for the Police Department.

cortez/0.title: Lodger's Tax 4% increase on the November ballot
cortez/0.summary: Council took up Ordinance No. 1375 to set ballot language asking voters to approve a four percent increase in the city's Lodger's Tax at the November 3, 2026 general election. It was on the July 28 agenda and had a public hearing on August 11. Resolution No. 13 also set up the county-run 2026 election.

cortez/1.title: Water System Master Plan and Comprehensive Plan water supply update
cortez/1.summary: Council saw a draft Water System Master Plan in July, toured the water treatment plant in August, and considered adopting Resolution No. 16 approving the 2026 Water System Master Plan on September 22. In October it considered awarding the Comprehensive Plan update on Strategic Growth and Water Supply to SE Group.

cortez/2.title: Park Village on 7th affordable housing and 7th Street property
cortez/2.summary: Council got an update on the 7th Street property in August. On October 13 it considered authorizing the Mayor to sign CHFA's notification form for Park Village on 7th, a proposed affordable rental development on city-owned land at the former high school site.

cortez/3.title: Airport Advisory Committee and fixed base operator lease
cortez/3.summary: Council amended the code on Airport Advisory Committee member qualifications and officer terms, then appointed members, including a youth member after an interview in August. On August 11 it also had a notice of termination of the Fixed Base Operator lease and operations agreement on its agenda.

cortez/4.title: Historic designations: Garland Home and 209 West Main
cortez/4.summary: Council moved to place the Garland Home at 120 East North Street on the City Register of Historic Resources, with second reading on September 22. It also took up the building at 209 West Main Street, with first reading September 22 and second reading October 13. Council also accepted a 2026 Certified Local Government grant and a $50,000 supplemental state grant amendment for historic preservation.
cortez/4.where: 120 East North Street; 209 West Main Street

cortez/5.title: Montezuma-Sligo Drainage Improvement Project Phase 2
cortez/5.summary: Council considered awarding Phase 2 of the 2026 drainage project to D&L Construction and authorizing the City Manager to sign a contract.

cortez/6.title: Land Use Code changes (Ordinance 1374)
cortez/6.summary: Staff brought an ordinance changing various sections of the Cortez Land Use Code, with first reading on August 25 and second reading on September 8.

cortez/7.title: Mobile food vendor licensing rules
cortez/7.summary: Council discussed in August a draft ordinance (No. 1371) revising the annual licensing process for mobile food vendors, then considered the ordinance on October 13.

cortez/8.title: 127 N. Market Street site plan
cortez/8.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission reviewed a major site plan for 127 N. Market St. Council then considered Resolution No. 15 approving the site plan on August 25.

cortez/9.title: Carport setback permit at 1411 Montelores Avenue
cortez/9.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission heard a conditional use permit and minor deviation request. Council then held a public hearing on September 22 for a carport on a single-family lot that would encroach into the front and side setbacks.

cortez/10.title: City spending authority limits and City Attorney pay
cortez/10.summary: Council considered Resolution No. 14 to supersede a 2001 resolution and amend spending authority limits. On August 11 it also had an amendment increasing the City Attorney's compensation. A work session executive session addressed the Municipal Judge's contract.

cortez/11.title: Parks: Master Plan committee and ash tree beetle
cortez/11.summary: Council was to choose a representative for the Parks and Recreation Master Plan Project Committee. Parks staff also briefed council on how the emerald ash borer affects ash trees in city parks.

craig/0.title: Craig Business and Industrial Park sketch plan
craig/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission reviewed a major subdivision sketch plan for the Craig Business and Industrial Park at TBD West 1st Street. Commissioners raised concerns about how vague the plan is, building sizing and infrastructure capacity. The recommendation to Council was to approve it on condition that sidewalks are added or the plan is otherwise brought into compliance with the Land Use Code.

craig/1.title: Local Marketing District dissolution fund grants
craig/1.summary: Council approved the Economic Development Advisory Committee's recommendations for grants from the Local Marketing District dissolution fund. Awards included $15,000 for the Moffat County Balloon Festival, $4,000 for the Bear River Young Life car show, $15,000 for Powder Mountain Ventures/Powderbound Adventure, and $3,500 for another request. The Downtown Business Association Rock Fest also had a request approved.

craig/2.title: Moratorium extension on certain business applications
craig/2.summary: Council was scheduled to consider Resolution No. 33 (2026), which would extend and reimpose a moratorium on submitting, accepting, processing and approving applications for the establishment of a certain type of business. The agenda text does not say which type of business.

craig/3.title: Mike Thompson hobby shop site plan at 791 Industrial Ave.
craig/3.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission was asked to recommend a site plan for a personal hobby shop at 791 Industrial Ave. in Green Tree Business Park. The site plan then went to a Council public hearing on October 13.
craig/3.where: 791 Industrial Ave., Green Tree Business Park, Lot 6, Block 1

craig/4.title: Tunatua RV Resort deferred amenities agreement
craig/4.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission was to consider a recommendation to Council on a Deferred Recreational Amenities and Certificate of Occupancy Agreement for the Tunatua RV Resort.

craig/5.title: Business Plan Competition and school bond measure presentations
craig/5.summary: On October 13 Council was to hear from the City Manager and the Economic Development Advisory Committee chair on the Business Plan Competition. Cuyler Meade of 4A for Moffat County Kids was also to present a school bond measure.

craig/6.title: Timberg vacant land plan at Pine Street and East 12th Street
craig/6.summary: Bruce Timberg was to present a tentative plan to the Planning and Zoning Commission for vacant land he owns east of Pine Street and East 12th Street.
craig/6.where: East of Pine Street and East 12th Street

craig/7.title: Carbon Free Futures Development Advisory Board representative
craig/7.summary: Council was to consider Resolution No. 32 (2026) designating Rich Thompson as the city's representative to the Carbon Free Futures Development Advisory Board.

crawford/0.title: Water and sewer rate overhaul
crawford/0.summary: A Water Rate Committee, with consultant Rita Trick of RCAC, found current rates ($35–$41) far below what is needed to cover the $238,800 annual operating need and reserves. Options include a $125/month rate recommendation, bulk water at $2–$3 per 100 gallons, and a tap fee increase from $5,000 to about $11,230. Sewer rate work was authorized in June, and a single proposal is expected to go to public hearing.

crawford/1.title: Crawford State Park water and sewer rate structure
crawford/1.summary: The committee is reviewing how the state park is billed, since it has about 76–78 points of use modeled as ~31 equivalent taps and is billed as a rural commercial tap. The park has grown greatly since the 1990s, and the issue returned on the October 2026 agenda.

crawford/2.title: Spring water project, grant reimbursement and staff overtime
crawford/2.summary: The spring project came in under $400,000 of a $537,000 grant. Staff logged about 150 overtime hours and council debated comp time versus pay, waiting on Bureau of Reclamation guidance. Final reimbursement was received by June 2026.

crawford/3.title: Potable water tank replacement
crawford/3.summary: Tank replacement awaits CDPHE approval of the final design, and CDPHE requires review of the whole project before bids can be split. Bidding is planned for July 2026.

crawford/4.title: 2026 budget and fee schedule
crawford/4.summary: Council held a public hearing on the 2026 budget, which included a $10/month water increase per meter and a sewer deficit of $21,000. Fee schedule Resolution 6-2025 was reviewed (liquor renewal $75, special meeting $1,000) but discussion was deferred in November.

crawford/5.title: Fire-damaged properties cleanup
crawford/5.summary: Council raised concerns about two properties on Dogwood and Elm damaged by fire. Letters were sent to the owners requesting cleanup plans.

crawford/6.title: Cemetery land boundary adjustment
crawford/6.summary: The Cemetery District seeks to buy land from Ann Landreth through a boundary adjustment and final plat. Survey work indicates the historic cattle-drive easement was abandoned decades ago. The item was scheduled for June 22, 2026.

crawford/7.title: Region 10 partnership and campus master plan
crawford/7.summary: Region 10 offered help with planning, grants, broadband, and Enterprise Zone credits ($19,000 reinvested locally last year). Council discussed a master plan for town-owned property.

crawford/8.title: Building permits and enforcement concerns
crawford/8.summary: A resident asked for permit renewal and raised inconsistent enforcement, and was allowed to renew for $50. Council also discussed variance procedures and clearer permit requirements. Unauthorized excavation on town property on K Street is being pursued.

crawford/9.title: 2026 municipal election
crawford/9.summary: Three council seats are up for election, with petitions due January 26. Staff reviewed the intergovernmental agreement with the County Clerk.

crawford/10.title: Public access to meeting packets
crawford/10.summary: A resident reported difficulty accessing agendas online and asked for packets, including water rate reports, to be public. The clerk said she would work on it.

crested-butte/0.title: Zoning and subdivision code rewrite (Chapter 16) with affordable housing incentives
crested-butte/0.summary: Council and the Board of Zoning and Architectural Review worked through a full rewrite of the town's zoning and subdivision code from Nov 2025 to Aug 2026. The work covered residential and commercial districts, Belleview Avenue and Sixth Street incentives tied to deed-restricted space, and the Resident Occupied Affordable Housing (ROAH) program. A final draft was reviewed June 15, with a proposed effective date of September 1, 2026. Ordinances 12-16, including a new official zoning map, went to first reading Aug 4 and second reading Aug 17.

crested-butte/1.title: Non-primary home excise tax and long-range financial planning
crested-butte/1.summary: Staff described structural budget pressures from heavy reliance on sales tax and asked Council about an excise tax on vacant or underused homes and a resident property tax rebate. Council reviewed revenue options of $1.0M and $1.5M. Draft ballot language was discussed Aug 4, and a resolution calling a November 3, 2026 election was on the Aug 17 agenda along with a 2027 Budget Advisory Committee.

crested-butte/2.title: Affordable housing strategy and town home purchases
crested-butte/2.summary: Council reviewed the town's affordable housing portfolio and adopted a 5-year Housing Strategy, with amended 2026 housing guidelines. The town authorized purchases of homes on Gothic Avenue (816, 818, 810, 806 #5A) and 16 Ninth Street, and moved to sell a unit at 16 Ninth Street. It also handled the Whetstone and Paradise Park housing projects.
crested-butte/2.where: Gothic Avenue, Ninth Street, Whetstone and Paradise Park

crested-butte/3.title: Red Lady Avenue and Sixth Street roundabout
crested-butte/3.summary: The town is designing a roundabout at Highway 135/Sixth Street and Red Lady Avenue, where the intersection runs at level of service E at peak hours. In June the Gunnison Watershed School District asked for a cost-sharing discussion on the project.
crested-butte/3.where: Red Lady Avenue and Sixth Street (Highway 135)

crested-butte/4.title: Gunnison to Mt. Crested Butte Corridor Plan
crested-butte/4.summary: Council worked on its values and priorities for the Gunnison County-led Corridor Plan and Transportation Strategy. It held a listening session with the county on Aug 4 and discussed an MOU with the county.
crested-butte/4.where: Gunnison to Mt. Crested Butte corridor (Highway 135)

crested-butte/5.title: Drought water restrictions and water/sewer penalties
crested-butte/5.summary: In June Council discussed changes to water restrictions to address drought. On July 6 it took up Emergency Ordinance 10, amending the violations and penalties for water and sewer regulations, and it ratified the ordinance July 20.

crested-butte/6.title: Mt. Crested Butte Water and Sanitation District biosolids dispute and loan
crested-butte/6.summary: Council held legal discussions about the district's failure to pay for biosolids, and considered a loan agreement with the district in January.
crested-butte/6.where: Mt. Crested Butte Water and Sanitation District

crested-butte/7.title: Parks, Recreation, Open Space and Trails (PROST) plan
crested-butte/7.summary: Council reviewed the PROST plan in work sessions covering the open space definition, success measures, cost recovery philosophy and a parks decision framework. The plan was scheduled for adoption May 4, 2026.

crested-butte/8.title: Single-use plastics reduction
crested-butte/8.summary: Staff sought feedback on a Plastic Pollution Reduction Act ordinance after a survey in November. Council later discussed single-use plastic policies for special events.

crested-butte/9.title: Trash bin fees and wildfire code
crested-butte/9.summary: Council examined 2026-27 Save-As-You-Throw bin fees to fund sanitation. It also adopted the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code as a new article of the municipal code and reviewed the Wildfire Ready Action Plan update.

crested-butte/10.title: Food trucks, parklets and special event rules
crested-butte/10.summary: Council considered The Hideout's request to use a trailer or food truck, extended a suspension on food trucks, and discussed expanding parklets along Elk Avenue at the request of Sherpa Café. It also amended special event permitting rules.
crested-butte/10.where: Elk Avenue and downtown Crested Butte

dacono/0.title: Emergency data center moratorium (Ordinance 1023)
dacono/0.summary: On Aug. 24 the City Council considered Ordinance 1023, an emergency ordinance imposing a temporary moratorium on building permits, special use permits, business licenses and land use applications for any business that includes a data center.

dacono/1.title: Police Advisory Board complaint investigation and process rewrite (Ordinance 1024)
dacono/1.summary: The Police Advisory Board took up a complaint filed July 28, 2026 and reviewed an investigation, while a proposed ordinance would repeal and reenact Municipal Code Section 2-75 on the board's process. Council had first reading Aug. 24 and a public hearing set for Sept. 14.

dacono/2.title: Northern Lot CNS Annexation
dacono/2.summary: The city is moving a petition to annex the Northern Lot CNS property. Council found substantial compliance Sept. 14, Planning Commission reviewed initial zoning Oct. 13, and council considered eligibility and first reading of annexation and zoning ordinances 1026 and 1027 on Oct. 26.

dacono/3.title: Water supply master plan, efficiency plan and water purchases
dacono/3.summary: Council saw a Water Supply Master Plan and Water Efficiency Plan presentation, held a closed session on water supply and a possible land purchase, adopted the 2026 Water Efficiency Plan via Resolution 26-58, and considered a water dedication agreement for Strata Filing 2. Council also toured United Water and Sanitation District.

dacono/4.title: 2027 budget
dacono/4.summary: Council discussed the 2027 budget Oct. 7, received the draft 2027 budget Oct. 12 and set a public hearing. The Urban Renewal Authority also set its own 2027 budget hearing date.

dacono/5.title: City Center Park design and urban renewal funding
dacono/5.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority heard a City Center Park presentation, amended its design services agreement with Wenk Associates, and approved a third amendment to the reimbursement agreement with the city for capital projects. Council approved the matching Resolution 26-55.

dacono/6.title: Sales tax credit for property at Colorado Boulevard
dacono/6.summary: Ordinance 1025 would provide a sales tax credit for taxable transactions at a property on Colorado Boulevard. First reading was considered Sept. 28 and again Oct. 26 with an agreement attached.

dacono/7.title: Strata Dacono Subdivision Filing No. 3
dacono/7.summary: The Planning Commission recommended and council considered a preliminary plat and development plan for Strata Dacono Filing No. 3 (Resolution 26-51).

dacono/8.title: QuikTrip #4224 development agreements
dacono/8.summary: Council considered a subdivision improvement agreement and master development agreement for the QuikTrip #4224 development. Council also took up a right-of-way deed and construction easement for roadway improvements at Colorado Boulevard and 6th Street.

dacono/9.title: Silver Peaks Warehouse site plan
dacono/9.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on a site plan and industrial use application for the Silver Peaks Warehouse.

dacono/10.title: Impact fees and PUD ordinance discussions
dacono/10.summary: Council held staff discussions on impact fees on Oct. 26 and a planned unit development (PUD) ordinance on Sept. 28. A Sept. 26 retreat covered budget, capital planning, land use and economic development.

dacono/11.title: Extensions for Ridge Lands and Sendero subdivision conditions
dacono/11.summary: Council granted or considered repeated extensions of deadlines for conditions of approval for Ridge Lands Filings 1 and 2 and Sendero Filings 1A and following.

de-beque/0.title: Water, wastewater, irrigation and trash fee schedule (Resolution 2026-30)
de-beque/0.summary: The council is set to discuss and act on a resolution adopting a fee schedule for water, wastewater, irrigation and trash services in town. The agenda does not state the amounts or the outcome.

de-beque/1.title: Preliminary 2027 town budget
de-beque/1.summary: Town staff are scheduled to present the preliminary 2027 budget for the Town of De Beque at the September 22 meeting.

de-beque/2.title: HomewardBound of the Grand Valley funding request
de-beque/2.summary: Marvin Duarte is scheduled to give an operational update for HomewardBound of the Grand Valley and make a funding request to the council.

de-beque/3.title: Ordinances 576 and 577 amending the municipal code
de-beque/3.summary: The council is scheduled to consider Ordinance 576, which amends Title 9 of the De Beque municipal code, and Ordinance 577, which amends the municipal code further. The agenda excerpt does not give details of the changes.

de-beque/4.title: Animal Assistance Foundation grant application (Resolution 2026-31)
de-beque/4.summary: The council is to act on a resolution approving the town's application for a grant from the Animal Assistance Foundation.

del-norte/0.title: Outdoor Entertainment Overlay District (Ordinance 789)
del-norte/0.summary: The Council set a public hearing for an Outdoor Entertainment Overlay District, with boundaries and changes to Table 16-4A of the municipal code. A hearing was noticed for September 9, and Ordinance 789 appeared on the September 9 and October 14 agendas, with another hearing on October 14. The documents do not state the outcome.

del-norte/1.title: Moratorium on Flock Safety cameras
del-norte/1.summary: Council discussed a temporary moratorium on Flock Safety license-plate cameras on September 9. Resolution 13-2026 for a moratorium on Flock cameras was on the October 14 agenda.

del-norte/2.title: Cherry Street housing project
del-norte/2.summary: The Council scheduled a July 29 work session on the Cherry Street Housing Project. It was for information and discussion only, with no decisions and no public comment.

del-norte/3.title: 2027 Town budget
del-norte/3.summary: On October 14 the Council was to accept the proposed 2027 Town budget, set a public hearing for November 11, and schedule a budget work session.

del-norte/4.title: Police Department policy manual
del-norte/4.summary: Council discussed adopting Police Department policy and procedure on September 9. Resolution 12-2026 to adopt the Police Department Manual as a stand-alone policy was on the October 14 agenda.

del-norte/5.title: South water well and Water Fund allocation
del-norte/5.summary: The August 12 agenda included allocating Water Fund balance to approve the South Water Well expense. A resident also asked to speak about the Town's water treatment plant property on County Road 14.

del-norte/6.title: Lookout Mountain annexation and GOCO grant
del-norte/6.summary: Gary Blakley was scheduled on September 9 to discuss annexing the Lookout Mountain property and GOCO grant funding. The same agenda included a request from D Mountain Recreation for a changing stall at River Park.

del-norte/7.title: Nuisance violations and civil abatement process
del-norte/7.summary: Council discussed the town's nuisance violation and civil abatement process on September 9.

del-norte/8.title: Rio Grande County Comprehensive Plan engagement
del-norte/8.summary: The town and county planned an open house on October 27 and a Town Board stakeholder meeting on November 4 about the Rio Grande County Comprehensive Plan.

del-norte/9.title: Master Print web and design contract
del-norte/9.summary: Council considered either holding Master Print to a signed contract with specific price and deliverable expectations, or starting an RFP to find another firm for print and web design work.

delta-county/0.title: Clear Water Enterprises rezone (PLN26-022), 378.5 acres from A-35 to RES-1
delta-county/0.summary: Peter Edwards' Clear Water Enterprises LLC asked to rezone about 378.5 acres from A-35 to RES-1 for residential use, with future subdivision. The Planning Commission heard it Aug 12 and the commissioners held a public hearing Sept 15. A water attorney's letter says the water rights and augmentation plan are adequate, citing Golden Eagle Water Company taps and Gunnison River diversions.

delta-county/1.title: Land Use Code update: battery storage, natural medicine businesses and general amendments
delta-county/1.summary: The county held public hearings on Land Use Code amendments, including rules for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and natural medicine businesses, plus setbacks, site plan review, temporary special events and intensive agricultural setbacks. The commissioners considered resolutions adopting the BESS and natural medicine rules and repealing the related moratoriums. In October they submitted further amendments to the Planning Commission for a recommendation.

delta-county/2.title: 2027 county budget
delta-county/2.summary: The proposed 2027 Delta County budget was presented at a special meeting on Oct 13. The Assessor also presented the 2026 Property Assessment Study on Oct 6.

delta-county/3.title: Fire Mountain speed limit and road right-of-way dedications
delta-county/3.summary: The commissioners considered a speed analysis and resolution to change the speed limit on Fire Mountain. They also accepted right-of-way dedications for Fire Mountain Road (2.03 acres), Barrow Mesa Road, H Road, and Surface Creek Road and NE Shady Oak Avenue. A School Bus Ahead sign on G Road west of the railroad tracks was discussed.
delta-county/3.where: Fire Mountain Road, G Road, Surface Creek Road

delta-county/4.title: CAFO land use regulations working group
delta-county/4.summary: The commissioners considered forming a working group to evaluate, review and draft amendments to the county's regulations for Concentrated Animal Feeding Operations.

delta-county/5.title: Hotchkiss skate park request at the fairgrounds
delta-county/5.summary: Hotchkiss resident Tanner Wilson asked the commissioners to support a skate park, suggesting the county fairgrounds as a site. He offered to help with fundraisers and noted the fairgrounds master plan.

delta-county/6.title: 2001 Roadless Rule comment letter and Forest Service road agreement
delta-county/6.summary: The commissioners discussed a county comment letter on the 2001 Roadless Rule and a road agreement between the U.S. Forest Service and Delta County.

delta-county/7.title: Portable chemical toilets policy and septic variance
delta-county/7.summary: The Board of Health scheduled discussion of a public health policy on portable chemical toilets and an on-site wastewater system variance request.

delta-county/8.title: Ginter Grove Public Improvement District
delta-county/8.summary: The commissioners held a special-meeting discussion and advice on the Ginter Grove Public Improvement District.

delta/0.title: Data centers discussion
delta/0.summary: City Council set aside time at its August 4, 2026 work session to discuss data centers, with no packet materials. The documents do not say what was decided.

delta/1.title: Unified Development Code (Ordinance #9, 2026)
delta/1.summary: Council took up Ordinance #9, 2026 on first reading on August 4 to adopt a Unified Development Code, and returned to it on the October 6 agenda.

delta/2.title: 7th Street property and Proposition 123 housing funding
delta/2.summary: Council discussed the city's role in housing and the 7th Street property with Proposition 123 grant funding in August. Resolution #20, 2026 on Proposition 123 was scheduled for October 20 with public comment.

delta/3.title: 2027 budget, TABOR projections and capital plan
delta/3.summary: Council reviewed historical budget trends, the 2026 financial update, TABOR projections and the 5-year Capital Improvement Plan. The 2027 budget was on agendas October 6, 13 and 20.

delta/4.title: Homelessness grant program and Unhoused Task Force
delta/4.summary: Council considered Resolution #15, 2026 for a homelessness resolution program grant on August 4. Carrie Boyd's appointment to the Unhoused Task Force was on the September 15 agenda, and the task force met October 7 at the Delta Police Department with public comment.

delta/5.title: Massano rezone (Ordinance #7, 2026)
delta/5.summary: Council considered the Massano rezone on second and final reading on August 4, with public comment on the agenda.

delta/6.title: Litter and junk code amendments (Ordinance #8, 2026)
delta/6.summary: Council considered amendments to the city's litter and junk codes on second and final reading on August 4.

delta/7.title: South Main Street gateway traffic and Main Street discussions
delta/7.summary: Council scheduled a South Main Street Gateway traffic conversation on September 15 and 22, and a Main Street discussion on October 13.

delta/8.title: North Delta Waterline and wastewater digester projects
delta/8.summary: On October 6, council considered awarding a contract for the North Delta Waterline Project and accepting construction of the wastewater treatment facility digester improvements.

delta/9.title: Subdivision approvals: Stone Mountain, Quintana, O'Connor
delta/9.summary: Council considered the Stone Mountain Filing No. 10 final plat, the Quintana Minor Subdivision, and an extension request for the O'Connor Subdivision.

delta/10.title: Riverbend Resource Center conference and office space
delta/10.summary: Council considered a Riverbend Resource Center conference and office space item on August 18. The documents give no details.

delta/11.title: Comprehensive Elements DOLA grant
delta/11.summary: Council scheduled discussion of a DOLA grant for Comprehensive Elements on October 20.

denver/0.title: Data center moratorium update
denver/0.summary: The Community Planning and Housing Committee heard an update on Denver's data center moratorium on Aug 18, 2026. The documents give no details on what was reported or decided.

denver/1.title: Mayor's Proposed 2027 Budget and sales tax changes
denver/1.summary: Council set a public hearing on the Mayor's Proposed 2027 Budget for Oct 26, 2026, and the budget is open for public inspection beforehand. Committees also reviewed the Finance budget book, a proposal to change sales tax initiatives, and budget working group updates.

sources.body: Operations Meeting of the City Council
Operations Meeting of the City Council

denver/2.title: Council Rules of Procedure amendment (Resolution 26-1096)
denver/2.summary: A resolution amending City Council's Rules of Procedure was postponed in committee on July 28 and again on Aug 11, 2026.

denver/3.title: Entertainment license and fee ordinance (Council Bill 26-0921)
denver/3.summary: Council amended and passed on final consideration a bill updating entertainment license rules and application and license fees across several chapters of the city code. One amendment concerns requests from law enforcement or city officials.

denver/4.title: Minority, women and small business contracting ordinance rewrite
denver/4.summary: Council Bill 26-1216 revises the city's minority-, women-owned and small business contracting rules (Chapter 28). It was filed in committee Aug 25 and placed on final consideration Sept 21, 2026.

denver/5.title: Contract amendments rejected by Council (video, consulting, tech and public health contracts)
denver/5.summary: Council failed to adopt several contract amendments on the floor: Sunny Side Up Solutions videos ($600,000, Aug 10), Jefferson County Public Health food security ($241,000, Aug 17), and Citibot ($3.9 million) and Slalom ($5 million) on Oct 13, 2026. A smaller Sunny Side Up add of $250,000 was adopted Oct 5.

denver/6.title: Homelessness shelters and rapid resolution funding
denver/6.summary: Council approved a series of contracts for rapid resolution and rapid rehousing services, including the Salvation Army, Housing Connector ($1.77 million) and Volunteers of America ($852,000). It also advanced shelter work: a funding amendment for the Sand & Sage/Westerner Motel emergency shelter and a pallet shelter license at 3815 N Steele Street.

denver/7.title: Housing Stability one-year strategic plan continuation for 2027
denver/7.summary: An ordinance and resolution let the Department of Housing Stability submit a one-year continuation plan for 2027. Its next long-range plan comes to Council in September 2027, taking effect January 2028.

denver/8.title: Denver Health sales tax spending
denver/8.summary: Council advanced a contract amendment with Denver Health to implement the .34% sales tax passed in November 2024, including services at 777 Bannock Street, and heard a spending update.

denver/9.title: DIA airline lease agreements and airport construction contracts
denver/9.summary: Council approved a block of use and lease agreements with Air Canada, Air France, Alaska, Lufthansa, WestJet and others at Denver International Airport. It also approved large airport contracts, including $135 million for North Terminal project management support and a $44.9 million pond rehabilitation.

denver/10.title: Downtown Development Authority boundary changes and funding agreements
denver/10.summary: Council approved ordinances amending the boundaries of the Denver Downtown Development Authority and advanced DDDA project funding agreements for the Midland Condominiums, the University Building and 101 West Colfax.

denver/11.title: Broadway Station stadium site and pedestrian bridge
denver/11.summary: Council committee advanced an amendment to the 2025 stadium site agreement with the Broadway Station Metropolitan District and a state grant for the Broadway Station Pedestrian Bridge. The bridge would connect the RTD station with the NWSL soccer stadium and Santa Fe Yards.

denver/12.title: Flood control and drainage projects: Sanderson Gulch and Globeville Levee
denver/12.summary: Council approved agreements with the Urban Drainage and Flood Control District for Sanderson Gulch (new total $22.2 million) and the Globeville Levee (31st Street to East 50th Avenue), plus a federal grant for Sanderson Gulch.

denver/13.title: Civic Center Park and Parks Department capital work
denver/13.summary: Council added $1.63 million to the Studio Gang contract for Civic Center Park (Next 100, Phase 1) and approved an $8.1 million addition for the new Parks facility at Cuernavaca Park. It also approved a $3 million Five Points plaza design contract and on-call parks contracts of up to $20 million each.

denver/14.title: District 6 police station replacement
denver/14.summary: Committee advanced contracts with Roth Sheppard Architects and Fransen-Pittman Construction for a new District 6 police facility and garage at 1566 N Washington Street.
