denver/15.title: Rezonings and landmark designation
denver/15.summary: Council committees advanced rezonings including 3418 W. 14th Avenue and 1371 N Julian Street, and 3343-3351 North Mariposa Street. They also advanced a landmark designation for 740 N. Washington Street. A public hearing was held on a rezoning at 76 North Hazel Court and 80-90 North Yates Street.
denver/15.where: West Colfax, North Mariposa Street, 740 N. Washington St

dolores/0.title: Broc's Development PUD and rezoning of 206 and 207 South Third Street
dolores/0.summary: Broc Smith's (KKV Development) project on 3rd Street/Riverside Avenue went through a PUD concept review in May 2026, with residents raising concerns about parking, three-story height, infrastructure and density. The Board then took up Ordinance 592 rezoning 206 and 207 South Third Street from Downtown Mixed Use. It had a first reading in August, with speakers calling it possible spot zoning and asking for a traffic study, and was approved on second reading on Sept. 14.
dolores/0.where: 206 and 207 South Third Street / Riverside Avenue

dolores/1.title: Phase 2 Water Project funding and water main replacement
dolores/1.summary: The town is funding Phase 2 of its water project through a DWRF loan agreement (Resolutions 700 and 719) and about $700,000 in DOLA funding. Phase 2 construction is expected to start in spring 2027, and the water main replacement continues. Water rates were also on the agenda.

dolores/2.title: 2026 fee schedule, business license fees and Ordinance 591
dolores/2.summary: The Board reworked town fees. Ordinance 591 sets procedures for license renewal, late fees and enforcement and lets fees be set by resolution. It passed on second reading Aug. 10. On July 27 the Board set the business license fee at $30 with a $50 late fee. Short-term rental permit fees were questioned, and a business owner objected to a late fee.

dolores/3.title: Comprehensive Plan update
dolores/3.summary: The town is updating its Comprehensive Plan with a consultant, a community questionnaire and outreach events that ended July 10. Public comments close July 31, and a draft plan is expected in October.

dolores/4.title: Sheriff's contract
dolores/4.summary: The 2026 Sheriff's contract was on the October 2025 agenda. In August 2026 the Board discussed a draft contract and metrics to judge the value and level of law enforcement service.

dolores/5.title: 2027 budget and community center funding
dolores/5.summary: Staff presented the preliminary 2027 budget in October, with a public hearing process ahead. The Community Center Advisory Board asked for direction, and the Board said community center funding would be reviewed in the budget process. Residents want park improvements prioritized.

dolores/6.title: Town Attorney resignation and new legal services
dolores/6.summary: Town Attorney Ethan Sumrall resigned, and the Board accepted his resignation on Oct. 12 (Resolution 723). It approved a legal services agreement with Holligan Westendorff, PLLC. The Board also agreed to hire a water law attorney for river water rights.

dolores/7.title: Public comment rules and public records policy
dolores/7.summary: The Board discussed personal attacks on staff during public comment and planned signage on expectations. A speaker argued the First Amendment limits restrictions. The Board also reviewed a public records request policy and form, and considered adding a public comment period before workshops.

dolores/8.title: Special events, parks and Flanders Park projects
dolores/8.summary: The Board discussed rules for large events and special event liquor permits. A softball tournament organizer asked for a park fee waiver. The Galloping Goose Historical Society asked to add a structure in Flanders Park. The Board also took up a GOCO project, dry parks and a scoreboard.

dolores/9.title: Fire hazards, fire bans and wildfire code
dolores/9.summary: The town adopted county fire restrictions in April and hired tree cutting along the escarpment to reduce fire risk. Residents thanked the Board for not adopting the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. Ordinance 594 adopting the 2024 International Codes had its first reading in October.

dolores/10.title: Dog licensing ordinance and feral cats
dolores/10.summary: Ordinance 589 revised dog licensing requirements to make them more enforceable, passing first reading in March and a second-reading hearing in April. In September staff and trustees discussed ways to address feral cats.

dolores/11.title: Housing grant pass-through and regional housing needs
dolores/11.summary: Resolution 714 makes the town the pass-through agent for a housing project funded by federal and state grants. The Board also discussed the SB24-174 Housing Needs Assessment from Region 9 EDD.

douglas-county/0.title: Ballot measure to expand the Board of County Commissioners from 3 to 5
douglas-county/0.summary: The commissioners fixed a ballot title for expanding the board from 3 to 5 members and debated a resolution referring the measure to voters. On Aug. 31 about two dozen residents spoke, and an amended referral resolution (R-026-062) was moved. A ballot title protest administrative hearing was set for Sept. 3 and 4.

douglas-county/1.summary: The board considered a Business Personal Property Tax Incentive Agreement between Douglas County and Flexential Corp (ED2025-002). Five residents from Parker, Highlands Ranch and Castle Rock spoke, and a motion to approve was made.

douglas-county/2.title: Private activity bonds for Ponderosa Pines and another project
douglas-county/2.summary: A $50,000,000 private activity bond authorizing resolution for Ponderosa Pines was continued at the Aug. 11 land use hearing. A separate $37,000,000 private activity bond resolution appeared on the Sept. 22 agenda.

douglas-county/3.title: Bloom Metropolitan District service plan
douglas-county/3.summary: The commissioners approved a new service plan for the Bloom Metropolitan District (SV2026-001) on Aug. 4. Staff found it met all approval criteria.

Board of County Commissioners Land Use Meeting/Public Hearing

douglas-county/4.title: Zoning rule changes: Section 27 site plans, codification, nonfunctional turf, animal training
douglas-county/4.summary: The county amended Section 27 (Site Improvement Plan) of the zoning resolution and codified the Zoning Resolution in August. Planning Commission is also reviewing rules for nonfunctional turf and artificial turf (DR2026-001) and training of non-owned animals (DR2026-004), with hearings on Sept. 28.

douglas-county/5.title: Trinity Substation and Peaking Facility and Highlands Ranch Filing 159 review
douglas-county/5.summary: The Planning Commission was to review location and extent for the Trinity Substation and Peaking Facility (LE2026-009) and Highlands Ranch Filing 159, Lot 1 (LE2026-010) on Aug. 17.

douglas-county/6.title: Highlands Ranch Parkway reconstruction and traffic signal easement
douglas-county/6.summary: The board accepted an easement from the Highlands Ranch Metropolitan District for traffic signal improvements on the Highlands Ranch Parkway (Broadway to Burntwood) reconstruction, project CI 2026-005.

douglas-county/7.title: Pine View Circle road vacation
douglas-county/7.summary: The board approved vacating Pine View Circle (SB2026-017) on Aug. 25 with two conditions. No public comment was made.

douglas-county/8.title: Road and bridge projects: Dakan Road, Waterton Road, Pine Drive/Pine Lane
douglas-county/8.summary: The county approved temporary closures for the Pine Drive and Pine Lane improvements. It also added contracts for Dakan Road bridge replacement ($51,717 amendment to Rocksol and up to $534,840 to Volkert). A $2,151,870 Muller Engineering contract for Waterton Road (Wadsworth to Campfire) was on the Oct. 20 agenda.

douglas-county/9.summary: A $106,463 construction contract with 53 Corporation for Woodmoor drainage and road repair (SP2025-020) was approved Aug. 25. It also went to the Woodmoor Mountain General Improvement District on Sept. 8.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Business Meeting

douglas-county/10.title: Gold Crown Foundation parks funding and parks projects
douglas-county/10.summary: The board approved a parks funding agreement with the Gold Crown Foundation. It also sought a GOCO grant for Wildcat Regional Park, set up a name change and up to $30k in open space funds for the Mark Weston Open Space Memorial, and contracted for a Macanta Regional Park pedestrian bridge.

douglas-county/11.summary: The board approved a major agritourism permit for Gilly's Pumpkin Patch with six conditions on Sept. 8. Sterling Ranch Filing 6A, 2nd Amendment went to Planning Commission and the commissioners in September.

douglas-county/12.title: Water planning and Rueter-Hess Reservoir
douglas-county/12.summary: Planning Commission was to discuss the 2050 Water Plan and the Comprehensive Master Plan. The Rueter-Hess Advisory Board reviewed budget updates, recreation requests (sailing, e-foil), budget reallocation and Incline Trailhead improvements.

sources.body: Planning Commission Pre-Meeting & Administration Training Session

douglas-county/13.title: Homelessness grant and older adult programs
douglas-county/13.summary: The county applied for a $125,000 Homelessness Resolution Program grant with a $62,500 match. It also gave out Older Adult Initiative grants to local groups and approved transit and in-home services agreements.

dove-creek/0.title: Town Manager hiring and contract
dove-creek/0.summary: Council reviewed applications for the Town Manager position in August, then held an executive session on the Town Manager contract and offer and listed possible action on the contract on Aug. 25.

dove-creek/1.title: Water and sewer enforcement order, sludge removal and capital plan
dove-creek/1.summary: Council has received repeated project updates on a state enforcement order, discussed sludge removal, and reviewed a Capital Improvement Plan request for proposals. Council also considered a letter of support for the Southwest Domestic Water Study.

dove-creek/2.title: Foundational ordinance draft
dove-creek/2.summary: On Sept. 22 the board reviewed a draft foundational ordinance and considered approving it for public release. An Oct. 15 meeting covered a proposed ordinance overview, presentations, discussion and proposed changes.

dove-creek/3.title: Preliminary budget
dove-creek/3.summary: A preliminary budget was on the Oct. 13 agenda for review.

dove-creek/4.title: Town Clerk and Treasurer hiring
dove-creek/4.summary: The board took up a contract for the Treasurer on Sept. 29 and planned to review applications for Town Clerk/Treasurer on Oct. 13.

dove-creek/5.title: Water and sewer tap exemption requests
dove-creek/5.summary: Council considered requests for exemption or forfeiture for water and/or sewer taps at its July 28 meeting.

dove-creek/6.title: Trench box safety equipment purchase
dove-creek/6.summary: The board considered buying a trench box for safety on Sept. 22.

durango/0.title: City Manager's proposed 2027 budget
durango/0.summary: Council held a budget retreat on Oct. 14 to review the City Manager's proposed 2027 budget. On Oct. 20 a public hearing on the proposal was requested, and a joint session with La Plata County covered the 2027 joint sales tax budget.

sources.body: City Council Special Meeting - Budget Retreat
City Council Joint Study Session with County Commissioners

durango/1.title: Land use code changes for the 2025 Housing Needs Assessment
durango/1.summary: An ordinance amending the Land Use and Development Code in response to the 2025 Housing Needs Assessment and 2026 state law was introduced at the Oct. 20 Council meeting. The Community Development Commission also gave a quarterly report on innovative housing and economic development.

durango/2.title: Moving the city into the Durango Fire Protection District on the April 2027 ballot
durango/2.summary: A resolution would direct the City Manager to start the steps to include the City of Durango in the Durango Fire Protection District on the April 2027 election ballot. It was on the Oct. 20 Council agenda.

durango/3.title: South Durango Urban Renewal Plan Area
durango/3.summary: The Durango Urban Renewal Authority study session covered tax increment financing, plan adoption and public finance agreements. It also covered the status, decision points and timeline for the South Durango plan area.

durango/4.title: New City Hall and Police Station site plan
durango/4.summary: The Community Development Commission reviewed early design guidance for the City Hall/Police Station major site plan (PR-26-52) at its Oct. 22 study session and Oct. 26 meeting.

durango/5.title: Noise rules in the Land Use and Development Code
durango/5.summary: Proposed text amendments on noise (PR-26-68) were reviewed at a study session on Oct. 22. They went to a public hearing before the Community Development Commission on Oct. 26.

durango/6.title: Old Hire firefighter and police pension cost-of-living adjustment
durango/6.summary: A resolution would direct the City Manager to start an annual cost-of-living adjustment, equal to the prior year's national inflation rate, for Old Hire firefighter and police pensions.

durango/7.title: Neighborhood parking permit options
durango/7.summary: Council considered a resolution giving staff direction on neighborhood parking permit options on Oct. 20.

durango/8.title: Organic waste management feasibility analysis
durango/8.summary: A resolution would direct the City Manager to study ordinance and policy options for managing organic waste. It was submitted by the Sustainability office.

durango/9.title: Airport terminal development and parking expansion
durango/9.summary: The Airport Commission received updates on the terminal development project and on the Phase III parking expansion and rental car quick turnaround area design.
durango/9.where: Durango-La Plata County Airport, 1000 Airport Road

sources.body: Durango - La Plata County Airport Commission

durango/10.title: Camino Crossing underpass and drone delivery discussion
durango/10.summary: The Community Development Commission heard a presentation on the Camino Crossing underpass. It also discussed drone deliveries, a topic proposed by the Chair.

eagle/0.title: Proposed pickleball courts at Town Park
eagle/0.summary: Residents near Town Park spoke at several Council meetings against proposed pickleball courts, citing noise (courts as close as 68-78 feet from homes), cost and park character. Council heard results of an August 25 open house and online survey on September 8, and residents asked it to redirect the money elsewhere.

eagle/1.title: 2026 supplemental and 2027 town budget and capital priorities
eagle/1.summary: Staff presented a draft 2027 budget with a General Fund operating surplus of $466,340 before transfers and $350,000 in assumed vacancy savings. Council work sessions on September 1, 15 and 29 set capital priorities (Nogal Park, Brush Creek Road extension right-of-way, Grand Ave. Grill demolition/parking) and MEAC and community grant funding. A public hearing on the budget was set for October 21.

eagle/2.title: Eagle River Park funding and engineering
eagle/2.summary: The Eagle River Park Coalition asked Council to include funding for river park maintenance, development and an engineering project in the 2027 budget. Residents spoke in favor and asked Council to work with the Coalition rather than a third-party contractor. Council planned a site visit at 200 Fairgrounds Rd.

eagle/3.title: Variance and appeal/call-up rules in the Land Use Code
eagle/3.summary: Council approved Ordinance 13, amending variance rules in Chapters 4.17 and 4.20, but deleted the subsection prohibiting call-up and directed staff to draft language on appeals and referrals. Planning & Zoning reviewed the variance changes, which end financial hardship as a basis for approval, and was to consider a follow-up resolution on appeal, referral and call-up of land use applications on October 20.

eagle/4.title: Mixed-use step-back standards (LUDC26-04)
eagle/4.summary: Staff proposed changes to Section 4.10.050 on mixed-use and commercial building design, including step-back requirements for multi-story buildings. The proposal went to Planning & Zoning hearings on September 1 and October 20.

eagle/5.title: Red Mountain Ranch Metropolitan District service plan
eagle/5.summary: Council held a public hearing on Resolution 52 approving the consolidated service plan for Red Mountain Ranch Metropolitan Districts 1 and 2. Council discussed financial risks and utility ownership and maintenance responsibilities.

eagle/6.title: Downtown projects: Capitol Street, 215 Capitol purchase, St. Mary's Church and alley vacation
eagle/6.summary: Council took up Ordinance 14 to purchase real property at 215 Capitol Street and Ordinance 10 to vacate an alley in the block bounded by Capitol, Grand, Howard and East Second in exchange for three easements. The town is under contract to buy St. Mary's Church, which may operate there until January 2028, and a property is to be demolished for the Grand Avenue corridor and Brush Creek Road extension.

eagle/7.title: Downtown Development Authority: 212 E. Third Street inclusion, parking and 2027 budget
eagle/7.summary: The DDA approved Resolution 05 to include 212 E. Third Street in the district and discussed other possible inclusions (214 Capitol Street, Big Bear building). It reviewed a draft 2027 budget with a commercial activation rebate program and $10,000 EV charging grant carryover, and scheduled a downtown parking assessment and Broadway activation funding request.

eagle/8.title: Bike Park maintenance funding
eagle/8.summary: Council reviewed who pays for Eagle Bike Park upkeep. The 2023 license makes VVMTA responsible for maintenance, but the town has funded it, with a $44,500 budget in 2026 shifted to the Sales Tax Capital Improvement Fund. Council sought direction on 2027 funding.

eagle/9.title: Haymaker Trailhead restroom cost
eagle/9.summary: The Open Space committee reviewed the Haymaker Trailhead restroom project, whose allocation rose from $90,000 to about $160,000 but drew a single bid of about $380,000. It considered a relocatable vault toilet as an interim option.

eagle/10.title: Right-of-way parking rules and enforcement
eagle/10.summary: Council asked how town code handles parking in the public right-of-way. Police found the code does not specifically prohibit it, though vehicles left 24 hours or more can be treated as abandoned and the Model Traffic Code bars parking near driveways, hydrants and crosswalks. A work session on October 6 covered it with a Grand Avenue map.

eagle/11.title: Water conservation policy and climate programs
eagle/11.summary: Council pulled Resolution 50, a water conservation policy, from the consent agenda for separate discussion. A resident urged limits on grass clipping collection and rainwater collection steps, and Council reviewed climate programs including Beyond Lawn and heat pumps, climate group memberships, and net-zero targets.

eagle/12.title: West and East Eagle sub area plan updates
eagle/12.summary: Council and Planning & Zoning discussed whether to update the 2011 West Eagle Sub Area Plan (density, connectivity, traffic) and the 2021 East Eagle plan (housing amounts and locations), possibly alongside a Comprehensive Plan update.

edgewater/0.title: Zoning Code Update and rewrite (RLI, RMLI, RMHI districts)
edgewater/0.summary: The city is rewriting its zoning code with a Technical Focus Group. The group's June 8, 2026 meeting reviewed proposed residential districts (RLI, RMLI, RMHI), rear-lot intensification, building heights and floor area limits, balancing more housing against Edgewater's cottage-scale character. The code update is also tied to HB24 state housing requirements and the Edgewater 2040 Comprehensive Plan.

edgewater/1.title: Transit-Oriented Communities housing study (HB 24-1313)
edgewater/1.summary: Consultant Matrix Design Group is running a Transit-Oriented Communities planning project and presented existing conditions, housing market and economic feasibility findings to Planning and Zoning on Aug. 12, 2026. The work is meant to shape Edgewater's response to HB 24-1313 housing capacity requirements and to guide housing, land use and transportation strategies.

edgewater/2.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing fast-track review policy
edgewater/2.summary: Staff proposed a resolution adopting an expedited review policy for qualifying affordable housing, with a 90-day review period. Adopting it by June 30, 2026 makes Edgewater eligible for about $45,000 in state incentive funding, which staff would use for affordable housing tools in the zoning code update.

edgewater/3.title: Sheridan Boulevard safety improvements with CDOT
edgewater/3.summary: Planning and Zoning was briefed on the updated Sheridan Corridor Multimodal Plan, coordinated with CDOT, for Sheridan Boulevard between 17th and 26th Avenues, a high-injury corridor. The design adds ADA improvements and signal timing changes, and construction is expected to begin in late 2026.

edgewater/4.title: 2026 budget, tax levy and audit findings
edgewater/4.summary: Council reviewed department budget presentations, set the 2025 tax levy, and scheduled adoption of the annual budget in December. The City Manager called next year's budget very tight. The 2024 audit presentation prompted talk of water, sewer and trash losses, segregation of duties and rate increases.

edgewater/5.title: Local minimum wage ordinance 2025-23
edgewater/5.summary: Council took up an ordinance amending the local minimum wage and tip provisions of the municipal code, effective January 1. First reading was Nov. 25, 2025 and second reading was scheduled Dec. 16.

edgewater/6.title: Right-of-way funding sales tax ballot measure
edgewater/6.summary: A sales tax ballot measure for right-of-way funding was presented to city boards, including the HARP board and the Board of Adjustment, in August and September 2026.

edgewater/7.title: Rezonings at 2525 Harlan St. and 2403 Fenton St.
edgewater/7.summary: Planning and Zoning held public hearings and recommended approval to City Council of a rezoning of 2525 Harlan Street to Residential 2, and of 2403 Fenton Street from R-1 and R-3.

edgewater/8.title: Accessory dwelling unit ordinance and home rule dispute
edgewater/8.summary: Planning and Zoning recommended an ordinance amending Chapter 16 on accessory dwelling units, driven by state legislation. Resident Larry Welshon objected, citing home rule authority. Council tabled Resolution 2025-14 affirming home rule authority.

edgewater/9.title: Foothills Animal Shelter intergovernmental agreement
edgewater/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-02 approving an amended intergovernmental agreement with Jefferson County, Arvada and others on animal sheltering, licensing and funding for the Foothills Animal Shelter.

edgewater/10.title: Accessory structure height variance
edgewater/10.summary: The Board of Adjustment heard a variance request for a 20'2" accessory structure, over the 15-foot limit. It also approved a variance allowing rear-lot parking access closer than five feet to the side lot line.

el-paso-county/0.title: Hillpointe Apartments rezone to RM-30
el-paso-county/0.summary: Hillpointe, LLC asks the county to rezone 14.09 acres from Commercial Regional to RM-30 multi-dwelling residential, keeping the commercial airport overlay. The request was on the Sept. 24 land use agenda.

el-paso-county/1.title: Triple H Ranch preliminary plan (244 lots)
el-paso-county/1.summary: P760 Land, LLC seeks approval of a preliminary plan for 752.68 acres creating 244 single-family lots, with about 40.6 acres of tracts and 67.9 acres of right-of-way, in the RR-2.5 zoning district.
el-paso-county/1.where: Triple H Ranch, El Paso County

el-paso-county/2.title: Highway 83 rezoning from RR-5 to RR-2.5
el-paso-county/2.summary: North Ranch LLC requests rezoning of a 47.55-acre property along State Highway 83, about 0.7 miles south of an intersection, from RR-5 to RR-2.5, allowing smaller rural residential lots.

el-paso-county/3.title: 2027 county budget and regional building department budget
el-paso-county/3.summary: The commissioners held the first 2027 budget hearing on the preliminary balanced budget on Sept. 29. On Oct. 13 they were asked to approve the 2027 Regional Building Department budget and heard a Treasurer's property tax dashboard presentation.

el-paso-county/4.title: Updated weed, rubbish and unsafe structure ordinances
el-paso-county/4.summary: First readings of Ordinances 26-02, 26-03 and 26-04 revise enforcement procedures and legal remedies for weeds and brush, rubbish accumulation, and unsafe structures to comply with Colorado House Bill 26-1239.

el-paso-county/5.title: Mesa Ridge Parkway condemnation and road projects
el-paso-county/5.summary: Commissioners were asked to approve condemnation of property for the Mesa Ridge Parkway improvements between Powers Blvd and Marksheffel Rd. They also considered agreements for the US-24 and Judge Orr Road intersection and the Commerce Road bridge replacement.
el-paso-county/5.where: Mesa Ridge Parkway (Powers Blvd to Marksheffel Rd)

el-paso-county/6.title: Sugarbowl Urban Renewal tax increment agreement
el-paso-county/6.summary: The board considered a Tax Increment Revenue Agreement with the Colorado Springs Urban Renewal Authority for the Sugarbowl Urban Renewal Plan.
el-paso-county/6.where: Sugarbowl urban renewal area, Colorado Springs

el-paso-county/7.title: Courthouse construction contract
el-paso-county/7.summary: Commissioners were asked to approve a $3,633,791 trade contractor agreement with Adolfson and Peterson Construction for the courthouse construction project.

el-paso-county/8.title: November 2026 ballot initiative positions
el-paso-county/8.summary: The board considered a resolution supporting or opposing various statewide ballot initiatives on the November 2026 ballot.

elizabeth/0.title: Gold Creek Commons Sketch Plan
elizabeth/0.summary: The Planning Commission took up the Gold Creek Commons Sketch Plan on Sept. 15 and was asked to recommend Resolution 26R28. The Board of Trustees held a public hearing and was set to consider approving the resolution on Oct. 13.

elizabeth/1.title: 2027 Town budget
elizabeth/1.summary: The Board of Trustees held a budget workshop on Sept. 26, reviewed the 2027 draft budget at its Oct. 13 meeting, and held another 2027 budget workshop on Oct. 17.

elizabeth/2.title: Extending water restrictions
elizabeth/2.summary: The Board of Trustees was to discuss and possibly act on extending the town's water restrictions at its Oct. 13 meeting, presented by Travis Scurlock.

elizabeth/3.title: Pine Ridge wastewater service agreement
elizabeth/3.summary: The Board of Trustees was to consider Resolution 26R21, an intergovernmental agreement for wastewater service between the Town and the Pine Ridge Metropolitan District.

elizabeth/4.title: Accessory building size and permit rules
elizabeth/4.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on Ordinances 26-11 and 26-12, which amend the town code on accessory building size and permit requirements.

elizabeth/5.title: E86 Annexation Agreement
elizabeth/5.summary: The Board of Trustees was to consider Resolution 26R29 on the E86 Annexation Agreement at its Oct. 13 meeting.

elizabeth/6.title: Building permit calculations
elizabeth/6.summary: The Board of Trustees had a discussion on how building permit fees are calculated, led by Alexandra Cramer.

elizabeth/7.title: Friday Night Markets recap and Main Street events
elizabeth/7.summary: The Board of Trustees was to hear a 2026 recap of the Friday Night Markets from Tony Briggs of Elizabeth Brewing Company. The Main Street Board planned to discuss recent Main Street events and a communication plan.

elizabeth/8.title: Town Administrator recruitment
elizabeth/8.summary: The Board of Trustees planned a closed session on recruiting a Town Administrator and discussing candidates.

erie/0.title: Town mineral rights sale to SM Energy repealed; lease talks for the Draco drilling project
erie/0.summary: Council approved Ordinance 26-028 on June 23 to sell Town mineral rights to SM Energy. SM Energy terminated the contract Aug. 19 and Council repealed the ordinance Aug. 25. On Sept. 1 Council was asked for direction on a possible lease (an offer of $12,000 per net mineral acre, about $1.36M bonus) and on the state ECMC process for the Draco pad.

erie/1.title: 2027 Town budget and revenue slowdown
erie/1.summary: Staff say sales tax growth is below 2% and use tax and building permits are down over 40%, so the 2027 budget limits new staff to health-and-safety needs. Council held study sessions Aug. 18 and Oct. 6, with public hearings Oct. 27 and Nov. 10. Advisory boards were asked to cut budgets, such as Tree Board to $4,750 and Sustainability to $9,928.

erie/2.title: Oil and gas regulations update (Title 10, Chapter 12)
erie/2.summary: Planning Commission reviewed proposed revisions to oil and gas rules, including doubling inspection fees, per-well fees, legacy wells, noise, air quality, notification periods and bonding. One resident spoke on the updates.

erie/3.title: Page property rezoning and open space protection
erie/3.summary: The Open Space and Trails board recommended rezoning Page property land west of the Cottonwood Extension Irrigation Ditch as Reserved Open Space. Council discussion of the property is set for Nov. 10. A rezoning at 1025 Weld County Road 1 1/2 was also on the board's agenda, and a joint session with Planning Commission on Oct. 21 covered how to protect open space, which needs voter approval to sell or rezone.
erie/3.where: Page property, near CR 1.5 and Reliance Park

sources.body: Open Space and Trails Advisory Board
Open Space and Trails Advisory Board
Open Space and Trails Advisory Board

erie/4.title: New Town Manager appointed
erie/4.summary: After receiving 60 applications in August and holding interviews, Council considered a resolution appointing Kelli Johnson as Town Manager starting Jan. 4, 2027, with an employment agreement.

erie/5.title: Colliers Hill urban renewal tax increment agreements
erie/5.summary: Town Council and the Urban Renewal Authority took up agreements on sharing tax increment revenue in the Colliers Hill plan area. An amendment with Weld County, approved by the County Sept. 2, removes the requirement that revenue between $10M and $14M go to Weld County Road 5 and adds parks and recreation facilities as eligible uses.
erie/5.where: Colliers Hill Urban Renewal Plan Area

erie/6.title: Downtown Briggs Street improvements and Old Town bridge design
erie/6.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority approved paying the Town for downtown infrastructure construction and a $30K design contract amendment with Felsburg Holt & Ullevig, adding to a prior $271K reimbursement. The URA also considered a disposition and development agreement for 150 Briggs. Council considered right-of-way encroachment licenses for businesses at 500, 502 and 545 Briggs Street.

erie/7.title: Vista Ridge golf course PD amendment and Vista Reserve plat
erie/7.summary: Planning Commission held a hearing on Vista Ridge PD Amendment No. 9 for the golf course. Council considered Vista Ridge PD amendment and Vista Reserve preliminary plat Sept. 8 and a hearing on the amendment Oct. 13.

erie/8.title: Short-term rental regulations
erie/8.summary: Planning Commission considered a new UDC chapter on short-term rentals, and Council scheduled a public hearing on the ordinance Oct. 13.

erie/9.title: Airport hangars, through-the-fence fees and noise
erie/9.summary: The airport board discussed residential through-the-fence fees, commercial fees, a charter change to allow land leases longer than 20 years on the ballot, and a hangar presentation to Council Oct. 13. A resident asked for more regulation of early-morning touch-and-go flights.

erie/10.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing and comprehensive plan amendment
erie/10.summary: Erie is requesting that its Prop 123 affordable housing unit requirement be reduced to 30 units. Planning Commission and Council also considered amending the 2024 Elevate Erie Comprehensive Plan and planned a Unified Development Code update with a DOLA grant application.

erie/11.title: Erie Lake Dam seepage project and County Line Road stream restoration
erie/11.summary: Council considered contract amendments for the Erie Lake Dam seepage project and authorized negotiations to acquire property and easements for the County Line Road and Coal Creek stream restoration.
erie/11.where: Erie Lake; County Line Road and Coal Creek

erie/12.title: Community center, recreation campus and Linear Park projects
erie/12.summary: Council considered design amendments for the Erie Community Center renovation and expansion, a recreation campus feasibility study, and a construction contract for Linear Park mainline work. Bids for irrigation at Linear Park were received.

erie/13.title: Montessori Children's World special use at 480 Cheesman Street
erie/13.summary: Planning Commission scheduled a public hearing on a special review use for the Montessori Children's World, along with a Coal Creek property rezoning.

estes-park/0.title: Development Code update: 50% draft, new zoning districts and housing density bonuses
estes-park/0.summary: Headwaters Planning presented the 50% draft of the Development Code update, which adds Mixed-Use and Open Space districts, more housing types in multi-family and mixed-use zones, and density and height bonuses for workforce housing. Staff noted a split between affordable-housing advocates and residents wanting to keep current densities. The Board also discussed lower parking minimums (EPHA said 1.2 to 1.4 cars per unit would suffice) and, on Sept 8, new rezoning review criteria in Section 3.3.

estes-park/1.title: Fall River Village II PUD and subdivision plats
estes-park/1.summary: Resolutions 87-26, 88-26 and 89-26 on the Fall River Village II PUD and plats were continued from July 28. The hearing was re-opened Aug 11, with staff noting code and state statute deadlines that would deem the application approved if no action was taken.

estes-park/2.title: Annexation of Fawn Valley and Highway 7 enclaves
estes-park/2.summary: Staff reviewed costs and benefits of annexing two enclaves. Estimates were $50,000 for a consultant to prepare maps and legal descriptions, about $12,750 a year in sales tax and $1,900 in property tax, and $2,400 a year for 25 years for road work on Chalet Ridge Court. Highway 7 area surveys drew four responses opposed and one in favor, and staff will research who owns an unannexed gap parcel.

estes-park/3.title: Housing needs, Housing Action Plan and Housing Authority
estes-park/3.summary: Residents urged the Board to address workforce housing, including a list of people in immediate need. The Housing Authority is struggling with recruitment, drew 14 applicants for three board seats, and is working on its funding plan and 2027 budget. A Housing Assessment Addendum and Housing Action Plan came before the Board Sept 22.

estes-park/4.title: Water: Windy Gap units, administrative penalties and Colorado-Big Thompson subcontract
estes-park/4.summary: The Board declined to buy Windy Gap water units from Platte River Power Authority, since the Town doesn't need them and would have had to buy two units for nearly $10 million. Staff proposed administrative fines to enforce repair of surface water lines, and set dates for water rate hearings. The Board also pulled for discussion the C-BT subcontract extension with YMCA of the Rockies and the effort to include Town water customers in the Northern Water district.

estes-park/5.title: Dark Sky certification and draft lighting ordinance
estes-park/5.summary: Visit Estes Park pitched International DarkSky Community certification as a tourism draw. Board members raised concerns about a draft lighting ordinance requiring residential properties to switch to compliant fixtures within ten years. Members asked for examples from other certified communities.

estes-park/6.title: Parks and Open Space Master Plan
estes-park/6.summary: Staff presented the final draft plan covering 11 parks, two natural areas and two town parcels; 76% of households are within a 15-minute walk of a park. Board members asked for an urban forestry program, more dog parks and wildlife conflict reduction, and staff said implementation depends on funding. The draft was available for public comment.

estes-park/7.title: Fire district funding and Town budget
estes-park/7.summary: A resident raised Estes Valley Fire Protection District funding, and the Town Administrator clarified the Board had not discussed cutting current funding. The Board also heard Larimer County budget shortfalls and prepared for a joint study session with the county commissioners.

estes-park/8.title: Events Center storage building contract and impact grant
estes-park/8.summary: The Board approved a $424,350 contract with Kinley Built to design and build a storage building at the Events Center Complex. It also accepted a $100,000 state energy and mineral impact grant toward a design project.

estes-park/9.title: Micromobility devices and feather flag sign rules
estes-park/9.summary: Police proposed four changes to Municipal Code Chapter 9 to clarify rules for micromobility devices such as e-bikes and scooters. The Board also weighed whether to make temporary feather flags permanent, with a one-per-lot limit, 12-foot height cap and setbacks, and was split on requiring a fee and permit.

fairplay/0.title: Gemenskap development sewer system negotiations and mediation
fairplay/0.summary: The Board repeatedly went into executive session to discuss negotiation strategy over the sewer system at the Gemenskap development in Park County. The sessions cover a mediation with the developer held July 27, 2026, and related discussions. A joint executive session with the Park County commissioners was set for Sept. 15. The agendas also list settlement of Sallie Williard's potential claim.

fairplay/1.title: Land swap with Park County (Ordinance No. 5)
fairplay/1.summary: On first reading, Ordinance No. 5 would authorize the Town to convey Park County Parcel No. 32670 to Park County in exchange for property from the county. The Board and the county commissioners also held a joint session on Sept. 15.

fairplay/2.title: Park County use of Fairplay water for contaminated wells
fairplay/2.summary: The Board scheduled a discussion of Park County's use of Town of Fairplay water for wells that are contaminated. The agenda excerpt does not state the cause or any decision.

fairplay/3.title: 2027 budget and amended 2026 budget
fairplay/3.summary: The Board reviewed the 2027 budget timeline, the initial proposed 2027 Police Department budget, preliminary staffing and salary proposals, and special events and visitor center budgets. The proposed amended FY2026 and FY2027 budgets were submitted on Oct. 19 with a hearing and adoption schedule.

fairplay/4.title: Wastewater lagoon liner project and sewer plant repairs
fairplay/4.summary: Bills show ongoing engineering, dewatering, crane and liner repair work on the wastewater lagoons. A new pump and motor for the treatment plant and sewer line jetting were also paid for. A Wastewater ORC report was on the Aug. 17 agenda.
fairplay/4.where: Fairplay wastewater treatment plant and lagoons

fairplay/5.title: Water conservation, source water protection and water rights planning
fairplay/5.summary: The Board discussed water conservation plans on Aug. 17. On Oct. 19 it heard a Colorado Rural Water Association presentation on the Source Water Protection Plan and held a work session on Town water rights, resources and the utilities capital improvement plan.

fairplay/6.title: Funding requests from the Park County Senior Coalition and Rocky Mountain Rural Health
fairplay/6.summary: The Park County Senior Coalition asked the Town for funding for meals, transportation and other services for seniors across the county. The Board reviewed this request and one from Rocky Mountain Rural Health together with final-quarter 2026 recurring funding requests.

fairplay/7.title: The Bluffs development update
fairplay/7.summary: Steve Crozier of FP Land, LLC was scheduled to update the Board on The Bluffs Development on Aug. 17. The documents give no details of the update.

fairplay/8.title: Police Department personnel matter and station assessment
fairplay/8.summary: The Board planned executive sessions for legal advice and personnel matters involving Chief of Police Jeff Worley and an officer who is the subject of an investigation. A structural assessment of the police station was also underway, with a first pay application of $16,955.29.

fairplay/9.title: Mardi Gras fundraiser, Burro Days and community event funding
fairplay/9.summary: The Board set up an application for nonprofits to be the Mardi Gras fundraiser beneficiary, and applicants presented on Oct. 19. It also considered a Burro Days funding request from South Park School District RE-2, a Halloween Spooktacular request, and a $1,000 donation to a South Park High School football car show fundraiser.

fairplay/10.title: Property improvement incentive (PIIP) agreements and downtown design review
fairplay/10.summary: The Board considered PIIP agreements for 711 Front Street (Andrew Schofield) and for window replacements at 305 4th Street and 402 Hathaway Street (Greg Johnson). It also held architectural review hearings on a Central Colorado Water Conservancy District mural at 548 Front Street and exterior work at 711 Front Street.
fairplay/10.where: Front Street, 4th Street and Hathaway Street

fairplay/11.title: Unified Development Code and Comprehensive Plan update
fairplay/11.summary: The Board considered adding members to the steering committee for the Unified Development Code and Comprehensive Plan update project.

fairplay/12.title: Town fee schedule amendment and fireworks show
fairplay/12.summary: The Board took up Resolution No. 33 to amend the Town's schedule of fees on first reading. It also discussed whether to hold a 2026 fireworks show.

federal-heights/0.title: Public safety tax discussion
federal-heights/0.summary: City Manager Jacquie Halburnt is scheduled to lead a council discussion of a public safety tax at the October 20, 2026 meeting. The documents give no details on the amount or any decision.

federal-heights/1.title: 2027 draft budget changes and fee schedule
federal-heights/1.summary: Finance Director Tim Weitzman is scheduled to present changes to the 2027 draft budget. Council will also consider a resolution adopting the 2027 fee schedule.

federal-heights/2.title: Police Department concerns and calls to dismiss the City Manager
federal-heights/2.summary: Residents told council that, in their opinion, the Police Department is in disarray, the city has a high crime rate, and the City Manager should be dismissed. These comments came as council also took up police items such as a code enforcement van replacement and a Motorola VESTA NXT project.

federal-heights/3.title: Police equipment: code enforcement van and Motorola VESTA NXT
federal-heights/3.summary: Council is to consider a request to replace and upfit a Police Department code enforcement van. It will also consider a 2027 Motorola VESTA NXT project presented by Acting Chief Karl Ballard.

federal-heights/4.title: Holiday market proposal at Water World parking lot
federal-heights/4.summary: Moses Chavez told council he wants to hold a holiday market in the Water World parking lot.

federal-heights/5.title: Intergovernmental agreement with Hyland Hills Park and Recreation District
federal-heights/5.summary: Council is to consider a resolution approving an intergovernmental agreement between the city and Hyland Hills Park and Recreation District, presented by Community Development Director Tim Williams.

federal-heights/6.title: Local Natural Hazard Mitigation Plan agreement
federal-heights/6.summary: Council is to consider an intergovernmental agreement with neighboring governments for a local natural hazard mitigation plan.

federal-heights/7.title: More frequent City Council meetings
federal-heights/7.summary: Council is scheduled to discuss increasing how often it meets.

firestone/0.title: Comprehensive plan update
firestone/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission held a public hearing on approving an update to Firestone's comprehensive plan.

firestone/1.title: Barefoot Lakes Filing 5 subdivision changes
firestone/1.summary: The planning commission recommended an amended preliminary plat for Barefoot Lakes Filing 5, with a neighbor raising concerns about views and buffering.

firestone/2.title: Parks and trails projects and 2027 budget requests
firestone/2.summary: The parks commission ranked trail fixes and new connections, including links toward St. Vrain State Park, rotted bridge boards south of Gateway Park and possible pickleball courts, as budget recommendations.

sources.body: Parks, Trails, Recreation and Open Space Commission

firestone/3.title: Town hall summer hours pilot
firestone/3.summary: Trustees discussed a pilot program for summer office hours.

fort-collins/0.title: 2027-2028 Biennial Budget
fort-collins/0.summary: Council held a series of work sessions in September and October on the City Manager's Recommended 2027-2028 budget, the first under Priority Based Budgeting. Staff found a gap between ongoing revenue and expenses and asked service areas to identify 8% in cost reductions. Council is to give direction on changes before adoption in November; residents raised concerns about higher Lincoln Center rental rates and user fees.

fort-collins/1.title: Joining the Northern Integrated Supply Project (NISP) instead of enlarging Halligan Reservoir
fort-collins/1.summary: The Water Utility Enterprise Board is asked to approve agreements for Fort Collins to become a NISP participant and store some of its own water rights in Glade Reservoir. Staff cite permitting uncertainty at Halligan and say NISP is projected to mean lower rate increases. The city would notify the Army Corps and withdraw its Clean Water Act Section 404 permit application for the Halligan Project.

fort-collins/2.title: Montava wholesale water agreement with ELCO
fort-collins/2.summary: Council reviewed a wholesale water arrangement with East Larimer County Water District to serve Montava, a 4,000+ unit mixed-use development in northeast Fort Collins. Councilmembers supported advancing it, while asking about development fees, utility revenue, water supply sufficiency under climate change, and the non-potable system. Long-term water planning is to be addressed in an Integrated Water Resources Plan proposed for 2027.

fort-collins/3.title: North College Urban Renewal: 1505 N College grant, 1630 N College purchase, Bristlecone housing loan and community charter
fort-collins/3.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority considered a roughly $1 million redevelopment agreement with façade, infrastructure and community food-system improvements at 1505 N College Ave, a $250,000 appropriation to acquire 1630 N College, and a $2 million loan term sheet for Bristlecone Affordable, a 112-unit income-restricted project. It also discussed a draft community Coalition Charter for 1636 N College and the superblock, plus plan finances before TIF ends. Executive sessions covered possible property purchases including eminent domain.
fort-collins/3.where: North College Avenue (1505, 1630 and 1636 N College)

fort-collins/4.title: Downtown paid parking pilot
fort-collins/4.summary: Council discussed a paid-parking pilot at the Oak & Remington surface lot and other options including on-street paid parking, and asked staff to return with revised pilot options and downtown employee parking ideas. A code update is being prepared for an on-street pilot. The College Avenue waterline delay gives more time. Residents have commented on parking messaging and fees.
fort-collins/4.where: Downtown Fort Collins / Oak & Remington lot

fort-collins/5.title: Conveyance of city-owned land at 314 North Howes Street for affordable housing
fort-collins/5.summary: Council took up Ordinance 098 conveying city-owned property at 314 N Howes Street to support affordable housing. A resident called it a large giveaway. Another speaker said Housing Catalyst was given the site though funding for its project at the EcoThrift site is not in place, and a councilmember attributed the delay to competitive housing subsidies.

fort-collins/6.title: Real Estate Strategic Framework and Civic Center Master Plan
fort-collins/6.summary: Council broadly supported a strategic portfolio approach to managing city-owned property and asked for valuations, zoning, evaluation criteria and disposition information. Members generally backed updating the Civic Center Master Plan but cautioned about scope, timing and budget.

fort-collins/7.title: Restricted Products Program (tobacco, nicotine, kratom)
fort-collins/7.summary: Council discussed a program to regulate age-restricted products beyond tobacco and nicotine, including kratom. Flavored tobacco would be assessed after the initial program, and staff were encouraged to involve the Youth Advisory Board. A draft ordinance will come back.

fort-collins/8.title: Safe Parking Pilot Program
fort-collins/8.summary: Staff briefed Council on a possible safe parking pilot and asked whether to pursue it and what code and enforcement changes are needed. Input was mixed on whether an ordinance is needed to ensure neighbor voices are heard.

fort-collins/9.title: Economic Development Investment Program
fort-collins/9.summary: Council gave broad support to a new Economic Development Investment Program. Members favored using it for community vitality and micro-business ideas over jobs or sales tax, preferred after-the-fact review, and were uneasy about ongoing annual commitments. Council adopts the 2027/28 budget in November.

fort-collins/10.title: Land Use Code Ordinance 118 and RP3 parking permit charges
fort-collins/10.summary: Ordinance 118 amending the Land Use Code was pulled from consent for discussion, and residents spoke in support. A resident opposed the RP3 change to charge for the first vehicle parked in front of a home; a councilmember said she requested a pause on the new rates.

fort-collins/11.title: Platte River Power Authority rollback of 100% non-carbon electricity by 2030 goal
fort-collins/11.summary: Several residents opposed the Platte River Power Authority Board's discussion of rolling back its goal of 100% non-carbon electricity by 2030.

fort-collins/12.title: College and Drake Urban Renewal Plan amendment
fort-collins/12.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority considered funding an existing conditions study around College and Drake to amend the plan, since its original intent is no longer viable. The study would evaluate adding properties.

fort-collins/13.title: Election Code changes
fort-collins/13.summary: The Election Code Committee reviewed proposed code changes, including letting the City Clerk issue fines directly for late campaign reports, precinct boundary changes, and campaign coordination limits. Longer-term items include public campaign funding.

fort-lupton/0.title: Temporary pause on data center applications (5 MW or more)
fort-lupton/0.summary: On the Oct. 20 agenda, Council considered an ordinance (AM 2026-158) temporarily suspending submission, acceptance, processing and approval of applications to establish or expand data center facilities with a demand of 5 megawatts or more. The documents do not state the outcome.

fort-lupton/1.title: Western Midstream Parsnip Pipeline special use permit
fort-lupton/1.summary: Western Midstream is seeking a special use permit for two buried gas gathering pipelines through I-2 industrial, mining and agricultural parcels in the city. At the Planning Commission hearing, neighbors including Joseph and Sue Hubert and Leeroy Sack of County Road 10 asked about pipe size and whether their land would be accessed. The permit went to City Council for a public hearing.
fort-lupton/1.where: Pipeline route through I-2 parcels near County Road 10 and S. Denver Ave.

fort-lupton/2.title: Water and sewer plant investment (tap) fee changes
fort-lupton/2.summary: Council approved a revised Water and Sewer Infrastructure Investment Fee Schedule effective December 1, 2026. Staff surveyed regional tap fees, noted METRO Water Recovery is raising its fee to $6,290, and cited ongoing upgrades to the water and wastewater treatment plants and distribution system. Further 2027 fee changes were on the Sept. 8 agenda.

fort-lupton/3.title: Street reconstruction design contracts funded by CR 12 UPRR funds
fort-lupton/3.summary: Council awarded design work for 5th Street and Broadway Avenue to JVA (up to $143,095), for Homestead Drive and Columbine Avenue to IMEG, and the 3rd and 5th Street project to HKS. A JVA amendment of up to $16,585 followed in October. The work is paid from CR 12 UPRR project funds.
fort-lupton/3.where: 5th St & Broadway Ave; Homestead Dr & Columbine Ave; 3rd & 5th St

fort-lupton/4.title: Water tower project contracts and easement
fort-lupton/4.summary: Council took up a construction management contract amendment with Burns & McDonnell, a change order with HPM and an easement from Murray Farms, all for the water tower project.

fort-lupton/5.title: Comprehensive Plan update, housing action plan and land use categories
fort-lupton/5.summary: The city is updating its Comprehensive Plan with Ayres Associates, whose contract was amended to add a water supply element. The Planning Commission reviewed the draft Housing Action Plan, strategic growth plan and proposed land use categories. Council also backed a DOLA Local Planning Capacity grant application, and the Design Workshop contract is for the Parks and Trails plan.

fort-lupton/6.title: 2027 budget and property tax limit exclusion
fort-lupton/6.summary: Council received the 2027 requested budget on Sept. 29 and held a budget retreat Oct. 17 on the preliminary budget. Council also considered an application for exclusion from the 5.5% assessed valuation limit, and the Urban Renewal Authority reviewed its own 2027 draft budget.

fort-lupton/7.title: Ewing Annexation Agreement amendment
fort-lupton/7.summary: Council took up a first amendment to the Ewing Annexation Agreement, originally approved April 16, 2024, with ordinance readings on Sept. 1 and Sept. 29.

fort-lupton/8.title: New metropolitan district service plans: Lancaster Crossing and 277
fort-lupton/8.summary: Council was scheduled on Sept. 29 to consider a resubmitted service plan for Lancaster Crossing Metropolitan District Nos. 1-5 and a service plan for the 277 Metropolitan District.

fort-lupton/9.title: Urban Renewal Authority grants and projects
fort-lupton/9.summary: The Fort Lupton Urban Renewal Authority discussed El Rey Del Taco's request for a six-month grant extension and a resolution to fund 50% of an $86,820 survey and engineering project. It also tracks TIF reimbursements for Vincent's and the Rec Center.

fort-lupton/10.title: Koshio Park renovation
fort-lupton/10.summary: Council handled change orders for Koshio Park, including temporary irrigation and Change Order No. 2, as the park is renovated. The Urban Renewal Authority noted the groundbreaking.

fort-lupton/11.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment
fort-lupton/11.summary: Council directed the Planning Department to file the local affordable housing commitment for 2027-2029 so the city can take part in Proposition 123 funding programs.

fort-lupton/12.title: Police K-9 program
fort-lupton/12.summary: Council considered approving a Police K-9 program supported by donations.

fort-morgan/0.title: Police chief departure and interim chief appointment
fort-morgan/0.summary: At the Oct. 6 meeting, many residents criticized the council over the former police chief's departure and urged a quick hire of a new chief. The Oct. 20 agenda includes appointing Steve Brown as Interim Police Chief and a personnel executive session with a check-in with the interim chief.

fort-morgan/1.title: Electric rate increase (Ordinance No. 1338)
fort-morgan/1.summary: Following a rate study presented in May, council passed first reading on Aug. 18 and held a Sept. 1 public hearing. Resident Cynthia Ruppel opposed the increase. Council approved second reading, with the city saying it passes on its power purchase costs.

fort-morgan/2.title: 2027 budget process
fort-morgan/2.summary: Council has been reviewing 2027 department expense budgets over several meetings. The city manager said the direction would be adjusted after Cargill and the Teamsters agreed on a labor contract. The police department asked for a records technician. The Oct. 20 agenda covers the capital improvement, conservation trust and perpetual care funds and the fee schedule.

fort-morgan/3.title: Aquatic facility and certificates of participation financing
fort-morgan/3.summary: Council heard that the aquatic facility design, budget and timeline are unchanged and excavation is set to begin this fall. An ordinance authorizing certificates of participation to fund it had first reading on Oct. 6. Ordinance 1339 had its second reading and public hearing on the Oct. 20 agenda.

fort-morgan/4.title: Main Street historic landmark designations
fort-morgan/4.summary: Council approved local historic landmark status for 325, 327 and 329 Main Street, the 33rd local landmark. The buildings are being remodeled with the Main Street Advisory Board. The Historic Preservation Board is tracking federal Section 106 changes and a state tax credit rule change.

fort-morgan/5.title: Special use permit for upstairs apartment at 305-307 Main St.
fort-morgan/5.summary: Council approved a special use permit for a new residential living space above a tattoo shop. Downtown zoning requires council approval, and the state health department requires a separate outdoor entrance. No public comments were received.

fort-morgan/6.title: Pointe Village Commercial Park lot sale for grocery store
fort-morgan/6.summary: Council authorized selling three lots totaling 1.5 acres in Pointe Village Commercial Park to K&M LLC. It also approved a development agreement for a grocery store.

fort-morgan/7.title: Water agreements: irrigation lease and Southern Water Supply Project
fort-morgan/7.summary: The Oct. 20 agenda includes resolutions extending the riverside irrigation and quality water lease and amending the allotment contract in the Southern Water Supply Project Pipeline. It also covers amending and extending a development agreement with NCHD.

fort-morgan/8.title: Airport apron expansion naming and obstruction light project
fort-morgan/8.summary: The Airport Advisory Board has repeatedly discussed naming the aircraft parking apron expansion in honor of an individual. It also has an obstruction light project update.

fort-morgan/9.title: Economic incentive negotiations in executive session
fort-morgan/9.summary: Council went into executive session in August to discuss economic incentives and negotiation strategy, with the economic development specialist and outside parties present. No outcome is stated in the documents.

foxfield/0.title: Speeding and traffic calming: radar speed signs and traffic study
foxfield/0.summary: The town has reviewed speed data from engineer SEH, looked at options such as radar feedback signs, speed humps and enforcement, and put $120,000 toward traffic work in the 2026 budget. In July trustees moved to buy four solar radar signs for Hindsdale and Waco, with a total cost of about $22,373. In September trustees questioned the purchase and favored a resident speeding-report tool on the town website, and Trustee Pakanati asked to revisit it with all trustees present.
foxfield/0.where: Townwide, including Hindsdale and Waco streets

foxfield/1.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption and fire prevention
foxfield/1.summary: Trustees considered Ordinance 2026-03, which adopts the state-recommended Wildfire Resiliency Code by reference. After public hearings with no public comments, the Board approved it on August 6. Trustees also worked with South Metro Fire on outreach, a wildfire prevention training and a fire prevention meeting, and discussed the 6-inch versus 12-inch grass rule and evacuation planning.

foxfield/2.title: Land Use Code rewrite (Ordinance 2026-02)
foxfield/2.summary: Ordinance 2026-02 amends Articles 1-6 of Chapter 16 of the municipal code, the Land Use Code. The public hearing was continued several times and trustees reviewed the draft, including with an AI review. The Board approved the ordinance unanimously on August 6, 2026.

foxfield/3.title: Home Rule exploration and charter timeline
foxfield/3.summary: The town attorney presented on becoming a home rule town. Trustees debated next steps, with one saying the process was being rushed. A timeline was laid out for an ordinance initiating the process and special elections that could put a charter before voters in 2027. The Board also discussed home rule authority and land use regulation in July.

foxfield/4.title: 2026 town budget and finances
foxfield/4.summary: The Board held a study session and a public hearing on the 2026 budget, then adopted it. General Fund spending rose about 25%, largely for speed and traffic work. The mill levy stayed at 4.982 and the property tax levy was approved. Trustees later noted sales tax had dropped over four years and discussed vacancies at Foxfield Village Center.

foxfield/5.title: Road maintenance: crack seal and pavement program
foxfield/5.summary: The town approved the SEH engineering fee estimate for the 2026 pavement repair and surface treatment program. Terracare asked to bid on the work, and Vance Brothers was the bidder in the earlier rounds. In October staff asked to approve an extra $6,300 for 2 more tons of crack seal, bringing the Vance Brothers bid to $11,800. Roads Maintenance Fund money remaining for 2026 is $19,047.

foxfield/6.title: Waco Street drainage and culvert repair
foxfield/6.summary: Engineering recommendations described erosion and roadway deterioration near Waco Street and Arapahoe Road. Trustees weighed seeding versus riprap rock. In September they approved a revised Terracare quote that dropped the culvert cleanout but kept seeding and watering, with work to be scheduled for fall.

foxfield/7.title: Streetlight and tunnel light repairs
foxfield/7.summary: Trustees followed several broken streetlights and tunnel lights, including on S Lewiston Way and Parker Road. They approved a CLI Services proposal to replace three roadway light fixtures and a fuse kit at Lewiston Way and Parker Road, with not-to-exceed pricing.

foxfield/8.title: Short-term rental litigation
foxfield/8.summary: In July trustees discussed a Summary Judgment ruling in the town's short-term rental litigation and future steps.

foxfield/9.title: Law enforcement and code enforcement contracts
foxfield/9.summary: The Board approved the 2026 law enforcement services agreement and a new SafeBUILT code enforcement contract with changed rates, asking that an 8-hour rate be added. Trustees also asked for a ride-along with code enforcement.

foxfield/10.title: Foxfield Trustee vacancy and canceled April 2026 election
foxfield/10.summary: The Board canceled the April 2026 election and declared candidates elected. A trustee vacancy was expected and applicants were interviewed, with Trustee Hodge applying. Doug Hodge was sworn in as an appointed trustee in May, and trustee compensation and rules of procedure were revised.

fraser/0.title: St. Louis Landing workforce housing and new market tax credit financing
fraser/0.summary: The Board and Fraser Housing Authority approved resolutions authorizing the Town Manager and Housing Authority director to take new market tax credit (NMTC) actions for the St. Louis Landing project. The NMTC financing is to go toward the playground and buildout of the early childhood space. In October the Housing Authority took up housing regulations, community rules, and initial rents and fees for the development.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/1.title: Grand Park Overlook Filing 2 final plat and planned development plan
fraser/1.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on a 135.1-acre plan with 104 single-family attached units, 70 multi-family units, 500 lodging units and commercial space, with building heights up to 65 feet. It voted 7-0 to recommend approval of the final plat and plan. Commissioners raised concerns about golf course irrigation on town wells, the lack of public parks and trails, the Leland Creek Trail connection, and 5 acres of public land owed under the annexation agreement. A final condition is the West Mountain Water Master Plan, and no public comment was received.

fraser/2.title: Chapter 18 and 19 land use code amendments
fraser/2.summary: Planning Commission is workshopping rewrites of Fraser's zoning and subdivision chapters, aiming to have them in effect by January 1, 2027 to meet the Proposition 123 fast-track requirement for affordable housing. Topics include plat and site plan sequencing, permit extensions, special use permits, water and sewer proof of service, fee waivers, and drought and fire-resilient landscaping. A town hall and October hearing are planned, with Board adoption in November or December. Annexation policy will be handled separately.

fraser/3.title: 2027 town budget and priorities
fraser/3.summary: The Board held budget workshops in October on the draft 2027 budget, which was presented October 7 and updated October 16. The Downtown Development Authority also reviewed its own 2027 preliminary budget in September.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/4.title: Cornerstone vs. Fraser mediation
fraser/4.summary: The Board went into executive session about upcoming mediation in a conservation matter and then took up a resolution on a mediation submission agreement with Cornerstone. The documents give no details on the dispute or its outcome.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/5.title: Water and sewer fee reassessment for properties with changed usage
fraser/5.summary: The Board repeatedly met in executive session on legal options for reassessing water and sewer tap fees on properties whose water usage has expanded or changed since the original tap fee was issued. No decision is recorded in the documents.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/6.title: Mandatory watering restrictions and water supply projects
fraser/6.summary: The Board voted 7-0 to amend the town's mandatory watering restrictions. It also issued a Water Supply Protection District permit for the public works fuel station at 150 Grand County Road 72, and in October considered a Windy Gap Environmental Fund application and a groundwater study with the Upper Colorado Watershed Environment Team.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/7.title: Wastewater plant expansion and discharge permit appeal
fraser/7.summary: The Joint Facilities Oversight Committee, made up of Fraser and two water districts, was set to hear updates on plant capital projects and expansion from Tetra Tech and on the appeal of the new discharge permit. It also considered authorizing its manager to contract with Tetra Tech and reviewed regional wastewater alternatives.
fraser/7.where: Upper Fraser Valley Wastewater Treatment Plant

fraser/8.title: Transit budget and service options
fraser/8.summary: The Board considered transit budget and service options and voted to approve a service option. The documents do not specify which option.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/9.title: Grand Kids Learning Center lease and child care
fraser/9.summary: The Board considered a lease for the Grand Kids Learning Center, reviewing its budget and projected finances. In September it authorized a Grand County child care strategic matter on consent.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority
Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/10.title: Pole Yard development community wishlist
fraser/10.summary: The Board scheduled a 20-minute discussion of the community wishlist for the Pole Yard development, with a presentation by Ron Jones. The documents give no outcome.

sources.body: Board of Trustees and Fraser Housing Authority

fraser/11.title: Mural Fest and Fire & Ice, and a possible shift to wall murals
fraser/11.summary: The Public Arts Committee recapped the 2026 Mural Fest, in which all 30 murals sold, and planned Fire & Ice 2027. It discussed moving toward painting building walls in 2027, which would need a bigger budget than the roughly $91,000 Art in Public Places budget, perhaps $50,000 more. Fire & Ice planning covers fire artists, shuttles, emergency vehicle placement and a possible crosswalk.

fraser/12.title: Fraser Valley Arts parking variance
fraser/12.summary: The Board of Adjustment held a public hearing on Fraser Valley Arts' request for a variance from the town's off-street parking requirements. An interim order resolution was on the agenda.

frederick/0.title: Roads and Routes transportation sales tax ballot measure
frederick/0.summary: Trustees put a 1% transportation sales tax and related debt question on the November ballot to fund the Roads and Routes program, and discussed it at several meetings.

frederick/1.title: Land use code amendments and retail marijuana ban
frederick/1.summary: The planning commission and trustees worked through land use code amendments, including a ban on retail marijuana businesses.

frederick/2.title: Water resources and the Firestone water case
frederick/2.summary: Trustees discussed water supply issues, including opposing Firestone's water court case and treating a reservoir for phosphorus.

frederick/3.title: Public Works and Parks campus
frederick/3.summary: Trustees discussed plans for a new combined Public Works and Parks campus.

frederick/4.title: Historic preservation plan
frederick/4.summary: The town took up a historic preservation plan for its older buildings and downtown.

frederick/5.title: Public art murals and carvings
frederick/5.summary: The arts commission reviewed new murals and carvings for public spaces.

frederick/6.title: Youth commission work on mental health and bullying
frederick/6.summary: The youth commission focused on student mental health and bullying prevention.

frederick/7.title: Parks, open space and trails design standards
frederick/7.summary: The town reviewed new design standards for parks, open space and trails.

frederick/8.title: Wheatlands plat expiration and KO Industrial land
frederick/8.summary: Trustees dealt with the expiration of the Wheatlands plat and a land conveyance for the KO Industrial site.

frederick/9.title: 2027 budget
frederick/9.summary: The 2027 town budget was introduced to trustees.

fremont-county/0.title: Cañon Dolomite Quarry truck traffic permit amendment (CUP 11-001)
fremont-county/0.summary: Amrize asked the county to amend the truck traffic condition (Section K) of the quarry's conditional use permit to use the "Annual Average Daily Traffic" wording from the original CDOT approval. The quarry operates only a day or two a month and wants room for sales surges on those days without adding operating days.

fremont-county/1.title: Outside consultant review fees for RV roof business application
fremont-county/1.summary: Planning & Zoning asked the commissioners to bill an applicant for outside consultant review costs that exceed the application fee. The applicant had requested an outside consultant after voicing a perceived staff bias, and Section 306 of the county resolution lets the board assess the extra fees. The project is a business that maintains and repairs RV roofs.

fremont-county/2.title: 152-lot Planned Unit Development at 1337 County Road 3A
fremont-county/2.summary: A public hearing was set for a Planned Unit Development proposing 152 lots at a minimum of 3 acres each near Cañon City. The October 13 agenda lists it, and no decision is shown in the documents.

fremont-county/3.title: Zone change from Business to Residential One (R1)
fremont-county/3.summary: A property owner asked to rezone a lot from commercial to residential for personal use, planning to add a full bathroom to the unit. The public hearing was held August 25 after being scheduled July 28.

fremont-county/4.title: Aspen Acres Fire and evacuation planning
fremont-county/4.summary: Public Health reported that before firefighters gained control of the north side of the Aspen Acres Fire, the Bruce McCandless Veterans Community Living Center was in a very vulnerable position. Agencies have been planning and practicing for a potential evacuation since the 24 Fire. Fire danger remained extreme and DOT stopped mowing for fear of sparks.
fremont-county/4.where: Aspen Acres / Bruce McCandless Veterans Community Living Center

fremont-county/5.title: New liquor license for restaurant, bar and mercantile off Grant Street
fremont-county/5.summary: Commissioners considered a new malt, vinous and spirits-style license for a 134-person restaurant, bar and mercantile. The applicant needs a CDOT highway access permit, since the old permit allowed only 20 trips a day, and CDOT has now completed a traffic analysis. Commissioner Grantham asked about the access complications and moved to approve.

fremont-county/6.title: Ballot measure resolutions: Amendment 83, Amendment 87, Proposition NN
fremont-county/6.summary: The October 13 agenda includes resolutions supporting Amendment 83 and opposing Amendment 87 (graduated income) and Proposition NN. No vote outcome is shown.

fremont-county/7.title: Colorado River shortage and county water concerns
fremont-county/7.summary: Commissioner McFall reported on Colorado Counties Incorporated discussion of Colorado River negotiations. The Lower Basin must reduce its water use by 1.25 million acre-feet after the states failed to reach an agreement.

fremont-county/8.title: Cotopaxi Fire Station lease renewal
fremont-county/8.summary: The commissioners' October 13 agenda includes renewing the Cotopaxi Fire Station lease with the Deer Mountain Fire Protection District.

fremont-county/9.title: Commissioners hear summary of state semi-automatic firearm law
fremont-county/9.summary: During the July 28, 2026 meeting, minutes record a discussion of a state law restricting the transfer, sale, or purchase of a long list of semi-automatic firearms. It bans rapid-fire conversion devices and requires buyers to complete a firearm safety training program through Colorado Parks and Wildlife. The excerpt does not show any vote on this item.

fremont-county/10.title: Resolution on Amendment 83 (constitutional right) on Oct. 13 agenda
fremont-county/10.summary: The Oct. 13, 2026 agenda lists a resolution supporting Amendment 83, whose title is cut off after "Constitutional Right." The excerpt does not say what the amendment covers, so whether it concerns firearms is unclear.

frisco/0.title: Short-term rental cap and income-restricted housing units
frisco/0.summary: Staff asked Council at the October 13 work session whether to draft an ordinance changing how the short-term rental license cap is calculated. Today all residential units, including deed-restricted ones like the Scout income-restricted rental development, count toward the total.

frisco/1.title: Fast-track affordable housing review and Unified Development Code amendments
frisco/1.summary: The Planning Commission held hearings on Unified Development Code changes, including a fast-tracked review process for affordable housing to meet Proposition 123 state requirements and changes to allowed uses, accessory uses and parking. Council took up Ordinances 26-17 and 26-18 on first reading Sept. 8, with second reading on the Sept. 22 agenda.

frisco/2.title: 2027 budget and mid-year financial outlook
frisco/2.summary: Council reviewed 2026 finances in a mid-year work session. A difficult winter with low snow, reduced visitation and lower sales tax means 2027 budget planning will need care. The 2027 budget was discussed Sept. 8, and Ordinances 26-22 (appropriations) and 26-23 (mill levy) came up for first reading Oct. 13.

frisco/3.title: Summit County Strong Future mill levy reauthorization
frisco/3.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-19 supporting the county's referred ballot question to reauthorize the existing Strong Future mill levy in perpetuity. It is not a new or increased tax, and the current levy sunsets in 2028.

frisco/4.title: Summit School District mill levy override (Measure 4A)
frisco/4.summary: Council heard from the Summit County Education Association and the school district and considered Resolution 26-26 supporting Summit School District RE-1 Ballot Measure 4A, a mill levy override for teacher and staff pay.

frisco/5.title: 207 Granite Street eight-townhome development
frisco/5.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a sketch plan for eight townhomes at 207 Granite Street. Issues included access from 2nd Avenue, a dumpster access waiver, tandem parking, stepbacks, a possible Granite Street sidewalk, and fit with the historic park across the street. Commissioners noted the zoning allows the use by right.

frisco/6.title: Sixth Degree Town Homes at 121 E Main Street
frisco/6.summary: The Planning Commission conducted a final review of a mixed-use project with six residential and two commercial units. Commissioners raised parking lifts without a covenant, an unlocated water line in an easement, and compliance with the new lighting rules.

frisco/7.title: Telecommunication facility at 101 W Main Street
frisco/7.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled a special use permit hearing for a new freestanding telecommunication facility at 101 W Main Street. The applicant is BMF Development LLC.

frisco/8.title: Lagoon Drive water main replacement
frisco/8.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-18 authorizing a contract with Western States Reclamation, LLC to replace a water main on Lagoon Drive.

frisco/9.title: Thermal energy network test bore at Town Hall
frisco/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-23 approving a revocable license and right of entry for a utility thermal energy network test bore on the Town Hall property, tied to the town's geothermal partnership with Xcel.

frisco/10.title: Childcare tuition assistance and grant program
frisco/10.summary: Council received an update on childcare tuition assistance: 430 applications were submitted, no rate increase is planned for the 26/27 program year, and providers' tuition increases of 3-5% a year could price out families. Future applications involving DEI initiatives will not be approved. Council also has 2027 grant committee recommendations on its Sept. 22 agenda.

frisco/11.title: Downtown winter parking
