frisco/11.summary: Council scheduled an update on downtown winter parking for its Sept. 22 meeting.

frisco/12.title: Council strategic planning retreat
frisco/12.summary: Council held a retreat on Aug. 25 at the Summit Fire & EMS building to review the strategic plan and set priorities. Topics included infrastructure, water rates, housing (90-100 new income-restricted units since 2023), Dark Skies certification, and the Arts and Culture Plan.
frisco/12.where: Summit Fire & EMS Building, 0035 County Shops Road

fruita/0.title: 1925 J Road annexation, rezone and new housing development
fruita/0.summary: The Planning Commission was set to hear a request on Aug. 11 to annex about 36.14 acres at 1925 J Road and rezone it to Community Residential. At the Aug. 4 council meeting a resident raised concerns about irrigation water for a proposed development of at least 40 homes, noting the Encanto irrigation system lost water for over 24 hours in late June, and asked for a long-term irrigation plan and recorded workshops.

fruita/1.title: Raptor Crossing PUD amendment
fruita/1.summary: The Planning Commission considered a major amendment to the Raptor Crossing PUD Guide. Council introduced Ordinance 2026-17 on Aug. 18 to allow certain residential and other uses, with a public hearing set for Sept. 15.

fruita/2.title: Fruita Co-op annexation and industrial rezone
fruita/2.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled to hear a request on Oct. 13 to annex about 40.16 acres for the Fruita Co-op and rezone it to Industrial. The land is currently under county AFT zoning.

fruita/3.title: State-mandated Water Supply and Strategic Growth plan elements
fruita/3.summary: By Dec. 31, 2026, the state requires Fruita to adopt Water Supply and Strategic Growth elements in its Comprehensive Plan. Planning Commission and Council discussed a community engagement strategy and a draft water survey. The city is seeking a grant to hire a consultant, and the mayor called the requirement an unfunded mandate.

fruita/4.title: Metro District policy and model service plan
fruita/4.summary: Council discussed Fruita's amenity-based metropolitan district policy and model service plan, which let developers form separate districts and seek tax-exempt bonds. Council directed edits so the policy and plan align, including limiting to commercial and industrial uses and requiring council approval of applications and development plans.

fruita/5.title: 2027 city budget
fruita/5.summary: The City Manager presented the recommended 2027 budget, with few surprises and smaller capital projects. The largest item is $2 million for building J Road from Wildcat Avenue to Skiff Road, with grants being sought. Other items include $100,000 for sidewalks, $320,000 for four police trucks and market-rate pay increases. Police budget discussion was tied to the public safety sales tax increase.

fruita/6.title: CDOT Highway 6 widening and access control plan amendment
fruita/6.summary: CDOT presented an amendment to the US 6 West/SH 139 Access Control Plan for a future widening from 18 Road to 22 Road. It includes right-in/right-out intersections with dedicated U-turns and changes to property access. An updated intergovernmental agreement is expected in January 2027.

fruita/7.title: Police department strategic plan and speeding concerns on 18 Road
fruita/7.summary: Chief Krouse presented the 2026-2030 police strategic plan and organizational chart. Council discussed residents' perception of speeding on 18 Road, and the chief said there is no data supporting traffic calming there. Staffing needs are to be reviewed during 2027 budget talks.

fruita/8.title: E-bike and e-scooter rules on trails and in parks
fruita/8.summary: The Parks and Recreation Commission heard a police presentation on classifications and rules for e-bikes on trails and in parks. On-road vehicles need a license and registration, off-road ones are barred from roads and pedestrian areas, and police are educating families. E-scooters have little regulation.

fruita/9.title: Park wear and water use during drought
fruita/9.summary: Commissioners discussed worn grass at Civic Center Park, possibly moving or alternating the Farmers Market to Reed Park, and closing part of Aspen Street. Salt Wash soccer fields are turning to dirt because water use is being cut during drought, and the city will try to restore water to them.
fruita/9.where: Civic Center Park, Reed Park, Salt Wash soccer fields

fruita/10.title: Public sculpture selections for downtown pedestals
fruita/10.summary: The Arts and Culture Board reviewed artist applications for sculptures on pedestals including South Mesa Street and near the Bark Park, weighing community identity, durability, safety and accuracy of representation. Members visited the sculptures Aug. 17 and are deciding how to announce selections.
fruita/10.where: South Mesa Street, Dinosaur Journey parking lot, FARM

fruita/11.title: Residents ask for regular council town halls
fruita/11.summary: At the Sept. 15 meeting a resident asked the council to hold town halls regularly for two-way conversation rather than only listening to public comment. The same meeting recognized a suicide prevention proclamation.

fruita/12.title: New municipal judge appointment and judge powers ordinance
fruita/12.summary: Council interviewed candidates in executive session on Sept. 22 and recommended the City Manager negotiate a contract with a chosen Municipal Court Judge. First reading of Ordinance 2026-16 on municipal judges' powers was also introduced in August.

fruita/13.title: Bee City USA designation
fruita/13.summary: Council heard a proposal to make Fruita Mesa County's first Bee City. It would require adoption of a resolution and a $200 annual fee, with the Livability or Parks and Recreation Commission suggested to lead the application.

garden-city/0.title: New Police Department building construction
garden-city/0.summary: The board repeatedly approved Mark Young Construction change orders (COR 002 through 010) and monthly invoices, including a $301,598.32 November 2025 invoice, and approved a June 2026 invoice. Staff also noted the PD floor will be entirely replaced.

garden-city/1.title: 2026 budget, 4% COLA and property tax levy
garden-city/1.summary: After a public hearing, the board was set to adopt the 2026 budget, appropriation and property tax levy (Resolutions 10, 11 and 12-2025) on Dec. 9. It also considered a 4% cost-of-living raise and a larger health insurance stipend for employees.

garden-city/2.title: Town Administrator/Clerk transition and alternate attorney
garden-city/2.summary: In July 2026 the board approved Town Administrator Cheryl Campbell's resignation letter and discussed handing the position over once Linda Blackston starts. It also discussed an employment agreement and alternate town attorney options.

garden-city/3.title: Speed humps on 27th Street Road
garden-city/3.summary: The board considered speed hump proposals for 27th Street Road in November 2025. In July 2026 staff were to check on an issue at the end of 27th Street Road.

garden-city/4.title: 2026 Greeley Transit contract
garden-city/4.summary: The board considered approving the 2026 contract with Greeley Transit for services.

garden-city/5.title: Building codes and 2026 building permit fees
garden-city/5.summary: The board considered adopting the 2026 building permit fee schedule. It also took up Ordinance 11-2025, adopting by reference building codes including the Electric and Solar Ready Code and Colorado wildfire resiliency code, with a hearing on Dec. 9.

garden-city/6.title: Award Alliance incentive
garden-city/6.summary: Paul Hlad of Award Alliance presented to the board in November 2025. On Dec. 9 the board was set to consider Resolution 13-2025, an incentive for Award Alliance.

garden-city/7.title: Marijuana business licenses and special review use
garden-city/7.summary: The board considered several retail marijuana store, cultivation and manufacturing licenses and renewals in November 2025. In July 2026 it considered a Star Buds license at 2502 8th Ave and adopted Resolution 10-2026 granting a use by special review.

garden-city/8.title: Commercial Revitalization Grant for El Rodeo Night Club
garden-city/8.summary: The board was to give final review and approval to El Rodeo Night Club LLC's Commercial Revitalization Grant.

garden-city/9.title: Coordinated election and community development grants
garden-city/9.summary: In July 2026 the board approved a memorandum of intergovernmental agreement for the coordinated election, discussed the election, and approved an IGA for the Weld County Community Development Block Grant program.

garden-city/10.title: Police department sells last Smith & Wesson
garden-city/10.summary: The board approved lowering the price of the last Smith & Wesson firearm held by the police department.

garfield-county/0.title: Mitchell Creek Community PUD rezoning and sketch plan
garfield-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on Aug. 26 for a rezoning from Rural to PUD and a major subdivision sketch plan for the Mitchell Creek Community PUD at 50235 Highway 6/24 near Glenwood Springs. The owner is AMICHAUX Limited Partnership LLLP.

garfield-county/1.title: Lake Springs Ranch PUD amendment and subdivision plan
garfield-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission was to hear a substantial PUD amendment, a preliminary plan for the Lake Springs Ranch subdivision, and rezoning of properties removed from the PUD on Oct. 14. The site is about 3.5 miles southeast of Glenwood Springs off County Road 114.

garfield-county/2.title: McClure River Ranch PUD amendment and 12-lot preliminary plan
garfield-county/2.summary: Commissioners were asked to sign resolutions approving a substantial amendment to the 98-acre McClure River Ranch PUD and a preliminary plan dividing 48.96 acres into 12 lots and 2 tracts. The applicant is Aspen Polo Partners, LLP.

garfield-county/3.title: Xcel Hopkins to Basalt transmission line rebuild
garfield-county/3.summary: The Planning Commission was to conduct a location and extent review of Xcel Energy's Hopkins to Basalt Transmission Line 9256 rebuild, starting at the Hopkins Substation east of Carbondale. Xcel also gave a presentation to commissioners on Oct. 12.
garfield-county/3.where: Hopkins Substation, Red Canyon Road and Fisher Cemetery Road, east of Carbondale

garfield-county/4.title: Hogback View Estates subdivision
garfield-county/4.summary: Commissioners were asked to sign the resolution for the preliminary plan of the Hogback View Estates major subdivision east of New Castle. A separate Hogback discussion was held at the Aug. 4 work session.
garfield-county/4.where: 24 County Road 138, east of New Castle

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session

garfield-county/5.title: Affordable housing: USDA programs, Housing Authority and Cavern Springs mobile home park
garfield-county/5.summary: Commissioners heard from the USDA Rural Development state director and the Garfield County Housing Authority, which requested $90,000 in 2027 funding. They were also asked for a letter of support for the Cavern Springs Mobile Home Park's limited partnership request.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session

garfield-county/6.title: Slaughterhouse Gulch mudslide landfill fee waiver
garfield-county/6.summary: A resident asked commissioners to waive landfill tipping fees because of the Slaughterhouse Gulch mudslide.

garfield-county/7.title: 2027 county budget hearings and workforce analysis
garfield-county/7.summary: Commissioners held budget hearings starting Oct. 6 and department presentations on 2027 proposed budgets on Oct. 12, plus Budget Supplement #4. They also reviewed an MGT workforce analysis and presentations from the Early Childhood District and Forest Improvement District.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session
Board of County Commissioners - Budget Hearings

garfield-county/8.title: Library District tax extension on November ballot
garfield-county/8.summary: The Garfield County Public Library District asked commissioners to place a question on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot to extend part of its property tax levy.

garfield-county/9.title: Sheriff's Office and jail budget and programs
garfield-county/9.summary: The Sheriff asked for a $267,000 supplement for jail overtime and presented on new jail standards. The office also sought grants for opioid treatment medications for inmates ($39,903) and bulletproof vests ($12,100).

garfield-county/10.title: Parachute funding: 1st Street/US 6 reconstruction and transit
garfield-county/10.summary: The Town of Parachute asked for $600,000 toward the 1st Street/US 6 reconstruction project and disbursement of $200,000 for the Parachute Area Transit System, plus a 2027 funding request.

garfield-county/11.title: Madison AI assistant purchase
garfield-county/11.summary: The county IT department sought a $43,200 supplemental appropriation and a Carahsoft contract for a 12-month Madison AI subscription covering countywide and Community Development assistants.

garfield-county/12.title: Senior meals and transit programs (Traveler, RFTA IGA)
garfield-county/12.summary: Commissioners discussed the Traveler program and reviewed a draft RFTA/Traveler IGA and a seven-party senior programs MOU. They also considered a sole-source contract with the City of Rifle for congregate meals in western Garfield County.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners - Work Session

garfield-county/13.title: Rifle Garfield County Airport improvements
garfield-county/13.summary: The county ratified FAA grant agreements for airport improvements and approved paving of Lot A7. It also ratified an emergency roof repair and awarded a concrete improvements contract.

gilpin-county/0.title: Rollinsville area fire-protection cisterns
gilpin-county/0.summary: The commissioners considered Resolution 26-085 to develop and jointly procure fire-protection cisterns in the Rollinsville area, choosing between the East/Gold Dirt and West/Public Works sites. By Sept. 8 the resolution covered both projects.

gilpin-county/1.title: Short-term rental regulations (Ordinance 26-01)
gilpin-county/1.summary: Ordinance 26-01 on rental regulations had its first reading on Aug. 25 and a second-reading public hearing on Sept. 22. It was presented by the Community Development director and county attorney.

gilpin-county/2.title: County roadway manual, road inventory and designations
gilpin-county/2.summary: Staff presented the Roadway Design and Construction Manual and county road inventory on Aug. 11. On Aug. 25 a public hearing covered Resolution 26-084 designating and classifying county roads and Resolution 26-088 adopting the road manual. The county also sought Special Highway funds in October.

gilpin-county/3.title: Comprehensive fee schedule and Parks & Recreation fees
gilpin-county/3.summary: The county reviewed its Comprehensive Fee Schedule on Sept. 8 and took up Resolution 26-093 adopting the updated schedule on Sept. 22. A Parks and Recreation fee structure and equipment purchase plan was also discussed in August.

gilpin-county/4.title: 2027 draft budget and employee compensation and benefits
gilpin-county/4.summary: The county manager and finance staff presented the 2027 proposed draft budget on Sept. 22. Related items included the 2026 compensation plan (Resolution 26-089) and 2027 employee benefits renewal (Resolution 26-097).

gilpin-county/5.title: Ballot issue referred to Gilpin County voters
gilpin-county/5.summary: Resolution 26-077 referring a ballot issue to registered electors appeared repeatedly from July to August, and ballot propositions were discussed on Sept. 8. Resolution 26-083 concerned November election matters involving Central City and Timberline Fire.

gilpin-county/6.title: Wildfire restrictions, forest health and wildfire planning
gilpin-county/6.summary: The county lowered Stage 2 fire restrictions to Stage 1 on Sept. 8, then removed restrictions in late October. It committed $51,000 over three years as a match for the Clear Creek Watershed & Forest Health Partnership's wildfire mitigation grant. Staff also coordinated wildfire defense grants and updated wildfire and hazard mitigation plans.

gilpin-county/7.title: Affordable housing: Proposition 123 credits and commitment
gilpin-county/7.summary: The commissioners considered an intergovernmental agreement on Proposition 123 affordable housing unit credits on Aug. 25. They also took up a resolution authorizing an affordable housing commitment filing in October.

gilpin-county/8.title: Rollinsville Plan grant extension
gilpin-county/8.summary: The county requested a nine-month extension of DOLA EIAF Grant No. 9953 for the Rollinsville plan and infrastructure feasibility study. It cited staff turnover in 2025 and problems with the consultant's work, including scope and water-use assumptions. The scope and grant amount are unchanged.

gilpin-county/9.title: Public records (CORA) policy and fees
gilpin-county/9.summary: The county amended its public records request policy (P-9) on Sept. 8. In October staff gave an update on the CORA process and fees.

gilpin-county/10.title: Code enforcement policy and COMBA bike trail
gilpin-county/10.summary: A draft code enforcement process policy was discussed Aug. 18. The same session covered the COMBA bike trail outside I-70 project.

glendale/0.title: Xcel Energy franchise agreement (Question 2B)
glendale/0.summary: On the Oct. 6 agenda, Council considers a resolution tied to Question 2B, which grants a franchise to Public Service Company of Colorado (Xcel) and approves a franchise agreement.

glendale/1.title: 2026 city budget and tax levy ordinances
glendale/1.summary: Council is slated to introduce Ordinance No. 6 adopting the city budget and appropriating money, and Ordinance No. 8 levying taxes for 2026. Introduction is set for Oct. 6.

glendale/2.title: Four Mile Project legal advice
glendale/2.summary: Council planned an executive session on Oct. 6 to receive legal advice about the Four Mile Project. The documents give no further detail.

glendale/3.title: Entertainment Advisory Board events: car show, Music on the Plaza, Get To Know Glendale
glendale/3.summary: The advisory board's teams are working on a car show, Music on the Plaza and a Get To Know Glendale effort. They prepared presentations to City Council on 9/1 and are reviewing the budget and proposed activities in October.

glendale/4.title: Infinity Park discussion
glendale/4.summary: Infinity Park is a discussion item at the Oct. 6 City Council meeting, presented by Kieran Nelson. The agenda does not say what is being discussed.

glendale/5.title: Ordinance corrections to Ordinance No. 1 references
glendale/5.summary: Council is to introduce Ordinance No. 5, which amends and corrects reference numbers from Ordinance No. 1 of 2026.

glenwood-springs/0.title: JG Housing Solutions special use permit and enforcement at 100 Midland Avenue
glenwood-springs/0.summary: After Planning and Zoning revoked the special use permit, Council heard a public update and discussed legal enforcement, sanctions and injunctive relief against JG Housing Solutions over land use violations at Units 110 and 210. A resident raised a complaint again on Aug 20, and the lawsuit was on the Oct 15 executive session list.

glenwood-springs/1.title: Short-term rental renewal rules (Ordinance 2026-22)
glenwood-springs/1.summary: The city is amending its code so short-term and accessory tourist rental permit holders must actually rent and remit lodging tax to renew. Planning and Zoning reviewed data on STR activity and permit counts, and Council took up the ordinance in September, with an amendment to a minimum of 20 nights and $150 in sales tax over two years. It returned on the Oct 1 consent agenda.

glenwood-springs/2.title: Appeal of short-term rental permit denial at 319 Park Drive
glenwood-springs/2.summary: The owner of 319 Park Drive appealed the denial of her STR permit renewal, which was denied because the unit had not been rented or paid lodging taxes. She argued the ordinance requires only that taxes be paid, and the city says renting is required. The appeal was on the Council agenda Aug 6 and was heard again by Planning and Zoning.

glenwood-springs/3.title: Fire department funding and November 2026 property tax ballot question
glenwood-springs/3.summary: Council discussed fire department funding and a property tax increase for the November 2026 ballot. On Aug 20 it considered a resolution certifying the ballot issue, title and content, and the Mayor commented on a resolution supporting the fire tax.

glenwood-springs/4.title: Parking on Bennett Avenue and the 1600 Bennett fee-in-lieu request
glenwood-springs/4.summary: Many residents spoke at multiple Council meetings about parking and tree stumps on Bennett Avenue. Council's Oct 1 agenda included a parking fee-in-lieu request for 1600 Bennett.

glenwood-springs/5.title: Canyon Vista affordable housing preliminary plat at 51993 Highway 6 & 24
glenwood-springs/5.summary: Cohen-Esrey Development Group seeks a preliminary plat combining three parcels totaling 3.93 acres for Canyon Vista, an 80-unit deeply affordable multifamily project Council approved in April 2025. Staff recommends approval; Planning and Zoning reviews it Oct 6 and Council takes up the plat and a right-of-way encroachment license Oct 15.

glenwood-springs/6.title: Funding request for 130 Midland affordable homeownership project
glenwood-springs/6.summary: Council considered a funding request for the 130 Midland affordable homeownership project on Oct 1 and continued it to Oct 15. Housing policy was also on the Oct 15 work session agenda.

glenwood-springs/7.title: 506 Maple Street fire sprinkler appeal
glenwood-springs/7.summary: Owners of the Splendor Mountain Spa guest cottage, a 400-square-foot unit at 506 Maple Street, appealed the requirement to install fire sprinklers in an R-1 occupancy. They say the cost of replacing the water service line is prohibitive and offered extinguishers; a member of the public raised concerns about compliance.

glenwood-springs/8.title: 2027 budget and 2026 appropriation amendments
glenwood-springs/8.summary: Council was scheduled to receive the 2027 budget presentation, the Tourism Promotion Fund budget and a public budget hearing in October. It also considered Ordinance 2026-21 amending the 2026 appropriation for carryovers and reallocations.

glenwood-springs/9.title: Mountain Waste and Recycling pay-as-you-throw contract
glenwood-springs/9.summary: Council planned a work session and a vote on the Mountain Waste and Recycling pay-as-you-throw contract on Oct 15.

glenwood-springs/10.title: Ride Glenwood on-demand pricing and transportation planning
glenwood-springs/10.summary: Council scheduled a decision on Ride Glenwood on-demand pricing, a comprehensive transportation discussion, and joint work sessions with the Transportation Commission. It also discussed an intergovernmental agreement with Roaring Fork Transportation Authority and, in September, truck weight limits and haul routes.

glenwood-springs/11.title: Electric vehicle charging code amendment (Ordinance 2026-18)
glenwood-springs/11.summary: Council took up an ordinance amending the municipal code on regulation and permitting of EV charging projects, following Planning and Zoning findings. It appeared on the Sept 3 consent agenda.

glenwood-springs/12.title: Community center climbing wall contract
glenwood-springs/12.summary: Council considered awarding RFP 2026-18P for a climbing wall at the community center, presented by the interim Parks and Recreation Director.

golden/0.title: Racist incident in Fire Department and City Manager separation
golden/0.summary: After a racist incident in the Golden Fire Department, residents spoke at several meetings. Council formed a temporary subcommittee (Resolution 3344), began an outside investigation, and on Aug 11 appointed Carly Lorentz Interim City Manager and moved to negotiate a separation agreement. Resolutions 3349 and 3350 on an acting manager and separation agreement were on the Aug 25 agenda, and a third-party investigator contract (Res. 3357) followed in September.

golden/1.title: The Junction urban renewal plan and TIF request
golden/1.summary: GURA is evaluating a new urban renewal area for The Junction, a 51-acre light industrial business park west of Highway 93. The developer seeks 100% tax increment financing to cover about $59 million in public improvements, including a Highway 93 roundabout and a pedestrian bridge to the North Table Mountain trailhead. Consultant reports found blight factors and low impact on taxing entities, and the Planning Commission also reviewed the boundary.
golden/1.where: West side of State Highway 93, North Table Mountain area

golden/2.title: Clear Creek management and behavior problems
golden/2.summary: Residents complained about creek parking, charcoal grills and behavior problems, and said enforcement has not solved them. Staff gave Council a creek update and presentation on July 28, and park board members noted creek vegetation restoration work.

golden/3.title: 2027-2028 city budget and revenue outlook
golden/3.summary: Staff presented the proposed 2027-28 biennial budget to Council and the Citizens' Budget Advisory Committee, with flat to modest sales tax growth and declines in property tax and building use tax. Revenue constraints are shaping requests from boards such as sustainability and economic development. The committee also recommended more marijuana tax money for rent assistance and food insecurity.

sources.body: City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm

golden/4.title: Flock license plate camera contract
golden/4.summary: Council held a study session on Flock technology used by Golden Police. Councilors Knecht and Kurzinski proposed reconsidering the city's Flock contract and needed support from three councilors to bring it to a vote.

sources.body: City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 7:00pm

golden/5.title: Clayworks development: natural gas amendment and parking
golden/5.summary: Clayworks developers asked to amend their Official Development Plan to allow limited natural gas for pool and spa heating, fireplaces and grills. Sustainability board members and a Sustainable Golden resident urged keeping the original all-electric commitments. The amendment will go to Planning Commission and Council, and the mobility board has been tracking the project's parking and transportation demand plan.

golden/6.title: 2122 Jackson Street cottage development and alley spur
golden/6.summary: Council called up site plans for a cottage development at 2122 Jackson Street for Planning Commission review, focused on whether the narrow alley spur meets the alley definition. Neighbors raised concerns about the narrow alley, trash, parking, lighting and green space.

golden/7.title: Heart of Golden East Zone and public art
golden/7.summary: The Arts and Culture Commission is planning public art for the Heart of Golden East Zone and the new Municipal Building, including a mural on the 10th and Vasquez parking garage with $38,000 earmarked. Construction between Ford and Archer is expected in 2028-29. The commission also worked on Lions Park playground artwork and a combined strategic plan.
golden/7.where: East Zone, Municipal Building, Tucker Gulch, Lions Park

sources.body: ACC Strategic Planning Subcommittee - No Recording
ACC Lion's Park Art Selection Panel Meeting - No Recording
ACC Art in Public Places Subcommittee Meeting - No Recording
ACC Strategic Planning Subcommittee - No Recording

golden/8.title: Visit Golden strategic plan, budget and DVA marketing contract
golden/8.summary: The Community Marketing Board reviewed a 2026-2029 strategic plan emphasizing residents and off-season visits, questioned a 17 million visitor figure, and asked for more detailed 2027-28 budget lines. Council was to consider a marketing services contract with DVA Advertising (Res. 3345). Board members also discussed how the program is funded by suspending the sales tax vendor fee credit.

golden/9.title: Special events impacts and grants
golden/9.summary: A west 10th Street resident asked for a broader review of event impacts on parking and traffic from the farmers market, tubing and park events. The Special Events Review Committee is also considering the new Golden Skull Marathon, a $5,000 shuttle and parking grant request, and revisions to the grant program.

golden/10.title: Historic demolitions and new cottage at East Street district
golden/10.summary: The Historic Preservation Board approved a certificate of appropriateness for a rear cottage at 2024 Ford Street. It also reviewed demolition requests for 612 10th Street (Schall residence), 1735 and 403 18th Street, where a stay of up to 190 days may apply.

golden/11.title: Nazarene affordable housing plan area and Prosper project
golden/11.summary: Council adopted the Nazarene urban renewal plan area on July 14, and staff are ready to begin TIF negotiations with the developer, who secured key grant financing. Demolition and site work are underway for the Prosper affordable housing project at 817 14th Street. A draft TIF agreement was up for GURA review in October.

golden/12.title: Regional homelessness and Jefferson County agreements
golden/12.summary: Council agenda items included an IGA on the Navigation Center and an MOU with Jefferson County on regional homeless navigation efforts, along with EMS and fire agreements. Details of the outcomes are not in the documents.

golden/13.title: Downtown DDA projects and holiday partnership
golden/13.summary: The DDA took on projects including the 11th Street sidewalk and streetscape, legacy shade trees, and 14 street trees on Arapahoe for under $10,000. It considered a $7,500 holiday sponsorship with KOSI and the Golden Hotel, a holiday light contract extension, and an emergency repair grant for 807 13th Street.

golden/14.title: Universal recycling ordinance and EV charging
golden/14.summary: Staff are developing a universal recycling ordinance, likely starting with hauler licensing, backed by a state grant. The sustainability board also discussed overnight EV charging overstay fees and expanding charging for multifamily residents.

golden/15.title: Ore Cart service and overhead power line undergrounding
golden/15.summary: Council planned a study session on renewing the Ore Cart shuttle agreement with Colorado School of Mines and on a policy for undergrounding overhead power lines. A Ford Street undergrounding update also appeared at the DDA.

sources.body: City Council Study Session 5pm-Regular Business Meeting 6:30pm

granby/0.title: Data center workshop
granby/0.summary: The Board of Trustees scheduled a Data Center Workshop led by the Town Manager for its August 25, 2026 meeting. The agenda gives no details on any proposal or rules.

granby/1.title: Comprehensive zoning code and zoning map update (Ordinance 1041)
granby/1.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on August 3 on comprehensive amendments to the town zoning regulations and a legislative update of the official zoning map. The Board of Trustees took up the ordinance in public hearings on August 25 and September 22.

granby/2.title: Town Manager separation and recruitment
granby/2.summary: The Board held executive sessions on the Town Manager's employment and potential separation, then considered ratifying a separation agreement on September 8. On October 13 it discussed an interim Town Manager and recruitment of a permanent one.

granby/3.title: Nuche Village apartment agreement extension and funding
granby/3.summary: The Board considered extending the Nuche Village apartment agreement on September 8 and discussed funding for the apartments on October 13. A Nuche Village hearing board appointment also came up on August 25 and September 8.

granby/4.title: Ten Mile Crossing Planned Development preliminary plan
granby/4.summary: The Planning Commission considered the preliminary plat and plan for the Ten Mile Crossing Planned Development Overlay District, subject to conditions, on October 5. The Board of Trustees held a public hearing on the preliminary plan on October 13.

granby/5.title: Granby Sanitation District property at 843 Saddle Ridge and Granby Ranch Metro District service plan
granby/5.summary: Public hearings on 843 Saddle Ridge for the Granby Sanitation District and on a service plan amendment from Granby Ranch Metro District were continued from July 28. The 843 Saddle Ridge hearing returned on September 22.

granby/6.title: 2027 town budget and Grand Elk GID budget
granby/6.summary: The Finance Director led a 2027 Town of Granby budget discussion on October 13. The Grand Elk Ranch General Improvement District held its own 2027 budget discussion at the same meeting. The FY2025 audited financial statements were presented earlier, on July 28.

granby/7.title: Annexation proceedings
granby/7.summary: On September 22 the Board considered a resolution initiating annexation proceedings and setting a hearing on the eligibility of certain lands. The agenda does not name the property.

granby/8.title: Animal crematory conditional use permit in Central Business District
granby/8.summary: The Board was asked to recommend approval or denial of a conditional use permit for an animal crematory in the Central Business district, subject to conditions. A related final plat for Silvercreek West and a parking adjustment were on the same agenda.

granby/9.title: Peddler, mobile vendor and solicitor regulations
granby/9.summary: Ordinance 1040 would amend Chapter 5.05 and add Chapter 5.06 of the municipal code to regulate peddlers, mobile vendors, solicitors and canvassers.

granby/10.title: Wildfire resiliency code workshop
granby/10.summary: The Board held a workshop on wildfire resiliency code on August 11. The agenda gives no details on proposed rules.

granby/11.title: Granby Trails revegetation and tree planting with CSFS grants
granby/11.summary: A resident and the Middle Park Conservation District's executive director presented on revegetation and tree planting at Granby Trails funded by Colorado State Forest Service grants. The resident gave an update on August 25.

granby/12.title: Alley traffic concerns and Bark Park pond
granby/12.summary: The Board scheduled a discussion of alley traffic concerns on September 8. On October 13 it was set to discuss the Bark Park pond.

grand-county/0.title: 2027 Grand County budget hearings
grand-county/0.summary: Commissioners scheduled budget hearings October 5-9, 2026, covering every department, including Road and Bridge, airports, the Housing Authority, Economic Development, and a 5-year budget projection, followed by deliberations.

grand-county/1.title: Devil's Thumb Ranch High Lonesome Lodge lot split
grand-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission unanimously recommended approval of an outright exemption splitting a 44.33-acre parcel into two lots: an 8.82-acre lot for the existing lodge and a 32.60-acre lot for a possible future single-family home. Staff set 14 conditions, and no public notice was required.
grand-county/1.where: Devil's Thumb Ranch, High Lonesome Lodge, unincorporated Grand County

grand-county/2.title: Good to Go portable toilet storage special use permit
grand-county/2.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a request for a special use permit to store up to 200 clean, empty portable toilets on land in the Forestry and Open zone outside the growth boundary. Staff recommended conditional approval.
grand-county/2.where: Former Bergquist Outright Exemption property, unincorporated Grand County

grand-county/3.title: Subdivision, PUD regulations and Master Plan updates
grand-county/3.summary: The September 9 Planning Commission agenda included amendments to the county's subdivision and planned unit development regulations and a Master Plan update, along with a replat in Winter Park Ranch Second Filing.

grand-county/4.title: County departmental fee changes
grand-county/4.summary: Commissioners set a public hearing on October 20 on changes to Grand County departmental fees.

grand-county/5.title: St. Joseph's Foundation Retreat camping special use permit
grand-county/5.summary: A public hearing was scheduled October 20 on a special use permit for camping at the St. Joseph's Foundation Retreat.

grand-county/6.title: Model Traffic Code amendment (Ordinance 23)
grand-county/6.summary: Commissioners were to hold the second reading of an ordinance amending the county's Model Traffic Code on October 20.

grand-county/7.title: Drought preparedness and fire restrictions
grand-county/7.summary: Commissioners were to consider a Drought Preparedness Memorandum of Understanding through Water Resources and a Sheriff's Office action on fire conditions and restrictions. A FirePermits contract with Road and Bridge/Natural Resources was also on the agenda.

grand-county/8.title: 2027 Middle Park Fair and Rodeo contractor RFP
grand-county/8.summary: The Fair and Rodeo board was to approve a request for proposals for the 2027 rodeo contractor. The fair also appeared in the county budget hearings.

grand-junction/0.title: 2027 budget and the $6 million General Fund structural gap
grand-junction/0.summary: Staff reported a $6 million structural gap in the General Fund before new requests. The recommended 2027 budget is $317.4 million, with a $120.8 million General Fund. It includes about $2 million in personnel cuts, reduced Lincoln Park Pool hours and Dos Rios staffing, and shifting some housing programs to partners. It also adds six police officers and three fire battalion chiefs. Workshops continued Oct. 26, with formal adoption starting in November.

grand-junction/1.title: Temporary moratorium on large data centers
grand-junction/1.summary: Council discussed a temporary moratorium on large data centers because the code does not address them and they could use large amounts of power and water. No applications are pending. The ordinance was introduced Oct. 7 with a hearing set for Oct. 21. The moratorium would last until data center code amendments are adopted or 365 days pass, whichever is first.

grand-junction/2.title: Significant Tree Ordinance repealed
grand-junction/2.summary: At the request of the Housing Affordability Code Task Force, Council took up removing the significant tree protections (§21.07.040) from the Development Code, and the Forestry Board reported Council voted to remove them. The Forestry Board expressed disappointment, said public support for the ordinance was strong, and noted a consultant may propose an alternative, possibly incentive-based, in the Code review.

grand-junction/3.title: Galley Meadows rezone at 2590 Galley Lane and 675 26 Road
grand-junction/3.summary: Monument Homes Development and Cuesta Verde asked to rezone about 13.04 acres to RL-4 for future housing. Neighbors raised concerns about traffic, lighting, construction traffic and density, and asked that the entrance be on 26 Road rather than Galley Lane. The Planning Commission recommended approval, and Council passed Ordinance 5341 on Sept. 16 after the first hearing was delayed by a notice error.

grand-junction/4.title: Juniper Grove affordable homeownership at the Salt Flats
grand-junction/4.summary: Grand Junction Homes would buy about 3.3 acres of the city-owned Salt Flats property at 450 28 Road to build 48 for-sale homes for households under 100% AMI, with no HOA. The city would also cover $593,340 in water and sewer fees. Council continued the sale hearing to Sept. 16; completion is anticipated by Winter 2027.

grand-junction/5.title: Housing Action Plan and Housing Affordability Code Task Force
grand-junction/5.summary: Council reviewed a revised Housing Action Plan that drops a proposed Housing Advisory Board and moves exploring new housing revenue to later years. It will return for a public hearing and adoption. Meanwhile the Code Task Force is working with consultant KLJ to simplify the development code and the TEDS manual, with a focus on housing costs, and plans to finish by early 2027.

grand-junction/6.title: Unhoused services funding requests
grand-junction/6.summary: Council heard providers' year-two funding requests under the unhoused services RFP. Hilltop asked for $300,000 after receiving $250,000, and Homeward Bound asked for $225,000. No funding decisions were made; requests go through the budget process.

grand-junction/7.title: Water Supply Element and turf conversion vs. tree health
grand-junction/7.summary: Staff presented a Comprehensive Plan Water Supply Element required by state SB 24-174, saying current supplies are sufficient for projected needs. It will go to the Planning Commission after consultation with water providers. The Forestry Board discussed how turf conversion can harm mature trees.

grand-junction/8.title: Materials Recovery Facility financing
grand-junction/8.summary: Council approved Ordinance 5338 on final passage, authorizing an additional $9,312,127 in Certificates of Participation to finish acquiring and improving the city's Materials Recovery Facility.

grand-junction/9.title: Lincoln Park Barn and Certified Local Government
grand-junction/9.summary: The Historic Preservation Board discussed the city's pursuit of Certified Local Government status and its effect on design review in historic districts. Members of the public asked the board to nominate the Lincoln Park Barn, and the board asked staff to schedule a special meeting on it.

grand-junction/10.title: Matchett Park Bike Park future
grand-junction/10.summary: A survey showed strong support for keeping the Matchett Park bike park, with 56% strongly supporting. Given budget limits and the Lunch Loop project, the Parks and Recreation Advisory Board moved to hold off on further development.

grand-junction/11.title: Regional fire and EMS funding and rural fire district
grand-junction/11.summary: Staff cited the cost of providing rural fire and EMS service as a major budget pressure. The city plans to give the Rural Fire District the required two-year notice to renegotiate. The city manager is pursuing a regional fire district as a long-term solution.

grand-junction/12.title: 2324 Highway 6 & 50 rezone
grand-junction/12.summary: RAMS 1 Ho LLC asked to rezone 2.88 acres from light industrial to general commercial for retail and office development. The Planning Commission recommended approval and Council set a hearing for Oct. 21.

grand-junction/13.title: Redlands 360 development expansion and annexations
grand-junction/13.summary: Council held a hearing on amending the Redlands 360 plan to add about 29 acres, for about 629 acres total. Later, annexation of right-of-way along Easter Hill, South Broadway, 23 Road and Highway 340 was introduced.

grand-junction/14.title: I-70B corridor and US 6 CDOT projects
grand-junction/14.summary: The Historic Preservation Board prepared comments to CDOT on I-70B improvements affecting the former Union Carbide building and possible buried streetcar tracks. Council also heard an update on the US 6 Access Control Plan.

grand-lake/0.title: 2027 Town budget and grant-funded contracts
grand-lake/0.summary: Trustees held a series of workshops on a preliminary 2027 budget built from the 2025 audit. It shows a General Fund deficit of about $589,184 after the Town's share of four grant contracts, with $2.87M of the $7.51M in General Fund revenue coming from grants. A public hearing is set for November 9 and final approval for November 23, 2026, with discussion of wages, benefits and a budget officer appointment.

greeley/0.title: Global AI data center campus: pre-annexation agreement and interim water service
greeley/0.summary: Global AI (Colorado) LLC bought about 438.58 acres east of Highway 257 (the former Kodak/Carestream campus) and is evaluating a data center campus. Council agendas show a pre-annexation agreement requiring annexation by March 31, 2028. The Water and Sewer Board took up an interim water service agreement tied to it, replacing the existing water contract that expires March 31, 2027. Residents spoke against a data center over water contamination fears.
greeley/0.where: East of State Highway 257, south of Eastman Park Drive

greeley/1.title: Ballot Question 2F: sales tax increase for West Greeley and Civic Campus
greeley/1.summary: Council moved to put a 0.60% sales and use tax increase (2027 through 2067) to fund capital projects on the November 3, 2026 ballot, and later passed a resolution supporting Question 2F. It was discussed in executive session for legal advice. The tax is tied to the West Greeley and Civic Campus projects. Many residents spoke against combining the tax with contested projects, while some supported a dedicated sales tax.

sources.body: Union Colony Civic Center Advisory Board
West Greeley Project Citizen Oversight Committee

greeley/2.title: Civic Campus financing and development
greeley/2.summary: Council considered certificates of participation to finance the Civic Campus with its amenities and public improvements. The Planning Commission reviewed preliminary subdivisions for the Judicial Center and the 4-lot Civic Campus downtown. Redevelopment begins with a temporary juror parking lot while the new City Hall is built. The Judicial Center alley vacation was also on council agendas.
greeley/2.where: Downtown Greeley, near 10th Avenue, 11th Avenue, 9th Street and 10th Street

greeley/3.title: West Greeley / Catalyst (Cascadia) project
greeley/3.summary: Residents criticized the Catalyst/Cascadia project debt, called for a public vote, and questioned the timing of financial decisions. The West Greeley Citizen Oversight Committee was to discuss whether Greeley should keep pursuing the project without a known financial partner. The first West Greeley debt payment appears in the 2027 capital plan, and a Metropolitan District service plan for West Greeley Commons was on a council agenda.

sources.body: West Greeley Project Citizen Oversight Committee

greeley/4.title: 2027 budget cuts and the September 11 budget retreat
greeley/4.summary: The City Manager's recommended 2027 budget came out September 4 and Council held a budget retreat September 11. It follows tiered department cuts and 67.75 FTE lost through voluntary separations. First reading of the budget was set for October 20. Culture, Parks and Recreation identified $2.9 million in reductions, leaving an $800,000 gap. Residents and advisory boards objected to cuts affecting museums and parks.

sources.body: Union Colony Civic Center Advisory Board

greeley/5.title: Greeley History Museum cuts and staffing
greeley/5.summary: Proposed museum budget cuts would leave services staffed minimally, with the research assistant role at risk and possible closure to the public or appointment-only access. The Museum Advisory Board and the Historic Preservation Commission wrote to Council, and a former employee cited open-records requests. The recommended budget later added $150,000 for CPRD for museum funding.

greeley/6.title: Flock Safety license plate readers and police drones
greeley/6.summary: Residents repeatedly urged Council to end the Flock Safety contract, citing the lack of a public vote, costs, Fourth Amendment concerns and misuse. Councilmember DeBoutez requested a presentation. A September 8 work session covered Greeley's 17 Flock cameras, 30-day data retention and the drone first-responder program.

greeley/7.title: Great Western Industrial Park annexations and Windsor's reconsideration motion
greeley/7.summary: Residents raised concerns about the Great Western Industrial Park annexation's effects on services and possible data center use. Council went into executive session September 22 over annexations 1-15 and a Motion for Reconsideration from the Town of Windsor.

greeley/8.title: Arroyos del Sol annexation and zoning
greeley/8.summary: The Planning Commission heard the roughly 999.72-acre annexation northwest of Highway 257 Spur, west of Weld County Road 19 and south of the Cache la Poudre River, and recommended approval to Council. Zoning was set to the conservation district, with much of the land under a conservation easement and a master plan focused on public recreation.
greeley/8.where: Northwest of State Highway 257 Spur, south of the Cache la Poudre River

greeley/9.title: Artificial turf and front-yard landscaping rules
greeley/9.summary: Council considered letting residents install artificial turf in single-family front yards by permit with licensed installers. Members split on stormwater, heat and water conservation. Staff were to refine the draft, and a resident spoke on the issue. Staff also discussed landscaping code compliance, with 66 cases opened through June.

greeley/10.title: MERGE highway project and 2027 capital plan
greeley/10.summary: The roughly $204 million 2027 Capital Improvement Plan includes MERGE, backed by over $50 million in federal grants, state funds and anticipated TIFIA financing, but a substantial local share is still needed. The project proposes underpasses at 35th and 47th Avenues, roundabouts and property impacts, and the Art Commission is weighing up to $400,000 for public art. The plan also includes a temporary 25% cut in annual facility maintenance funding.

greeley/11.title: Downtown stormwater and 2027 water, sewer and stormwater rates
greeley/11.summary: The Stormwater Board recommended an 8% rate increase for 2027 (options were 6%, 8% and 10%), prioritizing the Downtown Revitalization and 12th Street Outfall to reduce flooding. The Water and Sewer budget proposes a 4.5% water and 3.0% sewer rate increase, with the F Street Operations Facility delayed.

greeley/12.title: Greeley Urban Renewal Authority and tax increment financing
greeley/12.summary: Council and GURA held a joint session on urban renewal law, tax increment financing and bonding, including possible links between the Greeley Mall TIF area and 17th Street and new HB 1348 requirements. GURA also scheduled a mobility hub presentation, Western Sugar multimodal connectivity project and TIF balance update.

greeley/13.title: Club Carwash at Two Rivers Marketplace
greeley/13.summary: Two Rivers Marketplace LLC #4 asked the Planning Commission for a Use by Special Review to allow a car wash in the C-H zone at 8503 11th Street. The hearing was July 28, 2026.

greeley/14.title: Water supply: Upper Laramie groundwater application and Halligan 401 lawsuit
greeley/14.summary: The Water and Sewer Board approved filing a Water Court application with the State Land Board for nontributary Upper Laramie groundwater in Weld County, about 1.1 million acre-feet. Council also authorized legal action over the Halligan Water Supply Project Clean Water Act Section 401 certification. Parks are cutting watering at 13 sites after the Greeley-Loveland ditch shut off early.

greeley/15.title: Housing: federal funding cycle, Prop 123 and needs assessment
greeley/15.summary: The Housing for All Advisory Board reviewed the first CDBG and HOME funding cycle, with Council making no changes to the 2026 Annual Action Plan. Staff warned that unspent HUD funds hurt the city's entitlement award. Council was asked to approve a Housing Needs Assessment contract and a Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment.

green-mountain-falls/0.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption (Ordinance 2026-05)
green-mountain-falls/0.summary: The town introduced Ordinance 2026-05 on March 31 to adopt the state-mandated Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which takes effect July 1, 2026. A public hearing was held April 23, the board approved it May 5 with a correction, and on Aug. 4 it approved changes replacing WUI references with the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. A resident questioned the penalties.

green-mountain-falls/1.title: Sale of town land, open space rezoning and annexation of enclaves
green-mountain-falls/1.summary: The board has discussed selling town properties, whether rezoning town open space to park would make sales harder, and annexing enclaves. In June it sent annexation of an enclave property back to the Planning Commission and put the open space-to-park rezoning on July's agenda. The 1997 annexation/3-mile plan is being updated. A resident urged an ordinance or rezoning to protect open space.

green-mountain-falls/2.title: 2026 sales tax increase ballot question and capital projects
green-mountain-falls/2.summary: Town Manager Patterson presented a 'Closing the Gap' plan for a sales tax increase to fund sidewalks, culverts, sewage, and pool, park and playground updates. On April 7 the mayor moved to place a 0.05% sales tax for four years on the ballot for the Capital Improvement Fund, with the old Marshal's building a priority. Ballot resolutions followed in May, and a general election call in August.

green-mountain-falls/3.title: 2026 budget, fee schedule and 2027 draft budget
green-mountain-falls/3.summary: The 2026 budget was presented in October 2025 and adopted in December along with the mill levy certification and fee schedule. A new fee schedule was approved May 5. Work sessions on the 2027 draft budget were being set up for fall 2026.

green-mountain-falls/4.title: Short-term rental tax and rule changes
green-mountain-falls/4.summary: In December 2025 the council took up an STR tax ordinance (2025-06) and a short-term rental amendment (2025-09) alongside the budget.

green-mountain-falls/5.title: Comprehensive Plan addendum
green-mountain-falls/5.summary: The town is working on a 2026 Comprehensive Plan addendum, with a work session set for August 18 at 5:30 p.m. and further review dates being scheduled. A resident has stressed the board's job to carry out Comp Plan goals.

green-mountain-falls/6.title: Downtown parking, road and drainage work
green-mountain-falls/6.summary: The town is paving and reworking parking near the Blue Moose and Lake Street, completed in June with 78 downtown spaces, plus a Maple Street parking survey, trailhead parking concerns, road base and 2026 drainage improvements.
green-mountain-falls/6.where: Downtown, Lake Street and Maple Street

green-mountain-falls/7.title: Wastewater, septic and sewage issues
green-mountain-falls/7.summary: Septic pumping for the Marshal's building and park was estimated around $16,000. A wastewater feasibility study was announced in April, and sewage is a priority in the sales tax plan. Water rights attorney services were tabled in January pending creek flow measurement.

green-mountain-falls/8.title: El Paso Trail property
green-mountain-falls/8.summary: The board requested an appraisal for the El Paso Trail property in February. In June the mayor reported the Board of Health voted 7 to 1 to remove the transfer of title resolution for El Paso, effective July 11.

green-mountain-falls/9.title: Election date change and Lake Street bathrooms/pool
green-mountain-falls/9.summary: Ordinance 2026-03 moved the town election date from the first Tuesday of April. The board also handled pool opening and Lake Street bathrooms discussions.

greenwood-village/0.title: Emergency permit parking districts near Cherry Creek High School
greenwood-village/0.summary: On Aug. 3 Council passed emergency ordinances 08-26 and 09-26 expanding the Cherry Creek Village North permit parking district and creating one in Village on the Lake, ahead of a student parking shortage caused by the Cherry Creek High School rebuild. By October, police reported 88 warnings, 18 citations and permits issued to about 125 households, and Council held a study session on the districts.
greenwood-village/0.where: Cherry Creek Village North and Village on the Lake neighborhoods

greenwood-village/1.title: Grace Chapel place of worship at 8500 E. Orchard Road
greenwood-village/1.summary: Grace Chapel asked for a Special Use Permit and Site Development Plan to repurpose an existing building and parking lot at 8500 E. Orchard Road as a place of worship, with 250 parking spaces and new LED lighting. Planning and Zoning recommended approval, and Council held the quasi-judicial hearing Aug. 17; staff found the approval criteria met.

greenwood-village/2.title: Recreation use with pickleball courts and new plat
greenwood-village/2.summary: Council held a quasi-judicial hearing on a site plan amendment, special use permit and final plat for a recreation use in the Mixed Commercial district. The plan removes a parking lot, adds open space and builds four pickleball courts. Public comments asked for a noise study.

greenwood-village/3.title: 2027 budget and mill levy
greenwood-village/3.summary: Council held first-reading public hearings on Ordinance 12-26 adopting the 2027 budget and Ordinance 13-26 setting the mill levies. A budget workshop was held Sept. 28.

greenwood-village/4.title: EV charging station rules
greenwood-village/4.summary: Staff briefed Council on adding Land Development Code standards for commercial EV chargers, including screening of equipment, since the code is silent on them. This follows state law (HB 24-1173) requiring permitting standards, and the charger installation at 7600 E. Orchard Road. Staff is not recommending changes to approval processes, and an ordinance would come back later if Council directs.

greenwood-village/5.title: EV chargers at 7600 E. Orchard Road
greenwood-village/5.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission considered a fourth amendment to the site plan to approve four EV chargers where two were previously approved. A county recording error had led the city to issue a building permit based on the wrong plan.

greenwood-village/6.title: High Line Canal irrigation phase two
greenwood-village/6.summary: Council considered a license agreement with Arapahoe County to install the second phase of well-water irrigation along the High Line Canal, running from Long Rd to Steele to Garden Ln. Work would continue through winter. Council also discussed Curtis Park, which stays on Denver Water because it would need a large booster pump.

greenwood-village/7.title: Carson Park public art sculptures
greenwood-village/7.summary: The Arts and Humanities Council and staff asked Council to approve fabrication and installation of three sculptures by Kevin Shaffer in Carson Park, tied to the park improvements and the city's 75th anniversary. A public input meeting was held Aug. 26 in the park.

greenwood-village/8.title: Side yard setback variance for garage addition, Monaco Heights
greenwood-village/8.summary: A homeowner in the Monaco Heights PUD requested a variance to build a garage addition about 15 feet from the side line instead of the required 20 feet. Staff found the request does not meet the criteria and noted a compliant garage is possible.

greenwood-village/9.title: Side yard variance for home addition (PZ-26-00028 area)
greenwood-village/9.summary: The Board of Adjustments and Appeals heard a variance for a 1959 home's north side yard setback, with 17% of the side yard and 1,303 sq ft encroached, and continued one case to Oct. 22. At that meeting an adjacent neighbor spoke against a variance, saying setbacks exist for a reason.

greenwood-village/10.title: Brinkerhoff Landmark Restaurant site plan at 5390 Greenwood Plaza
greenwood-village/10.summary: Council scheduled a public hearing on the site development plan for the Brinkerhoff Landmark Restaurant, with a related development improvement agreement.

greenwood-village/11.title: City use of artificial intelligence
greenwood-village/11.summary: Council discussed a careful approach to using AI in city operations, focused on protecting sensitive information before any broader adoption.

gunnison-county/0.title: Lower Verzuh Ranch subdivision sketch plan (LUC-25-00004)
gunnison-county/0.summary: Commissioners deliberated on a Major Impact sketch plan for the Lower Verzuh Ranch Subdivision. They voted not to hold an additional public hearing. On July 28 they sent the application back to the Planning Commission for a more refined basis and conditions. On August 11 the decision was postponed to a later meeting. Commissioners were split, with some concerned about the north valley and the level of public opposition.

gunnison-county/1.title: 0.50% countywide sales tax for roads and bridges on November ballot
gunnison-county/1.summary: On August 18 commissioners approved Resolution 2026-29 referring a 0.50% countywide sales tax for roads, bridges and related transportation infrastructure to the November 3, 2026 election. They also approved an agreement with the Clerk and Recorder to run the ballot question. Commissioners stressed the money would go only to road and bridge work.

gunnison-county/2.title: 2027 county budget draft and December 8 public hearing
gunnison-county/2.summary: The first draft of the 2027 budget was presented October 13. Commissioners asked for work sessions on Road & Bridge, Public Health, Human Services, the Housing Authority and Whetstone, and the Capital Improvement Plan. A $10,000 late-night taxi request may be added to contracts for services, and a public hearing was set for December 8 at 5:30 pm.

gunnison-county/3.title: Whetstone housing and Housing Authority budget amendment
gunnison-county/3.summary: The Housing Authority amended its 2026 budget and appropriation (Resolution 2026-005) for Whetstone because of how the bond documents work. Whetstone is also set to include family childcare units, and its business plan is slated for a budget work session.

gunnison-county/4.title: Mineral Point property agreements
gunnison-county/4.summary: The Housing Authority and commissioners went into executive session on September 15 to get legal advice on proposed Mineral Point Property agreements and to develop negotiation strategy. No outcome is stated in the documents.

gunnison-county/5.title: Senior property tax exemption appeal (Haack)
gunnison-county/5.summary: On September 1 the Board of Equalization heard an appeal from Teresa Haack, whose senior property tax exemption was disputed because voter registration and address records pointed elsewhere. The board voted to deny the appeal.

gunnison-county/6.title: Solid waste rate study
gunnison-county/6.summary: Commissioners approved awarding the Solid Waste Rate Study contract to Raftelis for $87,693 as part of the August 4 consent items.

gunnison-county/7.title: Cumberland Pass rehabilitation project funding application
gunnison-county/7.summary: A resolution on August 4 authorized a program application for the Gunnison County Cumberland Pass Rehabilitation Project, committing to implementation, matching funds and long-term commitments.

gunnison-county/8.title: Airport pavement maintenance and airport contracts
gunnison-county/8.summary: The county approved a $719,737 construction agreement with Maxwell Asphalt for 2025 airfield pavement maintenance at Gunnison-Crested Butte Regional Airport, plus a food and beverage/retail concession amendment.

gunnison-county/9.title: October 6 land use items and Land Use Resolution amendment
gunnison-county/9.summary: The October 6 agenda included resolutions on minor impact permits LUC-25-00043 and LUC-24-00036, a tax abatement petition, and an amendment to the Land Use Resolution and its fee schedule. Earlier, a development improvement agreement for LUC-25-00038 (Simco Ventures) and the Alpenview Townhomes plat (LUC-26-00009) were on consent.

gypsum/0.title: License plate readers and security cameras
gypsum/0.summary: A resident asked for an independent investigation of the Town's license plate reader cameras and potential legal claims. Council heard a staff presentation on the camera technology on Sept. 8 and held a dedicated public comment period on cameras and license plate readers on Sept. 22, including discussion of the contract with the Sheriff's Office.

gypsum/1.title: Tower Center PUD amendment and Filing No. 2 final plat
gypsum/1.summary: Council amended the Tower Center PUD Guide (Ordinance 10) after a second-reading hearing on Aug. 11. It tabled, then on Aug. 25 approved, Resolution 22 for the Filing No. 2 final plat and subdivision improvement agreements. On Sept. 8 it approved Resolution 25 assigning the improvement agreement.

gypsum/2.title: Lodging tax ballot measure
gypsum/2.summary: Council approved Resolution 23 calling a special coordinated election on a town lodging tax that would replace the existing county tax rather than add a new one. Discussion covered a resident's letter about the ballot measure and the ballot language.

gypsum/3.title: State collection of sales tax (Ordinance 11)
gypsum/3.summary: Council passed Ordinance 11, rewriting Chapter 3.02 so the Town's sales tax rules comply with state statutes and allow the state to collect the tax. It was approved on first reading Aug. 11 and on second reading Aug. 25.

gypsum/4.title: Clubhouse restoration project
gypsum/4.summary: Council approved Change Order 2 ($241,269.06) with A.J. Construction on Aug. 11, and Change Order 3 on Sept. 8. Staff said the project is complete apart from a final punch list.

gypsum/5.title: 2027 budget and municipal financial advisor
gypsum/5.summary: Staff are developing the draft 2027 budget. Council approved a municipal financial advisor contract with UMB Financial Services for up to $50,000 and accepted the 2025 audit presentation.

gypsum/6.title: I-70 Eagle Airport Interchange grant application
gypsum/6.summary: Council authorized an application to the FHWA PROTECT grant program for planning and design of the I-70 Eagle Airport Interchange project.

gypsum/7.title: Public comment policy change
gypsum/7.summary: After a legal review from the Town Attorney, Council decided to move to a general public comment period at the start of each meeting.

gypsum/8.title: Road and public works contracts
gypsum/8.summary: Council approved Change Order 2 ($14,570.63) for the 2025/2026 chipseal and slurry seal street renovations, and change orders for the Gypsum Recycling Center totaling $28,598.27, of which Gypsum pays $12,111.63 and Eagle County the rest. A bid selection for a Cooley Mesa Road pump station generator is on the Oct. 13 agenda.
gypsum/8.where: Townwide; Cooley Mesa Road pump station

gypsum/9.title: Sweetwater Lake NEPA project and Abrams Creek crossing
gypsum/9.summary: Council received an Aug. 11 item on the Sweetwater Lake NEPA project covering safety, wildlife and history. On Aug. 25 it heard an update on the Abrams Creek crossing project and water quality.

gypsum/10.title: Water and wastewater returned payment rules
gypsum/10.summary: Council held a public hearing and approved Ordinance 8, amending the municipal code on returned payments for water and wastewater service so the Town can require certified funds. An ordinance amending other water code sections (Ordinance 9) was also heard.

gypsum/11.title: Bear-resistant trash and wildlife
gypsum/11.summary: Council heard statistics on bears from Colorado Parks and Wildlife and discussed the availability and cost of bear-resistant cans.

haxtun/0.title: Electric rate increase (Ordinance 2025-2)
haxtun/0.summary: Council adopted Ordinance 2025-2 amending Section 54.20 of the municipal code to raise residential and commercial electric rates, citing cost increases from MEAN and WAPA. All present voted in favor.

haxtun/1.title: 2026 budget and mill levy adoption
haxtun/1.summary: After a public hearing with no public comment, council adopted the 2026 budget and appropriations (Resolutions 2025-9 and 2025-10), including a general property tax levy and funds for water and sewer. Discussion touched on a crack-fill machine for streets and a supplemental fund to be handled once the generator project price is complete.

haxtun/2.title: MEAN wholesale power service agreement renewal
haxtun/2.summary: MEAN is restructuring its service contract procedures, requiring each municipality to sign a new agreement because current contracts expire January 1, 2026. Council voted to approve the new service agreement.

haxtun/3.title: 2026 employee health insurance increase
haxtun/3.summary: Public Sector Health notified the Town of an 18% rate increase for 2026 employee health insurance. Council acknowledged similar increases may recur and said alternative options may need to be considered next year.

hayden/0.title: Spruce Summit battery storage site: master plan amendment and rezone
hayden/0.summary: The Town of Hayden has applied to change the future land use of a 73-acre parcel to Industrial/Business/Light Industrial and rezone it from Commercial to I-2 Industrial. If approved, the site is planned for battery and energy storage systems through a later major site plan application. The Planning Commission was set to review both requests on July 30, 2026.

hayden/1.title: Data center moratorium study and state/federal letters
hayden/1.summary: Town Council reported that a citizen committee for the data center moratorium study will be announced shortly. Council also asked staff to draft letters to state and federal representatives about data center bills and related legislation.

hayden/2.title: Council position on 2026 ballot measures (fire district, school, CMC, RTA)
hayden/2.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-14 endorsing Measures 6A (West Routt Fire mill levy override), 4B (annexing Hayden RE-1 into Colorado Mountain College district), 7A (half-percent sales tax for Yampa Valley Regional Transportation Authority) and 4A (Hayden RE-1 mill levy override). Councilmember Haight objected to the RTA language and moved to remove it. A separate Resolution 2026-16 on endorsing 7A also appeared on the Oct. 15 agenda.

hayden/3.title: 2027-2029 draft budget and property tax
hayden/3.summary: The Town, its Housing Authority and the Northwest Colorado GID received presentations on the 2027-2029 draft budget. Town documents show operating mill levy of 25.067 and debt service levy of 3.990, with about $1.54 million in budgeted property tax revenue and sales tax projected near $2.35 million.

hayden/4.title: New road from business park to Highway 40 and hotel lot
hayden/4.summary: The Northwest Colorado GID was told design is starting for a new road from the business park to Highway 40. The GID is also closing on another business park lot intended for a hotel.

hayden/5.title: Pickleball court and 3rd Street Park
hayden/5.summary: Parks and Recreation discussed creating an outdoor pickleball court, possibly split to serve other uses, with a cost estimate of $260,000 and a search for grants. A pickleball co-op was suggested. 3rd Street Park updates remained on agendas through October.

hayden/6.title: New animal ordinance (Ordinance 752)
hayden/6.summary: Council held second reading and a public hearing on Ordinance 752, a new ordinance on animals in town with conforming changes to Section 14.20.040. No one spoke at the hearing.

hayden/7.title: Housing Authority rent increases
hayden/7.summary: Housing Authority minutes note rent increases are expected to start August 1 at $900, with grants pending. A presentation on more housing initiatives to Council is planned for early 2027.

hayden/8.title: Emergency fee schedule change with Apex
hayden/8.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-15 adopting an emergency fee schedule change involving Apex.

hayden/9.title: Support for Western Resilience Center
hayden/9.summary: Council was asked to continue supporting the Western Resilience Center, formerly the Yampa Valley organization.

hayden/10.title: Hayden Center budget and farmers market changes
hayden/10.summary: Parks and Recreation discussed Hayden Center budget season and changes to the market and events, including dropping the vendor fee, an October date for pumpkins, and volunteer incentives.

hooper/0.title: 2026 budget, property tax levy and attorney contract
hooper/0.summary: At the December 3, 2025 meeting the Town held a public hearing on the 2026 budget. Trustees were also set to consider Resolutions 6, 7 and 8-2025 to adopt the budget, levy property taxes and appropriate funds. The agenda also listed an attorney contract rate increase and a legal services contract (Resolution 5-2025).

hooper/1.title: Town park safety concerns and 2026 park improvements
hooper/1.summary: Ramona Smith presented park safety concerns in December 2025. In March 2026 the Board planned to discuss a 2026 park grant led by Trustee Mimi Dolan, hiring a park and town maintenance employee, and placing a library box in the town park.

hooper/2.title: Public nuisance and ground fowl ordinances
hooper/2.summary: The March 18, 2026 agenda included Ordinance 1-2026 amending public nuisance provisions and Ordinance 2-2026 amending standards for ground fowl in the municipal code.

hooper/3.title: 2026 regular town election
hooper/3.summary: Resolution 4-2025 on the December 2025 agenda called the town's regular election.

hotchkiss/0.title: Drought restrictions, water moratorium and bulk water standpipe
hotchkiss/0.summary: In February the board passed an emergency ordinance (2026-01) pausing new out-of-town water taps and limiting sales from the town standpipe. In April and May it discussed drought restrictions, Resolution 2026-04, and raising bulk water rates to $12 per thousand gallons outside the 81419 ZIP code. Water rates and the standpipe were sent to a separate work session.

hotchkiss/1.title: Hiring a permanent Town Administrator and new Town Attorney
hotchkiss/1.summary: The board worked with KRW Associates on a search for a permanent Town Administrator, with executive sessions in May and June. Kimberly States was in the job by July, and Ordinance 2026-04 set out the office's powers. The board also sought proposals for a new town attorney and had the contract reviewed. Sarah Ross was serving as attorney by July.

hotchkiss/2.title: Proposed park on Bridge Street lots and skate park request
hotchkiss/2.summary: Don Foster proposed a park on the empty lots at 171 and 191 E Bridge Street, and the board agreed to form a working group in August. Resident Larry Wilkening opposed it and said the land should host a revenue-generating business. Tanner Wilson asked the town to consider a skate park, and the town offered a letter of support.

hotchkiss/3.title: Ordinance 2026-07 on demonstrations and special events in public rights-of-way
hotchkiss/3.summary: The board took up an ordinance setting content-neutral safety, access and permit requirements for demonstrations and special events on public rights-of-way. Residents commented, and the board approved it on August 27. In September the parade permit process had to change, and the board waived the permit for the North Fork Miners homecoming parade.

hotchkiss/4.title: Staff wage study and benefits
hotchkiss/4.summary: Graves Consulting presented a wage compensation study, with implementation proposed for June 1, 2026 and no increase to the 2026 budget. Staff also proposed more vacation time and insurance improvements costing $3,000 to $5,000. Trustee Sven Edstrom said there was too much information to decide on that night.

hotchkiss/5.title: Wildland-Urban Interface Code and wildfire planning
hotchkiss/5.summary: Ordinance 2026-03 adopting a Wildland-Urban Interface Code came to a public hearing in July, with a fire-risk map covering the whole town. The Western Slope Conservation Center presented a Wildfire Ready Action Plan in December. Staff also noted a wildfire near the town's water source could cut off supply, and talks are underway to fund a study.

hotchkiss/6.title: Variance requests: drive-thru lot and parking, sheds and fences
hotchkiss/6.summary: In November the board tabled a variance for a nonconforming lot at 6th Street for a drive-thru, sending the applicant back for a documented parking agreement with City Market. Neighbors raised parking concerns. In June it considered variances for a shed at 159 E Orchard, an 8-foot fence at 791 Barrow Mesa Road, and a 6-foot fence at 319 Knob Hill Circle Drive.
hotchkiss/6.where: 6th Street; 159 E Orchard; 791 Barrow Mesa Road; 319 Knob Hill Circle Drive

hotchkiss/7.title: Master Plan and housing
hotchkiss/7.summary: The town worked with Urban Rural Continuum on a new Master Plan, and the Planning Commission approved the final plan in April. Trustees also discussed the difficulty of finding housing in town.

hotchkiss/8.title: Sidewalk repair funding
hotchkiss/8.summary: A resident said no progress had been made on sidewalk repairs since a 2022 rating of sidewalks. He suggested a utility bill fee that would need voter approval.

hotchkiss/9.title: Police vehicles and Police Department policies
hotchkiss/9.summary: The board discussed transferring police vehicles in exchange for tuition at Technical College of the Rockies. It directed the chief to seek a contract amendment so the town avoids extra tuition costs. In September the board approved revisions to the Police Department vehicle use policy.

hotchkiss/10.title: Trustee compensation ordinance
hotchkiss/10.summary: After a work session discussion, the board passed Emergency Ordinance 2026-02 on trustee pay in March. It was set to take effect before the next election, with pay aligned with other valley towns.

hotchkiss/11.title: DMEA broadband franchise and telecom purchase
hotchkiss/11.summary: A franchise agreement with DMEA concerning broadband was planned for January. In July the board considered Ordinance 2026-05, a franchise agreement for the purchase of Delta County Tele-Com.

hudson/0.title: Prestige Builder Group settlement over Canterbury Meadows (Ravenna St & Stow Rd)
hudson/0.summary: Council held a public hearing on Resolution 26-118, settling litigation and a multi-million-dollar takings claim with Prestige Builder Group for a 32-lot conservation development on about 94.56 acres. Neighbors say it bypasses the Planning Commission and the Land Development Code and worry about water runoff and a high water table. The Planning Commission has discussed the agreement and asked for separate legal counsel.

hudson/1.title: Clinton Crossing downtown site plan and financing
hudson/1.summary: Council and staff are reviewing three refined site plans for Clinton Crossing, with residents preferring single-family homes, townhomes and duplexes plus a market hall, community center and boutique hotel. Staff are weighing a Planned Development review and public finance tools such as TIF and special districts. A resident objected to the residential component.
hudson/1.where: Clinton Street and Morse Road area, downtown

hudson/2.title: Low-speed vehicle (golf cart) rules, Ordinance 26-113
hudson/2.summary: Council is amending Chapter 478 on low-speed vehicles, with requirements for licensing, insurance, speed limits and a ban on state routes and 35 mph roads. Residents asked that short crossings be allowed and questioned equipment rules. The ordinance had second reading Aug 18 with amendments pending.

hudson/3.title: Capital plan, unfunded projects and 2027 budget
hudson/3.summary: Council reviewed the 2027-2031 five-year capital plan and discussed how to use excess carryover funds on unfunded projects such as Fiber-to-the-Home, stormwater and the Barlow Road sidewalk. Income tax revenue and the loss of a store were part of the discussion. Council also accepted county-determined property tax rates.

hudson/4.title: Hudson Innovation Park at 996 Hines Hill Road
hudson/4.summary: Staff updated Council on the park, including moving the salt barn, excess soil, property tax abatement options and Hines Hill Road improvements. Council asked for details on abatement and road costs.
