hudson/5.title: Brandywine Creek watershed study and stormwater projects
hudson/5.summary: Council heard the final draft Brandywine Creek Watershed Study with a ranked list of capital projects. Stormwater work also includes the Ellsworth Meadows golf course project, bid alongside pond retaining wall work.
hudson/5.where: Brandywine Creek watershed; Ellsworth Meadows Golf Course

hudson/6.title: Utility construction rules and Velocity Broadband rollout
hudson/6.summary: Ordinance 26-115 would add construction requirements such as directional drilling and vacuum excavation to protect utilities. Council discussed time and cost effects on the Velocity Broadband schedule; a motion to pass it on one reading failed.

hudson/7.title: Maple Grove Park lease termination with Summit Metro Parks
hudson/7.summary: Council is considering a settlement ending the city's lease with Summit Metro Parks for Maple Grove Park.

hudson/8.title: West Barlow Road railroad crossing exemption and traffic measures
hudson/8.summary: Council agreed to ask the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio to exempt the W. Barlow Road tracks. Staff also discussed truck restrictions and a turn radius fix at SR 91 and SR 303, and a signal ordinance at SR 303 and N. Hayden Parkway.
hudson/8.where: W. Barlow Road; SR 303 and N. Hayden Parkway

hudson/9.title: Downtown Windstream property financing on Owen Brown Street
hudson/9.summary: Council is considering notes of $740,000 and $925,000 to refinance and finance former Windstream properties bought for Downtown Phase II.

hudson/10.title: Historic district reviews: 88 N Main door, Owen Brown townhomes, Standard Shop
hudson/10.summary: Boards are handling a door installed without a permit at 88 N Main, with a dispute over an executive session. A townhome project at Clinton and Morse is under appeal after denial, and the Standard Shop Company approval expires October 2026.
hudson/10.where: 88 N Main Street; 86 Owen Brown Street; Terex Road

hudson/11.title: Fire/EMS staffing and emergency communications
hudson/11.summary: Fire and EMS went to 24/7 staffing, with renovations under way. Staff presented the crisis communication plan and discussed relocating the fireworks display.

huerfano-county/0.title: GroAway, LLC conditional use permit hearings (LU-26-000154)
huerfano-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on the GroAway, LLC conditional use application on Sept. 10, 2026, then voted to continue discussion. On Oct. 8 and Oct. 22 it weighed whether to reopen the hearing and admit new material received afterward, including public comment and a letter from Colorado Parks and Wildlife. It could also recommend that the commissioners hold a separate hearing.

huerfano-county/1.title: Preliminary 2027 county budget
huerfano-county/1.summary: County Administrator Carl Young presented a preliminary balanced 2027 budget on Oct. 15. It includes a 3.6% cost-of-living raise, extra pay increases in Human Services and Road and Bridge capped at $4,000 combined, and a warning that County General must cut costs amid fuel and jail-housing costs. Fund balances are not shown yet and will appear in the final budget.

huerfano-county/2.title: Camping ordinance (Ordinance 26-04)
huerfano-county/2.summary: The commissioners approved a county camping ordinance creating Article V of Chapter 14 after discussion with residents about the ordinance and camping rights. The second reading was approved Sept. 15 (meeting listed Sept. 1).

huerfano-county/3.title: Revitalization authority plans: Gardner Main Street and Rio Cucharas
huerfano-county/3.summary: The County Revitalization Authority worked on outreach to taxing entities such as the water conservancy and hospital districts, plan adoption timing, a Gardner Main Street update, and the Rio Cucharas Inn project agreement to negotiate. The commissioners then approved the Gardner Main Street Revitalization Plan and Rio Cucharas CRA Plan (Resolutions 26-35 and 26-36).

huerfano-county/4.title: Housing programs and pre-approved home plans
huerfano-county/4.summary: The county is building housing tools: pre-approved house plans (Resolution 26-43), codifying a Housing Authority (26-44), a Prop 123 down payment assistance program, and an affordable housing revolving loan fund. Impact Development presented loan program details, a land banking and donation policy (26-45) was adopted, and the building authority looked at tiny home, barndominium and other floor plans.

huerfano-county/5.title: Fox Theater loan guaranty
huerfano-county/5.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 26-41 guaranteeing a First Southwest Bank loan for the Fox Theater in Walsenburg, to be repaid from the sale of tax credits. A further Fox Theatre guaranty (Resolution 26-48) and a McKinstry change order for the Fox were also on the agendas.

huerfano-county/6.title: Water augmentation lease-purchases and Gardner sewer project
huerfano-county/6.summary: Commissioners approved lease-purchase financing for eight acre-feet of water augmentation certifications for the Gardner Public Improvement District and three acre-feet for the Road and Bridge department. The Gardner Sewer Project bid tabulation was also before them and was moved to correspondence on Oct. 13.

huerfano-county/7.title: Recreation and cultural mill levy and voter survey
huerfano-county/7.summary: Magellan Strategies presented a county voter survey touching on parks and rec and jail renovation projects. Commissioners then approved Resolution 26-34 on a recreation and cultural mill levy, with Commissioner Wardell explaining the projects it focuses on.

huerfano-county/8.title: Marijuana licenses and water use concerns
huerfano-county/8.summary: At a hearing on the ISO99, LLC marijuana license (ML-26-000008), a resident asked about water restrictions and drought; the applicant provided proof of city water taps and past water bill payments. Other licenses for TKJ Investments and Focus Buds were also handled.

huerfano-county/9.title: School Creek Gravel Pit conditional use permit
huerfano-county/9.summary: The Planning Commission held a long public hearing (1:34 to 3:53 pm) on the School Creek Gravel Pit CUP (LU-26-000122) and approved it with a recommendation to go to the Board of County Commissioners. Conditions included permits for structures used during events.

huerfano-county/10.title: Spanish Peaks Airfield projects and finances
huerfano-county/10.summary: The airfield advisory board discussed a turnaround taxiway project, a five-year capital improvement plan, upgrading the access road on County Road 101, land acquisition advised by the FAA, and a budget running in the red. A resident raised concerns about the airfield's marketing presentation.

huerfano-county/11.title: Trash dumping and Safe Streets
huerfano-county/11.summary: The sheriff and county administrator discussed illegal trash dumping, what the current ordinance says and what a future ordinance could add, and a resident asked about dumpster requests. The Aguirre Community Center board also discussed a Safe Streets project and shoulder widening in the 10-year plan.

sources.body: Raymond Aguirre Community Center Advisory Board

huerfano-county/12.title: Jail renovation and DOLA grant extensions
huerfano-county/12.summary: The commissioners considered a jail renovation agreement with McKinstry Essention and extension requests for DOLA grants for Strong Communities and Jail Improvements.

huerfano-county/13.title: Cuchara Mountain Park liquor license and ski pond dam
huerfano-county/13.summary: The commissioners accepted the Liquor License Authority's recommendation that a special event liquor license for Cuchara Mountain Park not be approved. They also approved a $10,600 geotechnical services agreement for the park's ski pond dam.

huerfano-county/14.title: Wildfire and fire restrictions
huerfano-county/14.summary: The county moved from Stage 2 to Stage 1 fire restrictions and then lifted Stage 1. Commissioners backed forest restoration and wildfire mitigation grant applications and took up a Community Wildfire Protection Plan.

hugo/0.title: Water restrictions and water share shortage
hugo/0.summary: Hugo went to Level One water restrictions to stay within its state water allocations, after LAWMA explained the Town owns only common shares. The Town leased two preferred shares, replaced the restriction ordinance (Ordinance 300), and passed emergency Ordinance 302 on watering hours and days after a resident objected to three-days-in-a-row watering. Restrictions lifted October 1.

hugo/1.title: Water system improvements, loans and grants
hugo/1.summary: The Town approved a Colorado Water Resources and Power Development Authority loan of up to $5,395,767 for water facilities. It also held CDBG and WPCRF hearings on the Water System Improvements Project, with design underway for water tank repairs, well pump replacements and other GMS-managed work. Board also approved a sewer lift station purchase for Roundhouse Estates and project draws.

hugo/2.title: Water, sewer and trash rates and 2027 fee schedule
hugo/2.summary: The Town is working with Colorado Rural Water Association on a rate study. Resolutions 2026-13 and 2026-14 would set water, wastewater and refuse rates and a fee schedule effective January 1, 2027. GMS also was approved to do a tap fee study and impact fees were discussed for new development.

hugo/3.title: Proposed 1% sales tax for pool, culture and recreation
hugo/3.summary: The Town held a community meeting on November 12 about a possible 1% sales tax for the pool, culture, recreation and capital improvements. It was slated for the ballot as Ballot Issue #2 in January discussions.

hugo/4.title: 2027 budget and strategic plan
hugo/4.summary: The Town scheduled a 2027 budget review and workshop for October 19 where the draft Strategic Plan will also be reviewed. A 2025 audit presentation was set for October 13.

hugo/5.title: Hugo Main Street program
hugo/5.summary: The Town is exploring running Hugo Main Street under the Town and recruiting board members. A steering committee works with Colorado Main Street and the Board approved a resolution supporting Hugo becoming an official Main Street Community.

hugo/6.title: New firehouse and Fire Protection District land
hugo/6.summary: A new firehouse plan was presented in March. The Board disconnected tracts owned by the Hugo Fire Protection District via Ordinance 301 and waived one water and one sewer tap at 5th Street and 9th Avenue. Earlier the Board declined to add the fire department driveway to the CDOT sidewalk project.

hugo/7.title: Code enforcement, trash and property ordinance updates
hugo/7.summary: Hugo adopted ordinances on penalties for violations and code enforcement authority, and contracted Willdan for code enforcement services. A trash ordinance revision is coming in August and staff are applying for a DOLA Local Planning Capacity Grant for an abandoned and dilapidated property ordinance. The Board also approved an automated vehicle identification system ordinance.

hugo/8.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code (Ordinance 295)
hugo/8.summary: The Board tabled Ordinance 295, which would adopt the 2025 Wildfire Resiliency Code by reference; a trustee said the town learned late about its effect.

hugo/9.title: Housing: Housing Authority, expedited review and new housing
hugo/9.summary: The Hugo Housing Authority sought grant help for plumbing repairs and is working toward compliance with new staff. The Board adopted Resolution 2026-07 on expedited review for affordable housing projects. County economic development reports on possible new housing and DOLA demo funding.

hugo/10.title: Street repair and CDOT sidewalk project
hugo/10.summary: A pavement study is planned to set a street maintenance plan, and the Board approved a pothole repair proposal from Millan Asphalt & Crushing. The CDOT Sidewalk Project was waiting on asphalt approvals.

hugo/11.title: Main Street Live building survey and geotechnical work
hugo/11.summary: The Board directed OLC to proceed with survey and geotechnical evaluation depending on the Colorado Historical Grant outcome; work was in progress by October.

hugo/12.title: Parks, playground and football field safety
hugo/12.summary: Staff are seeking quotes and grants for playground equipment, and the Board approved a BYO Recreation proposal. Concerns about children playing on a hard football field led to direction to the Clerk.

hugo/13.title: Backflow prevention program
hugo/13.summary: Colorado Rural Water Association reviewed the state backflow program, found many businesses were not inventoried, and a resident raised concerns about installing a device at the RV Park.

idaho-springs/0.title: Carlson Elementary / 1300 Colorado Blvd 50-unit affordable housing plan denied
idaho-springs/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on a Final Development Plan (FDP26-001) for a 50-unit affordable multifamily development at the old Carlson Elementary site. Residents wrote in and spoke about parking, building size and historic design standards. Council's Aug. 10 agenda included Resolution #15 formally denying the plan.

idaho-springs/1.title: Roberts Brothers Garage: Clear Creek Center for Arts & Education fee waivers and contributions
idaho-springs/1.summary: The arts center has a $1.538 million state grant that needs a 1:1 match and has about $700,000 in hand. It asked the city for in-kind contributions and fee waivers worth up to $729,307. Council took up Resolution #27 granting fee waivers for the 121 15th Avenue redevelopment. Parking arrangements and a parking fee-in-lieu request also came up, and Ordinance #20 would designate the property as historic.

idaho-springs/2.title: Recreational occupation tax on outdoor recreation providers
idaho-springs/2.summary: Council considered Ordinance #19 referring a ballot measure to voters for a new occupation tax on outdoor recreation outfitters, with revenue dedicated to impacts such as streets, parking, public safety and water. The tax could be up to $5 per customer and would be paid by the provider. Rafting businesses brought requests about the tax to Council in October.

idaho-springs/3.title: Downtown parking: paid parking moratorium, parking study and library parking
idaho-springs/3.summary: Council considered Ordinance #18, a temporary moratorium on permits for private paid parking facilities. Planning staff presented preliminary parking study results, and Council had a parking requirements study on its Sept. 28 agenda. Residents asked for free parking to be returned at the Library and for Disabled Veteran plates to get free managed parking. In October the parking enterprise's name and scope were being amended.

idaho-springs/4.title: Two-way traffic on downtown Miner Street
idaho-springs/4.summary: Council was asked on Oct. 26 to approve two-way vehicle traffic on downtown Miner Street. The Miner Street Market was scheduled to run through Halloween, with the street reopening to traffic Nov. 5.

idaho-springs/5.title: 2027 city budget
idaho-springs/5.summary: The proposed 2027 budget was described as extremely difficult to prepare. It moves community promotion costs to the Parking Fund and pauses some employee benefits, and General Fund revenue is projected to be only about $100,000 above 2024. The city's property tax share falls from $282,237 to $267,546 at the same 6.310 mill rate. The promotions board recommended a $211,109 baseline budget.

idaho-springs/6.title: Affordable and senior housing incentives, Prop 123 and Fair Housing code changes
idaho-springs/6.summary: Council worked on affordable housing incentives, an Affordable Senior Housing Project, and a DOLA predevelopment funding application. It also covered its Proposition 123 commitment for 2027-2029. Ordinance #17 amends the city code on housing for people with disabilities to conform with state and federal Fair Housing law, and a group homes code amendment was also discussed.

idaho-springs/7.title: 2026 Comprehensive Plan adoption
idaho-springs/7.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the draft and held a hearing on a resolution recommending the 2026 Comprehensive Plan. Council took it up again in a September discussion and approved it by resolution on Oct. 26.

idaho-springs/8.title: Noise ordinance with decibel limits
idaho-springs/8.summary: The city code sets no maximum decibel level, so police have no objective standard to enforce. Staff proposed adding decibel limits by zone, measured at the property line, with a professional dB reader. Council discussed this in August and September.

idaho-springs/9.title: Golddigger Park and Fieldhouse development park conveyance
idaho-springs/9.summary: Council considered accepting a new park conveyed by the Fieldhouse development, and Resolution #29 accepts Lot 3 of the former Golddigger Field subdivision as a city park named Golddigger Park. A related minor subdivision of Lots 1-12 to create a fourth lot was heard by the Planning Commission and Council. A neighbor also raised concerns about apartments at the Field House.

idaho-springs/10.title: Water use and city landscaping during restrictions
idaho-springs/10.summary: A resident told the Planning Commission the city should follow the residential water restrictions, citing the waterfall running, sprinklers on city property and water running down the street. She urged native plant landscaping.

idaho-springs/11.title: I-70 Floyd Hill project and Exit 240 agreement
idaho-springs/11.summary: Council received an I-70 Floyd Hill project update. It also considered Resolution #18 approving an agreement for a project near Exit 240, tied to a downtown RAISE planning grant.

idaho-springs/12.title: Stop signs and traffic complaints
idaho-springs/12.summary: A resident asked for stop signs at 16th Avenue and Colorado Blvd, citing increased traffic.

jefferson-county/0.title: Lakewood Navigation Center operating costs agreement
jefferson-county/0.summary: Commissioners reviewed in September and on Oct. 13 unanimously approved an intergovernmental agreement and memorandum of understanding with Arvada, Edgewater, Golden, Lakewood, Westminster and Wheat Ridge on sharing the operating costs of the Lakewood Navigation Center.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/1.title: Red Rocks Amphitheatre transportation hub
jefferson-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled on Oct. 14 to consider a site approval for a transportation hub with 397 parking spaces and road improvements to serve Red Rocks Amphitheatre.
jefferson-county/1.where: 17355 Jurassic Road and 17900 Trading Post Road, Golden

jefferson-county/2.title: 143-unit planned development rezoning
jefferson-county/2.summary: A request to rezone land from Agricultural-Two and Commercial-One to Planned Development for up to 143 dwelling units went to the Planning Commission on Aug. 12. On Sept. 1, after staff and applicant presentations and public testimony, commissioners approved it by majority vote (not unanimous).

jefferson-county/3.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing agreements and Belveron bond allocation
jefferson-county/3.summary: The county approved a 2026 private activity bond award, carryforward and assignment involving Denver and Arvada tied to the Belveron project and a Prop 123 agreement. A Prop 123 unit-sharing agreement was approved Sept. 15, and a supplemental funding request for the expedited review incentive bonus was slated for Oct. 20.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/4.title: Preliminary and final plat pulled for public discussion
jefferson-county/4.summary: The plat case 24-114721PFP went to the Planning Commission Sept. 9. On Sept. 29 it was moved to the regular hearing agenda at the public's request, and after public testimony the Board unanimously approved it.

jefferson-county/5.title: New special district service plan approved
jefferson-county/5.summary: Service plan case 25-124167SV was continued from July 28 to allow proper notification. On Aug. 18, after public testimony, the Board unanimously approved it.

jefferson-county/6.title: Appointment of new County Manager
jefferson-county/6.summary: On Aug. 11 the Board approved the appointment of a county manager and an employment agreement. Laura Aldrete appears as County Manager in later meetings. A second amendment to the County Attorney's contract was approved Oct. 13.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/7.title: Head Start expansion and federal rule changes
jefferson-county/7.summary: The county approved Head Start policy updates and a continuation grant application, and commissioners praised the Lakewood Head Start expansion. A public comment on proposed federal changes to Head Start performance standards was on the Sept. 22 agenda.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/8.title: Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport leases and Taxiway D reconstruction
jefferson-county/8.summary: Commissioners approved a Winston Air hangar ground lease, new airport lease agreement policy, and Premier Hangar Group ground leases. They also approved a contract with Amrize West Central for the Taxiway D Phase II reconstruction.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/9.title: Parks and Open Space projects and easements
jefferson-county/9.summary: The Board approved a West 32nd Ave and Kipling St bus stop agreement with trails funding, Meyer Ranch Park forestry contract, Pleasant View Community Park utility easements, and Van Bibber Park canal agreements. Briefings also covered North Table Mountain Park improvements and the Hildebrand Ranch diversion structure replacement.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions
Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/10.title: Denver Water purchase and sale agreement
jefferson-county/10.summary: The county briefed and then approved a purchase and sale agreement with Denver Water through Facilities Management on Oct. 13.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/11.title: Positions on 2026 ballot measures
jefferson-county/11.summary: At a Sept. 23 special meeting, commissioners took positions on statewide and regional measures. They supported Amendment 87 (graduated income tax) and Front Range Passenger Rail Measure 7A by majority vote, and opposed Amendment 84 (mail ballot voter ID).

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Special Meeting

jefferson-county/12.title: Junction Urban Renewal Plan TIF revenue-sharing negotiations
jefferson-county/12.summary: Commissioners planned a closed session on Oct. 20 for legal advice and negotiation guidance on tax increment revenue sharing for the Junction Urban Renewal Plan.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Staff Briefings and Work Sessions

jefferson-county/13.title: Evergreen High School shooting one-year anniversary recognized
jefferson-county/13.summary: At the September 15, 2026 hearing, Sheriff Reggie Marinelli and David Clark, a representative of Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen, spoke on the one-year anniversary of the Evergreen High School shooting and how the community has come together since. The Commissioners recognized the Evergreen community. The minutes do not describe any new firearm policy action.

johnstown/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data centers
johnstown/0.summary: The Town Council took up Ordinance 2026-295 on Aug. 3, establishing a temporary moratorium on data centers. At the Aug. 17 meeting a resident asked about plans for future AI centers and what happens next.

johnstown/1.title: Permanent property tax mill levy cut of 8 mills
johnstown/1.summary: Ordinance 2026-299 would permanently reduce the town's mill levy by 8.000 mills in four annual steps of 2.000 mills. Any increase above the reduced levy would need new voter approval, and staff would handle the General Fund impact without restoring mills. This came to a public hearing on Oct. 19.

johnstown/2.title: FY 2027 budget and mill levy
johnstown/2.summary: Council held a preliminary FY 2027 budget work session on Sept. 28. Staff recommended keeping the full 23.947-mill levy because property tax revenue keeps declining, and the budget also covers sewer and water revenue bond debt. On Oct. 5 Council took up a resolution acknowledging receipt of the preliminary budget, and a FY 2026 budget amendment was also on the Sept. 9 agenda.

johnstown/3.title: Senior Center construction
johnstown/3.summary: Council discussed the Senior Center project in August, and a resident spoke in support of continuing it. On Oct. 5 Council considered awarding the construction contract to Fransen Pittman Construction Co., Inc., with contingency funds for unforeseen expenses at the Town Manager's discretion.

johnstown/4.title: YMCA contract and facility management agreement
johnstown/4.summary: Council discussed a June 22 motion regarding the Town and the YMCA and held an executive session on the YMCA contract in August. On Oct. 5 it considered an amended and restated Facility Management Agreement with the YMCA of Northern Colorado, along with a Settlement & Release Agreement and a reimbursement by the YMCA.

johnstown/5.title: Repeated power outages in Centerra and Johnstown
johnstown/5.summary: Residents wrote in to Council on Aug. 17 about constant power outages in Centerra and repeated outages across Johnstown.

johnstown/6.title: I-25 East Frontage Road transfer from CDOT
johnstown/6.summary: Council held a public hearing on Ordinance 2026-297 on Aug. 17. It would accept a portion of the I-25 East Frontage Road between mile markers 253.2 and 257.1 and approve an intergovernmental agreement with CDOT to devolve the road to the town. The ordinance was back on the Sept. 9 agenda.
johnstown/6.where: I-25 East Frontage Road, mile markers 253.2 to 257.1

johnstown/7.title: Stormwater rate study and fee increase
johnstown/7.summary: Council heard a Stormwater Master Plan rate study on Aug. 10. The stormwater fee of $5 per equivalent residential unit per month and the $1,100 per acre development charge have not been adjusted since the enterprise was set up in 2004. Staff proposed rate adjustments to pay for a tiered list of capital projects.

johnstown/8.title: Downtown Development Authority plan and DDA fund
johnstown/8.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission reviewed the Johnstown DDA Plan of Development, and Council held a public hearing on it Aug. 17. Ordinance 2026-298 to establish a DDA Fund followed in September and October, and a new DDA executive director was introduced.

johnstown/9.title: Housing needs assessment and comprehensive plan update
johnstown/9.summary: To comply with state Senate Bill 24-174, consultant ECOnorthwest drafted a housing needs assessment plus strategic growth and water supply elements for the comprehensive plan. Council held a work session Oct. 26. Planning and Zoning is to consider the drafts Nov. 18 and Council is to consider adoption Dec. 2, with a Housing Action Plan to follow in mid-2027.

johnstown/10.title: Whitehall rezoning and Riverbend Estates development
johnstown/10.summary: Council considered Ordinance 2026-294 rezoning the Whitehall property, after the Planning and Zoning Commission heard the Whitehall Filing No. 2 rezone and preliminary plat. Council also held a hearing on the Riverbend Estates P.U.D. Filing No. 1 final plat and final development plan, with related development and water and sewer service agreements.

johnstown/11.title: Lucky Star wireless monopine tower
johnstown/11.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission reviewed a Use by Special Review for a wireless communications facility (the Lucky Star Monopine) on Tract C of Podtburg Subdivision. The site is northeast of County Road 42 and west of Colorado Blvd. Council took up Resolution 2026-40 approving it on Sept. 9.
johnstown/11.where: Northeast of County Road 42 and west of Colorado Blvd

johnstown/12.title: Water system plan, water rates and water use
johnstown/12.summary: Council considered a $326,400 agreement with J-U-B Engineers for a Water System Master Plan update. A resident commented on water usage at town-owned facilities and on water rates. A Little Thompson Water District intergovernmental agreement was also on the Sept. 9 agenda.

johnstown/13.title: Town Attorney selection
johnstown/13.summary: Council interviewed firms for the appointed Town Attorney position on Aug. 24, including Hoffmann Parker Wilson & Carberry. On Oct. 5 Council considered a legal services agreement with Wilson Williams Fellman Dittman.

johnstown/14.title: Sale of Quality Liquid Feeds property
johnstown/14.summary: Council held executive sessions on the QLF property and considered Resolution 2026-42, a purchase and sale agreement with Quality Liquid Feeds, Inc. A purchase and sale agreement with Gillam Development Corporation was also on the Oct. 19 agenda.

johnstown/15.title: Weld County Road 15 resurfacing
johnstown/15.summary: Council considered awarding the Weld County Road 15 Resurfacing Project contract to Mountain Constructors, Inc. Funds were also approved for unforeseen construction expenses, not to exceed the budgeted amount.

kersey/0.title: 6 P's annexation, industrial zoning and land-use map change at 24822 Highway 34
kersey/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission held a public hearing on a request to annex a 49.5-acre property northeast of the Kuner/Five Rivers feedlot. It would be zoned I-Industrial, and the Comprehensive Plan map changed from Agriculture/Tourism to an employment-oriented designation for an oil/gas and agricultural support business. Neighbors who want to buy the property said industrial use is inappropriate and raised traffic concerns, and the Town may also annex adjacent County Road 56.
kersey/0.where: 24822 Highway 34, northeast of Kuner/Five Rivers feedlot

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/08.04.2026 Planning Commission Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202607311024090

kersey/1.title: Ballot Issue 2B: ten-year extension of the 17.205-mill property tax levy and 2027 budget
kersey/1.summary: The Board is considering a ballot issue to extend the Town's existing 17.205-mill property tax levy for ten years (2028-2037) without raising the rate. An ordinance referring a related ballot question about fixing the rate at 12.000 mills and a resolution of Board support were on the October 13 agenda, alongside the preliminary 2027 budget presentation and a September work session on the budget.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/October 13, 2026 Regular Meeting Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202610092015300
https://www.kerseygov.com/September 22, 2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202609221902470

kersey/2.title: Kersey Water Blueprint Plan
kersey/2.summary: The Town started a $50,000 Water Blueprint planning effort with the Brendle Group to protect long-term water supply amid regional buy-and-dry pressure. Northern Water now requires native supply for new development, so Kersey's Colorado-Big Thompson water alone may not support growth. The project is funded by a $37,500 DOLA grant, $10,000 from Northern Water and a $2,500 Town match; the first of three working sessions was September 22.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/September 22, 2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202609221902470

kersey/3.title: Clark Street Storm Sewer Project contract
kersey/3.summary: The Board awarded the construction contract for the Clark Street Storm Sewer Project to Mountain Constructors, Inc. after 13 bids; staff passed over the lowest bidder over reference and bid-item concerns. The bid came in well below the engineer's estimate, and the price is held for 180 days while the Town awaits FEMA funding.

kersey/4.title: Adoption of the 2024 International Fire Code
kersey/4.summary: The Board took up an ordinance adopting the 2024 International Fire Code, first read August 11 and set for a public hearing and second reading September 8. The Platte Valley Fire District currently uses the 2018 code, and adoption would align it with the Town's 2024 building codes and address newer issues like energy storage systems. No public comment was made at the hearing.

kersey/5.title: Renaming duplicate streets in Berryman Farms
kersey/5.summary: Staff asked the Board to authorize renaming streets east of 1st Street in the Berryman Farms subdivision because their names duplicate or resemble streets elsewhere, which could confuse emergency responders. Residents and property owners would need to update addresses, and staff would coordinate with Weld County and dispatch.
kersey/5.where: Berryman Farms subdivision, east of 1st Street

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/08.25.2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202608211214270

kersey/6.title: Community Center staffing and 2025 audit
kersey/6.summary: At a July 28 work session the Council was to hear the 2025 audit results and discuss community center staffing, prompted by feedback from a departing employee's exit interview.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/July 28, 2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202607241245290

kersey/7.title: Kersey holiday event changes
kersey/7.summary: Staff sought Board feedback on changes to the Kersey holiday event, following community input at the RTAP workshop that showed it as a high priority.

sources.url: https://www.kerseygov.com/08.25.2026 Work Session Agenda and Packet.pdf?t=202608211214270

kiowa/0.title: New 2026 Zoning Code replacing Chapter 16
kiowa/0.summary: The Planning Commission was asked to approve the 2026 Zoning Code Update as the town's official zoning ordinance (Resolution 2026-PC-01). On Oct. 13 the Board of Trustees holds a public hearing on Ordinance 2026-08, which would repeal and replace Chapter 16 and adopt a new zoning code.

kiowa/1.title: Proposed 2027 budget for the town and water authority
kiowa/1.summary: The Board of Trustees and the Kiowa Water and Wastewater Authority both have the proposed 2027 budget on their Oct. 13 agendas for discussion. The documents give no figures.

kiowa/2.title: Affordable housing commitment filing
kiowa/2.summary: Resolution 2026-19 would authorize the Town Administrator to file an affordable housing commitment with a state or other agency. The agenda excerpt does not name the agency.

kiowa/3.title: Floodplain permit fee
kiowa/3.summary: The Trustees have the town's floodplain permit fee, set by Resolution 2026-18, on their Oct. 13 agenda for discussion.

kiowa/4.title: Water authority contract with Gen-Tech, LLC
kiowa/4.summary: The Kiowa Water and Wastewater Authority is considering an agreement for professional services with Gen-Tech, LLC at its Oct. 13 meeting.

kiowa/5.title: Real property purchase discussions in executive session
kiowa/5.summary: The Trustees plan a closed session on Oct. 13 about the town's possible purchase or acquisition of real property, including negotiation strategy.

kit-carson-county/0.title: Carousel Wind III and IV pre-construction permits
kit-carson-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled on Aug. 18, 2026 to consider pre-construction permit applications from Carousel Wind III, LLC and Carousel Wind IV, LLC. The documents do not state the outcome.

kit-carson-county/1.title: Engie Resources conceptual site plan and setback variance
kit-carson-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission on Oct. 20 had an Engie Resources conceptual site plan on its agenda, along with a request for a setback variance. A setback variance request also appeared on the Oct. 21 county commissioners agenda alongside a land use permit for L3 Communications, LLC. The documents do not say whether these items are linked or how they were decided.

kit-carson-county/2.title: CDOT Stratton Spur project
kit-carson-county/2.summary: CDOT representatives Bradyn Tacha and Jay D. Johnson were scheduled to meet with the county commissioners at 2:15 PM on Oct. 21 about the Stratton Spur project. No details of the project are given in the agenda.

kit-carson-county/3.title: Human Services contracts and state funding amendments
kit-carson-county/3.summary: The Department of Human Services and commissioners were set to take up a $10,000 contract with the Early Childhood Council for Yuma, Washington and Kit Carson Counties. They also had a $9,381.15 HCPF Medicaid IGA amendment and a state TANF MOU amendment with a $203,136.62 allocation.

kit-carson-county/4.title: Road easements for Black Hills Energy and a feedlot waterline
kit-carson-county/4.summary: Commissioners had seven road easements for Black Hills Energy on their Oct. 21 agenda. They also had an easement for Happy Creek Inc. to run a 6-inch waterline for a feedlot.

kit-carson-county/5.title: County attorney contract with Richards Carrington
kit-carson-county/5.summary: Commissioners were to consider a contract with Richards Carrington, with Jeffrey Cure as county attorney, at $300 per hour.

la-junta/0.title: 2027 city budget, mill levy and appropriation
la-junta/0.summary: Finance Director Aliza Libby presented the 2027 budget on Sept. 8, and council held budget workshops and a meet-and-greet earlier in August. The Oct. 19 agenda has council approving the proposed 2027 budget, with first readings of the mill levy and annual appropriation ordinances.

la-junta/1.title: 2027 electric, water, wastewater and sanitation rates
la-junta/1.summary: The Board of Utilities agenda for Oct. 13 lists resolutions changing 2027 prices for electric, water, wastewater and sanitation, plus a recommendation on the 2027 utility fund budgets. Mayor Ayala noted in August that people say La Junta has the highest utility rates in Colorado.

la-junta/2.title: Economic Development Board ordinance
la-junta/2.summary: Council passed an ordinance creating a city Economic Development Board on first reading Sept. 21 and on second reading Oct. 19. It is meant to restart economic development as an arm of the city, like tourism, with its budget under the city, instead of a nonprofit with IRS problems. The City Clerk will call for letters of interest for board vacancies.

la-junta/3.title: Pueblo sewage spill and Arkansas River safety
la-junta/3.summary: Water Director Tom Seaba reported on a major raw sewage spill in Pueblo that reached the Arkansas River. Residents were told not to use untreated river water for food preparation or bathing, while local drinking water is safe and the treatment plant is working properly. Reservoir releases were increased to help flush the river.

la-junta/4.title: Urban Renewal Authority Spark Grants and Chestnut Apartments project
la-junta/4.summary: The URA tabled a Spark Grant request from Sangre de Cristo Community Care for its storefront at 207 Colorado Ave. because the work was done before approval. The Chestnut Apartments project is about 52 days past its 180-day contract term, with fire suppression, HVAC, plumbing and doors outstanding. The URA is also reviewing blight and life-safety applications from Arkansas Valley CASA and La Junta Associated Charities.

la-junta/5.title: Temporary event ordinance for side-by-sides and low-speed vehicles
la-junta/5.summary: Council passed on first reading (Sept. 8) and second reading (Sept. 21) a temporary event ordinance allowing side-by-sides and other approved low-speed vehicles during events. It grew out of Main Street and Urban Renewal discussions and committee needs for events like Tarantula Fest and Early Settlers Day.

la-junta/6.title: Ethics and conflict of interest rules for officials
la-junta/6.summary: Council discussed adopting a conflict of interest disclosure form and a broader ethics process covering elected officials and employees. Council also re-adopted Resolution R-13-2026 on Sept. 21 to allow Council Member Rikhof's recusal.

la-junta/7.title: Lodging tax collection from short-term rental hosts
la-junta/7.summary: Council took up the second reading of an ordinance amending Ordinance 1688 so lodging taxes are remitted on behalf of hosts in the city. Council said it had been discussed extensively.

la-junta/8.title: Derelict property cleanup under the Copper Grant
la-junta/8.summary: Council approved a resolution on city-owned junk properties tied to a larger grant called the Copper Grant, with discussion of abatement costs and using EPA grants for asbestos. Council asked about plans for the four properties.

la-junta/9.title: Consolidation Agreement third amendment and emergency grant
la-junta/9.summary: The Oct. 19 agenda has council considering a third amendment to the Consolidation Agreement. Council also reported a grant of up to about $30 million from an emergency program.

la-junta/10.title: Naming the field at Potter Park for Jim Sullivan
la-junta/10.summary: Residents asked to name the field Jim Sullivan Field at Potter Park, without renaming the park, under the city's naming procedure.

la-junta/11.title: Flooding and drainage at Lewis Avenue and 2nd Street
la-junta/11.summary: A Ward 1 resident said that after recent rainstorms the area has only two drains, causing flooded roads and water in basements of homes and businesses.

la-junta/12.title: Smell at Industrial Park and golf course, wastewater plant work
la-junta/12.summary: Water Director Tom Seaba addressed odors near the Industrial Park and golf course. The utility has a new dewatering press, lagoon discussions and a system extension on 24th Street between Carson and Belleview.

lafayette/0.title: New Land Use Code and citywide rezoning
lafayette/0.summary: Council passed the new Land Use Code and zoning map on first reading in August after a public hearing, then adopted it on second reading in September with amendments, after heavy testimony about housing diversity, parking, wildlife corridors and how the code follows the comprehensive plan.

lafayette/1.title: Old Town OTX-3 zoning and building heights on Public Road
lafayette/1.summary: Residents objected to the new OTX-3 zone allowing larger, taller buildings along Public Road south of Emma Street; a joint council and planning commission workshop agreed to shrink the maximum building footprint from 25,000 to 10,000 square feet and revisit height in a second ordinance.
lafayette/1.where: Public Road south of Emma St, Old Town

lafayette/2.title: Data center and advanced air mobility moratoriums
lafayette/2.summary: After council asked how the new code regulates data centers, it adopted an 18-month moratorium on land use applications and building permits for data centers in October, alongside an emergency 18-month moratorium on advanced air mobility facilities.

lafayette/3.title: Flock license plate reader cameras
lafayette/3.summary: Many residents urged council to end the Flock Safety license plate camera contract, and council weighed two versions of the 2027 budget, one with no Flock funding, and discussed a formal policy for automatic license plate readers.

lafayette/4.title: Naming the 701 S. Public Road pocket park for Rosebelle Lueras
lafayette/4.summary: Residents spoke at meeting after meeting asking that the new pocket park at 701 S. Public Road be named for Rosebelle Lueras, and council took up the naming in October.

lafayette/5.title: Zoning for churches along Highway 287
lafayette/5.summary: Church members raised concerns about how the new code zones churches, and council directed that the church parcels at Highway 287 and South Boulder Road be zoned like Immaculate Conception.

lafayette/6.title: Boulder Ranch development off Baseline and Burlington
lafayette/6.summary: Residents wrote in opposing the proposed high-density Boulder Ranch development on 78 acres near Baseline Road and Burlington, citing traffic, open space and the buffer agreement with Boulder, with over 2,000 petition signatures.

lafayette/7.title: LaMont Does Park and water park tax extension
lafayette/7.summary: Council put the extension of an expiring property tax for LaMont Does Park and the Great Outdoors Water Park on the November ballot, with residents speaking for and against.

lafayette/8.title: 2027 budget, fees and pay plan
lafayette/8.summary: Staff introduced a $128 million 2027 recommended budget, and council held a public hearing, adopted the budget and mill levy, amended fees and adopted the pay plan.

lafayette/9.title: Capital bond projects and general obligation bonds
lafayette/9.summary: Council authorized general obligation bonds for the voter-approved recreation center, service center and civic center projects and toured capital projects including the water treatment plant and West Baseline Road safety improvements.
lafayette/9.where: Bob L. Burger Recreation Center, Service Center, West Baseline Rd

lafayette/10.title: Douglass Elementary School closure concerns
lafayette/10.summary: Council directed staff to draft a letter asking the Boulder Valley School District to reconsider its process on Douglass Elementary's future after Lafayette families said they had no voice.

lafayette/11.title: Human Rights Board renamed and rescoped
lafayette/11.summary: Council adopted an ordinance changing the name, scope and duties of the Human Rights Board.

lafayette/12.title: Expedited review for affordable housing
lafayette/12.summary: Council considered a resolution supporting an expedited review policy for affordable housing projects.

lafayette/13.title: Street racing on South Public Road
lafayette/13.summary: An Avalon Flatirons resident complained about street racers gathering in a church parking lot off South Public Road.

lake-city/0.title: Elk Fire emergency and local disaster declaration
lake-city/0.summary: Town Manager Alexander Mulhall declared a local disaster on August 7, 2026 due to the Elk Fire, and Council ratified it by Resolution 2026-10 on August 12. The town approved an emergency agreement with the USDA Forest Service for potable water and grey water disposal at $0.03 per gallon, and thanked Estes Park and Windsor for lending backup generators. Resolution 2026-13 to terminate the emergency was on the October 21 agenda.
lake-city/0.where: Elk Fire on the Lake City border, unincorporated Hinsdale County

lake-city/1.title: July 24 flash floods, debris flows and stormwater
lake-city/1.summary: Council discussed the July 24, 2026 flash floods and mud and debris flows, then followed up on cleanup and recovery on August 5. A resident raised concerns about loss of containment of stormwater, especially its depth and velocity.

lake-city/2.title: Phase 1 Hinsdale County/Lake City Comprehensive Housing Plan implementation
lake-city/2.summary: Six proposals were received for the Phase 1 housing plan work. Council accepted the implementation grant agreement and on August 19 selected Collegiate Peaks Law & Mediation, approving its service agreement September 2. By October the consultant selection was being revisited, and a notice of award to Western Spaces LLC was on the October 21 agenda.

lake-city/3.title: DOLA ADU grant and pre-approved accessory dwelling unit designs
lake-city/3.summary: Council discussed a DOLA accessory dwelling unit grant application, including a reduced match request and incentive funding. The October 21 agenda sought approval of a $107,000 application with a 13% match of $13,910 for pre-approved ADU designs.

lake-city/4.title: 2027 budget, water and sewer rates, and health insurance
lake-city/4.summary: Council reviewed the draft 2027 budget, 2027 water and sewer rates, capital improvement projects and available funds for donations. It also considered appointing Alexander Mulhall as budget officer and choosing between alternate health plans or keeping the current CEBT plan.

lake-city/5.title: Armory apartment rent and applicant criteria
lake-city/5.summary: Council discussed rent and applicant criteria for the apartment at the Armory on October 7 and again on October 21.

lake-city/6.title: Wastewater treatment plant renovation change order
lake-city/6.summary: Council considered Ridgway Valley Concrete Basin Electrical Change Order #3 for the WWTP renovation, in the amount of $23,331.11.

lake-city/7.title: Ordinances on 8th Street right-of-way lease and zoning standards
lake-city/7.summary: Council held public hearings on second reading of Ordinance 2026-10, leasing part of the 8th Street right-of-way, and Ordinance 2026-11, amending performance standards in the MHR, CBD and GBD zoning districts.
lake-city/7.where: 8th Street; MHR, CBD and GBD zoning districts

lake-city/8.title: Colorado Ride 2027 tent camping in Memorial Park
lake-city/8.summary: Summit Cycle Solutions asked to use Memorial Park for tent camping August 11-13, 2027, with about 70 participants. Council approved the request and then Resolution 2026-12 on October 7.

lake-city/9.title: International Dark Sky Community designation
lake-city/9.summary: Council discussed Dark Sky Community certification requirements and the designation application.

lake-city/10.title: Wildfire resiliency code and future grant funding
lake-city/10.summary: Council discussed CML and DOLA responses on adopting the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code and how it might affect future grant funding.

lake-city/11.title: Pickleball courts public engagement and 2026 audit RFP
lake-city/11.summary: Council discussed public engagement on pickleball courts for spring/summer 2027 and directed staff to draft a request for proposals for the 2026 audit.

lake-county/0.title: Lake County E911 Authority: dispatch restructuring, 2027 budget and PUC surcharge application
lake-county/0.summary: The E911 Authority spent August to October on reorganizing dispatch, a revised 2027 budget, and an application to the Colorado PUC for an increase in the emergency telephone charge (Resolution 26-01), citing the dispatch facility, NG911 GIS and radio recording needs. Resolution 26-02 would adopt the 2027 budget. The board also took up hiring standards and a CentralSquare software agreement that replaces the current Motorola/Flex contract.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Work Sessions

lake-county/1.title: Moratorium work session and Land Development Code rules for rural lodging and outdoor recreation
lake-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed draft rules for campgrounds, event sites and rural lodging that would replace the moratorium imposed by Resolution 2026-06, extended to October because of the Willow fire. Draft rules cover site selection, water, septic, parking, emergency plans and conditional use permits. Commissioners considered Resolution 2026-35 to amend the code on Oct 20.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/2.title: CMC student and workforce housing project near Leadville
lake-county/2.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on Colorado Mountain College's housing proposal on its existing campus, with 48 parking spaces and wildfire-resilience compliance. Staff said it is not subject to zoning review under state statute. Commissioners expressed support and a motion to approve was made.

lake-county/3.title: Leadville-Lake County fire rescue IGA and fire funding
lake-county/3.summary: The Fire Management Board reviewed a draft intergovernmental agreement between Leadville and Lake County on fire protection, covering two stations (816 Harrison Ave and 141 County Road 10), cost sharing and fallback funding, plus preliminary fire budget figures. The commissioners were set to consider the IGA on Oct 20 along with shared services with the City.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/4.title: Lake County 2027 budget and capital certificate of participation
lake-county/4.summary: Commissioners held many work sessions on the 2027 preliminary budget, including elected officials' presentations, department budgets, capital requests and a Certificate of Participation. The preliminary budget was to be acknowledged Oct 13.

lake-county/5.title: Affordable housing: Proposition 123 commitments and Regional Housing Authority
lake-county/5.summary: The Housing Authority gave its semi-annual report on its 2026-2028 strategic plan, housing pipeline and 2027 budget. Commissioners also considered a first amendment to the Prop 123 IGA covering the county's affordable housing commitments, including a 9 percent increase in affordable inventory and expedited review.
