lake-county/6.title: Willow Fire debrief and fire restrictions
lake-county/6.summary: Commissioners scheduled a Willow Fire debrief and lessons-learned session, and ratified rescinding all fire restrictions in unincorporated areas. The fire also delayed the moratorium timeline.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings
Board of County Commissioners Work Sessions

lake-county/7.title: Aurora water deliveries and storage IGA
lake-county/7.summary: Commissioners were to consider an amended and restated IGA with the City of Aurora on water deliveries and storage, led by the Water + Natural Resources Director.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/8.title: Highway safety and Gateway Mobility Plan
lake-county/8.summary: A work session covered transportation and safety issues on state highways and the Lake County Gateway Mobility Plan.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Work Sessions

lake-county/9.title: Animal shelter staffing, budget and IGA changes
lake-county/9.summary: The Animal Shelter Advisory Board discussed staffing, hours, budget, the 2027 budget, a possible Ark Valley partnership and changes to the shelter IGA.

lake-county/10.title: Onsite wastewater rules and public health items
lake-county/10.summary: The Board of Health took up the Public Health Improvement Plan, proposed amendments to onsite wastewater treatment system (OWTS) rules, the cottage food law and the local tobacco ordinance.

lake-county/11.title: Courthouse public-space rules and Planning Commission vacancies
lake-county/11.summary: Commissioners considered Resolution 2026-34 adopting courthouse rules on use of county property, noting that approvals at staff level create legal risk. They also considered appointing three new Planning Commission members after early resignations.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings
Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lake-county/12.title: Safety in Schools (PASS) MOU with Lake County School District
lake-county/12.summary: Commissioners considered an MOU with the school district's PASS team to review school climate data and meet grant requirements. It is a budgeted request.

sources.body: Board of County Commissioners Regular and Special Meetings

lakewood/0.title: Ballot Issue 2G: 0.5% sales tax increase for public safety
lakewood/0.summary: Council adopted Resolution R-2026-58 on Aug. 24 to put a one-half percent sales and use tax increase on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot as Ballot Issue 2G. Revenue would be dedicated to public safety and traffic safety improvements, including crime prevention and homelessness response. On Oct. 12 council considered a resolution supporting the measure.

lakewood/1.title: Automated license plate readers and proposed AVIS
lakewood/1.summary: Police briefed council on the 17 fixed Flock Safety license plate cameras in use, which were first funded by a federal JAG grant and are now paid from the police budget. Council was to consider whether more safeguards are needed and how the proposed Automated Vehicle Identification System relates to the existing cameras.

lakewood/2.title: Neighborhood traffic-calming and speed hump policy changes
lakewood/2.summary: Public Works proposed changes to the traffic-calming policy, including shortening speed hump spacing from 700 feet to about 400 feet, raising the volume threshold on local streets, and moving to an allocated budget instead of a fixed 25 humps a year. Staff are also planning speed cushions and crossings on Mississippi east of Pierce and on Harlan near Deane Elementary and Ray Ross Park, working with West Metro Fire District.
lakewood/2.where: Mississippi Ave. east of Pierce; Harlan St. near Deane Elementary

lakewood/3.title: Purchase of 1081 Vance Street for open space and park
lakewood/3.summary: Council considered an ordinance (O-2026-32) authorizing the city to buy 1081 Vance Street for municipal open space and park purposes. It was heard on first reading Sept. 28 and on second reading with public comment Oct. 12.

lakewood/4.title: Rezonings at 2555 S. Kipling St. and 7201 W. Mansfield
lakewood/4.summary: Council took up first reading of two rezoning ordinances, O-2026-33 for land at 2555 S. Kipling St. and O-2026-34 for land at 7201 W. Mansfield.
lakewood/4.where: 2555 S. Kipling St. and 7201 W. Mansfield

lakewood/5.title: Waste hauler licensing rewrite (Chapter 5.29)
lakewood/5.summary: Ordinance O-2026-30 would repeal and replace the city's hauler licensing chapter, adding definitions, an application review process, enforcement with hearings, and moving license fees into rules and regulations. Staff say it helps track recycling and compost tonnage toward the city's Zero Waste goal. It was on first reading Aug. 10 and second reading Aug. 24.

lakewood/6.title: 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption
lakewood/6.summary: Council considered an ordinance adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code with local amendments, on first reading Aug. 24 and second reading with public comment Sept. 28.

lakewood/7.title: Revised 2026 and proposed 2027 city and LRA budgets
lakewood/7.summary: Council held a Sept. 14 study session on the revised 2026 and proposed 2027 city budget. The Lakewood Reinvestment Authority also received its proposed 2027 budget, with approval sought Oct. 19. Council also approved 2027 budgets for the Alameda Corridor and West Colfax business improvement districts, and a $225,000 amendment to the 2026 budget was moved forward in August.

lakewood/8.title: Neighborhood Participation Program project funding
lakewood/8.summary: Staff asked council to approve recommended projects for the 2026 Neighborhood Participation Program, which funds small neighborhood-proposed projects such as playgrounds, public art and community gardens. 176 projects have been funded since the program began in 1992.

lakewood/9.title: Permanent police committee and city manager contract
lakewood/9.summary: Council amended its resolution on an ad-hoc committee working toward a permanent police committee and appointed a member to it on Sept. 28. A city manager contract was also on the Aug. 24 agenda.

lamar/0.title: Data center moratorium and community standards
lamar/0.summary: Council discussed data centers in September, including draft Community Benefit & Responsible Data Center Development Standards and interest from parties considering the Lamar area. On Oct. 12 residents voiced concerns, and council debated a proposed 24-month moratorium to give time to write regulations. The mayor said no nondisclosure agreements have been signed and no deals are in the works.

lamar/1.title: Possible SECPA purchase of Lamar Utility
lamar/1.summary: Council agreed to investigate an offer from SECPA to buy the Lamar Utility. A Utility Board member questioned the decision, and the mayor clarified that council is only investigating and lacks authority to sell a utility. Appointment to the Lamar Utility Board seat is on hold until outside counsel finishes a document and internal review.

lamar/2.title: Main Café Brownfield cleanup
lamar/2.summary: The city sought bids for EPA Brownfield grant cleanup of the Main Café site, holding a mandatory pre-bid walk-through in August. On Sept. 28 council awarded Bid 46-002 to Rockies Environmental for $483,299. A new assessment grant is also being set up.

lamar/3.title: Street repaving budget and 2026 paving list
lamar/3.summary: Annual asphalt paving was delayed by milling machine availability. Public Works said materials alone are estimated at $380,362 against a $400,000 budget, and urged a larger budget given rising asphalt costs. PMC will pay for materials to repave its parking lot, with the city providing in-kind work. The Willow Valley water line project is nearing completion, after which streets will be repaired.
lamar/3.where: Citywide, including Grant St. from Main to 6th and Willow Valley

lamar/4.title: 2027 budget preparation and revenue outlook
lamar/4.summary: The treasurer began budget work, with director meetings starting the week of Aug. 17 and a council work session on revenue projections on Aug. 24. Sales tax is up 5% year to date, and insurance renewals came in lower than feared. A federal funding application through Senator Bennett's office is still pending.

lamar/5.title: Tyler software rollout
lamar/5.summary: The city is moving finance and other functions to Tyler software, with sales tax, accounts receivable, court, parks and recreation, cemetery and utility billing modules still being finished. Project accounting went live Aug. 10.

lamar/6.title: Subdivision regulations amendment (Ordinance 1287) and Valco annexation
lamar/6.summary: Council approved on second reading Ordinance No. 1287 amending Chapter 22 Subdivisions of the municipal code. Planning and Zoning discussed an upcoming annexation of the Valco property.

lamar/7.title: Parks and recreation fields and facilities
lamar/7.summary: Residents and councilmembers raised concerns about the youth soccer field's grass and divots and the community building's worn carpet. Escondido Field was topsoiled, reseeded and treated for weeds and fungus. The city will look for grants for ADA-accessible playground equipment.
lamar/7.where: Escondido Field, youth soccer field, community building

lamar/8.title: Colorado State Patrol Taser donation
lamar/8.summary: Council accepted Taser X26P units and equipment donated by the Colorado State Patrol, worth about $50,000.

lamar/9.title: Ward I council vacancy filled
lamar/9.summary: Robert 'Bob' Seay was the only applicant for the Ward I vacancy. After an open-session interview and executive session, council appointed him to serve until November 2027.

limon/0.title: 2026 budget and property tax levy
limon/0.summary: Council held a November 18 budget workshop, then a December 10 public hearing and votes on the 2026 budget, the property tax levy and the appropriation ordinance (No. 648). A December 29 hearing covered a supplemental appropriation to the 2025 budget.

limon/1.title: Water and sewer projects report and recommendations
limon/1.summary: Council took up a GMS report and recommendations for water and sewer projects on April 2, with a follow-up report on the projects on August 6. The documents do not state the decisions.

limon/2.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption
limon/2.summary: Council held a public hearing on March 5 on Ordinance 649, which would adopt the 2025 edition of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. The ordinance appeared again on the April 2 agenda.

limon/3.title: Municipal code changes on vehicles, licenses and penalties
limon/3.summary: Council considered ordinances to enforce state vehicle rules (No. 650), require a valid license or permit while driving (No. 651) and amend municipal penalties (No. 652).

limon/4.title: E-bike regulation (Ordinance 646)
limon/4.summary: Council had Ordinance 646 on e-bike regulation on its November 6 agenda. The agenda does not say what the rules are.

limon/5.title: Irrigation water rights ordinance (Ordinance 647)
limon/5.summary: Council considered Ordinance 647 on irrigation water rights at its November 6 meeting.

limon/6.title: Affordable housing project review policies
limon/6.summary: On June 4 council considered Resolution 26-06-12, which would establish review policies for affordable housing projects. A Housing Authority board appointment followed on August 6.

limon/7.title: Limon Municipal Airport and transfer of entitlements
limon/7.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-04-07 on April 2 to transfer airport entitlements to Archuleta County. An airport presentation was scheduled for August 6.

limon/8.title: Street chip sealing and Limon Events contract
limon/8.summary: On May 7 council considered a proposal from A-1 Chipseal to chip seal designated streets. On July 2 it took up a contract with Big Sandy Builders for work at Limon Events.

limon/9.title: Tamarack Golf Club user rates
limon/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 26-03-06 on March 5, which would set user rates for the Tamarack Golf Club.

littleton/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center applications
littleton/0.summary: On Oct. 20, 2026 council took up Ordinance 22-2026 on first reading. It would pause acceptance, processing and approval of data center applications and direct staff to study and recommend land use regulations for them.

littleton/1.title: Geneva Village site redevelopment options
littleton/1.summary: Council discussed process options and advisory services for redeveloping the Geneva Village site on Aug. 11, 2026. The documents do not state a decision.

littleton/2.title: Utility rate study and South Platte Renew governance
littleton/2.summary: Council reviewed Part 2 of the utility rate study results. It also looked at governance model options for South Platte Renew, the shared wastewater plant with Englewood, using earlier FCS Group analyses.

littleton/3.title: Economic partnership incentives for RIG Mineral and Scheels
littleton/3.summary: Council considered an updated Economic Partnership Incentives Policy (Resolution 61-2026). It also took up an amendment to the RIG Mineral LLC sales tax share-back agreement and a new incentive agreement involving RIG Mineral and Scheels.

littleton/4.title: Lower speed limit to 25 mph and Safer Streets
littleton/4.summary: Ordinance 17-2026 would set a maximum lawful speed limit of 25 mph. It had first reading Aug. 18 and second reading on Sept. 1 agenda. Council also got a Safer Streets update on Sept. 8.

littleton/5.title: E-bike and e-motor safety ordinance
littleton/5.summary: Council discussed a draft ordinance on e-bike and e-motor safety on Aug. 25, 2026.

littleton/6.title: Hauler licensing and waste diversion ordinance
littleton/6.summary: Council discussed trash hauler licensing and an Equal Space Ordinance on Aug. 18. Ordinance 19-2026 amending Title 3 was on the Oct. 20 agenda, with waste diversion plan documents attached. A subaward with Circular Action Alliance was also on the Sept. 15 agenda.

littleton/7.title: Main Street investment and 2450 W Main sign variances
littleton/7.summary: Council heard a Main Street investment strategy on Sept. 22. The Appeals & Adjustment Commission considered seven sign variances for 2450 W Main Street, including a marquee projecting 6 ft, height of 30 ft, and exposed bulb lighting. The Historical Preservation Commission also reviewed a restaurant façade remodel at 2589 W Main Street.

littleton/8.title: Transportation Master Plan update and Elati Street corridor
littleton/8.summary: Council reviewed an Elati Street Corridor Study update on Sept. 1. On Oct. 20 it considered a professional services agreement for the Transportation Master Plan update (Resolution 78-2026). Contracts for the 2026 mill and overlay and surface sealing projects were also on the Aug. 18 agenda.

littleton/9.title: Land use code update and planning study topics
littleton/9.summary: Planning Commission reviewed transition standards and previewed the Unified Land Use Code update. It and council discussed joint study session priorities in September and October.

littleton/10.title: High Line Canal storm sewer license agreements
littleton/10.summary: Council considered license agreements with the Arapahoe-area canal owner and Denver Water to build and maintain storm sewer crossing the High Line Canal at West Fremont Avenue.
littleton/10.where: West Fremont Avenue at High Line Canal

logan-county/0.title: Rural Health Transformation grant and ambulance funding for Logan County Ambulance
logan-county/0.summary: Sterling Fire and county EMS leaders discussed applying for the Rural Health Transfer/Transformation grant (deadline Aug. 3) to fund whole blood, a community paramedic program and interfacility transports. They also looked at replacing ambulances (a $337,000 quote) using a CDPHE grant with a 10% match waiver. By Sept. 29 they reported the group was approved for something under the grant.

logan-county/1.title: CR 26 bridge closure and county bridge grants
logan-county/1.summary: The Board weighed applying for a bridge planning and engineering grant for the CR 26 bridge, but decided not to pursue it and not to close the bridge for a multi-year project. They planned a public meeting, and a public hearing on a bridge closure near CR 26 and CR 29 was set on the Oct. 20 agenda.

logan-county/2.title: Sterling sales tax increase for road repair
logan-county/2.summary: A City of Sterling representative briefed commissioners on a ballot question raising the city sales tax from 3% to 4% for five years, dedicated to road maintenance. A similar measure failed last year. The county attorney will draft a resolution, since the Board can encourage but not spend public money on the vote.

logan-county/3.title: Summit Carbon Solutions pipeline and carbon sequestration resolution
logan-county/3.summary: Summit Carbon Solutions told the Board it is in early stages, with surveys starting and construction not expected until mid- to late-period, and hopes to use voluntary landowner agreements. The county has just adopted new pipeline fees and setbacks, and a revised carbon sequestration resolution 2026-32 came up Oct. 6.

logan-county/4.title: Fire suppression water tank at CR 70 and CR 11
logan-county/4.summary: Centennial Soil Conservation District won a $30,000 state resiliency grant to bury a 10,000-gallon fire water tank in the northwest corner of the county, where tender hauls are long. The Board agreed to maintain the road, including snow removal, and help as possible.

logan-county/5.title: DOLA grants and county/Sterling comprehensive plan update
logan-county/5.summary: DOLA's regional manager said state grant money is tight but CDBG and REDI funds remain, and a possible $50,000 housing planning award for a joint Sterling and county comprehensive plan would require a county match. The county plan dates to 2013 or earlier and predates data centers and battery storage.

logan-county/6.title: Battery storage facility and wind project road use
logan-county/6.summary: Commissioners toured a battery energy storage facility and noted its setbacks and fire suppression, and it has operated three years without incident. Niyol Wind sought a road use agreement to replace blades on two turbines, including temporarily removing signs at CR 67 and CR 24.

logan-county/7.title: Fairgrounds master plan, electrical upgrades and Fair Board decisions
logan-county/7.summary: The fairgrounds manager sought direction on capital spending for the master plan for the 2027 budget. Pending items include a Public Service Co. easement for new transformers, a bid for relocating electrical service, and Fair Board debates on ticket prices, contracts and sponsorship.

logan-county/8.title: Permit Gateway for oversize/overweight transport permits
logan-county/8.summary: Road and Bridge staff proposed Permit Gateway, a free-to-county online system with carrier-paid fees, to automate oversize and overweight permits and route trucks around restricted bridges. The Board indicated support for moving forward.

logan-county/9.title: Fiber internet expansion: Viaero and Vistabeam
logan-county/9.summary: Viaero is installing fiber along Highway 14 to its Sterling store and discussed serving city buildings. The Oct. 20 agenda includes a right-of-way permit for Vistabeam fiber under CR 31.5.

logan-county/10.title: Railroad crossing closure near Peetz at Highway 138
logan-county/10.summary: The Board planned to meet the railroad about closing a crossing at Highway 138 near Peetz; the railroad is also considering closing two crossings in Nebraska.

logan-county/11.title: County employee health insurance rates
logan-county/11.summary: The County Health Pool rates fell after the county dropped a band, and dental moved to Ameritas with rates unchanged. Employees asked for separate tiers and a bigger family discount, and a stipend for older employees was discussed.

lone-tree/0.title: Hillcamp development: roadway plat and water booster pump station
lone-tree/0.summary: The Planning Commission is holding public hearings on Oct. 13 for infrastructure serving the Hillcamp development: the Hillcamp Trail Filing No. 1 final plat and a water booster pump station (use by special review and site improvement plan). The remaining Hillcamp applications are still under review and will get hearings later.

lone-tree/1.title: Brick Wall project: construction management contract
lone-tree/1.summary: Council is considering a professional services agreement with Alfred Benesch & Company for construction management of the Brick Wall project. Council also had a Brick Wall update and communications plan on the study session agenda.

lone-tree/2.title: Douglas County School District mill levy override and Ballot Issue 5A
lone-tree/2.summary: Council discussed the school district's mill levy override and was set to vote on Resolution 26-46 supporting a yes vote on the district's 2026 Ballot Issue 5A.

lone-tree/3.title: Off-highway and low-speed electric vehicle rules
lone-tree/3.summary: Council holds a public hearing and second reading of Ordinance 26-08, amending municipal code Chapter 8 to regulate off-highway vehicles and low-speed electric vehicles.

lone-tree/4.title: City Admin building renovation contract
lone-tree/4.summary: Council is considering awarding a general contracting services contract for the City Admin renovation project.

lone-tree/5.title: Proposition 123 implementation
lone-tree/5.summary: Council is considering Resolution 26-43 on how the city will implement Proposition 123, the state affordable housing program.

lone-tree/6.title: Happy Canyon Trail connection land deed
lone-tree/6.summary: Council is considering Resolution 26-45 accepting a special warranty deed from Schweiger Ranch Foundation for the Happy Canyon Trail Connection project.

lone-tree/7.title: High Note Park costs and capital projects
lone-tree/7.summary: Council reviewed the High Note Park guaranteed maximum price and wrap-up of new facilities, plus a public works capital project update. A five-year capital projects plan is also on the Oct. 5 strategy session agenda.

lone-tree/8.title: Parks, Open Space and Trails Master Plan and Entertainment District Park
lone-tree/8.summary: The Recreation Advisory Committee is working on the Parks, Open Space, and Trails Master Plan, and discussed the Entertainment District Park and the South Suburban strategic plan.

lone-tree/9.title: Staffing, compensation and police department planning
lone-tree/9.summary: The Oct. 5 strategy session covered compensation, a five-year staffing plan, the police department and community development.

lone-tree/10.title: Unified Development Code overview
lone-tree/10.summary: Council will hold a preliminary discussion of the city's Unified Development Code at an Oct. 26 strategy session.

lone-tree/11.title: Snow removal agreement with Douglas County
lone-tree/11.summary: Council is considering Resolution 26-42, an intergovernmental agreement with Douglas County for 2026-2027 snow removal on certain city streets.

lone-tree/12.title: Civic Center security deposit fee
lone-tree/12.summary: Resolution 26-41 would amend the fee schedule to add a Civic Center security deposit.

longmont/0.title: 1st and Main urban renewal plan, transit center and parking garage financing
longmont/0.summary: Council took up the 1st and Main Urban Renewal Plan, a blight finding, lease-purchase financing for a parking garage, and a development agreement with Main Street Tebo, LLC for the transit center and a transit-oriented project. The Urban Renewal Authority approved tax increment agreements with the city, Boulder County, Northern Water, the St. Vrain Valley School District and the Downtown Development Authority.
longmont/0.where: 1st Avenue and Main Street, downtown Longmont

sources.body: City Council Joint Meeting with Boulder County Commissioners

longmont/1.title: November 2026 ballot: public safety tax increase
longmont/1.summary: Council considered ballot language for increases in sales and use tax and property tax (up to 4.06, 3.25 and 2.44 mills in the optional ordinances) to fund police, dispatch, fire and emergency services. Council also drafted a resolution urging a yes vote and called the special election.

longmont/2.title: Charter amendments on the November ballot: open space sales and ranked choice voting
longmont/2.summary: Council referred charter amendments to the November 3 ballot requiring voter approval to sell or convey open space, plus ranked choice voting and changes on how mayor and councilmembers are elected. A resolution urging a yes vote on the open space question was also on the agenda.

longmont/3.title: 2027 proposed budget and capital improvement program
longmont/3.summary: Council received the 2027 proposed budget and 2027-2031 capital improvement program, held two public hearings, and set tax levies for the 2027 fiscal year. Final council direction was scheduled for October 6.

longmont/4.title: Dry Creek, 8513 St. Vrain Road and other annexations
longmont/4.summary: Council moved annexations forward, including Dry Creek along Airport Road and Clover Basin Drive (zoned Residential Mixed Neighborhood) and 8513 St. Vrain Road east of Airport Road. It also took up Longmont Gateway Northwest at Highway 287 and Park Ridge Avenue. A neighborhood meeting covered a proposed annexation of the church property at 8979 Nelson Road.
longmont/4.where: Airport Road, Clover Basin Drive, St. Vrain Road, Highway 287 and Park Ridge Avenue

longmont/5.title: Airport future and noise monitoring
longmont/5.summary: Council held an Airport Vision Session on governance, trust-building with the community and facilities, and heard options for an Airport Monitoring System. Council members said the airport's future is under discussion.

longmont/6.title: Composting subsidy and sanitation rate structure
longmont/6.summary: Council discussed a possible subsidy for composting services and aligning waste rates with policy goals. The Sustainability Advisory Board was asked for feedback on the sanitation rate structure.

longmont/7.title: Water exchange with St. Vrain and Left Hand Water Conservancy District, and drought
longmont/7.summary: The Water Board considered a one-year exchange of 148.8 acre-feet of Colorado-Big Thompson water so the district could cover its depletions. The district's supply could run out by 2028 if drought continues, and the exchange would let the city keep more storage in Ralph Price Reservoir. The board also reviewed Ralph Price Reservoir water rights and Dry Creek Fire impacts near Button Rock.

longmont/8.title: Affordable housing fee-in-lieu, tax review and Longmont Housing Authority actions
longmont/8.summary: Council took up the 2027 inclusionary housing fee-in-lieu adjustment and an expedited review process for affordable housing. The Housing Authority took up revenue bonds, private activity bond allocation, the Briarwood Apartments, its 2027 budget, and voucher plans. The countywide Affordable-Attainable Housing Tax was under a two-year review.

sources.body: Longmont Housing Authority Board of Commissioners Meeting
City Council Joint Meeting with Boulder County Commissioners
Longmont Housing Authority Board of Commissioners
Housing and Human Service Advisory Board

longmont/9.title: Extraterritorial water service for Hygiene Fire Protection District
longmont/9.summary: Council considered ordinances directing staff to process requests for a larger tap and an additional extraterritorial water service for the Hygiene Fire Protection District's fire house and fire suppression system. The Water Board was to make a recommendation.
longmont/9.where: Hygiene Fire Protection District fire house

longmont/10.title: Human services funding hearings and tier system
longmont/10.summary: The Housing and Human Services Advisory Board set a two-tier scoring system (3.25 per question for funding consideration). It then held agency hearings through September and October on funding requests.

longmont/11.title: Contractor's shops in MU-E zoning (citizen-initiated code change)
longmont/11.summary: A citizen-initiated request would allow Contractor's Shops as a permitted use in the MU-E zone. Staff recommended approval with conditions, and the Planning and Zoning Commission could continue the hearing to November 18.

longmont/12.title: Platte River Power Authority energy mix
longmont/12.summary: Platte River Power Authority briefed council and the Sustainability Advisory Board on its noncarbon goals. 100% noncarbon by 2030 is not possible, in part because a federal emergency order kept Craig Unit 1 running. Its resource plan is expected in January 2028.

longmont/13.title: Show cause hearing for liquor license at 333 Main Street
longmont/13.summary: The Local Licensing Authority scheduled a show cause hearing on a license over alleged disturbances, noise and open container violations. The first date was continued.

sources.body: Local Licensing Authority- CONTINUED TO DATE TBD

longmont/14.title: Avis car rental at 206 S. Main Street
longmont/14.summary: Avis proposed renting cars from the rear of the structure and storing vehicles in the back lot, which needs conditional use approval and City Council review because of the adjacent greenway.

louisville/0.title: Delo Boom mixed-use development at 1390 Cannon Street
louisville/0.summary: The Planning Commission took up Resolution 10 recommending approval of a final PUD, plat and special review use for a 135-unit mixed-use project (36 townhomes, 99 apartments, small commercial) on about 4.4 acres. The city's Community Development Director wrote in support, while a Delo resident argued the plan has about 161 on-site parking spaces against roughly 270 needed and asked where extra cars would park.

louisville/1.title: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance update (Ordinance 1936)
louisville/1.summary: Council moved an amendment to Title 17 on inclusionary housing from first reading (July 28) to second reading and public hearing on Aug 18, with a further public hearing on Sept 15. Strong Towns Louisville urged zoning reform first, by-right incentives and exemptions for small 10-12 unit projects, while another resident worried new market-rate units could raise prices.

louisville/2.title: Centennial Valley General Development Plan amendment, helipad and Redtail Ridge hospital
louisville/2.summary: Council considered a PUD with a helicopter pad for an Advent/Avista hospital and the Centennial Valley GDP amendment for residential development and parks (Ordinance 1935). A resident questioned the GDP's treatment of LEED requirements and solar obligations, and another commenter said the parks and open space are inadequate for a development that would grow the city's housing by about 12%. The Open Space board unanimously approved a resolution supporting a trail.

louisville/3.title: 2027-2028 budget, capital plan and deficit
louisville/3.summary: Staff reported an operating deficit, a General Fund gap and a Capital Fund gap. The City Manager's initial budget came Sept 1 and final budget public hearing Oct 20, with adoption expected at a later meeting, likely in early November. Council cut some items, such as the Community Event Sponsorship Program, and pulled the $780,000 northeast water loop from the budget.

louisville/4.title: Golf and recreation fee increases for 2027
louisville/4.summary: Advisory boards modeled golf green-fee increases because fees alone cannot cover projected deficits. The Recreation Advisory Board approved golf recommendations for Council and backed 3% and 7% increases to rec and senior center admission fees for residents and non-residents.
louisville/4.where: Coal Creek Golf Course and Recreation/Senior Center

louisville/5.title: Sustainability funding, bag tax and joint Council-LSAB meeting
louisville/5.summary: The Sustainability Advisory Board presented to Council on Aug 11 with ideas such as a dedicated sustainability tax, extending the bag tax, a climate impact fee on development and franchise renegotiation, plus water conservation data. Residents wrote in about urban heat, bag tax transparency, and electrification grants. Later LSAB approved electrification rebate reallocation and a resident urged emissions-focused budgeting.

louisville/6.title: PROS plan and Trails System Plan, open space concerns
louisville/6.summary: The draft Parks, Recreation and Open Space guidebook and Trails Plan went to the Open Space board and Council, with a resident group arguing it conflicts with the City Charter on open space, urging removal of Trail 18 and reconsidered land classifications. Residents also raised prairie dogs and bocce court upkeep, and the city purchased 101 Cherry St. and is buying the Gateway Open Space property.

louisville/7.title: Comprehensive Plan and Development Code update
louisville/7.summary: Planning Commission reviewed the draft Comprehensive Plan including growth projections and place types. Residents raised concerns on population growth, traffic, water, evacuation routes and wildfire risk. Council accepted DOLA grant funds and approved an agreement for the Development Code update.

louisville/8.title: Fire Smart Louisville and wildfire mitigation funding
louisville/8.summary: Staff proposed funding Fire Smart Louisville, a volunteer neighborhood wildfire-risk program with Boulder Watershed Collective, including a $10,000 NFPA grant and Wildfire Partners rebates. Council later put a $100,000 agreement with the Boulder Watershed Collective for wildfire work on its Oct 20 consent agenda.

louisville/9.title: Business assistance agreements and Revitalization Commission grants
louisville/9.summary: Council considered a $208,400 incentive for Arsenal Health and an enhanced $281,114 agreement with Infleqtion Quantum, plus an amendment for Louisville Cyclery. The Revitalization Commission weighed reallocating $344,400 of unspent property improvement funds, Grain Yard facade and property grants, and a TIF agreement for the Grain Elevator at 540 County Road. Concerns were noted about Front Street construction effects.

louisville/10.title: Property purchases at Empire Road and Pine Street
louisville/10.summary: Council considered a contract to buy 1501 Empire Road and the east part of 1303 Empire Road, zoned Industrial, with a subdivision not changing zoning. It also took up an ordinance extending the lease and purchase contract for 1155 Pine Street, and met in executive session on property acquisition.
louisville/10.where: 1501 Empire Road, 1303 Empire Road, 1155 Pine Street

louisville/11.title: Centennial Drive affordable senior housing and affordable housing policies
louisville/11.summary: Council reviewed a concept plan for affordable senior housing on Centennial Drive. It also considered expedited review for affordable housing projects, a state affordable housing commitment, and the Trestle Strategy housing framework, and private activity bond/multifamily housing bond actions.

louisville/12.title: Historic landmark designations and preservation grants
louisville/12.summary: Council and commission handled landmark designations and grants including the Caranci House at 1101 Main, James House at 700 Pine, Giorzelli House, Mudrock House at 613 Grant (up to $15,000), and a request to landmark the Methodist Church at 741 Jefferson. A Historic Preservation Tax measure was placed on the 2026 election.
louisville/12.where: 1101 Main St, 700 Pine St, 613 Grant Ave, 741 Jefferson Ave

louisville/13.title: Honeysuckle Lane lot consolidation (Centennial 8 Replat B)
louisville/13.summary: Council considered a replat combining lots at 1006 Honeysuckle Lane. Staff said zoning would still allow one single-family home plus an ADU, and noted a similar 2023 consolidation in the Enclave subdivision.

louisville/14.title: Utility policy and rate changes: sewer backups and refuse fees
louisville/14.summary: Council considered a policy for reimbursing cleanup after sewer backups or meter failures, prompted by a November 2025 backup affecting a business, and new refuse, recycling and compost fees. A revised 2027 utility rate presentation was postponed to a future meeting.

lyons/0.title: Planet Bluegrass annexation and PUD zoning at 19617 and 19661 N St. Vrain Dr
lyons/0.summary: Planet Bluegrass asks to annex 19617 N. St. Vrain Dr. and zone it and the adjacent 19661 parcel as a PUD (Ordinances 1225 and 1226). First reading began Aug. 3 and was continued, with a further continuation to Dec. 7 requested. Town boards and commissions (Utilities & Engineering, Sustainable Futures, Economic Vitality, Parks and Recreation, Ecology) reviewed it, raising stormwater, utilities, parking, traffic, a past hazmat cleanup and a new fire hydrant and sidewalk. Parks and Recreation notes community members' concerns.
lyons/0.where: 19617 and 19661 N. St. Vrain Dr. (Eagle Canyon)

lyons/1.title: 2nd & 3rd Avenue stormwater project, bond vote and Safe Routes to School
lyons/1.summary: The $3.8M 2nd and 3rd Avenue stormwater and sidewalk project lost its FEMA BRIC grant. The town plans a 20-year loan of about $268K/year, offset by $259K/year from the voter-approved half-percent sales tax, and bond lawyers say a ballot vote is needed. The Board of Trustees went ahead with the Safe Routes to School sidewalk grant, but stormwater funding is not secured.

lyons/2.title: Time-of-use electric rates and a proposed electric rate increase
lyons/2.summary: Lyons is moving to time-of-use electric tiers. Business owners on the Economic Vitality Commission said they were not consulted, citing evening businesses like Main Stage. Southwest Power Pool raised transmission rates 50%, and the utility board's analysis projects a 9% shortfall that rates would need to cover in 2027. A meter-collar policy for solar customers and the nameplate billing issue are also under discussion. TOU rate changes are anticipated in March.

lyons/3.title: Wildfire mitigation, roof permits and fire code
lyons/3.summary: Trustees discussed wildfire mitigation strategies, a mid-roof inspection and roof permit fee (Resolution 2026-45), and a town hall on fire risk in September. The town now operates under the state fire code, requiring fire-resistant roofing, and about 8 permits were issued after a hailstorm. A wildfire mitigation ordinance is being drafted by the town planner.

lyons/4.title: 2027 budget, supplemental 2026 items and resident survey
lyons/4.summary: Staff and boards are preparing the 2027 budget. Trustees held budget workshops on Sept. 8 with a public input survey and a 5-year capital plan, and boards submitted requests, with a final budget expected in late October. Priorities cited include wastewater, stormwater and sidewalks.

lyons/5.title: Wastewater treatment facility upgrade
lyons/5.summary: The town has a separate $5.8M wastewater plant need with about $2.5M saved and a $1.7M federal grant pending a January decision. Trustees saw a 60% design update on Sept. 21, and the utility board reviewed proposed process changes awaiting CDPHE approval.

lyons/6.title: Strategic growth and water supply element of the comprehensive plan (SB24-174)
lyons/6.summary: The town is drafting a state-required strategic growth and water supply addendum to the comp plan. Staff say the water supply has ample margin, and the regional housing needs figure recommends preparing for 87 more housing units, which is not mandatory. Several boards reviewed it before Trustee review.

lyons/7.title: Sundance Film Festival housing ordinance and task force
lyons/7.summary: Trustees adopted Ordinance 1222 on June 29 creating a Special Event Lodging License (SELL) for festival housing, requiring $1M liability insurance. The task force shifted toward private events and curated experiences, discussed transitioning under a nonprofit such as the Chamber, and was told to find $5,000 for beautification.

lyons/8.title: Special event and park use fee waivers
lyons/8.summary: The Parks and Recreation Commission recommended eligibility rules for special event fee waivers, and trustees took up the policy Aug. 17. The Economic Vitality and Historic Preservation commissions weighed in on local versus non-local entities.

lyons/9.title: 402 Main Street water rights cash-in-lieu and Roots to Revival redevelopment
lyons/9.summary: Roots to Revival asked to dedicate 1.4 Lake McIntosh shares plus cash in lieu for water at 402 Main Street, estimated at about $16.8K for the shares. Trustees ratified it by Resolution 2026-62 on the Oct. 19 agenda. The Urban Renewal Authority also tracks its redevelopment agreement.

lyons/10.title: Moss Rock hotel at 343-347 Main Street
lyons/10.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority reviewed updates and a third amendment to the redevelopment agreement with Moss Rock for the Main Street hotel.

lyons/11.title: LED streetlight upgrade contract
lyons/11.summary: Bids came in at $154K, far above estimates, largely due to CDOT traffic control on Main Street. Excluding Main Street lights the bid drops to $77.5K, in line with budget. Trustees considered awarding the contract to N-Line Electric (Resolution 2026-53). Dark Skies certification was also discussed.

lyons/12.title: Flagstone box culvert repairs
lyons/12.summary: Staff presented the flagstone culvert investigation and planned repairs, supported by an approximately $482,000 DOLA grant, near 4th and 5th Streets, and asked the Historic Preservation Commission for feedback. Trustees consider an engineering contract amendment.

lyons/13.title: Automated license plate readers
lyons/13.summary: Trustees discussed an automated license plate reader program, with a Flock Safety agreement among the materials.

lyons/14.title: Vacant to Vibrant downtown incentive program
lyons/14.summary: The Economic Vitality Commission is designing rebates for businesses filling vacant downtown spaces, floating up to 75% for projects under $5,000. Nothing is approved.

manzanola/0.title: 112 S. Canal brownfield cleanup and demolition
manzanola/0.summary: CDPHE awarded a Targeted Brownfields Assessment for 112 S. Canal, and the town later applied for grants. By spring 2026 the demolition was out for bid, and Earth Services & Abatement was named contractor, with the grant contract still to be awarded.

manzanola/1.title: Water plant storage study, Well #2 testing and water system mapping
manzanola/1.summary: Engineers GMS (Tom McClernan) have been working on a water plant storage study, which moved to a PER with flow and chemical tests on Well #2. The town is also considering a $15/month Diamond Maps system from Colorado Rural Water to map valves, meters and hydrants. A report noted 84% water loss in April 2026.

manzanola/2.title: MMOF/CDOT sidewalk grant of $474,041
manzanola/2.summary: The town received a $474,041 CDOT MMOF grant for sidewalks. The contract is budgeted for Colorado's 2029 budget year, and a related council resolution was held until the grant amount was known.

manzanola/3.title: Southeastern Water Conservancy District Conduit vault at water plant
manzanola/3.summary: The council asked Congress for support of the Conduit and heard from SECWCD's Hunter Willits on placing a conduit vault at the water plant, for Valley water. It remained on agendas through October 2026.

manzanola/4.title: Drought water restrictions and project water release
manzanola/4.summary: The council took up Resolution 2026-02 on drought water restrictions in April 2026. In July it discussed a 100 acre-foot project water release on 6/30/2026.

manzanola/5.title: Second Street repair and chip seal
manzanola/5.summary: Otero County was to repair Second Street for about $1,000 in mid-2026. A chip and seal of the street is planned for 2027 at about $10,000.

manzanola/6.title: Solar tax credit refund
manzanola/6.summary: The IRS sent a November 3 letter saying a tax credit refund is coming on the town's solar project.

manzanola/7.title: Federal procurement and grant compliance policies
manzanola/7.summary: In March 2026 the council took up a package of procurement policies, including 2 CFR 200 compliance and requirements for federally funded projects.

manzanola/8.title: Budget approval and insurance renewal
manzanola/8.summary: The council approved the budget and its resolutions in December 2025. It also considered the Gallagher insurance renewal at $36,216.

manzanola/9.title: Weed and tree removal ordinance, senior housing parking lot, and surplus vehicles
manzanola/9.summary: The council considered Ordinance 2026-05 on emergent weed and tree removal. It also discussed paving the Park Street Senior Housing parking lot and whether to sell or scrap a 2012 Dodge police car and a jetter truck.
manzanola/9.where: Park Street Senior Housing and Townwide

manzanola/10.title: Charter franchise agreement
manzanola/10.summary: A Charter franchise agreement was on the February 2026 agenda.

mead/0.title: Twelve-month moratorium on data centers
mead/0.summary: The Town Board adopted a twelve-month moratorium on data centers at its August 31 meeting, per the October 12 staff report. The Community Development Director told the Planning Commission the town has not yet received any data center proposals.

mead/1.title: New Mead Police Facility: site plan, DOLA grant and financing
mead/1.summary: The town is building a new police facility in the Liberty Ranch subdivision on Chaparral Street. The Board is approving the site plan (Ordinance 1118) and easement vacations (Ordinance 1119), and a groundbreaking ceremony was scheduled. The Urban Renewal Authority heard a DOLA grant presentation, a financing briefing from Piper Sandler on interest rates and schedule, and a cooperation agreement with the Town for construction.

mead/2.title: 2027 town budget
mead/2.summary: The 2027 proposed budget was presented September 28. A public hearing and adoption (Resolution 71-R-2026) were scheduled for October 26, with a budget amendment to the Municipal Facilities Impact Fee Fund. The town's two general improvement districts also held 2027 budget presentations and hearings with mill levies.

mead/3.title: Mead Urban Renewal Authority tax-increment incentive policy
mead/3.summary: Contract counsel presented a policy for evaluating developer requests for tax-increment reimbursement of public improvements. It sets eligibility thresholds, three evaluation criteria and a small-project track, and keeps the Board's discretion. A resolution approving the policy (03-URA-2026) was on the October 26 agenda.

mead/4.title: Waterfront Filing No. 2 preliminary plat
mead/4.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on a proposed mixed-use development and recommended conditional approval. Commissioners focused on traffic capacity, road improvements and trail connections. They also called for broader coordination of transportation improvements across nearby developments.

mead/5.title: Ariet's Grove Filing No. 1 preliminary plat
mead/5.summary: The Planning Commission considered conditional approval of the preliminary plat on October 21. The Board of Trustees held a public hearing on it on October 26 (Resolution 69-PC-2026).

mead/6.title: Public Facilities zoning for town-owned land, Valdez and 1785 WCR 32 annexations
mead/6.summary: The Planning Commission recommended Public Facilities initial zoning for the town-owned Valdez annexation and for the 1785 Weld County Road 32 annexation. A zoning map amendment (Ordinance 1121) putting Public Facilities zoning on certain town-owned properties went to the Board October 26.
mead/6.where: Valdez property and 1785 Weld County Road 32

mead/7.title: I-25 sewer relocation project
mead/7.summary: The Board awarded a construction bid to SMH West LLC for the I-25 Sewer Relocation Project (Project 2026-011). It then took up a common use agreement and easement amendment with the Colorado Department of Transportation for the sanitary sewer relocation.

mead/8.title: High Plains Boulevard road completion
mead/8.summary: Construction of two miles of High Plains Blvd between WCR 32 and WCR 36 is almost complete. It includes two travel lanes, bike lanes, roundabouts at CR 32 and CR 34, and a detached sidewalk. A celebration with the High Plains Boulevard Coalition and developers was scheduled.
mead/8.where: High Plains Blvd (WCR 9.5), WCR 32 to WCR 36

mead/9.title: Safe Routes to School construction contract
mead/9.summary: The Board awarded a bid and construction agreement to Colorado Paving Inc. for the Mead Safe Routes to School Project.

mead/10.title: New Mead Library conditional acceptance
mead/10.summary: The Board considered conditional acceptance of public improvements for the High Plains Library District's Mead Library. A community event to welcome the new library was planned for October 3.

meeker/0.title: Circle Park water rights discussion
meeker/0.summary: The Council's October 6 agenda includes a discussion of water rights for Circle Park, along with a final water report from Micheal Erion. The documents give no details on the outcome.

meeker/1.title: Draft Town of Meeker 2026 budget
meeker/1.summary: The Council is scheduled to see a presentation of the draft 2026 town budget on October 6. A presentation from Pioneers Medical Center is also on the same agenda.

meeker/2.title: Short-term rental conditional use permit at Chase Rule's property
meeker/2.summary: The Council held a public hearing on February 23 on a conditional use permit for Chase Rule to run a short-term rental. The street address is cut off in the agenda.

meeker/3.title: Setback variance requests (891 3rd Street, 325 Curtis Creek Drive, 390 Market Street)
meeker/3.summary: The Council heard variance requests to reduce setbacks. Theodore and Jana Dawson asked for a side yard setback of about 6 feet at 891 3rd Street. Renninger Investments asked for a 0-foot front yard setback at 325 Curtis Creek Drive. Training Grounds, LLC asked for a reduced side yard setback at 390 Market Street.
meeker/3.where: 891 3rd Street; 325 Curtis Creek Drive; 390 Market Street

meeker/4.title: Sign and fence variances (43904 Highway 13 and 172 Water Street)
meeker/4.summary: On August 3 the Council took up two variance requests. David Bradfield asked to put up a sign larger than the maximum at 43904 Highway 13. Jessica and Matt Franks asked to build an eight-foot fence at 172 Water Street.

meeker/5.title: Home occupation and right-of-way encroachment requests
meeker/5.summary: On July 13 the Council considered a home occupation conditional use for Tevin Pelloni at 440 Garfield Street. It also considered an encroachment request from Rebekah and Justin Grant to access the town's right-of-way in Sanderson Hills Subdivision.

mesa-county/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center applications in unincorporated Mesa County
mesa-county/0.summary: On Sept. 29 the commissioners were to consider a temporary moratorium on accepting, processing and approving land use applications for data center facilities in unincorporated Mesa County. It would also suspend negotiation of county inducements for such facilities. The documents do not state the outcome.

mesa-county/1.title: 32 1/2 Road Phase II roadway improvement project
mesa-county/1.summary: The county is moving ahead on the 32 1/2 Road Phase II project. Items include a $4,606,193.95 construction contract with Mountain Valley Contracting, an MOU with Clifton Water District, a regional stormwater detention facility agreement with Housing Resources of Western Colorado that supersedes a 2008 agreement, and a real property purchase for the project.

milliken/0.title: Water bills, new smart meters and rate increases
milliken/0.summary: Residents told the Board in September and October that new meters, tiered rates and a roughly 30-35% rate increase have produced high water bills. One resident at 1064 Sunrise Cr reported being billed over 30,000 gallons. Staff said rates come from a five-year cost-of-service study, and 2027 rates are normally adopted in December. Residents also filed open-records requests for rate history.

milliken/1.title: 2027 Town budget process
milliken/1.summary: The Board held budget retreat sessions on the General Fund in August and September and reviewed the proposed 2027 budget on October 14. The first public budget hearing was set for October 14, with final adoption at the November public hearing.

milliken/2.title: Water Supply Element of the Comprehensive Plan (SB 24-174)
milliken/2.summary: The Board considered a contract with Ayres Associates of up to $17,500 to prepare the Water Supply Element required by state Senate Bill 24-174. Staff reported in September that work on the update had kicked off. The Board also scheduled a joint meeting with the Northern Colorado Water Conservancy District.

milliken/3.title: New Town Administrator hire
milliken/3.summary: After interviews and negotiations, the Board approved an employment agreement offering the Town Administrator job to Greg Brinck. A resolution appointing him was on the September 9 agenda, and he was giving updates to the Board by October. Steven Krolczyk had been serving as interim administrator.

milliken/4.title: Town Hall rental program fees
milliken/4.summary: The Board discussed the long-term sustainability of Town Hall rentals and directed staff to develop a hybrid model. Staff proposed higher hourly rates, a tiered structure with reduced rates for residents and nonprofits, higher non-resident rates, a funeral/memorial class, and clearer rental agreement rules. The goal is to reduce taxpayer subsidy of private use.

milliken/5.title: County Road 44 paving and traffic concerns
milliken/5.summary: A resident spoke on October 14 about the possible paving of County Road 44. She raised concerns about higher traffic volumes and speeds, safety for cyclists, runners, pedestrians, school buses and emergency vehicles, and long-term costs. She asked the Board to consider seasonal agricultural traffic and to drive the road themselves.

milliken/6.title: Milliken Housing Authority 2027 budget and strategic plan
milliken/6.summary: The Housing Authority drafted its 2027 budget, planned to send it to the Town, and put approval on its October 15 agenda. It also worked on its strategic plan and Prop 123 meetings, and planned a presentation to the Board of Trustees. Commissioners questioned Dove Valley operating costs and an August water bill with possible sprinkler damage.
milliken/6.where: Dove Valley; Housing Authority, 1101 Broad Street

milliken/7.title: Student home construction partnership at 1398 Irene
milliken/7.summary: The Board put a discussion of a student home construction partnership at 1398 Irene on its October 14 agenda.

milliken/8.title: Food truck park discussion
milliken/8.summary: The Board scheduled a discussion about a food truck park on October 14. The documents give no further detail.

milliken/9.title: Highway 257 noise complaint and pipeline removal agreement
milliken/9.summary: The Board discussed a noise complaint along Highway 257 on August 12. It also had an agreement with WES DJ Gathering, LLC for pipeline removal on the agenda.

milliken/10.title: Meadow Farms encroachment agreement
milliken/10.summary: The Board took up an encroachment agreement for Meadow Farms on October 14, presented by Community Development Director Kevin Koelbel.

milliken/11.title: Little Thompson River project and infrastructure work
milliken/11.summary: Staff reported progress on the Little Thompson River project: documents approved by CDOT for the full request, with a construction RFP expected in August. The Metron meter replacement was 99% complete. Cora and Beulah drainage work and park trail repairs were also underway.
milliken/11.where: Little Thompson River; Cora & Beulah Drive

milliken/12.title: Social media policy and Town communications
milliken/12.summary: The Board discussed an update to the Town's social media policy in September, and continued with a social media and communications discussion on September 23.

minturn/0.title: Water moratorium amendment (Ordinance 11) and downtown water improvements
minturn/0.summary: Council took up Ordinance 11 - Series 2026 amending the town's water moratorium on Oct. 7, with second reading on Oct. 21. Council also considered Resolution 50 to repurpose CDS funds for downtown water improvements, and in September updated outdoor emergency watering restrictions (Resolution 44). Outcomes are not stated in the documents.

minturn/1.title: Minturn shooting range grant and USFS special use permit
minturn/1.summary: Minturn was awarded a $225,000 grant from Colorado Parks and Wildlife to improve the shooting range and address long-standing issues. The town is seeking possible in-kind help from Eagle County, such as road grading, and council is discussing a USFS special use permit application, with a status update on Oct. 21.

minturn/2.title: 2027 budget, staffing and compensation
minturn/2.summary: Staff and council began 2027 budget talks in August, set a budget schedule in September, and on Oct. 7 had the 2027 budget acceptance and a discussion of staffing, compensation and benefits. Sales tax was about $10K down year to date as of August. Traffic-calming items such as speed bumps are being weighed for the FY 2027 budget.

minturn/3.title: 2026 Historic Preservation Plan
minturn/3.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission reviewed and amended the final 2026 plan in September, discussing a possible historic district and budget funds for preservation. Council was set to vote on adopting it via Resolution 45 on Oct. 7. The plan is described as an educational guide, not a regulation. The commission also chose Ken Halliday as chair and Dan Brown as vice chair.

minturn/4.title: Main Street parking study and speed camera study
minturn/4.summary: A planning intern presented parking study findings in August. Commissioners suggested a winter study and later-evening counts, plus marking parking spaces on Main St. Staff will proceed with a Main Street speed camera study and options for neighborhood traffic calming.

minturn/5.title: Neighborhood traffic calming in Boulder and Pine Street area
minturn/5.summary: After resident requests, staff is evaluating funding for more speed bumps or speed tables in the Boulder and Pine Street area as part of the FY 2027 budget.

minturn/6.title: Land use code update including Bolts Lake zoning
minturn/6.summary: Planning Commission discussed draft code definitions and rules, including whether decks count as pervious surfaces, parking area drainage, bulk plane illustrations, and Bolts Lake zone district uses tied to a settlement agreement.

minturn/7.title: Mobile and modular business pilot program and drainage improvement
minturn/7.summary: Council considered Resolution 47 for a Mobile & Modular Business Pilot Program and Resolution 46 authorizing a drainage improvement on Oct. 7. Details are not in the documents.

minturn/8.title: DDA Investment and Incentive Policy
minturn/8.summary: The Downtown Development Authority board considered Resolution 02 adopting an investment and incentive policy. It includes a small project matching grant program, large redevelopment and catalyst projects, and strategic property acquisition.

minturn/9.title: 161 Main St variance extension
minturn/9.summary: Council considered Resolution 42 extending a variance for 161 Main St. Councilmember Spence N. recused himself as the applicant.

minturn/10.title: Sheriff service agreement, housing authority and regional coordination
minturn/10.summary: Council discussed a joint meeting with Eagle County on regional topics including the Regional Housing Authority and e-bike rules, and an Eagle County Sheriff's Office service agreement was on the Oct. 21 agenda.

minturn/11.title: Trash can violation letter dispute at 537 Pine St
minturn/11.summary: Resident Mark Sifers asked to have a letter about a trash can violation at 537 Pine St retracted from his record. He said he had not heard back and wants resolution.

moffat-county/0.title: Data center regulations and possible moratorium
moffat-county/0.summary: The Planning & Zoning Commission began a formal review of the county zoning resolution and data center rules at its August 5 meeting, covering water and cooling, electric demand and ratepayer impacts, wildfire and emergency risk, and taxation. A moratorium was proposed but not acted on August 25; on September 8 speakers split on whether a short moratorium is needed, and an October 6 expert panel was announced.

moffat-county/1.title: Trapper Reborn project and moratorium concerns
moffat-county/1.summary: Pure-Green Colorado's CEO and other speakers urged commissioners not to pass a data center moratorium that could affect the Trapper Reborn project, citing jobs and tax base. Yampa Valley Electric asked to be part of the energy discussion.

moffat-county/2.title: Term limits referendum on November ballot
moffat-county/2.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 2026-100 referring a term limits question to voters and an intergovernmental agreement with the Clerk's Office to place it on the November ballot. Both passed 3-0.

moffat-county/3.title: Loudy-Simpson Park Master Plan
moffat-county/3.summary: Development Services proposed hiring Logan Simpson to produce a master plan for Loudy-Simpson Park. The contract was on the September 22 consent agenda.

moffat-county/4.title: Craig skatepark grant applications
moffat-county/4.summary: Commissioners approved grant applications of $25,000 each to the Laura Jane Musser Fund and El Pomar Foundation toward building a skatepark. The Craig Skatepark Alliance also plans a GOCO application in January.

moffat-county/5.title: July budget supplemental (Resolution 2026-83)
moffat-county/5.summary: After a public hearing with no public comment, commissioners approved the July supplemental budget, which lets departments amend budgets for changed revenues, grants or unexpected needs.

moffat-county/6.title: Road department concerns: snow bank pay policy and chip seal
moffat-county/6.summary: A county Road & Bridge employee asked commissioners to examine inconsistencies in the snow bank payment policy and followed up on September 8. A resident also questioned excess gravel on the CR 7 chip seal project.

moffat-county/7.title: Employee Health Insurance Advisory Board reinstated
moffat-county/7.summary: Commissioners were asked to reinstate the Employee Health Insurance Advisory Board and appointed five employee-elected members to recommend plan improvements.

moffat-county/8.title: Wolf Creek Reservoir jurisdictional determination
moffat-county/8.summary: A request for a new approved jurisdictional determination for the Wolf Creek Reservoir Project was on the September 22 consent agenda.

moffat-county/9.title: Welba Peak mineral lease
moffat-county/9.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 2026-96 for the Welba Peak mineral lease.

montrose-county/0.title: 2026 Gold Mountain Fire response and FEMA support
montrose-county/0.summary: The county opened an Emergency Operations Center for the Gold Mountain Fire, and Road and Bridge crews supported the response. The county leased the Wells Basin property to stage fire mitigation crews, and the Chair signed a letter to President Trump asking for FEMA support.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/1.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code agreements with fire districts
montrose-county/1.summary: The commissioners approved intergovernmental agreements with the Montrose Fire Protection District and the Norwood Fire Protection District. Under them the districts share administration and enforcement of the county's adopted Wildfire Resiliency Code. The Norwood agreement passed on a 2-1 consent vote.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/2.title: 6400 Road flood response
montrose-county/2.summary: County Road and Bridge responded to a flood on the 6400 Road, which was reported at the August 5 meeting. The documents give no further detail on repairs or costs.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/3.title: Kinikin Road updates
montrose-county/3.summary: Public Works gave recurring Kinikin Road updates at the August work sessions. The condensed agendas do not say what work is planned.

montrose-county/4.title: 2027 county budget and 2026 supplemental appropriation
montrose-county/4.summary: The Finance Director presented a first supplemental appropriation to the 2026 budget in August. The proposed 2027 budget was presented at an October 14 special meeting with a public hearing. Community partnership funding was also discussed.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/5.title: West End Family Link emergency funding
montrose-county/5.summary: At a September 17 special meeting in Nucla, the commissioners heard a presentation and public comment on a funding request from West End Family Link. Commissioner Pond moved to fund the emergency request at $75,000.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/6.title: Housing: grant for needs assessment and private activity bonds
montrose-county/6.summary: Planning staff were to discuss a grant application for a Housing Needs Assessment tied to SB24-174. The commissioners also assigned $1,573,936 of the county's 2026 Private Activity Bond allocation to the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority, as part of a unanimously passed consent agenda.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/7.title: Property tax appeals and write-offs
montrose-county/7.summary: The Board of Equalization heard personal, commercial and residential property tax appeals. It supported denial of the High Oasis LLC appeal and temporarily amended the value of one residential property. It denied a senior property tax exemption appeal. Separately, the county wrote off uncollectable property taxes through Resolution 31-2026.

sources.body: Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - Board of Equalization - No Video Available
Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING
Special Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/8.title: Montrose Regional Airport projects and leases
montrose-county/8.summary: The county amended an on-call geotechnical contract for apron and taxilane reconstruction. It also released retainage on the AWOS installation project, amended a Colorado Parks and Wildlife hangar lease, and acted on baggage delivery permits and hangar leases.

sources.body: Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners

montrose-county/9.title: Road, bridge and paving contracts
montrose-county/9.summary: The county approved a $487,333 contract with Precision Dirt Works for B-24 bridge rail replacement. It also approved $142,313.20 for paving the Public Works parking lot and an agreement with Olathe for asphalt overlay on various streets. On-call structural inspection contracts were approved with SGM, HDR, J-U-B and Engineering Operations.

Regular Meeting - Board of County Commissioners - NO VIDEO RECORDING

montrose-county/10.title: Safe sleep program and Headwaters to Home
montrose-county/10.summary: Work sessions in October took up the Rocky Mountain Health Plans Safe Sleep Incentive Program, with a draft services agreement, and a Headwaters to Home item.

montrose-county/11.title: Montrose/Ouray county line and Colorado Parks and Wildlife changes
montrose-county/11.summary: An October 26 work session was set to discuss the Montrose/Ouray County line and proposed Colorado Parks and Wildlife changes.

montrose/0.title: City Charter amendments for the November ballot (Ordinances 2727-2730)
montrose/0.summary: Council worked through four charter amendments: moving municipal elections to November, 8-year lifetime term limits, and council approval over appointing and removing the police chief and the city clerk. Ranked-choice and gendered-language amendments were dropped from the November ballot. Many residents spoke for and against, and Ordinances 2727 and 2728 were heard on second reading Sept. 1.

montrose/1.title: City manager separation and interim manager
montrose/1.summary: Council went into executive session about a confidential memo and possible independent counsel, then approved a mutual separation agreement with City Manager Bill Bell. On Sept. 15 it ratified that agreement, appointed Ann Morgenthaler interim city manager under an open-ended agreement during recruitment, and named her executive director of the Montrose Urban Renewal Authority.

montrose/2.title: City Council District IV vacancy and Adam Woodden appointment
montrose/2.summary: The District IV seat was vacated Sept. 7 and the charter requires an appointment within 30 days. Council agreed to appoint Adam Woodden to District IV, which opens the At-Large seat. Applications for the At-Large seat were set to run Oct. 7-21, with an appointment planned for Nov. 2.

montrose/3.title: Locust Road Addition annexation and zoning
montrose/3.summary: A 4.2-acre annexation at 1815 Locust Road, plus part of the road right of way, was requested by Gustavo Martinez. The Planning Commission unanimously recommended R-2 low-density zoning, with discussion of pedestrian infrastructure and rebuilding Locust Road. Council set a Sept. 15 hearing and heard Ordinance 2731 on second reading Oct. 6.

montrose/4.title: Data center moratorium request
montrose/4.summary: At the Aug. 18 meeting, Carol Howe urged Council to enact a moratorium on new data centers until regulations are in place.

montrose/5.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing opt-in and Shepherd's Hand shelter funding
montrose/5.summary: Council's Oct. 20 agenda includes Resolution 2026-16 committing to increase affordable housing units under Proposition 123. It also includes a $28,597 expenditure request tied to The Shepherd's Hand shelter.

montrose/6.title: Comprehensive plan update and growth policy
montrose/6.summary: Staff is preparing a five-year technical update of the Envision 2040 plan and land development code, including state-mandated housing needs assessment, housing action plan and water supply planning. The goal is approval by year's end. Residents urged that growth pay its own way and that the plan's standards be followed.

montrose/7.title: Rotary Park pump house replacement
montrose/7.summary: Council considered a $514,011 contract with FCI Constructors of Grand Junction to replace the 1980s irrigation pump house. It is $14,011 over the $500,000 budget, to be covered by savings from other 2026 Public Works capital projects.

montrose/8.title: Network Operation Center fire suppression system
montrose/8.summary: Council authorized $75,000 for a waterless clean-agent fire suppression system at the city's Network Operation Center, including a $69,987 sole-source contract with Pye Barker. The work was not formally bid; staff cited standardizing vendors for fire and security systems.

montrose/9.title: Student parking on residential streets near the high school
montrose/9.summary: Residents asked Council to reinstate permit-only parking on neighborhood streets near the high school and to increase police presence.
montrose/9.where: Residential streets near Montrose High School

montrose/10.title: Miami Road electronic speed sign
montrose/10.summary: Residents asked Council to install an electronic traffic speed sign on Miami Road near Cedar Creek.

montrose/11.title: 2027 fee schedule revisions
montrose/11.summary: Proposed changes effective Jan. 1, 2027 include higher cemetery lot and open/close fees, a larger school land dedication fee, a $75 park shelter electricity fee, and a $50 building reinspection fee after the third violation.

montrose/12.title: Chipeta Lake 2 annexation and Spruce Point subdivision
montrose/12.summary: The Planning Commission was to hear initial "P" Public zoning for the 1.14-acre Chipeta Lake 2 Addition annexation. It was also to hear an amended preliminary plat for Spruce Point Subdivision at the end of Sanctuary, Prospect and Sleep Rock Drives.
montrose/12.where: Chipeta Road; Spruce Point near 6400 Road

montrose/13.title: Star Court townhomes and Chelsi Lane PD amendment
montrose/13.summary: The Planning Commission recommended approval of the preliminary plat for townhomes at 739-749 East Star Court. It also heard a Chelsi Lane amendment reducing the 1992 planned development from 24 to 23 units.

monument/0.title: Monument 2040 Comprehensive Plan and Downtown Master Plan
monument/0.summary: The Planning Commission took up the draft 2040 Comprehensive Plan Update and Downtown Master Plan after nearly two years of outreach, with a hearing on Sept. 9 continued to Oct. 14. Residents raised concerns that conceptual downtown redevelopment renderings don't fit Monument's historic small-town character and asked about how many people took part in outreach.

monument/1.title: Use tax ballot measure and 2027 budget
monument/1.summary: The Citizens Service Levels Advisory Committee reviewed the preliminary 2027 budget and a use tax ballot initiative. Increasing the motor vehicle use tax to 3.5 would raise about $500K more, and construction use tax could add about $2.2M. Council was asked to refer ballot measures, and on Oct. 19 considered a resolution supporting the construction use tax increase (Ordinance 19-2026). Council also reviewed the draft 2027 budget and capital plan.

monument/2.title: Native Sun Construction PUD amendment at 15010 Woodcarver Road
monument/2.summary: The Planning Commission recommended approval of a major amendment that relocates the shop building, adds a deceleration lane on Wood Carver Road, and preserves 21 trees while planting 66. Council scheduled Ordinance 24-2026 for a hearing on Sept. 8.

monument/3.title: 7 Brew Drive Thru Coffee final PUD
monument/3.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the final PUD plan for a 7 Brew drive-thru coffee shop. Council took up Ordinance 23-2026 approving it on Sept. 8.

monument/4.title: Karl Malone Powersports final PUD
monument/4.summary: The Planning Commission recommended approval of the final PUD for a 30,000-square-foot RV sales and service facility. Discussion covered screening and security of outdoor storage, parking, and underground stormwater detention.

monument/5.title: Conexus Lot 1 Filing 2 and Tract E land transfer
monument/5.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed the final PUD for Conexus Lot 1 Filing 2, which includes 312 apartment units. Council later considered Ordinance 26-2026, a real property transfer, and Resolution 74-2026, a temporary construction easement in Tract E. No public comments were received at the hearing.

monument/6.title: Falcon Commerce Center Phase 2 PUD amendment
monument/6.summary: Council reconsidered Ordinance 15-2026, a preliminary PUD major amendment for the south 43 acres of Falcon Commerce Center, continued from Aug. 3. Staff gave a timeline of events.

monument/7.title: 309 Woodworth Street use classification appeal
monument/7.summary: An appeal of the Planning Director's use classification determination for 309 Woodworth Street came to a public hearing.

monument/8.title: Traffic, growth and Jackson Creek Parkway
monument/8.summary: The advisory committee discussed traffic impact fees, which may fund Jackson Creek Parkway, and expected pressure from a Target, new apartments, and a possible Costco. Members also raised traffic on Old Denver Highway.

monument/9.title: Water quality, water attorney and tap approvals
monument/9.summary: Council heard a presentation on water testing and sampling and appointed Nazarenus Stack & Wombacher as water attorney. It also considered a new tap for two properties, and a councilmember asked for a water workshop.

monument/10.title: Small Business Development Center funding request
monument/10.summary: The committee weighed a funding proposal from the Small Business Development Center Network. Members questioned its impact and the $250 consulting fee.

monument/11.title: Motorized devices ordinance and parking permit repeal
monument/11.summary: Council considered Ordinance 25-2026 regulating prohibited motorized devices. It also took up Ordinance 20-2026, repealing a municipal code subsection that waives parking permit requirements.

monument/12.title: Police fees, handguns and staffing
monument/12.summary: Council approved revised police department service fees effective Oct. 1 and considered buying Shadow Systems handguns for officers. The 2027 budget adds 4 police positions funded by impact fees.

morgan-county/0.title: Data center zoning regulations
morgan-county/0.summary: The county commissioners have been working on new data center rules for Chapter 4 of the zoning regulations. The Planning Commission recommended approval in April 2026, and the commissioners' hearing opened May 5 and was continued repeatedly, through August 4, for staff revisions. Open points include new definitions (edge, large and accessory data centers), setbacks, closed-loop cooling only, and decommissioning and emergency plans.

morgan-county/1.title: Fortress solar and battery project: road work enforcement hearing
morgan-county/1.summary: The county issued a Notice of Intent to Take Enforcement Action and Order to Show Cause against Fortress over its three-phase solar and battery project. The notice alleges violations of its special use permits and the Public Improvements Agreement for paving County Roads Q and R, including paving before county inspectors could observe roadbed preparation. Fortress responded in writing ahead of the October 23 hearing and said it will crush and rebuild the road.

morgan-county/2.title: Jail expansion and county financial report
morgan-county/2.summary: The 2025 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report was presented August 18. It notes that the commissioners are targeting a County Jail expansion funded partly by an Energy Impact Assistance Fund grant and a Jail Capital Improvement Fund set up in 2008. The county may also ask the cities and towns to help pay.

morgan-county/3.title: Home Rule Charter and special election
morgan-county/3.summary: On September 1 the commissioners heard a presentation on a Home Rule Charter from Charter Commissioner Brian McCracken. They also considered Resolution 2026 BCC 38 calling a special election.

morgan-county/4.title: Planning and building fee schedule changes
morgan-county/4.summary: The commissioners considered Resolution 2026 BCC 40 adopting new fees for planning services and building inspection on September 1. A revised 2026 county fee schedule for Planning, Zoning and Building Inspection came up again September 29.

morgan-county/5.title: Zoning enforcement process amendments and junk ordinance
morgan-county/5.summary: On September 29 the commissioners considered Resolution 2026 BCC 42, which cleans up the zoning regulations' enforcement processes and adds continuing county jurisdiction over permits. On September 15 they took up Ordinance No. 2, Series 2026, a first reading on county prohibitions on junk and refuse deposited in unapproved sites in unincorporated areas, with an exemption for operating junk yards.

morgan-county/6.title: Temporary RV housing special use permit near Wiggins
