morgan-county/6.summary: A special use permit hearing on August 4 concerned temporary residential use of RVs at 18975 County Road 1 while manufactured home placement permits are obtained. Once the homes are in place, the RVs would no longer be allowed as residences. The permit is meant to bring the property into compliance with county zoning.

morgan-county/7.title: Farm stand special use permit on County Road 19
morgan-county/7.summary: The commissioners heard a special use permit for a small family farm stand at 16255 County Road 19 on August 4, in an Estate Residential zone. Resolution 2026 BCC 33 approving it was on the August 18 agenda, following a Planning Commission recommendation of approval on July 13.

morgan-county/8.title: Solar lease amendment and wastewater plant road use agreement
morgan-county/8.summary: On October 6 the commissioners considered a second amendment to a 2024 solar energy system lease and easement covering about 17 acres. They also considered a road use agreement with Glacier Construction for the expansion of Fort Morgan's wastewater treatment plant.

morgan-county/9.title: Justice Center security fence and Proposition 123 presentation
morgan-county/9.summary: On October 20 the commissioners considered awarding a bid for a security fence project at the Morgan County Justice Center and East Point Building. They also heard a presentation on Proposition 123 from the United Way.
morgan-county/9.where: Morgan County Justice Center, Fort Morgan

morgan-county/10.title: Mission Goldwing Solar Project comments
morgan-county/10.summary: The county was asked for comments on the Mission Goldwing Solar Project in Adams County near the county line. It was on the September 1 agenda.

morrison/0.title: The Fort / Farm at the Fort annexation, zoning and extraterritorial water-sewer deal
morrison/0.summary: The Board considered an extraterritorial water and sewer agreement with Morrison RE Development, LP for The Fort, allowing up to 75 EQRs (50 residential) with $2.5 million in one-time impact fees and a public improvement fee on restaurant sales. Public hearings were noticed for Aug. 18 on annexing about 59.36 acres known as the Farm at the Fort and on initial zoning (Residential Estate and Mixed-Use Neighborhood). A resident asked for an update on the hearing.
morrison/0.where: The Fort / Farm at the Fort, unincorporated Jefferson County near Morrison

morrison/1.title: Green Tree Metro District extraterritorial sewer service
morrison/1.summary: The Board approved a term sheet for extraterritorial sewer service with the Green Tree Metro District after closed-door negotiation discussions. A sewer service agreement with the district was back on the Oct. 20 agenda.

morrison/2.title: Lodging tax changes and ballot questions
morrison/2.summary: Ordinance 562 aligns the lodging tax exemption with the 2012 voter-approved ballot language, effective Oct. 1, 2026. Two ballot issues would raise taxes by $125,000 by removing the exemption for small lodging and by $500,000 by raising the lodging tax from 6% to 8%. The Board ratified Ordinance 564 on ballot questions.

morrison/3.title: Downtown and interstate parking concerns
morrison/3.summary: Residents told the Board that new businesses should not be allowed without adequate parking in downtown Morrison. The Board discussed overnight parking and interstate parking and sought direction from the community.
morrison/3.where: Downtown Morrison, Bear Creek Ave. area

morrison/4.title: Mandatory watering restrictions and rewrite of the water and sewer code
morrison/4.summary: Due to drought, mandatory watering restrictions limit outdoor watering to two days a week and ban watering from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. The Board adopted Ordinance 565 repealing and reenacting Title 8 on water and sewer regulations, including backflow prevention. The Board also discussed raw water diversion in executive session.

morrison/5.title: 2027 draft budget and personnel costs
morrison/5.summary: The draft 2027 budget shows a 15.85% health insurance increase, a 3.6% cost-of-living raise, and lodging tax expected to become the second-largest tax source, ahead of property tax. A new hotel will add lodging and sales tax, and it uses the town's Enhanced Sales Tax Incentive Program. Budget hearings are set to start Nov. 4, and a new full-time position and a museum budget memo were also on the agenda.

morrison/6.title: Town Manager transition
morrison/6.summary: The Board approved an interim town manager employment agreement effective Aug. 14, 2026, held an exit interview session, and took up a Town Manager employment agreement in October. Residents also commented on the Town Manager application process.

morrison/7.title: East Planning Area pre-development agreement
morrison/7.summary: The Board met in executive session on negotiations over development of the East Planning Area and on Oct. 6 approved a pre-development agreement related to it.

morrison/8.title: Zoning code changes: garden sheds, motels, floodplain
morrison/8.summary: Ordinance 566 allows garden sheds up to 120 sq ft as an accessory use, adds motels as a permitted use in the HD district, clarifies floodplain grade measurement, and amends the definition of substantial improvement.

morrison/9.title: Faster nuisance abatement on public property
morrison/9.summary: Ordinance 567 lets the town abate nuisances on public property without notice, and was adopted Oct. 6.

morrison/10.title: Wildfire preparedness and Stage 2 fire ban
morrison/10.summary: The town newsletter reminds residents of a Stage 2 Fire Ban in unincorporated Jefferson County and urges emergency plans and Lookout Alert sign-up.

mountain-view/0.title: R3 Zoning District Update (R3/R4 zoning, General Plan and map changes)
mountain-view/0.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission is scheduled to hear the recommendation to adopt the R3 and R4 zoning amendments, precise plan and General Plan amendments, and a zoning map change on October 7. The map change would apply R4 in 14 change areas and new R3-A, R3-B and R3-C districts across the city, with an environmental impact report certification and statement of overriding considerations.

mountain-view/1.title: Rowhouse Gatekeeper Project at 924-940 San Rafael Avenue
mountain-view/1.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission is set to hear a proposal to rezone 924-940 San Rafael Avenue from General Industrial to R3-2 and build a 36-unit rowhouse development using state density bonus law, replacing two industrial buildings. It includes a General Plan amendment, two heritage tree removals on the 1.80-acre site, and a vesting tentative map.

mountain-view/2.title: Historic Preservation Ordinance and Historic Register update
mountain-view/2.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission held a public hearing on August 19 on amendments to the zoning code and zoning map for designating and preserving historic resources. The City Council is scheduled to adopt the ordinances on second reading on October 13. Public comments were attached to the staff report.

mountain-view/3.title: Rengstorff Avenue Complete Streets Study and Active Transportation Plan
mountain-view/3.summary: The Bicycle/Pedestrian Advisory Committee and the Council Transportation Committee reviewed three draft concept alternatives and corridor priorities for the Rengstorff Avenue Complete Streets Study (Project 25-39). Both bodies were also asked to review the final Mountain View Active Transportation Plan and recommend it to City Council for adoption.

mountain-view/4.title: 96 West El Camino Real affordable housing funding and bonds
mountain-view/4.summary: The City Council consent calendar included accepting $388,515 in state Permanent Local Housing Allocation funds, with allocations to the 96 West El Camino Real affordable housing project and a homeownership assistance pilot. It also included a resolution approving tax-exempt multifamily bond financing through the California Municipal Finance Authority for the project.

mountain-view/5.title: Shoreline athletic fields renovation and Google environmental reimbursement
mountain-view/5.summary: The Council, acting as the Shoreline Regional Park Community board, considered an $880,000 not-to-exceed agreement with Tetra Tech for Shoreline athletic field renovations. It also considered agreements with Google for reimbursement of past environmental work and ongoing monitoring, with $4,968,700 appropriated to the Shoreline fund.

mountain-view/6.title: LinkedIn development agreement amendment
mountain-view/6.summary: On October 13 the City Council is to introduce an ordinance approving a first amendment to the development agreement with LinkedIn for its sites at 700-810 East Middlefield Road and 1100-1200 Maude Avenue.
mountain-view/6.where: 700-810 East Middlefield Road and 1100-1200 Maude Avenue

mountain-view/7.title: Heritage tree removal appeals and ordinance update
mountain-view/7.summary: The Urban Forestry Board denied the appeal at 961 Eichler Drive, but approved removal of one heritage tree at 777 San Carrizo Way against staff's recommendation. A further appeal at 1473 Tyler Park Way is set for October 14, along with a heritage tree ordinance update process. A commissioner asked that Community Services and Community Development staff coordinate on how the ordinance is applied.
mountain-view/7.where: 961 Eichler Drive, 777 San Carrizo Way, 1473 Tyler Park Way

sources.body: Parks and Recreation Commission and Urban Forestry Board
Parks and Recreation Commission and Urban Forestry Board

mountain-view/8.title: Heritage tree removals at mobile home park
mountain-view/8.summary: The Zoning Administrator is to consider a development review permit and a heritage tree removal permit to remove 26 heritage trees in an existing residential mobile home park on a 17.34-acre site near the creek trail and Highway 237. Valley Water correspondence is included in the materials.
mountain-view/8.where: Mobile home park near Highway 237 (17.34-acre site)

mountain-view/9.title: Rent stabilization appeal hearings
mountain-view/9.summary: The Rental Housing Committee heard a landlord's appeal of a hearing officer's June 4 decision on Petition C25260029 and is to hear a tenant's appeal of an August 14 decision on Petition C25260032. The October agenda also covers Rent Stabilization Ordinance items and survey feedback from petition parties.

mountain-view/10.title: Ambulance billing and user fees
mountain-view/10.summary: The City Council was asked to adopt revised ambulance billing and user fees for the Fire Department, to be reflected in the Master Fee Schedule.

mountain-view/11.title: Pathways to Housing homeless response report
mountain-view/11.summary: The City Council is to accept the first annual progress report on the 2026 Pathways to Housing Homeless Response Strategy Implementation and Expenditure Plan.

mountain-view/12.title: All-electric construction zoning incentives
mountain-view/12.summary: The Environmental Planning Commission is to consider a zoning amendment allowing exceptions to development standards in R1 and R2 districts for single-family and duplex homes that voluntarily build all-electric.
mountain-view/12.where: R1 and R2 zoning districts citywide

mountain-view/13.title: Downtown issues and Castro Street
mountain-view/13.summary: The Downtown Committee is to receive a downtown development update, a Castro Street update and the annual Business Improvement Area renewal overview. Its list of possible future topics includes vacant storefronts, parking, restrooms, and a busking ordinance.

nederland/0.title: Rezoning 242 and 252 E 5th Street for A-frame homes
nederland/0.summary: The planning commission recommended rezoning two steep commercial lots on East 5th Street to medium density residential for two A-frame homes, after a neighbor worried about losing commercial zoning flexibility and another resident spoke in support.

nederland/1.title: Outdoor dining and sales rules
nederland/1.summary: The town moved to allow outdoor sales, eating and drinking in its zoning use table, with safety standards near roadways.

nederland/2.title: Temporary use permits
nederland/2.summary: The planning commission and trustees worked on Ordinance 893 for staff-approved temporary use permits of up to 90 days that staff can revoke over safety problems.

nederland/3.title: Flex zoning for housing and redevelopment
nederland/3.summary: The planning commission began discussing flex zoning to allow more housing types and mixed uses, including in the Wolf Tongue industrial area and near East Street Garage.

nederland/4.title: Parks, open space and trails master plan
nederland/4.summary: The parks board finished revisions to the parks, recreation, open space and trails plan for trustees to review, and kept planning a replacement for the Chipeta Park playground.

sources.body: PROSAB - Nederland Parks, Recreation, and Open Space Advisory Board

nederland/5.title: Merging the zoning adjustment board into the planning commission
nederland/5.summary: The town moved an ordinance to dissolve its Board of Zoning Adjustment and hand its variance work to the planning commission, citing few applications and trouble filling the volunteer board.

nederland/6.title: Safer Main Streets crosswalk and sidewalk project
nederland/6.summary: Trustees approved an engineering agreement for crosswalk and sidewalk improvements under the Safer Main Streets program, and backed the fire district's wildfire mitigation grant.

new-castle/0.title: Comprehensive Plan update (last adopted 2009)
new-castle/0.summary: The Town Attorney briefed Council on the legal process for updating New Castle's comprehensive plan, which was adopted May 27, 2009 and never updated. The discussion was meant to set next steps for starting the project.

new-castle/1.title: Garfield County School of Innovation charter school proposal
new-castle/1.summary: Council heard a presentation from backers of the Garfield County School of Innovation, who have applied to the Re-2 School Board to open a charter school in New Castle in 2027. The plan is to start right after Rosie's renovation, pending charter approval.

new-castle/2.title: Garfield County RE2 ballot issue and county libraries measure
new-castle/2.summary: Council heard presentations from the Garfield County RE2 Ballot Issue Committee and the Maintain Our County Libraries Committee. It was also set to consider a letter of support for the RE2 ballot measure.

new-castle/3.title: 2027 budget and trash/recycling fees
new-castle/3.summary: Council began discussing the 2027 budget. Mountain Waste is gathering landfill fee data that will set 2027 trash and recycling fees and was to present upcoming changes.

new-castle/4.title: Plastic bag fee fund, Community Market and cleanup days
new-castle/4.summary: The Climate and Environment Commission planned Community Market recycling and compost, a plastic reduction pledge, and a Dump Day/trash pickup on October 10, with about $12,000 left in the bag fee fund. It also planned a parade float for the Burning Mountain Festival and a business sustainability award.

new-castle/5.title: Building, planning and development update
new-castle/5.summary: Town Planner updated Council on development: 40 of 80 expected apartment units permitted, Coal Seam hotel/restaurant approved April 7, and the New Castle Center (Walters Center) amended PUD expected this fall. TC Midwest plans road and infrastructure work in fall/winter 2026.
new-castle/5.where: New Castle Center, Lakota, Castle Valley Ranch

new-castle/6.title: Police Department update and training
new-castle/6.summary: Chief Curry reported on increased training funded largely through Colorado POST grants. Council also discussed department needs ahead of its retreat.

new-castle/7.title: Senior housing residents' concerns at Canyon Senior Housing
new-castle/7.summary: A speaker raised residents' concerns at Canyon Senior Housing and asked about town ordinances that could apply. The administrator said Council could take it up at a future work session.

new-castle/8.title: Historic Preservation: Highland Cemetery plaque, survey grants and CLG audit
new-castle/8.summary: The commission approved a new designation plaque for Highland Cemetery, explored grants for a historic survey including Coryell Town and a GIS database, and worked on a videography project and the Certified Local Government annual report.

new-castle/9.title: EV charging station guidelines
new-castle/9.summary: Council was to consider guidelines for electric vehicle charging stations.

new-castle/10.title: Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act discussion
new-castle/10.summary: A discussion of the Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act was on the September 15 agenda.

norwood/0.title: Town-wide 15 mph speed limit
norwood/0.summary: The board discussed lowering the speed limit in April and June, then took up an ordinance in July to set a 15 mph limit on all town streets unless otherwise posted. An ordinance appeared again on the Aug. 12 agenda.

norwood/1.title: Moratorium on medium and large-scale development and land use code rewrite
norwood/1.summary: In January the board discussed extending the emergency moratorium on medium and large-scale development (Ordinance 0813, 2025). It has since worked with KLJ on a land use code contract, a master plan contract, and a land use code amendment ordinance in October.

norwood/2.title: Norwood Public School property purchase and rezone
norwood/2.summary: The board got an update in January on the town's purchase of Norwood Public School property. A May public hearing considered rezoning 2028 Maverick Way from Agriculture to a public zoning district.

norwood/3.title: Pocket park construction, signage and dedication
norwood/3.summary: The town took a bid from RMC Builders for the pocket park and handled updates, an address (1575 Grand Ave) and signage. A dedication was set for the Sept. 9 agenda.

norwood/4.title: Employee compensation and retention incentives
norwood/4.summary: The board reviewed legal advice on employee compensation in May. It then took up a resolution and ordinances in June and July authorizing additional compensation and retention incentives.

norwood/5.title: Short-term rental rules
norwood/5.summary: The board discussed short-term rentals in July, September and October.

norwood/6.title: Removal for cause hearing
norwood/6.summary: On Aug. 12 the board set a public hearing to consider removing an official for cause, amended the resolution in September, and then cancelled the hearing on Oct. 15.

norwood/7.title: CDOT Safer Sidewalks to School and school traffic
norwood/7.summary: The board approved job bids for the CDOT Safer Sidewalks to School project and an MOU with CDOT in June. It later discussed school traffic, sidewalks and upcoming CDOT projects.

norwood/8.title: Water commission, raw water and drainage
norwood/8.summary: The board handled the water commission's grant authority, a State Land Board property for the water treatment plant, raw water board rules, commission appointments and a drainage study and system design by SGM.

norwood/9.title: 2027 draft budget and mill levy
norwood/9.summary: The board set the mill levy in January and reviewed the 2027 draft budget in October.

norwood/10.title: Wildlife, wildfire and fireworks ordinances
norwood/10.summary: The board discussed wildlife and wildfire ordinances in January and February. Fireworks were on agendas in January, June and October.

norwood/11.title: EV charging stations and dark sky lighting
norwood/11.summary: The board discussed EV charging rates and install budget, streetlight dark sky compliance and updated Dark Sky Coalition rules.

nunn/0.title: North Weld Water Services Agreement and town water loss
nunn/0.summary: The town attorney has been reviewing and amending a water services agreement with North Weld County Water, with several areas still needing clarification as of April. Water loss remains a problem, so the town is looking at more meters and a grant to help find leaks. By October the board was discussing a water committee, an excess water usage ordinance and tap approvals.

nunn/1.title: Master Water Plan grant and bid selection
nunn/1.summary: The town has been waiting on an agreement for its Master Water Plan grant. A bid opening committee brought a recommendation for the engineer in August, and the board voted on bid selection.

nunn/2.title: CDBG Senior Center and Community Center grant and Town Hall improvements
nunn/2.summary: The town submitted a CDBG grant for the Senior Center and later learned it was approved, with a total of $206,739.34. The money covers asbestos abatement (bids ran from $56,000 to $161,000), a $17,500 engineering contract, interior painting and a trophy case. The board voted on allocation to finish the project and on a project manager.

nunn/3.title: Clayton Homes development and Blue Spruce Development
nunn/3.summary: Clayton Homes wants to move forward with 18 homes. The board said it needs to discuss plant investments, tap fees and future large developments. Permits for lots 2 and 3 of the RLD subdivision were processed in August, and a variance request for 1467 4th Street was on the September agenda. Blue Spruce Development on 4th Street has a development agreement under attorney review, and the developer must provide water shares.

nunn/4.title: Safer Streets grant and speed study
nunn/4.summary: The town hired an engineering firm for its Safer Streets grant and comprehensive plan. It collected resident input through an interactive map with a gift card giveaway, plus senior, first responder and youth outreach. The draft safety plan is to be posted online for 30 days for public comment.

nunn/5.title: Master Drainage Plan
nunn/5.summary: The board reviewed the Master Drainage Plan and gave comments to engineers. A community update was held June 11, and the plan is to be posted for 30 days of public review.

nunn/6.title: 2024 building code and Wildfire Resiliency Code
nunn/6.summary: The board adopted Ordinance 329 adopting the 2024 International Building Code at a public hearing in April, with no public comment. The Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code was split into a separate ordinance and is slated for adoption, with updates in October.

nunn/7.title: Sunrise Solar Project at CR 29.5
nunn/7.summary: The board reviewed a permit application for a 20-acre solar project at 49600 CR 29.5. It has a 10-foot fence with aluminum slats, and the town wants written plans for dust mitigation, a truck route and contingencies. A 50% plan is expected in mid-August.

nunn/8.title: Police equipment, vehicles and grants
nunn/8.summary: The police department asked for pepper ball guns at $969 each that were not in the budget. Other items included new tasers, a $1,800 Taser battery charger, police car repairs, vehicle leases and a Byrne JAG grant application.

nunn/9.title: 2026 budget, mill levy and 2027 budget draft
nunn/9.summary: The town previewed the 2026 budget, set the property tax levy and adopted the budget and appropriation resolutions in December. It began reviewing an initial 2027 budget draft in October.

nunn/10.title: Chalk Bluffs Energy Project presentation
nunn/10.summary: Representatives of the Chalk Bluffs Energy Project presented to the board in January. The documents give no details of the project.

nunn/11.title: Marijuana licensing and manufacturing applications
nunn/11.summary: A local applicant seeking a marijuana manufacturing license still had to get state approval before the town licensing authority votes. The authority also reviewed renewals for cultivation and manufacturing facilities in February and May.

nunn/12.title: RV ordinance, preliminary concept plan and county road costs
nunn/12.summary: October work session items included a concept plan for 20 acres on the former Antelope Run site, a possible RV ordinance, and the cost of Weld County road assistance.

oak-creek/0.title: New 2% sales tax chapter for capital improvements (Ordinance No. 678)
oak-creek/0.summary: The Town Board discussed an ordinance adopting a new Chapter 3.02 of the municipal code covering the town's 2.0% sales tax, to be used for construction and rehabilitation of capital improvements. It was discussed in August and September and Ordinance No. 678 was up for approval on October 8, 2026.

oak-creek/1.title: Lot 15, Sierra View Subdivision development agreement with MACOGA, LLC
oak-creek/1.summary: The board was asked to approve a development agreement for Lot 15, Sierra View Subdivision on October 8, and on October 22 it held a legal-advice session and considered a Development Improvement Agreement with MACOGA, LLC. The new agreement would terminate and replace an April 2025 improvements agreement, and requires a $5,000 deposit from the developer.

oak-creek/2.title: Sheriff Dam enlargement and reservoir project
oak-creek/2.summary: The board considered a Special Use Permit for the enlargement and rehabilitation of Sheriff Dam, as approved by the state Division of Water Resources, along with an agent authorization form for the Sheriff Dam Reservoir Project.

oak-creek/3.title: Law enforcement agreements with Routt County Sheriff's Office
oak-creek/3.summary: The August 13 meeting included a hearing on two draft law enforcement service agreements with Routt County and an off-duty overtime reimbursement agreement with the Routt County Sheriff's Office.

oak-creek/4.title: 2027 budget first draft
oak-creek/4.summary: The board reviewed the first draft of the town's 2027 annual budget on October 8, 2026.

oak-creek/5.title: Bulk water dispensing station upgrades
oak-creek/5.summary: The board discussed upgrades to the bulk water dispensing station, then took up buying a new control panel and a proposal to build a new shell for the station.

oak-creek/6.title: Trash hauling rate increases from Apex Twin Enviro
oak-creek/6.summary: Apex Twin Enviro was scheduled to discuss with the board its trash hauling rate increases beginning in November 2026.

oak-creek/7.title: Dog park proposal and flow trail grant
oak-creek/7.summary: The SOROCO Youth Action Council sought a letter of support for a grant and presented a proposed dog park in town. Separately, the board considered a resolution to apply for a $125,000 Colorado Parks and Wildlife trail grant to complete a downhill flow trail in Oak Creek Mountain Park.

oak-creek/8.title: South Routt Medical Center health service plan expansion
oak-creek/8.summary: The Planning Commission and Town Board held public hearings on an application to add 880 square feet of institutional space to the existing South Routt Medical Center facility.

oak-creek/9.title: Street and drainage projects: Sharp Avenue, Oak Ridge, Bell Avenue
oak-creek/9.summary: The board considered an asphalt patching project on Sharp Avenue and Oak Ridge and a bid for the Bell Avenue drainage improvement project. It also considered buying a $135,364 sewer jetter.
oak-creek/9.where: Sharp Avenue, Oak Ridge, Bell Avenue

oak-creek/10.title: South Routt Housing Authority funding request
oak-creek/10.summary: The South Routt Housing Authority asked the town for $13,000 in operations funding.

oak-creek/11.title: School running track condition and nuisance abatement
oak-creek/11.summary: The board planned to discuss the condition of the running track with the South Routt school district, and later discussed nuisance abatement actions in town.

ophir/0.title: Ban on short-term rentals (Ordinance 2026-7)
ophir/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission recommended 3-0 an ordinance amending Section 303.1 of the Land Use Code to make leasing short-term rentals unlawful, citing impacts on town services, neighbors and the town's limited housing stock. P&Z also discussed what minimum rental length should count, with one member suggesting anything under 63 days, and was to review a full draft from the Town.

ophir/1.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code and new exterior material rules
ophir/1.summary: Ophir must adopt the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code under state law (deadline noted as May). P&Z has reviewed wildfire-resistant siding, such as wood-styled cement board, and in October considered new exterior material requirements for siding, garage doors, decking and fences that comply with the code.

ophir/2.title: Revegetation ordinance for soil disturbance
ophir/2.summary: A draft ordinance would require a revegetation plan before any soil disturbance, including construction, septic, utility and road work, to protect native plants and pollinators, with penalties for non-compliance. P&Z recommended approval 5-0 in March, with the construction fencing requirement removed, after discussing an approved seed list.

ophir/3.title: Dark Sky and lighting ordinance
ophir/3.summary: A draft Dark Sky/Lighting Ordinance was reviewed by P&Z, which recommended approval 5-0 in March 2026.

ophir/4.title: Variance for side setbacks and 2/12 roof pitch on Aurum Street
ophir/4.summary: An applicant requested a variance to cut required side yard setbacks from 15 feet to 10 feet and to allow a 2/12 roof pitch for new construction on Lots 1 and 2, Block 2 on Aurum Street. The applicant presented the request to P&Z in March 2026, and approval would also involve the General Assembly.

ophir/5.title: Fence rules and the Bobtail Street fence
ophir/5.summary: P&Z considered whether a fence on Lots 5 and 6, Block 4 is a permitted accessory use to the residence on Lots 7 and 8, and decided new fencing needed neither a variance nor a Special Use Permit. It then took up fencing materials for a new fence at 112 Bobtail Street, and earlier discussed whether neighbor permission should be required for fences.

ophir/6.title: Residential building plan reviews
ophir/6.summary: P&Z reviewed building plans for the Aplin and Kondracki home on Bobtail Street, the Croke residence on Granite Street (recommended 4-0) and the Cooper residence on Aurum Street. Reviews check setbacks, parking, exterior materials and fire safety.

ophir/7.title: Low Energy and Carbon Code presentation
ophir/7.summary: EcoAction Partners was scheduled to give P&Z a 30-minute presentation on a Low Energy & Carbon Code in June 2026.

ophir/8.title: Wood stove permits and parking rules
ophir/8.summary: P&Z discussed requiring permits for replacement wood stoves, with free application and review. It also discussed parking spaces placed where roofs shed snow, and limiting parking of vehicles and boats to spaces or town rights-of-way.

ordway/0.title: Toni Evans annexation and zoning
ordway/0.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on Aug. 10, 2026 on a petition by Toni Evans to annex land into Ordway, and the trustees adopted resolutions on eligibility and the petition. A second reading of the annexation and zoning ordinances (#673 and #674) followed on Oct. 5. A separate 'Addies' annexation was also recommended and approved to move forward.

ordway/1.title: Water moratorium and water restrictions
ordway/1.summary: Council denied a water restrictions resolution in April, then approved Resolution 2026-07 in June placing a moratorium on additional water services. Water reports, well output and a town water restructuring were also discussed.

ordway/2.title: CIRSA coverage and settlement over former town attorney's contract change
ordway/2.summary: Documents in August include a CIRSA coverage letter and a settlement agreement, release and assignment. They concern losses the Town says began in 2022 after the former town attorney amended a water-rate contract and allegedly failed to advise the Town correctly. A malpractice lawsuit and a receivership are mentioned.

ordway/3.title: Historic preservation, Certified Local Government status and cemetery board
ordway/3.summary: Council advanced ordinances to establish a Certified Local Government and a Historic Preservation Advisory Authority, and created a cemetery board. A further historic preservation ordinance (#675) had a first reading in October, and a cemetery grant is moving forward.

ordway/4.title: 428 E. 3rd Street town-owned property sale and foreclosure
ordway/4.summary: Council considered resolutions in March authorizing the sale of town-owned property, including 428 East 3rd Street. In May and June it discussed the property in executive session and talked about restarting foreclosure.

ordway/5.title: Tax certificates, demolition and property requests on Arkansas, Idaho and E. 3rd
ordway/5.summary: In October the board approved negotiating tax certificates for 305, 317 and 319 Arkansas and 326 Idaho. It approved a demolition application at 318 E 3rd and an extension request for 215 E 4th Street. Discussion of 629 Idaho was postponed. An agreement on future affordable housing development was also on the agenda.

ordway/6.title: Street improvements, comprehensive plan and Old Pharmacy
ordway/6.summary: The town held a kickoff with the State for street improvements and is updating its comprehensive plan. It also discussed extending 1st Street, a master plan for the Old Pharmacy building, and a Stantec visit.

ordway/7.title: Fire department invoices and funding
ordway/7.summary: In June the town discussed a county invoice to the fire department, which will pay past due invoices with a subsidy. Workers' compensation for the fire department and Air Med Care membership were also discussed.

ordway/8.title: Budget, raises and health insurance
ordway/8.summary: The town held a preliminary budget work session on Oct. 19, approved a health insurance company, and approved 3% personnel raises in August.

ordway/9.title: Community library agreement
ordway/9.summary: Council approved a revised Community Library intergovernmental agreement in September after library discussion in April.

ouray-county/0.title: Land Use Code rewrite: definitions, ADUs and special use permits
ouray-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission is working through a multi-section rewrite of the county Land Use Code under Resolution 2024-029. Drafts address accessory dwelling unit size and distance limits (including a 'bonus ADU' concept), agricultural structures needing building permits, and new or revised Special Use Permits for guest lodges, guest ranches, event venues, campgrounds and commercial outdoor recreation. Staff plan to finish Section 2, move to Section 3 (Zoning), and hold a public hearing after revised drafts of Sections 3 and 13.

ouray-county/1.title: Fire flow and water supply definitions for subdivisions and PUDs
ouray-county/1.summary: Staff proposed a broader definition of 'water supply' for PUDs and subdivisions, with minimum fire flow as a narrower requirement. Tri-County Water has said its existing hydrants may not meet minimum fire flow pressure and flow recommendations.

ouray-county/2.title: Water-wise landscaping and artificial turf rules in Zoning Section 3.11
ouray-county/2.summary: Draft Section 3.11 adds state-driven 'water-wise' landscaping requirements for new development, including a broad invasive plant species definition and limits on artificial turf with an exception for athletic fields of play. Staff say the field-of-play wording needs further clarification.

ouray-county/3.title: Yurt limits and Colona zone changes in the zoning draft
ouray-county/3.summary: Staff suggested the Planning Commission and county commissioners consider limiting yurts to one per parcel in the Alpine zone or all zones, to prevent multiple yurts claiming building code exemptions. The draft also adds a 'Commercial Storefront' special use to the Colona Zone.

ouray-county/4.title: Curry subdivision at 1615 County Road 1
ouray-county/4.summary: The Planning Commission holds a public hearing on Kilpin and Sandra Curry's combined preliminary and final development plan to subdivide the parcel into 2 lots. The commission is to make a recommendation to the county commissioners.

ouray-county/5.title: Pastor subdivision exemption at 6549 County Road 24
ouray-county/5.summary: The Planning Commission hears Clifford Pastor's request for an exemption to divide a parcel into 2 lots and will make a recommendation to the county commissioners.

ouray-county/6.title: Joint planning agreement with the City and zoning map updates
ouray-county/6.summary: Staff say 2022 changes to the Joint Planning IGA on annexation authority raised legal and planning concerns that Section 3 may need amending quickly. Staff also proposed keeping overlay district designations off the official zoning map because amending it is a lengthy hearing process.

ouray-county/7.title: Tribal consultation for renewable energy projects
ouray-county/7.summary: Code changes respond to state law on Tribal consultation for renewable energy projects. Staff have contacted the Tribes and will shape the proposed language depending on their replies.

pagosa-springs/0.title: Data center moratorium (Ordinance 1037)
pagosa-springs/0.summary: Council passed a 6-month moratorium on accepting or processing permit and land development applications that include a data center, because the Land Use Development Code has no data center use classification. It must be extended every 6 months to reach the two years Council asked for, giving staff time to watch development statewide and codify rules. First reading was Aug 4 and second reading Aug 18.

pagosa-springs/1.title: 2027 budget, fee schedule and capital plan
pagosa-springs/1.summary: Council and the Sanitation GID reviewed the FY27 budget in September and Council adopted Resolution 2026-21 on Oct 6 with a public hearing. It sets expenditures of $24,536,628 and expenses of $30,594,569 across seven funds, a 1.561 mill levy raising $173,145, fee schedule changes, and a 5-year capital plan including the community center roof, vehicles and park improvements. The GID budget and fee schedule (Resolution 2026-02) were also up for adoption.

pagosa-springs/2.title: Sewer system repairs, McCabe Creek project and new wastewater treatment plant
pagosa-springs/2.summary: The Sanitation GID finished the McCabe Creek sewer replacement (Florida Street) and moved crews to Rosita Street manhole and line replacement. The district bought surge tanks and pumps, applied for a $900,000 grant for the 1st Street lift station, and is seeking an owner's advisor for the new Wastewater Treatment Facility, with an award expected Nov. 3, 2026. It follows the voter-approved sewer sales tax.
pagosa-springs/2.where: McCabe Creek, Florida Street, Rosita Street, 1st Street lift station

pagosa-springs/3.title: Project 64 workforce housing and housing planning
pagosa-springs/3.summary: Staff prepared talking points for Project 64 (formerly Project 102), where the Town won a bid to buy and renovate the property using grants and certificates of participation (COPs). Grants could lower the rents needed to cover the COP payment. The Town and County are also holding joint sessions on a Housing Action Plan, and Council considered an IGA on Proposition 123 shared affordable housing credits.

pagosa-springs/4.title: Ponderosa Mountain subdivision and planned development
pagosa-springs/4.summary: Planning Commission reviewed the Ponderosa major subdivision sketch plan and planned development agreement, and Council took up Ordinance 1042 (planned development agreement and zoning map amendment) on first reading Oct 6, continued to Oct 20.

pagosa-springs/5.title: Talisman Drive area rezoning (Ordinance 1040)
pagosa-springs/5.summary: Council passed Ordinance 1040 on first and second reading, rezoning Cornerstone Lofts and Talisman Pointe properties on Talisman, Eaton and Village Drives to Multi-unit Town Center. Planning Commission recommended approval Aug 25.
pagosa-springs/5.where: Talisman Drive, Eaton Drive, Village Drive

pagosa-springs/6.title: G&I Sanitation trash franchise (Ordinance 1039)
pagosa-springs/6.summary: Council gave first reading Sept 15 and second reading Oct 6 to a five-year franchise for G&I Sanitation Services to run refuse collection in town, with performance standards and a possible future franchise fee. A public hearing on the company's proposed rates was also held.

pagosa-springs/7.title: Dark sky Lighting Management Plan
pagosa-springs/7.summary: The Dark Sky Steering Committee held a work session and review of a Lighting Management Plan that would exceed current Land Use Development Code lighting standards, with rules on light height, shielding, curfews and no flashing lights. Related events include reduced downtown lights for the Perseid meteor shower watch night and an astronomy shed proposal.

pagosa-springs/8.title: Traffic, truck parking and calming on San Juan Alley
pagosa-springs/8.summary: Resident Eddie Archuleta repeatedly told Council that truckers park overnight in the library lot, the jake brake ordinance is not enforced, and San Juan Alley sees heavy speeding traffic. Staff recommended against a speed dip on San Juan Alley between 8th and 10th Streets based on neighbor feedback and are drafting a traffic calming policy.
pagosa-springs/8.where: San Juan Alley, library parking lot

pagosa-springs/9.title: Naming of San Juan River Park at 1040 E US 160
pagosa-springs/9.summary: Council voted to name the former Bob's LP/Basin Coop property, bought in May 2025, San Juan River Park instead of the Parks Board's recommended Gateway River Park. Staff may add other names later.

pagosa-springs/10.title: Town Manager contract extension
pagosa-springs/10.summary: After an executive session on the Town Manager's evaluation, Council moved to extend David Harris's contract, with Council Member Martinez and Mayor Pierce to craft the extension.

palisade/0.title: Draft 2027 Town of Palisade budget
palisade/0.summary: Staff presented the draft 2027 budget to the Board of Trustees as required by state law. The board was asked to set the public hearing to adopt the final budget for November 10, 2026.

palisade/1.title: 2027 special event calendar and blackout dates (Resolution 2026-17)
palisade/1.summary: The Board of Trustees was to consider Resolution 2026-17, approving the 2027 special event calendar and blackout dates.

palisade/2.title: Watershed wildfire mitigation presentation from Colorado State Forest Service
palisade/2.summary: The Colorado State Forest Service was scheduled to present on watershed wildfire mitigation and coordination with the town.

palisade/3.title: Tourism Advisory Commission interviews and appointment
palisade/3.summary: The board was to interview candidates and appoint a commissioner to the Tourism Advisory Commission by roll call vote.

palisade/4.title: Fall Town Cleanup Day and Trick-or-Treat Street events
palisade/4.summary: Fall Town Cleanup Day is Saturday, October 17 from 8 am to noon at the Riverbend Park parking lot, or until dumpsters are full. Trick-or-Treat Street and Touch a Truck is Friday, October 30.

palmer-lake/0.title: Temporary data center moratorium (Resolution 31-2026)
palmer-lake/0.summary: The Board of Trustees had Resolution 31-2026 on its September 10 agenda for discussion and possible action on a temporary moratorium on data centers. The documents do not state the outcome.

palmer-lake/1.title: Buc-ee's annexation withdrawal and related negotiations
palmer-lake/1.summary: The Board met in executive session on discussions and negotiations with the landowner's counsel and counsel for Buc-ee's following withdrawal of the annexation request. Later agendas also include executive sessions on a proposed lease with option to purchase Town property.

palmer-lake/2.title: Town-wide bear-proof trash ordinance
palmer-lake/2.summary: The Planning Commission discussed a mandatory town-wide bear-proof container requirement, certified receptacles, and CPW grants, and planned a workshop before making a recommendation. The Board's October 22 agenda includes Ordinance 6-2026 on bear mitigation and enforcement. A resident asked for strict enforcement.

palmer-lake/3.title: Water restrictions and stage one water emergency
palmer-lake/3.summary: The town remains under a stage one water emergency; an outdoor watering ban and seasonal changes cut demand by 25% and allowed a shift to the Denver well. A resident raised concern about how the town communicated the restrictions. Columbine Park plantings were put off until spring because of the restrictions, and a water main is being installed on the Shady Lane project.

palmer-lake/4.title: 2027 budget and budget workshops
palmer-lake/4.summary: The Town Administrator started 2027 budget projections, froze non-essential spending and new capital projects, and the Board held budget workshops. A draft 2027 budget and 2026 amended budget were up for review with a public hearing date to be set. The Parks Commission is ranking its own 2027 budget requests, and a consolidation of the Water, Roads and Parks departments was proposed.

palmer-lake/5.title: Annexation ordinance declaratory judgment and voter approval
palmer-lake/5.summary: The Board discussed seeking a declaratory judgment to clarify voter-adopted annexation ordinance language. Town boundaries stay frozen without voter approval, so details may need to go back to voters, possibly at a March 2027 special election.

palmer-lake/6.title: Hearing proceedings involving Trustee Roger Moseley and legal costs
palmer-lake/6.summary: The Town has retained a hearing officer and is finalizing a presenting officer agreement to schedule hearings pertaining to Trustee Roger Moseley. Trustees also questioned town attorney invoices and legal service costs, and a Lyons Gaddis check was pulled from the consent agenda.

palmer-lake/7.title: New Board policies and handbook
palmer-lake/7.summary: The Board took up several policies by resolution: Board handbook, code of ethics, capital project contracting, financial management, agenda setting, social media and snow removal.

palmer-lake/8.title: Centennial Park lake, pickleball courts and dogs
palmer-lake/8.summary: The Parks Commission reviewed a proposal for no-fishing zones at Centennial Park Lake and found no reason to restrict licensed anglers. Flooding, curbing and dogs at the pickleball courts remain on agendas, and Awake the Lake presented park ideas.

palmer-lake/9.title: Creek Week, poison hemlock and weed mitigation
palmer-lake/9.summary: The Board proclaimed Creek Week (Sept 26 to Oct 4, 2026) with the Fountain Creek Watershed District, including a joint Palmer Lake cleanup. The Parks Commission is working on poison hemlock and noxious weed control in Glen Park.
palmer-lake/9.where: Glen Park and Fountain Creek watershed

palmer-lake/10.title: Parks projects: Elephant Rock pavilion, pocket park, Crawford fence, playground
palmer-lake/10.summary: The Parks Commission is considering renovating the Elephant Rock open pavilion, a pocket park at Lovers Lane and Hermosa (pending Board review), repair of the Crawford memorial fence, CIRSA playground inspection recommendations, and volunteer service days and grant projects.
palmer-lake/10.where: Elephant Rock, Lovers Lane and Hermosa, Glen Park

palmer-lake/11.title: Motorized vehicles on Palmer Lake trails
palmer-lake/11.summary: Motorized vehicle restrictions on trails were on the Parks Commission agenda and mentioned in the Administrator's report.

palmer-lake/12.title: Lakeview lots conservation easement donation
palmer-lake/12.summary: The Board agenda included a conservation easement and donation of about 140 platted lots in Lakeview.

paonia/0.title: Short-term rental rules and the Common Ground Ordinance
paonia/0.summary: An ad hoc committee is going through the proposed Common Ground short-term rental ordinance section by section. It is working on registration with no numerical cap, a fee set by the Board and limited to administrative cost, owner-occupancy verification, tax compliance, self-certified safety, a local contact and liability insurance. Survey comments leaned cautious, with concerns about housing, noise, parking and water. The Board has extended the facilitator's contract through 2026 and the committee's scope has been expanded.

paonia/1.title: Stage 2 water restrictions and water supply
paonia/1.summary: After unusually high water use, the Board considered Stage 2 restrictions under Resolution 19-26 on August 18. The reported treated-water storage would last about eight days without restrictions. Hand and drip watering of gardens was allowed. Residents spoke about watering methods, fire hazards from dried lawns and penalties. On August 25 the Board asked for regular updates on tank levels and production, and on October 13 it was to consider Resolution 22-26 rescinding the restrictions.

paonia/2.title: Water projects: Raw Water Monitoring, Western Loop, trailer court
paonia/2.summary: The Board approved Amendment 2 to the RESPEC agreement for construction engineering on the Raw Water Monitoring Project, which includes meters to track water production. Staff also reported on the Western Loop water line easements and routes, water improvements at Lee's Trailer Court, and grants to protect Town springs from wildfire. A closed session on October 26 was set to discuss the Town's water rights.

paonia/3.title: Berg Foundation rezoning of 218 4th Street
paonia/3.summary: The Carl E. Berg Foundation applied to rezone 218 4th Street from Public District to C-2 so a project could proceed. Staff and the Planning Commission recommended approval. One speaker supported it, saying it would reactivate a long-underused building. The Foundation was scheduled to make a presentation to the Board on September 15.

paonia/4.title: David Warren rezoning application
paonia/4.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on David Warren's rezoning application on August 3. The Town Board continued the hearing from August 25 to its September 8 meeting.

paonia/5.title: Estate zoning density changes
paonia/5.summary: Staff found an inconsistency in Estate Zoning Table 16-2 and suggested allowing 1.5 to two acres per dwelling to support the Comprehensive Plan's density goals. The Board sent the issue to a work session and a revised ordinance. It was also on the September 1 agenda.

paonia/6.title: Housing Needs Assessment and SB24-174 addendum
paonia/6.summary: The Board took up an SB24-174 housing addendum to the 2023 Housing Needs Assessment and Housing Action Plan. The state housing department had given conditional approval and asked for more information.

paonia/7.title: Sewer tap fee waiver for septic users
paonia/7.summary: The Board discussed waiving sewer tap fees for septic tank users. Ordinance 02-26 was considered as an emergency sewer tap fee waiver, and the Board also discussed incentives to connect to the sewer system.

paonia/8.title: Town Administrator search and Police Chief appointment
paonia/8.summary: The Board reviewed proposals from executive search firms under RFP 26-03 and considered approving a search profile for the Town Administrator. An interim administrator is currently serving. The Board was also to consider appointing a Police Chief on October 13.

paonia/9.title: 2027 budget
paonia/9.summary: Staff are developing the 2027 budget. It was presented October 13 and was the subject of an October 21 work session. Employee insurance benefits were also on the September 15 agenda.

paonia/10.title: Town Hall roof and solar panels
paonia/10.summary: The Board was to consider a Town Hall roof replacement bid and a quote to have Empower remove the solar panels from Town Hall. A presentation on upgrading the panels was also on the September 1 agenda.

paonia/11.title: Town code rewrite and new ordinances
paonia/11.summary: The Town is rewriting its code through a recodification project, and the Board considered renewing the Sustainable Futures contract. It is reviewing consolidated ordinances, including a single nuisance ordinance, combined juvenile loitering and curfew rules, and solid waste rules (Ordinance 01-26). It is also considering repealing the business sidewalk-use ordinance, amending the animal code, and a tobacco sales ordinance (06-26). Ordinances from rejected citizen initiative petitions were also on the agenda.

paonia/12.title: West Fourth Street overlay and Safe Streets plan
paonia/12.summary: The Board approved an agreement with Delta County for a two-inch asphalt overlay on West Fourth Street, limited by the County's roughly $25,000 project cap. Consor Engineering was also to present traffic data for the Safe Streets for All safety action plan.

paonia/13.title: Street lights, dark skies and trail lights
paonia/13.summary: The Board put on its agenda a discussion of removing street lights and another on dark skies and trail lights. An ADA transition plan and eliminating liquor license distance requirements for certain classes were also on the October 20 agenda.

parachute/0.title: Data center regulations (Ordinance 838-2026)
parachute/0.summary: Town Council is set to consider Ordinance No. 838-2026, which would amend Title 15 of the municipal code to regulate data centers and technology facilities. It was on the October 15, 2026 agenda with a cover memo; the documents do not state an outcome.

parachute/1.title: Prop 123 expedited review for affordable housing (Ordinance 837-2026)
parachute/1.summary: The Council is considering a Title 15 amendment adding Section 15.02.214 to create expedited review for affordable housing under Prop 123 and updating the land use review procedures chart. The Planning Commission recommended approval. In July the council also heard a regional housing needs assessment from an Aspen analyst.

parachute/2.title: 2026 and 2027 town budget
parachute/2.summary: Council held a 2026 budget workshop in late 2025, including an employee benefits package assessment. A 2027 budget kickoff took place in September 2026, and the draft 2027 budget with a 2027-2031 capital improvement plan was presented October 15. Council also discussed sales tax ballot initiative options in February.

parachute/3.title: Highway 6 and 1st Street "Parachute Moves" reconstruction project
parachute/3.summary: Council backed multiple grant applications for the Highway 6 and 1st Street mobility, revitalization, reconstruction and safety project, including a USDOT BUILD grant, congressionally directed spending, and HUD funding. The town was later noted as recipient of a $600,000 CDBG grant for the 1st Street project, and committed local match dollars to a federal grant in October.

parachute/4.title: Water system: raw water tank, loan refinance and Stage 2 restrictions
parachute/4.summary: Council supported a DOLA grant for the raw water tank replacement and approved a loan amendment on the water enterprise loan with Alpine Bank (Ordinance 833-2026). Stage 2 water restrictions remained in place in May 2026. Council also celebrated the Shoshone instream flow agreement and later considered a resolution on the Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act with a water consultant report.

parachute/5.title: Town purchase of 147 1st Street from Qwest/Lumen
parachute/5.summary: Council considered Ordinance 834-2026 approving a contract to buy the property at 147 1st Street from Qwest Corporation. By May 2026 the town reported the purchase had closed and it was town-owned.

parachute/6.title: Parachute Area Transit System and bus service
parachute/6.summary: Council approved a services agreement with Glenwood Downtowner for public transit operations and a license agreement with Flix Bus for a bus stop. It also supported a state transit grant application and a regional transit planning grant in June 2026. Riders can use the ridepats.com app.

parachute/7.title: Community center and Senior Center future use
parachute/7.summary: The Valley Senior Center president asked Council in February to make the Senior Center more of a community center and noted the need for funding. In July 2026 Council reviewed a draft Community Center Management Plan with a rental agreement and liability waiver.
parachute/7.where: Parachute Community Center / Valley Senior Center

parachute/8.title: Wildland Urban Interface fire code and landscaping turf rules
parachute/8.summary: Council took up Ordinance 836-2026 revising and adopting the Wildland Urban Interface Fire Code in Title 15. Earlier, Ordinance 835-2026 added restrictions on nonfunctional artificial turf and invasive plant species in development projects.

parachute/9.title: Household pet limits ordinance (831-2025)
parachute/9.summary: Council approved Ordinance 831-2025 on animal rules and impound fines, amended to remove any household pet limits.

parachute/10.title: 6670 Transmission Line rebuild and Xcel easement
parachute/10.summary: Council held a special use review hearing for reconstruction of a public utility transmission line (6670 Transmission Line). In July it also considered a temporary construction easement for Xcel Energy. A solar project expansion of 50 acres at Straight Bottom Ranch was also noted.

parachute/11.title: Fun House Kids special use review at 201 East 1st Street
parachute/11.summary: Council scheduled a public hearing on Resolution 2026-39, a special use review for Fun House Kids LLC at 201 East 1st Street.

park-county/0.title: Fairplay landfill financial assurance and Land and Water Trust Fund contingency
park-county/0.summary: Commissioners adopted Resolution 2026-40 directing the county to identify a qualifying financial assurance mechanism for the Fairplay landfill, with conditions before any dedicated sales tax revenue is used. On Aug. 18 they approved Resolution 2026-44 raising the Landfill Contingency from $1,750,000. The Land and Water Trust Fund Board also reviewed a county landfill application and new application rules.

sources.body: Land and Water Trust Fund Board
Land and Water Trust Fund Board

park-county/1.title: County manager termination
park-county/1.summary: After an executive session on a personnel matter, commissioners ratified Resolution 2026-47 terminating the county manager. On Sept. 8 they approved Resolution 2026-48 amending it solely to correct statutory citations. A work session also took up delegation of duties for administration.

park-county/2.title: 634 County Road 62 agrotourism camping permit (Bez CUP A26-0021)
park-county/2.summary: The Advisory Board on the Environment raised wildlife, wetland, water-supply and flood concerns about a regenerative agrotourism business with cabins and bell tent sites on a 161-acre parcel. Setback variances were also requested. Commissioners backed conditional approval with seven conditions, added septic review and a flood evacuation plan, and approved Resolution 2026-50 on Oct. 6.

sources.body: Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments

park-county/3.title: 2027 county budget
park-county/3.summary: The commissioners reviewed the 2026 bi-annual budget and held department budget presentations for 2027. They adopted the proposed 2027 budget on Oct. 15 in a 2-0 vote. The Land and Water Trust Fund Board also reviewed its own 2027 budget.

sources.body: Land and Water Trust Fund Board
Land and Water Trust Fund Board

park-county/4.title: Emergency culvert and road repairs: CR 43, Deer Creek and Harris Park
park-county/4.summary: Commissioners approved $500,050 for emergency road work in Harris Park. They also approved Land and Water Trust Fund money for an emergency Deer Creek culvert repair (Resolution 2026-49) and a bid for emergency replacement of twin 72-inch culverts on County Road 43. CR 43 repairs were slated for a further public update.
park-county/4.where: Harris Park, Deer Creek, County Road 43

sources.body: Land and Water Trust Fund Board

park-county/5.title: Environmental blight ordinance (Ordinance 6, 2026)
park-county/5.summary: The county moved through readings of a new Ordinance 6 prohibiting accumulation of environmental blight in unincorporated areas. It replaces the 1991 ordinance, and commissioners approved the final reading Sept. 1.

park-county/6.title: Property tax valuation appeals and abatements
park-county/6.summary: After Board of Equalization hearings, commissioners adopted Resolution 2026-42 upholding valuations except one parcel, reduced from $1,106,396. They reconsidered abatement decisions for two schedules, with a $15,000 per acre alternative discussed. They granted 2024 and 2025 abatements for Circle C Ranch Tarryall LLC and continued hearings for other owners.

park-county/7.title: Bailey Water and Sanitation District site at 19 County Road 64A
park-county/7.summary: Commissioners approved Resolution 2026-45 for a conditional use permit and Resolution 2026-46 for a minor subdivision for the Bailey Water and Sanitation District.

park-county/8.title: Down to Earth minor subdivision and Overlook St right-of-way vacation
park-county/8.summary: Commissioners directed staff to write a resolution for the Down to Earth minor subdivision at 1525 Venture Road, including a 25-foot access easement, then approved it as Resolution 2026-51. They remanded a request to vacate 14 feet of the 30-foot Overlook St right-of-way at 128 Overlook St to the Planning Department.
park-county/8.where: 1525 Venture Road, Fairplay; 128 Overlook St, Harris Park Estates

park-county/9.title: Google North state-assessed property and fire pond next steps
park-county/9.summary: Commissioners scheduled discussion of the state assessment of Google North, Inc., and continued reviewing next steps for a county fire pond.

park-county/10.title: Advisory board changes and Planning Commission removal
park-county/10.summary: Commissioners adopted policies for appointed advisory boards and held a public hearing item on removing a member of the Planning Commission, listed again Oct. 20.

park-county/11.title: Rezoning and plat cases before the Planning Commission
park-county/11.summary: Pending cases include the McMillan rezoning from Residential, the Yoder common plat amendment combining lots, and the Lostfork PUD amendment at 49355 Hwy 285 combining with 373 County Rd 62. The rezoning requested a continuance.
park-county/11.where: Grant and other Park County locations

sources.body: Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments
Planning Commission and Board of Adjustments

park-county/12.title: Planning fee schedule update
park-county/12.summary: A resolution amending Planning and Zoning land use application fees was postponed to a future date.

park-county/13.title: South Park International Dark Sky designation and heritage projects
park-county/13.summary: The Heritage Area Board reported on an International Dark Sky preserve application focused on Eleven Mile State Park, with letters of support sought. Commissioners also approved a Paris Mill construction agreement with High Country Haulers and reviewed a historic preservation plan.
park-county/13.where: Eleven Mile State Park, Paris Mill, South Park

sources.body: South Park National Heritage Area Board

park-county/14.title: Sheriff's authority over fees for firearms safety course eligibility cards (Senate Bill 25-003)
park-county/14.summary: On July 28, 2026, the Park County commissioners voted 3-0 to approve Resolution 2026-41. It acknowledges the Park County Sheriff's statutory authority over fees for firearms safety course eligibility card applications under Senate Bill 25-003, pending final judicial determination. The minutes do not record any public comment on the item.

parker/0.title: Nine-month moratorium on drone dispatch and delivery facilities
parker/0.summary: Council passed an emergency ordinance on July 20, 2026 pausing applications for land use approvals or building permits for commercial drone dispatch and delivery facilities for nine months. Council affirmed it with first reading on Aug 3 and second reading on Aug 17; no public comment was received on second reading.

parker/1.title: Axon drone-as-first-responder and license plate reader programs
parker/1.summary: Police are proposing to adopt Axon's countywide Drone as First Responder and License Plate Reader programs, which would raise the Axon contract by about $175,000 a year. Council discussed transparency, accountability and video retention. A resident separately asked the Town to remove Flock cameras around Parker.

parker/2.title: Parker 2050 Comprehensive Plan adoption
parker/2.summary: The Planning Commission held a hearing on the Town's 2050 Comprehensive Plan in September, and Council adopted it by Resolution 26-060 on Sept 21 after a presentation by consultant CushingTerrell. The Planning Commission also took up the 2026 Three-Mile Area Plan in October.

parker/3.title: 2027 Town budget
parker/3.summary: Council held a budget workshop on Oct 2 and the proposed 2027 budget was published Oct 13. Council reviewed it at a study session on Oct 26 ahead of a public hearing on Nov 2 and adoption planned for Nov 16. Related items include a redesign of property and liability risk coverage, new funds, and Parker/Lone Tree agreements.

parker/4.title: Speeding, drag racing and teen disturbances in neighborhoods and parks
parker/4.summary: Residents complained of teens speeding and damaging O'Brien Park, drag racing on Victorian Drive and Longs Way, and littering, saying enforcement is lacking. Another resident asked for a traffic study on speeding on Mainstreet between Jordan Road and Twenty Mile Road.
parker/4.where: O'Brien Park, Victorian Drive, Longs Way, Mainstreet

parker/5.title: Future of Mainstreet as a pedestrian street
parker/5.summary: Two residents urged Council to turn Mainstreet into a pedestrian-only street for gatherings, citing safety and downtown culture.

parker/6.title: School resource officer agreement with American Academy
parker/6.summary: Council discussed American Academy's request for a school resource officer and reconsideration of the cost division, then on Sept 21 approved an amended agreement for SRO services for the 2026-2027 school year.

parker/7.title: Salisbury Regional Park Phase 2
parker/7.summary: The new 91-acre park's Phase 2 needs water service, and Council approved a water pipeline easement to Parker Water and Sanitation District. The Planning Commission and Council also considered the Phase 2 site plan amendment near Motsenbocker Road and Todd Drive.
parker/7.where: Salisbury Regional Park, southeast of Motsenbocker Road

parker/8.title: Security guard, massage facility and licensing ordinance rewrites
parker/8.summary: The Town is rewriting its security guard ordinance (Chapter 5.06, last amended in 2004) and merchant patrol rules, and repealed and readopted the massage facility chapter (5.10) under new state law. Council set massage license fees by Resolution 26-070 and also took up a related chapter 5.09 rewrite.

parker/9.title: Wildlife exclusion fencing for plant nurseries
parker/9.summary: A plant nursery asked to install deer fencing about eight feet tall, which the Land Development Ordinance limits to six feet. Council showed general support and staff returned Oct 19 seeking direction on amending the rules.

parker/10.title: Sign enforcement and code enforcement ordinance changes
parker/10.summary: Council and the Planning Commission considered Land Development Ordinance changes on enforcement, waivers and temporary signs.

parker/11.title: Twenty Mile Road improvements land acquisition
parker/11.summary: Council introduced an ordinance stating the Town's intent to acquire property interests to construct and improve Twenty Mile Road near E-470 and to notify affected owners.

parker/12.title: Parker Road and Hilltop Road intersection improvements
parker/12.summary: Council awarded a $1,339,679.75 contract to Denver Dirt Works for the intersection improvements. Council also approved added funds for Pine Drive reconstruction and the townwide resurfacing program.

parker/13.title: Parker Senior Center feasibility study and facility needs
parker/13.summary: Staff briefed Council on a completed feasibility study and facility needs including drainage, flooring and parking lot repairs. No funding was requested.

parker/14.title: Parker Heritage Center interpretive plan and tribal history
parker/14.summary: Council reviewed an interpretive plan to reimagine the Heritage Center, with $100,000 budgeted plus a $7,500 grant. It also discussed ways to honor Parker's Tribal history.

phillips-county/0.title: Regulations for wind, solar, battery storage and data center facilities
phillips-county/0.summary: The commissioners took up draft regulations covering wind energy, solar, battery energy storage and data center facilities on the Aug. 20 agenda. The same meeting canceled a Land Use Code public hearing. The documents do not state any outcome.

phillips-county/1.title: 2027 county budget
phillips-county/1.summary: A draft 2027 budget schedule was reviewed July 31. Budget work sessions were scheduled after the meetings on Sept. 9, Sept. 29, Oct. 9 and Oct. 19.

phillips-county/2.title: Landfill equipment purchase and landfill rates
phillips-county/2.summary: The landfill manager presented an equipment purchase on Aug. 20. Landfill rates were on the Aug. 31 agenda. The documents give no amounts or decisions.

phillips-county/3.title: Floodplain ordinance first reading
phillips-county/3.summary: A floodplain ordinance was scheduled for first reading on Oct. 19.

phillips-county/4.title: Housing needs assessment and water supply element RFQ
phillips-county/4.summary: The county considered a request for qualifications for a housing needs assessment and a water supply element on Oct. 9.

phillips-county/5.title: Viaero roadway occupancy agreements
phillips-county/5.summary: Roadway occupancy agreements with Viaero came up on Aug. 31 and again on Oct. 9. These govern use of county road right-of-way.

phillips-county/6.title: Road and Bridge propane contracts and equipment
phillips-county/6.summary: Road and Bridge brought a CHS propane contract on Sept. 29, propane contracts on Oct. 9, and a cutting edges equipment purchase on Sept. 29.

phillips-county/7.title: Fairgrounds entrance asphalt replacement
phillips-county/7.summary: A project payment for replacing asphalt at the fairgrounds entrance was on the Oct. 19 agenda. A Fair Board appointment was also on the Sept. 29 agenda.

phillips-county/8.title: Department of Human Services contract and carpet bids
phillips-county/8.summary: The DHS director presented a contract on Aug. 20. Carpet bids for DHS were on the Sept. 21 agenda.

phillips-county/9.title: Homeland Security grant
phillips-county/9.summary: The emergency manager presented on a Homeland Security Grant on July 31. A grant closeout letter was acknowledged Sept. 9.

phillips-county/10.title: Sheriff purchase request
phillips-county/10.summary: Sheriff David Romero brought a purchase request to the commissioners on Aug. 31. The documents do not say what was requested.

phillips-county/11.title: Minor land use change hearing and economic development
phillips-county/11.summary: A public hearing on a minor land use change for Jason Roberts was held Sept. 21. The commissioners also heard from economic development staff and a letter of support for the NoCo Foundation.

pitkin/0.title: 2026 Zoning Code adoption and the RV park fight
pitkin/0.summary: The Board worked through a full Zoning Code rewrite from November 2025 through February 2026, with public hearings in January. Residents argued over an RV park provision and Planned Development "mixed uses" wording, and the board agreed to remove the RV Park section and strike the "mixed uses" wording. Some trustees and residents said the code was not ready to pass.

pitkin/1.title: Western Slope Towers radio tower lease with Gunnison Met Rec
pitkin/1.summary: The Board reviewed a lease for marketing tower services on the town's radio tower site. Western Slope wanted 18 months at no charge, and the mayor thought the payment was too low. Concerns included the 2,500 square foot site size and a site cleanup clause. By February the board discussed final terms and heard no public comments.

pitkin/2.title: 2025 budget amendment, 2026 budget and mill levy
pitkin/2.summary: The Board amended the 2025 street maintenance budget, which had been $15,000 but had already spent $20,261.40, and the amendment was later raised further. After public hearings it adopted the 2026 budget and the property tax levy by resolution on Dec. 11. Stipends for the Environmental Health Agent, the Streets/Ditches Commissioner and Zoning Board members were also discussed.

pitkin/3.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code adoption
pitkin/3.summary: The state requires the town to adopt a Wildfire Resiliency Code by April 1, 2026, with enforcement starting July 1, 2026. The Board planned public hearings for early 2026, and a wildfire mitigation seminar was noted in April.

pitkin/4.title: On-site wastewater (OWTS) regulations update
pitkin/4.summary: After a public hearing on Nov. 19, 2025, the Board adopted Ordinance 1 of 2025 updating on-site wastewater treatment system regulations as required by state rules. The town also appointed Joshua Ackerman as its Environmental Health Agent.

pitkin/5.title: Pond operations agreement with Colorado Parks and Wildlife and ditch work
pitkin/5.summary: The Board considered a 5-year operations and maintenance agreement involving a pond that CPW would keep stocking. The mayor relayed concerns that the pond could be drained into the ditch. The Board also weighed an RFP for cleaning about 600 feet of fire and irrigation ditches.

pitkin/6.title: Open Board seats and Zoning Board vacancy
pitkin/6.summary: The Board declared two Board member positions open in April 2026, and a Zoning Board seat expiring at the end of April was posted. It also reappointed the Town Clerk/Treasurer and Town Attorney.

platteville/0.title: Regional water supply: NISP, Windy Gap and Chimney Hollow briefing
platteville/0.summary: Before the Oct. 6 meeting, trustees held a study session on water acquisition and got a legal briefing on regional water projects. Topics included the Northern Integrated Supply Project (NISP) status and participant withdrawals, Windy Gap units being sold by Platte River Power Authority at about $5 million each, uranium mitigation at Chimney Hollow Reservoir, and Colorado River and South Platte compact issues.

platteville/1.title: Affordable housing: needs assessment, expedited review and Proposition 123 commitment
platteville/1.summary: On Oct. 20 the Board is scheduled to consider a Housing Needs Assessment (public hearing, Resolution 2026-20), expedited review policies for affordable housing projects (Resolution 2026-21), and a Proposition 123 commitment for 2027-2029 (Resolution 2026-22).

platteville/2.title: 2027 draft budget presentation
platteville/2.summary: The Oct. 6 agenda includes a 2027 draft budget presentation, with Parks, Trees and Trails and Economic Development shown as budget areas. No figures appear in the documents.

platteville/3.title: Gray water ordinance 2026-858
platteville/3.summary: Ordinance 2026-858 on gray water is listed on the Oct. 6 consent agenda. The documents give no details of its provisions.

platteville/4.title: Main Street Program Advisory Committee
platteville/4.summary: Resolution 2026-17, concerning a Main Street Program Advisory Committee, is on the Oct. 6 consent agenda.

platteville/5.title: Slip line bid tab
platteville/5.summary: A bid tabulation for slip lining work, which typically means pipe rehabilitation, is on the Oct. 6 consent agenda. The documents give no location or amount.

pueblo-county/0.title: Aspen Acres Fire disaster emergency, recovery and flood mitigation
pueblo-county/0.summary: The commissioners have repeatedly renewed the local disaster declaration for the Aspen Acres Fire, which began around June 29, 2026. It has affected over 101,965 acres and destroyed about 240 homes and 9 businesses. The county has applied for federal watershed protection aid, accepted a grant for flooding and debris-flow measures, and approved an MOU for fire mitigation projects. A Stage-2 open fire ban was also continued.

pueblo/0.title: Speed safety camera (automated enforcement) program
pueblo/0.summary: Police Traffic Division presented a plan for photo-radar speed cameras on residential streets, park frontages and designated safety corridors, with projected monthly citation revenue of roughly $302,400 to $504,000 depending on pay rate. A later agenda adds a full-time Automated Enforcement position to Police staffing.

pueblo/1.title: 2027 city budget and public hearing
pueblo/1.summary: Council held departmental budget presentations (Police, Fire, Public Works, IT, Law, Finance, Parks) and reviewed a recommended 2027 budget of $117,785,907, with sales tax at 3.7%. A public hearing on the proposed 2027 budget was set for Oct. 26.

pueblo/2.title: Black Hills Energy electric rate increase
pueblo/2.summary: Council took up a resolution opposing Black Hills Colorado Electric's proposed rate increase and the ratepayer costs of its 2026 Electric Resource Plan and Clean Energy Plan (PUC Proceeding 26A-0333E), with copies to go to the Public Utilities Commission. It was also discussed in work session as a rate case.

pueblo/3.title: Leonardo da Vinci Museum funding and economic development agreement
pueblo/3.summary: Council discussed an economic development agreement and a funding request from the Leonardo da Vinci Museum from the 1/2 cent sales tax fund, which already has a $14 million-plus approval tied to the Regional Tourism Act project replacing the Professional Bull Riders University. The museum leases its building from PURA.

pueblo/4.title: Economic development partner RFP and project prospects
pueblo/4.summary: Council repeatedly reviewed an RFP for an economic development partner, and held closed-door discussions on prospects including Project Tortuga, Project Manta, St. Charles Industrial Park, and an option to purchase for Project Falcon, plus the PEDCO v. City of Pueblo litigation.

pueblo/5.title: Pueblo Masterplan Communities and Jackson Ranch annexations
pueblo/5.summary: Council found the petition to annex the 89.93-acre Pueblo Masterplan Communities Annexation No. 1 valid and referred it to Planning and Zoning. It also took first reading of ordinances zoning Jackson Ranch annexation parcels (250.1, 65.70 and 225.66 acres).
pueblo/5.where: Jackson Ranch and Pueblo Masterplan Communities annexation areas

pueblo/6.title: Twenty-four-month moratorium ordinance
pueblo/6.summary: Council took first reading of an ordinance imposing a 24-month moratorium on accepting applications for and issuing certain new permits or licenses; the condensed text does not state which.

pueblo/7.title: Regional Tourism/transportation authority (RTA) steering committee
pueblo/7.summary: Council reviewed a draft proposal for a broad voting steering committee to shape a regional transportation authority, including an IGA, project list, revenue structure and ballot language, with CDOT and legal advisors as non-voting members.

pueblo/8.title: Airport items: aviation asset defense funding, airline agreement, hangar
pueblo/8.summary: Council moved to establish Project CI2621 Aviation Asset Defense with a $300,000 transfer, and a motion to reconsider it came up at the next work session. Other airport business included an airline operating agreement, a $70,000 contingency for the taxilane rehab and new hangar, a new Airport Policy Advisory board, and a lawsuit with the airport.

pueblo/9.title: Pueblo Library District mill levy
pueblo/9.summary: The Library Foundation told council the library's funding is an existing 2019-approved mill levy and not a new tax or rate increase.

pueblo/10.title: Demolition cost assessment at 125 E. 7th Street
