pueblo/10.summary: Council held a public hearing and approved, as amended with interest raised from 7% to 10%, an ordinance assessing the cost of demolishing dangerous buildings at 125 E. 7th Street.

pueblo/11.title: Emergency sewer and storm sewer repairs
pueblo/11.summary: Council ratified emergency contracts including $210,648.29 for a sewer repair at 109 Vernon Pl, $295,504.20 plus a $62,485.12 change order for a storm sewer repair at 10th and Conley Streets, and smaller repairs at 132 Marian Dr and 31201 Bryan Cir.

pueblo/12.title: Pueblo Mountain Park next steps and blighted property acquisition
pueblo/12.summary: Council scheduled work session talks on next steps for Pueblo Mountain Park and on strategies for acquiring blighted properties under a housing Section 108 project, alongside the Pope Block Building at 301 W. B Street.
pueblo/12.where: Pueblo Mountain Park; 301 W. B Street

pueblo/13.title: BATTLE grant for police
pueblo/13.summary: Council accepted first presentation of a grant funding agreement for the BATTLE team, creating Project PS2605, and heard a work session presentation from the police chief.

rangely/0.title: Geothermal energy campus and proposed data center
rangely/0.summary: Council repeatedly took up the Energy Campus Development & Municipal Participation Study, stage 2 of Rangely's geothermal development. Residents such as Tanner Nielsen and Camille raised concerns about a data center tied to it, including water use, noise, jobs, transparency and NDAs, and one suggested a moratorium. A council member said he spoke with someone at a data center about noise.

rangely/1.title: Stage 3 water shortage and river supply
rangely/1.summary: Low river flow put the Town into Stage 3 water restrictions. The Rangely water conservancy district released 10 cfs from Kenney Reservoir, and the Town manager noted senior upriver water rights. Restrictions later eased back toward stage 1, and council discussed the water ordinance and bulk water customers under Emergency Ordinance 707.

rangely/2.title: White River Regional Water Supply Project storage agreement
rangely/2.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-07 declaring a state of municipal water urgency and a finding of municipal water supply need. It would authorize negotiation, but not execution, of a conditional storage agreement for the White River Regional Water Supply Project.

rangely/3.title: Water and wastewater plant repairs
rangely/3.summary: Staff reported the wastewater plant pond and lagoon liners need replacement, and the water plant has structural issues, with corrosion and a separate structural inspection of rafters and columns. The middle zone water tank re-coating project was proposed for delay, and grants are being sought for the costs.

rangely/4.title: 2027 budget and capital projects
rangely/4.summary: Council held budget and capital project work sessions starting in September and approved the draft 2027 budget as presented in October. A Main Street beautification project was among items under consideration, along with a revision to the Housing Assistance Fund budget.

rangely/5.title: Town Manager contract and outside employment concerns
rangely/5.summary: The Town Manager's contract was on the July agenda. In September a resident raised concerns about the manager, and council members discussed his employment outside of the Town.

rangely/6.title: Bell Street parking and crosswalk safety
rangely/6.summary: Public works repaired sidewalk on west Bell Street, and a No Parking area by the park will extend 50 feet. A resident thanked the Town for the crosswalk but raised sign placement, and a council member worried about the parking ban during events.

rangely/7.title: Police department staffing and leadership
rangely/7.summary: The Town reported two open police positions in August, and an interim police chief, Joseph McGuire, was sworn in in October. Council also amended the fee schedule for certified VIN inspections under Police Services.

rangely/8.title: Grant management contract with Community Centric Development
rangely/8.summary: Council considered engaging the Community Centric Development team at $75 per hour for grant management services.

rico/0.title: Letter of support for Montelores Bridge restoration trail grant
rico/0.summary: The Dolores Ranger District asked the Town of Rico for a letter of support for its 2027 Colorado Parks and Wildlife Non-Motorized Trail Grant application, seeking about $80,000 to repair the Montelores Bridge. The Forest Service wants letters by September 15, 2026, and the Town's support would be limited to endorsing the project. The Council was set to consider approving the letter on September 2, 2026.

ridgway/0.title: Beaver Creek Diversion Restoration and infiltration gallery
ridgway/0.summary: The Town amended its RESPEC engineering contract to $657,312 to redesign the infiltration gallery after the original contractor left it out of scope. In June 2026 Council awarded the gallery work to Meridian Contracting for up to $641,386. The project is funded by NRCS grants and a CWCB loan of up to $8.08 million, with total cost near $4 million.

ridgway/1.title: Housing Action Plan, Proposition 123 and workforce housing
ridgway/1.summary: The Town drafted a Housing Action Plan with five goal areas under state law (SB 24-174), reviewed it with the Planning Commission in August 2026, and scheduled a resolution to adopt it in October. The Home Trust of Ouray County runs regional housing services, and the Town is considering joining Prop 123 for 2027 and exercising a right of first refusal on 683 Frederick St. Council also backed a down payment assistance MOU with the Telluride Foundation and noted the Town's earlier shift of the lodge to workforce housing.

ridgway/2.title: 2026 budget and 2027 budget process
ridgway/2.summary: Council reviewed the draft 2026 budget amid a 22.64% drop in sales tax receipts from 2024, with 2.4% pay movements, and adopted the budget and property tax levies in December 2025. A draft 2027 budget and a schedule for preparing it came up in fall 2026, along with community grant awards of about $98,205 recommended from $117,385 requested.

ridgway/3.title: Wastewater treatment plant renovation and siting
ridgway/3.summary: Town engineer presented a needs assessment for renovating the wastewater treatment plant in May 2026, and a resident urged building the new plant for a 50-60 year life. In September 2026 Council was to discuss and give direction on plant siting options.

ridgway/4.title: Water supply, conservation and drought restrictions
ridgway/4.summary: Residents asked how planning accounts for water as the town grows. Staff pointed to a draft Water Supply Element of the Master Plan amendment. Council also took up lifting Stage 2 mandatory water restrictions and a resolution modifying the Water Conservation and Management Plan.

ridgway/5.title: Tourism strategy and lodging revenue loss
ridgway/5.summary: A Destination Development Mentor Program report said the lodge's conversion to workforce housing reduced lodging tax revenue by about $40,000 and cut sales tax revenue. Council heard a draft destination marketing plan and approved an agreement for visitor and business engagement services.

ridgway/6.title: Wildfire code, fire restrictions and Gold Mountain Fire
ridgway/6.summary: Council introduced an ordinance adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code and other building codes. In summer 2026 it managed Stage 1 and 2 fire restrictions, and a resident thanked the Town for support during the Gold Mountain Fire. The Mayor signed a letter supporting the Governor's disaster declaration request.

ridgway/7.title: Vehicle idling ordinance
ridgway/7.summary: Council considered an ordinance to limit vehicle idling in Chapter 15 of the municipal code in December 2025. In July 2026 a resident asked Council to reconsider addressing the proposed idling ordinance.

ridgway/8.title: Lawsuit over land use code
ridgway/8.summary: In March 2026 Council discussed filing a complaint for declaratory and injunctive relief, citing the importance of defending the land use code and not setting a precedent.

ridgway/9.title: Street closures for events and Clinton Street business concerns
ridgway/9.summary: Council approved closures of Clinton Street for a film shoot, Pride event and other events with no-parking stipulations. A business owner said he got insufficient notice of a Clinton Street closure and asked for business input before closures are approved.

ridgway/10.title: Athletic Park bike park and recreation fee
ridgway/10.summary: The Athletic Park Coalition asked for Town funds to pursue architectural and engineering design for a bike park. Council also considered a letter of support for a proposed recreation fee.

ridgway/11.title: Development applications on Liddell Drive and business parks
ridgway/11.summary: Council scheduled hearings on the Riverbend Townhomes site plan on Liddell Drive, an amended plat for Riverview Business Park, and an amended plat for Northridge Subdivision Lot 2A. It also awarded pre-approved accessory dwelling unit design plans.
ridgway/11.where: Liddell Drive, Riverview Business Park, Northridge Subdivision

ridgway/12.title: Council rules of procedure and public comment decorum
ridgway/12.summary: Council discussed formal procedural rules, time limits for presentations and public comment, and keeping comments on topic. A resident urged calm, respectful meetings.

rifle/0.title: Data center and Bulk Resource Consumer permit rules
rifle/0.summary: Staff began getting inquiries about data centers in Rifle and brought forward a draft Conditional Use Permit pathway for data centers and other 'bulk resource consumers' that use large amounts of electricity and water. The draft would limit them to industrial districts and require utility, water, noise, fiscal and decommissioning analyses, with discretion to deny projects that show no net public benefit. The Planning Commission discussed it in July, August and September, and City Council took it up October 14.

rifle/1.title: Warehouse definitions and other Municipal Code text amendments
rifle/1.summary: Staff proposed splitting the 'warehouse' definition into Local and Regional types (20,000 sq ft threshold) allowed in light industrial and industrial zones, after inquiries about where large warehouses can locate. The package also covers ADU size, height, lot line and variance application requirements and site plan rules. The ADU ordinance was set for a City Council public hearing October 21.

rifle/2.title: Rifle Business Incubator Center branch and 2027 budget
rifle/2.summary: The City asked the Grand Junction Business Incubator Center to price creating and running a Rifle branch focused on downtown startups. The current budget has $100k for it, and the finalized proposal raises the request to $137k, with a USDA grant request mentioned. It was to feed into the Council budget workshop on October 21, 2026.

rifle/3.title: 2026 Water System Improvements Project bid
rifle/3.summary: City Council was asked on October 21 to award the bid for the Rifle 2026 Water System Improvements Project to Martinez Western Constructors Inc. A Water Rights Report was also on the October 14 Council agenda.

rifle/4.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment and housing needs study
rifle/4.summary: Council was asked to consider the city's Proposition 123 commitment of affordable and attainable housing units. The Planning Commission also considered an amended 2025 Rooted in Rifle Housing Needs document.

rifle/5.title: GRIT downtown grants, façade improvements and wayfinding
rifle/5.summary: The GRIT board funded four grant applications totaling $22,200 and considered façade improvement grants for 126 W. 4th Street and ProMex at 233 Railroad Ave. It also discussed downtown wayfinding consultant selection, a proposed Third Street shade structure (about $20,000-$30,000 for roughly 400 sq ft), the 2027 GRIT budget, and a lodging-tax-funded participatory budgeting pilot.

sources.body: Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board
Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board
Greater Rifle Improvement Team (GRIT) Advisory Board

rifle/6.title: Rifle Community Foundation restructuring and grant awards
rifle/6.summary: After the board president's resignation, the Foundation recommended becoming a board under the City instead of a separate 501(c)(3), focused on grant decisions. It reviewed about a dozen grant requests, including $30,000 from Discovery Cafe and $6,250 from Health Solutions West.

rifle/7.title: Parks and Recreation plans, budget and park projects
rifle/7.summary: The Parks board took up the 2027-2028 Strategic Plan, the 2027 budget request, a Metro Pool weather closure policy, and letters of support for grants for the Centennial Park riparian restoration and a CPW outdoor equity program. A skate park comment was on the October agenda, and a bike rack for Rifle Mountain Park was on the list.
rifle/7.where: Rifle parks, Centennial Park, Rifle Mountain Park

rifle/8.title: Recognition plaque request at Rifle Mountain Park
rifle/8.summary: Jim Bell asked to place a recognition plaque by an apple tree between the ice caves. Staff supplied the city's Parks and Facilities Naming Policy, under which the advisory board reviews and City Council gives final approval.

rifle/9.title: Planning hearings on specific properties
rifle/9.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled hearings on a conditional use permit at 214 W 16th St, a CUP at 799 Buckhorn, a variance at 758 Railroad Ave, and a minor subdivision at 1317 E 17th St.
rifle/9.where: 214 W 16th St; 799 Buckhorn; 758 Railroad Ave; 1317 E 17th St

routt-county/0.title: Yampa Valley Gravel Pit special use permit expansion (PL20260026)
routt-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission took up a request to expand the permit boundary of the Yampa Valley Gravel Pit, on the north side of County Road 65. The commissioners considered it on Sept. 29 with a written public comment in the packet, and the Oct. 13 agenda has the chair signing the special use permit.

routt-county/1.title: Routt County 2027 budget
routt-county/1.summary: Commissioners heard 2027 budget presentations from Public Works, Facilities Management and the District Attorney. They then reviewed the proposed 2027 budget, county dues and outside funding requests, and the 2027 health and dental insurance plan. The Tri-County District Attorney personnel budget and the health insurance pool budget also came up.

routt-county/2.title: Nottingham Ranch conservation easement and other PDR projects
routt-county/2.summary: The Purchase of Development Rights board reviewed several projects (222, 224, 225), partly in executive session. Commissioners considered the board's recommendation to put $3,000,000 toward the conservation easement on Nottingham Ranch (Project 222). Projects 224 and 225 went to the commissioners for review on Oct. 20. The board also discussed with county planning how conservation easements affect development under the Unified Development Code.

sources.body: Purchase of Development Rights Board Meetings
Purchase of Development Rights Board Meetings

routt-county/3.title: Milner wastewater matter
routt-county/3.summary: Commissioners planned executive sessions on the Milner wastewater notice, on Sept. 8 and Sept. 22. The agendas give no outcome.

routt-county/4.title: Yampa Valley Airport west terminal expansion grant
routt-county/4.summary: Commissioners were asked to sign Amendment #3 to the FAA grant for the west terminal expansion at Yampa Valley Regional Airport. The airport commission also continues regular capital and budget updates.

routt-county/5.title: Stage 1 fire restrictions
routt-county/5.summary: The county proposed returning to Stage 1 fire restrictions under Ordinance 2026-001 in early September. Commissioners then moved to rescind them on Sept. 29.

routt-county/6.title: Housing financing: private activity bond volume cap with YVHA and CHFA
routt-county/6.summary: Commissioners handled delegation agreements, tax certificates and an inducement resolution (2026-062) tied to Routt County and Yampa Valley Housing Authority's private activity bond volume cap with CHFA.

routt-county/7.title: Proposed instream flow water rights on Lost Dog Creek and Butcher Creek
routt-county/7.summary: The Colorado Water Conservation Board is scheduled to present proposed instream flow water rights on Lost Dog Creek and a second creek to commissioners at an Oct. 19 work session. Commissioners also planned to comment on the draft regional water quality management plan (the 208 Plan).
routt-county/7.where: Lost Dog Creek and Butcher Creek

routt-county/8.title: Small modular reactor proposal electrical needs
routt-county/8.summary: The Planning Commission discussed the electrical needs of an SMR (small modular reactor) proposal after the project application was re-submitted. The minutes give few details.

routt-county/9.title: Certified Local Government status and historic review
routt-county/9.summary: The Historic Preservation Board is finalizing a resolution to make the county a Certified Local Government. It is also doing a historic review of a permit at 54200 CR 62, the Old Charter School site. Separately, the Museum and Heritage board is weighing grants, including $48,500 for a South Routt historic survey.

routt-county/10.title: Sparks residence wastewater variance
routt-county/10.summary: Commissioners were asked to consider a variance for the wastewater treatment system at the Sparks residence.

routt-county/11.title: Aspen Ridge Road garage setback adjustment
routt-county/11.summary: The Board of Adjustment approved a reduced setback adjustment of 2.4 feet for a garage expansion at 31650 Aspen Ridge Road. The original request was 5 ft 9 in. The approval came with conditions, including a plumbing agreement limiting use of the space above.

routt-county/12.title: Property valuation appeals and tax abatements
routt-county/12.summary: The Board of Equalization heard property valuation appeals, including Steamboat Villas Condominiums (Sunterra Steamboat Development LLC) and the Prewitt property. An abatement for the Broadwater property was also considered.

rye/0.title: Water tank inspections, cleaning and updates
rye/0.summary: Council held a special session on Nov. 3 to review water tank inspections and cleaning. Updates on Water Tanks #1, #2 and #3 were on the November and December agendas.

rye/1.title: Sewer main line replacement project
rye/1.summary: The sewer main line replacement capital project was an ongoing update item on the November and December agendas, alongside water treatment plant and infrastructure updates and a brainstorm on removing silt and reeds from the inlet.

rye/2.title: 2026 budget and supplemental appropriation
rye/2.summary: Council began 2026 budget preparation in November. In December the agenda included a 2025 supplemental budget and appropriation (2025-7) and adoption of the 2026 budget (2025-8).

rye/3.title: Intergovernmental agreements with Pueblo County and Colorado City Metro
rye/3.summary: Council took up an agreement with Pueblo County on road maintenance. It also considered a three-party agreement with Pueblo County and Colorado City Metro for a satellite office.

rye/4.title: Safer Routes to School grant
rye/4.summary: Council received an update on the Safer Routes to School grant in November.

rye/5.title: Wildlife-protection refuse ordinance and animal control rules
rye/5.summary: Council reviewed Ordinance 2020-11 on wildlife protection through refuse disposal, including an update on Account #87. It also planned to review the Pueblo County Animal Control Ordinance.

rye/6.title: Lien for unpaid ordinance violation fees (Account #69) and dumpster right-of-way fees
rye/6.summary: Council considered placing a lien on Account #69 for nonpayment of 2022 ordinance violation fees. December's agenda also had dumpster right-of-way service fees.

rye/7.title: EV charging stations and CERT program presentation
rye/7.summary: Matt Akers was scheduled to present on EV charging stations and the Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) program on Nov. 12.

salida/0.title: Temporary moratorium on data center applications
salida/0.summary: Council held the second reading and public hearing on Ordinance 2026-19, a temporary moratorium on submitting, accepting, processing and approving data center applications in Salida. No one spoke at the hearing.

salida/1.title: Short-term rental residency and active-use rules (Ordinance 2026-22)
salida/1.summary: Council amended the short-term rental license rules on residency and annual active use. On Sept. 1, after comments from Paula Givan and Nancy Wallace on the active-use requirement, Council moved to approve the residency amendment and remove the active-use amendment.

salida/2.title: 1st & D Space-to-Create workforce housing MOU with Trellis Housing Partners
salida/2.summary: Council considered a memorandum of understanding with Trellis Housing Partners, LLC for an affordable workforce rental housing project at 233 E. First Street and 102 D Street. The item was pulled from the consent agenda for separate discussion and a motion was made to approve it.
salida/2.where: 233 E. First Street and 102 D Street

salida/3.title: Housing needs and affordable housing agreements
salida/3.summary: Council previewed results of a Housing Needs Assessment on Aug. 17 and approved a Chaffee Housing Trust fee transfer for 8 deed-restricted units in the Two Rivers development. In October it had a regional Proposition 123 affordable housing MOU with Buena Vista, Poncha Springs, Chaffee County and the Chaffee Housing Authority on its agenda.

salida/4.title: 2021 Energy Conservation Code amendments (Ordinance 2026-23)
salida/4.summary: Council amended the city's adoption of the 2021 International Energy Conservation Code. It was approved on first reading Aug. 18, and the Sept. 15 public hearing drew comments from Madelyne Felsch, Felicia Houston, Craig Nielson, Alex Buck and Ken Fogle.

salida/5.title: Mountain Mail building renovation at 121-129 E. 2nd Street
salida/5.summary: The Historic Preservation Commission was to hear a Major Certificate of Approval application from Shavano Holding Co. LLC to renovate the old Mountain Mail building. Plans include a rooftop patio, two upper-floor residences, ground-floor retail, new egress windows and demolition of a deteriorated rear structure. The building is listed as non-contributing in the historic district.

salida/6.title: Land Use Code amendments and follow-up work
salida/6.summary: Council gave second reading to Chapter 16 Land Use Code amendments on Aug. 18, with no public comments. The Planning Commission then took up leftover issues, including separating cottage housing from co-housing and the standards for cottage housing, which now requires each unit on its own lot.

salida/7.title: 2027 budget and community budget survey
salida/7.summary: Council discussed a community budget survey on Aug. 31, then held preliminary 2027 budget discussions on Oct. 6 and continued them Oct. 19. A treasurer's comparison of the 2026 and 2027 budgets was also on the agenda.

salida/8.title: Comprehensive Plan update and water supply and growth elements
salida/8.summary: Council considered supporting a Local Planning Capacity grant application for the 2027 Comprehensive Plan update. The Planning Commission was to discuss amendments to the Water Supply Element and Strategic Growth Element.

salida/9.title: Regional sustainability project and waste policy
salida/9.summary: Staff updated Council on how EECBG grant funding supports a regional sustainability contractor, including energy code training, an EV readiness plan and a greenhouse gas inventory. Upcoming Council items may include recycling space requirements for multifamily housing and waste hauler licensing.

salida/10.title: 610 Walnut Street dangerous building
salida/10.summary: Council went into executive session about potential contracts related to the county Building Safety Department's Notice to Vacate and Notice of Demolition of a dangerous building at 610 Walnut Street.

salida/11.title: Support for 5-H LLC R-2 zoning question on Nov. 3 ballot
salida/11.summary: Council considered Resolution 2026-29 expressing support for the 5-H LLC R-2 zoning question on the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot.

salida/12.title: US-50 and SH-291 intersection improvements
salida/12.summary: Council considered sending a letter to CDOT about intersection improvements at US-50 and SH-291.

san-juan-county/0.title: Stage Two fire ban (Resolution 2026-07)
san-juan-county/0.summary: The council agenda for June 29, 2026 includes Resolution 2026-07 to put a Stage Two fire ban in place. The agenda gives no further detail on the restrictions or the outcome.

san-miguel-county/0.title: Natural resources Land Use Code rewrite: forestry, oil & gas, deep geothermal
san-miguel-county/0.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed new Land Use Code sections on forestry practices (including logging thresholds and streamlining wildfire mitigation), oil and gas operations, and deep geothermal. The Commissioners scheduled public hearings on Resolutions 2026-40 through 2026-43 for Oct 21 to add Article 6 Natural Resources sections and related amendments. Sheep Mountain Alliance commented on the forestry item.

san-miguel-county/1.title: Housing Code Update and affordable housing land use amendments
san-miguel-county/1.summary: The county is using a Proposition 123 capacity grant to remove barriers to workforce and affordable housing in unincorporated areas, with stakeholder roundtables on community housing zones, density bonuses tied to deed restrictions, and ADUs. The Planning Commission also reviewed a Qualified Developer amendment for affordable housing, and commissioners were asked to amend the Local Planning Capacity grant after adopting an expedited review.

san-miguel-county/2.title: Employee Housing Impact Mitigation Fee
san-miguel-county/2.summary: Commissioners discussed the county's Employee Housing Impact Mitigation Fee, which applies to new construction and additions in the unincorporated Telluride R-1 school district area. The fee was adopted in 2022 and amended in 2023, and funds housing purchases and community housing projects such as Sunnyside. Materials compare it with the Town of Telluride's gap fee.
san-miguel-county/2.where: Unincorporated county in Telluride R-1 school district

san-miguel-county/3.title: Mountain Village affordable housing project: fee waiver and setback variance
san-miguel-county/3.summary: The Commissioners held a public hearing on waiving county land use fees for the Town of Mountain Village's affordable housing project. The Board of Adjustment considered a variance cutting the setback from County Road 63L from 20 feet to 7 feet on a 56.34-acre parcel to keep housing away from the riparian corridor and wetlands. Staff recommended a five-year approval.

san-miguel-county/4.title: Natural medicine and nonconforming lots code amendments
san-miguel-county/4.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed a new Section 5-31 setting where and how natural medicine businesses may operate, including distance from daycares. It also took up amendments allowing uses on nonconforming lots, with attorney and consultant comment.

san-miguel-county/5.title: 2027 county budget and community support funding
san-miguel-county/5.summary: Commissioners reviewed the 2027 preliminary budget and took up 2027 Community Support Funding, including a $12,000 request from West End Family Link and the Telluride Historical Museum. The Open Space Commission also worked toward a Nov. 9 budget deadline. Commissioners also discussed a proposed state bill allowing voter-approved county excise taxes.

san-miguel-county/6.title: Lawson Hill Connector Trail construction
san-miguel-county/6.summary: Commissioners considered an agreement with Lawson Hill Property Owners Association and CDOT concurrence to award the Lawson Hill Connector Trail Project (#26003), then ratified the construction agreement.

san-miguel-county/7.title: Bridal Veil Falls water flow and black swifts
san-miguel-county/7.summary: Residents raised concerns that the town's diversion dropped Bridal Veil Falls flow to about 1 CFS versus a required 6.5 CFS, threatening nesting black swifts. No formal minimums exist; the Forest Service and US Fish & Wildlife were named as leads, and the issue was considered resolved for now as birds migrate.

san-miguel-county/8.title: Open Space Commission: Galloping Goose Park, new manager and property plans
san-miguel-county/8.summary: Galloping Goose Park is targeted for completion by an Oct 29 deadline, with a governor's visit for a sculpture unveiling. The commission is hiring a new Parks and Open Space Manager, and wants a short management plan, fire mitigation for dead trees, and a survey for a county property seen as inaccessible. Gunnison sage grouse work stays on the work plan.
san-miguel-county/8.where: Galloping Goose Park, Down Valley and county open space

san-miguel-county/9.title: Telluride Pines water system CDBG application
san-miguel-county/9.summary: Commissioners considered co-sponsoring a Colorado Community Development Block Grant application for Telluride Pines HOA to restore safe and reliable water.

san-miguel-county/10.title: Noxious weed grant and enforcement
san-miguel-county/10.summary: A $5,800 Colorado Department of Agriculture Noxious Weed Fund grant is available, and staff will draft allocation options. The group also discussed landowner response and enforcement, and a completed tamarisk removal in Dry Creek Basin.

san-miguel-county/11.title: Regional discussion of Southern Ute gas pipeline spill
san-miguel-county/11.summary: Five southwest counties planned an informal discussion with the Southern Ute Indian Council about a gas enterprise pipeline spill.

severance/0.title: Bower North and Northgate Lakes metropolitan district service plans
severance/0.summary: The Town Council scheduled public hearings on Ordinance 2026-11 (Bower North Metropolitan District consolidated service plan) and Ordinance 2026-12 (Northgate Lakes Metropolitan District consolidated service plan) for Sept. 22. The documents list the hearings but do not state the outcome.
severance/0.where: Bower North and Northgate Lakes districts

severance/1.title: 2027 Capital Improvement Program and budget
severance/1.summary: Town Council reviewed the final draft of the 2027 Capital Improvement Program, a 10-year plan in which only 2027 projects get funded in the 2027 budget. New or increased items include a 2036 Police Department addition, more money for the water acquisition program, and a restroom added to the Town Park improvements. A 2027 Town Projects and Budget town hall is set for Oct. 13.

severance/2.title: Land Use Code amendments before the Planning Commission
severance/2.summary: The Planning Commission took up several code changes: letting Town Council adopt time-sensitive Land Use Code amendments without a prior Commission recommendation, corrected setbacks in the Town Core and Development Node zones, oil and gas setbacks aligned with Weld County rules, and procedures for suspending land use applications at an applicant's request. It also considered electric service infrastructure rules for new development and an early grading permit ordinance. Several items drew a 'no action' vote, while the application suspension and electric service resolutions were approved.

severance/3.title: Comprehensive Plan update and public engagement
severance/3.summary: The Comprehensive Plan Advisory Committee reviewed the current 2020 plan and discussed an engagement plan and schedule for the update. The goal is to build trust and gather resident input on land use, transportation, parks and growth.

severance/4.title: Interim town attorney appointment
severance/4.summary: Town Council considered Resolution 2026-29R appointing an interim town attorney and amending the engagement agreement. The outcome is not stated in the documents.

severance/5.title: Mobile food vendor licensing
severance/5.summary: The Citizen Advisory Board heard a discussion from the Town Attorney on licensing mobile food vendors, along with a clerk overview of town permits such as special events and chickens.

severance/6.title: Severance High School After Prom community grant
severance/6.summary: The SHS After Prom requested a $2,000 Severance community grant for its 2027 program, after receiving $1,000 in February 2026. The Citizen Advisory Board would review it and Town Council would vote on funding if it is approved. A Severance Chamber grant application was also on the agenda.
severance/6.where: Severance High School, 1200 Hidden Valley Parkway

severance/7.title: Youth Council logo, appointments and service projects
severance/7.summary: The Youth Council is choosing a logo, giving feedback on possible code changes, and taking applications for 2026/2027 members from Aug. 7 to 28. It will also pick service projects and consider an event at the 2027 Severance Days.

sheridan/0.title: Public safety sales and use tax increase (Ordinance 13-2026)
sheridan/0.summary: Council took up Ordinance 13-2026 on first reading Aug. 10 and second reading Aug. 24. It would refer a city sales and use tax increase for public safety purposes. The agendas do not state the rate or the outcome.

sheridan/1.title: 2026 amended budget and 2027 budget
sheridan/1.summary: Council reviewed the 2027 proposed budget in work sessions from August to September, covering revenues, capital, open space, stormwater, volunteer fire and the general fund. A public hearing on the 2026 amended and 2027 budgets (Ordinances 14 and 15-2026) was held Sept. 28, with second reading Oct. 12. The Redevelopment Agency took up matching budget resolutions.

sheridan/2.title: Rezoning of 3600 S. Federal Blvd
sheridan/2.summary: Council held a public hearing Aug. 10 on Ordinance 11-2026, an application to rezone property at 3600 S. Federal Blvd. Speakers had to attend in person and were limited to two minutes each. The agenda does not state the outcome.

sheridan/3.title: Radcliff and Hampden plats
sheridan/3.summary: The Planning Commission held hearings Sept. 2 on preliminary and final plats for 2200 W. Radcliff Ave and 2500 W. Hampden. Council then held a public hearing Sept. 28 on the Radcliff Subdivision preliminary and final plats (Resolutions 24 and 25-2026).
sheridan/3.where: 2200 W. Radcliff Ave and 2500 W. Hampden Ave

sheridan/4.title: Housing plans, ADU law compliance and Housing Authority
sheridan/4.summary: Planning staff updated the commission on compliance with state ADU law HB24-1152, with code amendments to return later in the year. The commission was scheduled to discuss the Sheridan Housing Implementation Plan (SHIP) and an Equal Space ordinance in October. Council work sessions on Oct. 12 and Oct. 26 covered the Sheridan Housing Authority.

sheridan/5.title: KIMCO Sheridan reimbursement agreement amendments
sheridan/5.summary: The Redevelopment Agency considered amendments to the KIMCO Sheridan reimbursement agreements for the Series 2011A-1 and 2011A-2 bonds (Resolutions 2 and 3-2026).

sheridan/6.title: Wastewater pretreatment regulations
sheridan/6.summary: Council considered Ordinance 12-2026 on second reading Aug. 10, setting pretreatment regulation of wastewater.

sheridan/7.title: Flying Saucer RV Park subdivision and brownfields grant
sheridan/7.summary: Planning staff reported on the Flying Saucer RV Park subdivision application, a federal EPA Brownfields Grant award, the renewed South Metro Enterprise Zone and South Santa Fe planning projects.

sheridan/8.title: Crisis services contract with AllHealth Network
sheridan/8.summary: Council considered Resolution 28-2026 on Oct. 26, approving an agreement for crisis services with AllHealth Network.

silver-cliff/0.title: Workforce housing agreement with Westcliffe and affordable housing project
silver-cliff/0.summary: The Board considered a Workforce Housing intergovernmental agreement (IGA) with Westcliffe in September and October 2026, with a draft going back to the attorney for edits. Trustee Troy Bomgardner gave workforce housing updates, and the Planning Commission took up an affordable housing interior lot line request with site plans for five buildings. The board also acted on Resolution 06-2026 on Prop 123 in June.

silver-cliff/1.title: Park improvements: playground, pickleball and Silver Cliff Park lot lines
silver-cliff/1.summary: The town sought proposals in June 2026 for park work including dirt work, concrete curb and handicap parking at the playground, and pickleball site preparation, and the board was asked to award the contract. A part-time park employee was proposed, the GOCO grant account is being tracked, and the Planning Commission will look at vacating lot lines in Silver Cliff Park in October. The board also signed a release for the old playground equipment.

silver-cliff/2.title: Excessive noise ordinance (Ordinance 01-2026)
silver-cliff/2.summary: Ordinance 01-2026 amending Sec. 10-9-30 on excessive noise had a first reading in April, was tabled, and then went through second reading and a public hearing for consideration in June 2026.

silver-cliff/3.title: Zoning code rewrite and Title 16 changes
silver-cliff/3.summary: The Planning Commission has been working on a municipal code update through a rezoning committee and on Title 16 Zoning. The Board had a first reading of Ordinance 03-2026 amending Title 16 in June, and discussed state wildfire-resiliency building code requirements for the wildland-urban interface.

silver-cliff/4.title: Dutch Pantry additional parking and rezoning request
silver-cliff/4.summary: Matt Hershberger asked about buying land for additional employee and customer parking for Dutch Pantry. The property is zoned R3 and would need rezoning to B1 commercial.

silver-cliff/5.title: 2027 budget and budget workshops
silver-cliff/5.summary: The proposed 2027 budget was presented on October 6, 2026 with no discussion or decisions, and the board set about scheduling budget workshops. The Altitude Fitness funding request is to be taken up at the workshop.

silver-cliff/6.title: Board meeting quorum and attendance rules (Ordinance 02-2026)
silver-cliff/6.summary: After discussion of poor meeting attendance, the Board moved Ordinance 02-2026 amending Sec. 2-2-90 on meeting quorum through readings and a public hearing in June 2026. Trustees discussed requiring notice to the Town Clerk of absences.

silver-cliff/7.title: CloudBreak decommissioning bond
silver-cliff/7.summary: The board considered approving the CloudBreak decommissioning bond in April 2026. The documents give no further detail.

silver-cliff/8.title: Cemetery regulations update (Ordinance 05-2026)
silver-cliff/8.summary: The board had a first reading of Ordinance 05-2026 amending the 2021 cemetery regulations in fall 2026.

silver-cliff/9.title: Grants: Black Hills Energy and incentive award
silver-cliff/9.summary: The town received a grant award from Black Hills Energy and considered Resolution 05-2026 to accept it, plus Resolution 04-2026 accepting another grant. In October it considered Resolution 08-2026 on an incentive award grant.

silver-plume/0.title: Camping ordinance for Silver Plume town limits
silver-plume/0.summary: Camping within town limits is not defined in the Land Use Code (Ordinance 340) as allowed or prohibited. A resident asked for an ordinance after reports of overnight activity near an apartment building, with people looking for bathrooms and residents feeling unsafe. Staff will gather model ordinances, and a public hearing on a camping ordinance is on the Sept. 14 agenda.

silver-plume/1.title: 2027 budget and water and sewer rate increases
silver-plume/1.summary: The Budget Committee began 2027 budget work in August, with work sessions on Sept. 5 and Oct. 3 and a proposed budget on the table. The preliminary budget is due to the Board by October and the final by Dec. 31, 2026. Staff say water and sewer rates will need to rise because those fees have not increased in many years.

silver-plume/2.title: Wildfire Resiliency Code and Ordinance 359
silver-plume/2.summary: The Town is considering adopting the 2025 Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code through Ordinance 359. A public hearing for second and final reading is on the Sept. 14 agenda.

silver-plume/3.title: Main Street sidewalk concerns
silver-plume/3.summary: A resident raised problems with the sidewalks on Main Street between Jefferson and Silver Street, including a dumpster along the sidewalk. Sidewalk work is on the Town's priority list but comes after a water treatment tank repair, and the Road and Bridge committee is to discuss it.
silver-plume/3.where: Main Street between Jefferson and Silver Street

silver-plume/4.title: Cemetery forms, expansion and cleanup
silver-plume/4.summary: The Town reviewed new cemetery forms, including a contract replacing the old deed, an open/close request, a monument application and a transfer request. Officials discussed opening a new section for plot sales, possibly a non-resident section at market value, extending the access road, cleanup logistics and the cemetery gate.

silver-plume/5.title: Town shop electrical and door quotes
silver-plume/5.summary: The Board continued discussing quotes for electrical work and doors at the Town shop, with one quote around $20,500. The Clerk has contracted services from two firms, PME and MBIE.

snowmass-village/0.title: Ritz Carlton / Viewline sketch plan redevelopment
snowmass-village/0.summary: Elevate Snowmass, LLC's sketch plan would rebuild the Ritz Carlton/Viewline and Wildwood area with a lodge of about 167 units, roughly 125 workforce housing units and a 252-space subgrade garage. The Planning Commission has worked through lodge, housing and conference/commercial topics and was to discuss draft Resolution No. 4 on Oct 7. Part-time residents worry about scale and construction impacts, and a resident at the Sept 16 hearing raised height, traffic and Fall Lane concerns.

snowmass-village/1.title: Housing mitigation rate and nexus study update
snowmass-village/1.summary: After raising the employee housing mitigation rate from 60% to 100% (Ordinance 1, 2026), Council is reviewing updated employee generation rates and a fee-in-lieu based on a 750 sf unit, 1.75 employees per unit and $945/SF. Council asked for more information on residential operations and maintenance rates and added residential remodels as a mitigating activity.

snowmass-village/2.title: Draw Site workforce housing project
snowmass-village/2.summary: Council is reviewing next steps for the Draw Site workforce housing project as owner. The 2027 budget includes about $76.1 million for its construction.

snowmass-village/3.title: 2027 Town budget
snowmass-village/3.summary: Staff describe the 2027 budget as exceptionally tight after a low-snow 2026 ski season, with capital funds depleted by completed projects. Total capital spending is about $108 million. Council budget meetings run Oct 5, 12 and 19, with adoption by resolution expected Nov 4. The Financial Advisory Board and Tourism commented.

snowmass-village/4.title: Daly Lane employee housing sketch plan
snowmass-village/4.summary: The Snowmass Village Community Foundation, represented by TPEH, LLC, submitted a sketch plan for workforce housing on the Daly Lane site, reviewed at a joint Council and Planning Commission meeting Aug 17. Feedback from the March 2 pre-sketch meeting included increasing on-site parking.

snowmass-village/5.title: Snowmass Mall transit center project
snowmass-village/5.summary: A new transit center at the Snowmass Mall with RFTA improvements is estimated at $42M to $60M depending on scope and parking. The Part-Time Resident Advisory Board agreed improvements are needed but worried about scale, funding and timing given the Ritz redevelopment, and suggested modest upgrades as an alternative.

snowmass-village/6.title: Wildfire mitigation program and fire authority agreement
snowmass-village/6.summary: The town has launched a wildfire mitigation contractor bidding process and a $1,000 homeowner rebate program administered by the RFV Wildfire Collaborative. Council considered a Memorandum of Understanding with Roaring Fork Fire Rescue Authority, and a personal property fire mitigation discussion was held Aug 3.

snowmass-village/7.title: Cavern Springs mobile home park funding
snowmass-village/7.summary: Council took up Ordinance 15 appropriating funds for the Cavern Springs Mobile Home Park, plus Resolution 23 on an IGA, housing covenants and a grant agreement. First reading was Sept 22 and second reading Oct 5.

snowmass-village/8.title: SHOP final plan and PUD amendment
snowmass-village/8.summary: Council heard the SHOP Final Plan and PUD Amendment, Ordinance 14, on first reading Sept 8 and second reading Oct 5.

snowmass-village/9.title: Highway 82 congestion fee and Glenwood South Bridge
snowmass-village/9.summary: Council saw a regional plan to cut Highway 82 traffic that combines incentives with a congestion fee estimated at $10–20 million a year. Glenwood Springs also asked for regional support for its roughly $77.5M South Bridge project, which has a ~$5M shortfall.

snowmass-village/10.title: Noxious weed and pesticide spraying
snowmass-village/10.summary: Council discussed pesticide application Sept 8. The Environmental Advisory Board raised the lack of signage about trail spraying, and staff were asked for a more detailed noxious weed plan.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board

snowmass-village/11.title: Show cause hearings over unpaid sales taxes
snowmass-village/11.summary: The Liquor Authority scheduled show cause hearings Aug 19 for licensees, including Il Poggio, accused of being delinquent on town sales tax. Licenses could be suspended or revoked.

sources.body: Liquor Authority Hearing & Local Marijuana Licensing Authority Hearing

snowmass-village/12.title: Playground renovation at Town Park
snowmass-village/12.summary: The Parks board reviewed the playground renovation capital project, asking the vendor to show it can be themed with local motifs like the Mt Daly stripe and hot air balloons.

sources.body: Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board
Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board
Parks, Open Space, Trails & Recreation Board

starkville/0.title: Crypto currency data center special exception on Industrial Park Road
starkville/0.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission held a public hearing on SE 26-08, a request to use a site in an industrial zone as a "Data Center - Crypto Currency Generation Facility." The site is on the east side of Industrial Park Road, about 350 feet south of Miley Road. The documents do not state the outcome.
starkville/0.where: Industrial Park Road, about 350 feet south of Miley Road

starkville/1.title: Chronic nuisance property ordinance
starkville/1.summary: The Board of Aldermen called a first public hearing on adopting a chronic nuisance property ordinance on Aug. 4. A second public hearing and vote on adoption were on the Sept. 15 agenda.

starkville/2.title: Leisure and Recreation District ordinance amendment
starkville/2.summary: The board scheduled hearings to amend the Leisure and Recreation District ordinance to add specific language. A first hearing was called in August and a second hearing was on the Sept. 15 agenda.

starkville/3.title: 2026-2027 city budget, tax millage and pay raises
starkville/3.summary: Aldermen called public hearings on the 2026-2027 budget and tax millage in August. They also took up proposed 2027 budgets for outside agencies, including the Oktibbeha County Economic Development Authority. Pay raises for all departments were on the Sept. 15 agenda.

starkville/4.title: Jackson 128 mixed-use development downtown
starkville/4.summary: The Planning and Zoning Commission heard SE 26-06 for a mixed-use development at 128 South Jackson Street. The applicant sought five special exceptions, including a fifth story. A citizen, Steve Langston, spoke in favor.

starkville/5.title: Sterling Ridge phased preliminary plat
starkville/5.summary: The Planning Commission and then the Board of Aldermen considered PP 26-01, a phased preliminary plat for the Sterling Ridge subdivision. It is at the southwest corner of Mockingbird Road and Highway 182.

starkville/6.title: Airport runway extension and hangar grants
starkville/6.summary: The board took up state matching grants and FAA projects to extend the runway, taxiway and lighting. Later items covered change orders and grant applications for Corporate Hangar #3 and Phase III of the runway extension and overlay.

starkville/7.title: Pat Station Road and Highway 12 East multi-dwelling development
starkville/7.summary: The Board of Adjustments considered a variance (VA 26-07) and the Planning Commission a special exception (SE 26-11) for a multi-dwelling residential development near Pat Station Road and Highway 12 East.
starkville/7.where: Pat Station Road and Highway 12 East

starkville/8.title: Hotel development parking reduction on Mill Street
starkville/8.summary: The Planning Commission scheduled a hearing on SE 26-12, a request to reduce minimum parking for a proposed hotel east of Mill Street, directly east of the Cotton Mill Road intersection.
starkville/8.where: Mill Street near Cotton Mill Road

starkville/9.title: Skate park construction
starkville/9.summary: A skate park item was on the Sept. 15 agenda. On Oct. 6 the board considered a low quote of $46,190.78 from Econ Construction for skate park work.

starkville/10.title: Fire Department staffing and restructuring plan
starkville/10.summary: The board considered hiring three additional firefighters and approving a Fire Department staffing and organizational restructuring plan.

starkville/11.title: Southwire rail spur crossing easements and CC Clark Road
starkville/11.summary: The board considered crossing easements over the rail spur to Southwire for a roadway connection to CC Clark Road.
starkville/11.where: CC Clark Road / Southwire rail spur

starkville/12.title: Extension of tourism and restaurant/hotel taxes
starkville/12.summary: The board considered a resolution asking the 2027 Mississippi Legislature to extend the economic development, tourism and convention taxes on non-alcoholic beverages and the hotel/motel tax.

starkville/13.title: Electric Department projects and rates
starkville/13.summary: A Sept. 11 work session included a presentation on electric department projects and rates.

starkville/14.title: Police department to sell abandoned-property firearms to buy sighting and light devices
starkville/14.summary: On the September 1, 2026 Board of Aldermen agenda, the Starkville Police Department asked for approval to convert abandoned property firearms into sales so it could purchase sighting and light devices. The firearms would go to The Southern Connection, which gave the higher of two bids.

sterling/0.title: Proposed 1% sales and use tax for street improvements on November 3 ballot
sterling/0.summary: Council took up a resolution for a November 3, 2026 election on a 1% sales and use tax, which residents call a street improvement tax. Residents John Tyson and Lee Roth spoke, asking for more information, about exceptions to the tax, and that the $400,000 already budgeted for street repair be combined with any new tax funds.

sterling/1.title: Veterinary clinics as a conditional use (Ordinance No. 8) and Copper Gate Animal Clinic at 625-627 Holly Drive
sterling/1.summary: Porche Robison asked to open a small veterinary clinic at 625-627 Holly Drive, but the Planning Commission found a clinic is not permitted in the Medical Services zone and recommended a map or text amendment with fees waived. Council then took Ordinance No. 8 through first reading and a second-reading public hearing to allow veterinary clinics as a conditional use.

sterling/2.title: Rezoning 917 Hamilton Street from R-3 to Community Business
sterling/2.summary: J-Tab Rentals, LLC requested a map amendment for 917 Hamilton Street, from High Density Residential (R-3) to Community Business (CB). It went from Planning Commission review to first reading of Ordinance No. 10 on Aug. 25 and a second-reading public hearing on Oct. 13, where no one spoke.

http://www.sterlingcolo.com/Planning Commission/Agendas, Packets, Minutes/2026/08-05-2026 PC Agenda.pdf?t=202608101046310

sterling/3.title: 2026 Waterline Replacement Project and North 10th Avenue change order
sterling/3.summary: Council accepted a bid from Hard Rock Civil, LLC for the 2026 Waterline Replacement Project #26-001. In October it considered a change order with the contractor for the North 10th Avenue waterline replacement.

sterling/4.title: Sanitary sewer interceptor main failure declaration
sterling/4.summary: Council considered a resolution extending its declaration about a sanitary sewer interceptor main failure beyond seven days. An intergovernmental agreement with Logan County was also on the same agendas.

sterling/5.title: Intergovernmental agreement between Sterling and Logan County
sterling/5.summary: Council considered Resolution 7-5-26 approving an intergovernmental agreement with Logan County and authorizing the Mayor to execute it. The documents do not show the subject of the agreement.

sterling/6.title: Police Department Armory renovation and expansion design
sterling/6.summary: Council considered Resolution 9-3-26 approving a professional engineering design services agreement for renovating and expanding the Police Department Armory.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/09-22-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202609211636560

sterling/7.title: Master Plan update and DOLA planning grant
sterling/7.summary: Council considered Resolution 9-4-26 authorizing a funding request to the Colorado Department of Local Affairs Local Planning Capacity Grant Program to update the City's Master Plan.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/City Council/Agenda, Packet, Minutes/2026/09-22-2026 Agenda Amended.pdf?t=202609211636560

sterling/8.title: Shipping container rules concerns
sterling/8.summary: Resident Richard Bedford told Council the new shipping container updates cause unintended problems and do not properly address community business zoning. Ordinance No. 11 amending a code chapter had its first reading on Oct. 13, but the documents do not name its topic.

sterling/9.title: Garage-to-home conversion variance at 728 McKinley Street
sterling/9.summary: Resident Jesse Mull asked for an exception to convert his garage into his main home. Staff sent it to the Planning Commission, which scheduled a variance review on Sept. 2.

sterling/10.title: Sober living conditional use request from Milestone Community Wellness
sterling/10.summary: The Planning Commission was to review a conditional use request from Milestone Community Wellness to operate a sober facility.

sterling/11.title: Chicken permitting process complaints
sterling/11.summary: Residents including Lisa LeFevre asked Council to revisit the chicken code and clarify the building permit process tied to the chicken permit.

sterling/12.title: Marijuana regulations discussion with downtown dispensary
sterling/12.summary: Colin Mudd of Jay's Downtown Dispensary discussed marijuana regulations with the Planning Commission, which tabled the discussion to give dispensary owners time.

sources.url: http://www.sterlingcolo.com/Planning Commission/Agendas, Packets, Minutes/2026/08-05-2026 PC Packet.pdf?t=202608101046460

summit-county/0.title: Quikrete concrete and asphalt batch plant appeal at 28755 State Hwy 9
summit-county/0.summary: The Board of County Commissioners heard an appeal of the Lower Blue Planning Commission decision on PLN26-004, a Class 4 Conditional Use Permit for milling and concrete and asphalt batch plant operations on a 151-acre portion of a 605-acre A-1 parcel. The packet includes public comments, a stormwater plan, a landscape plan and a draft resolution.

summit-county/1.title: Verizon Wireless cell facility appeal at 6631 Heeney Road
summit-county/1.summary: The commissioners held a public hearing on an appeal of the Lower Blue Planning Commission decision on PLN26-009 and PLN26-010, a conditional use permit and site plan for a new Verizon Wireless telecommunication facility. Public comments received through 9/23/26 are in the packet.

summit-county/2.title: 2027 county budget
summit-county/2.summary: The commissioners reviewed the draft 2027 budget in a work session and a public hearing. They also held separate discussions on the Assessor, Capital Projects, Road & Bridge (including its 5-year capital plan), Lodging Tax and a District Attorney budget amendment.

summit-county/3.title: Purchase of mining claim sites for open space
summit-county/3.summary: The commissioners considered exercising option agreements to buy the Pirate, Canadian and Manerva mill sites in the Snake River Basin. They also considered exercising an option for the Summit Gulch Claims in the Upper Blue Basin.
summit-county/3.where: Snake River Basin and Upper Blue Basin

summit-county/4.title: Proposition 123 housing credits for Keystone's Soda Creek project
summit-county/4.summary: The commissioners discussed and then considered approving an intergovernmental agreement with the Town of Keystone on allocating Proposition 123 affordable housing credits to the Soda Creek project.

summit-county/5.title: County positions on 2026 ballot measures
summit-county/5.summary: The commissioners considered resolutions supporting Amendment 87, Proposition 137, Proposition NN and Referred Measure 4A. They also considered resolutions opposing Amendments 81, 82 and 85 and Proposition 136.

summit-county/6.title: SCRAP fee analysis
summit-county/6.summary: A special work session reviewed a rate study and fee analysis for SCRAP. The packet includes a rate study and supplement.

summit-county/7.title: Full maintenance of County Road 506
summit-county/7.summary: The commissioners considered a resolution on whether the county should take on full maintenance of CR 506.

summit-county/8.title: Background checks for massage facility personnel
summit-county/8.summary: The commissioners considered a proposed resolution requiring background checks for personnel at massage facilities.

summit-county/9.title: Head Start and Community Services Block Grant funding
summit-county/9.summary: The commissioners considered the 2027 Head Start continuation application and its budget justification. They also considered authorizing approval of the 3-year Community Services Block Grant Community Needs Assessment.

summit-county/10.title: Property tax abatements for Highlands Riverfront tracts
summit-county/10.summary: The commissioners considered 2025 property tax abatement requests for Tracts A, T and U of the Highlands Riverfront subdivision, one with a stipulation agreement.

superior/0.title: Marshall Fire Remembrance Project and 5-year anniversary event
superior/0.summary: The Town is planning a Marshall Fire Remembrance on Town-owned land, with a survey and geotechnical report done and a design team (Davis Partnerships + LandDesign) at work. Colorado Gives will act as fiscal partner, Louisville is committing $25,000, and Council is considering a fundraising advisor agreement. A Resilience Celebration is set for Friday, December 18, 6-8pm at the Community Center.

Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
