superior/1.title: 2027 budget and five-year financial plan
superior/1.summary: Council held budget review sessions in August and September on the 2027 budget and 2027-2031 financial plan, with adoption hearings set for October 12 covering the fee schedule, property taxes, and budgets for the metro districts and urban renewal authority. Mid-year figures show sales tax up 0.2%, vehicle use tax down 17.1%, and permit revenue down about 31%.

superior/2.title: Zaharias property PUD amendment (7500 S 88th Street)
superior/2.summary: The Planning Commission heard the Twenty-Fifth Amendment to the Rock Creek Ranch Planned Development for the Zaharias property, proposed by Garrett Companies, and recommended approval after a resident commented. Town Council then held a public hearing on the ordinance on September 14.

superior/3.title: Water conservation and turf reduction plan
superior/3.summary: The Town drafted a Waterwise Landscape Transformation Roadmap and a prioritization tool for reducing non-functional turf, with a survey on Shape Superior and an August 31 work session. Council is slated to consider adopting it October 12 along with a Northern Water Southern Water Supply Project allotment amendment.

superior/4.title: Pirate Park playground renovation
superior/4.summary: Council approved a design-build contract with Altitude Recreation, Inc. for the Pirate Park playground renovation. The Parks and Recreation committee and Council are receiving project updates.

superior/5.title: Pesticide spraying concerns in park
superior/5.summary: Residents raised concerns at the sustainability committee about a spraying event in a park near a pond. They said they were told spraying was limited to 20 feet away, and questioned whether the landscape contract should be competitively bid. Council is slated to consider a landscape agreement with Vargas Property Services on October 26.

superior/6.title: Coyote Ridge trails, open space, wildfire mitigation and prairie dog plan
superior/6.summary: The Open Space committee is reviewing consultant Pointe Strategies' draft trail recommendations for Coyote Ridge, an updated prairie dog management plan, wildfire mitigation work, a wildlife management plan, and the Open Space Master Plan, due for approval in October. Youth Corps crews completed weed, fence and trail work over the summer.
superior/6.where: Coyote Ridge and town open space

superior/7.title: 88th Street bike/pedestrian improvements and trail grants
superior/7.summary: Council approved an intergovernmental agreement with CDOT for the 88th Street Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvements Project. It is also considering a Colorado Parks and Wildlife trail grant submission, and the parks committee is discussing support for the McCaslin multi-use trail grant.

superior/8.title: International Fire Code 2024 adoption
superior/8.summary: Council took up an ordinance adopting the 2024 International Fire Code, presented by Mountain View Fire's Deputy Chief. The hearing was continued, and Council approved the second reading on September 28 as Ordinance 80.

superior/9.title: Boulder County child care mill levy measure
superior/9.summary: Council discussed the Boulder County Child Care Investment Initiative and approved a resolution supporting the county's Early Childhood Care and Education mill levy increase ballot measure.

superior/10.title: Rock Creek HOA tolling agreement and Rock Creek Parkway/community center construction
superior/10.summary: Council planned a closed session on extending a tolling agreement between the Town and the Rock Creek HOA. It is also receiving construction updates on Rock Creek Parkway, the Community Center and the north and south pools.

superior/11.title: Trash and recycling hauling, EV trucks and apartment recycling
superior/11.summary: Council received a presentation on contamination in recycling and organics streams and electric collection vehicles, in the context of a future hauler request for proposals. The sustainability committee also reviewed an apartment recycling and composting assessment.

superior/12.title: Business microgrant program and public art projects
superior/12.summary: The Town is planning a green business microgrant with $5,000 budgeted, awards up to $2,500, launching February 2027. The arts committee is planning ARTery art benches and utility box art in Circle Park, with a purchase recommendation going to Council October 26.

sources.body: Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)
Cultural Arts and Public Spaces Advisory Committee (CAPS)

teller-county/0.title: Ordinance 23 regulating short-term rentals in unincorporated Teller County
teller-county/0.summary: The commissioners held a first reading of Ordinance 23 on Aug 6 and scheduled a second reading on Sept 10. On Sept 24 they were to ratify an agreement with Neumo Group, LLC to administer short-term rental taxes and licenses. Residents raised concerns about STRs in the Four Mile area, including STR owners joining HOA boards.

teller-county/1.title: Quantum Tech compliance agreement for 10180 West property
teller-county/1.summary: The Planning Commission revoked a 1995 conditional use permit for a construction storage yard on May 12, 2026, and the Board of Adjustment took up the matter on July 9. Under a compliance agreement, Quantum Tech has 90 days to remove the non-permitted operations while keeping office use, and any future permit would need a new application. The commissioners were to approve it on Sept 2 and ratify it on Sept 10.

teller-county/2.title: NETCO impact fees for fire districts and housing costs
teller-county/2.summary: The county received an impact fee study from NETCO and is seeking public comment on the proposed fees. A commissioner argued the fees would raise housing costs while acknowledging the fire districts need funding.

teller-county/3.title: 2026 budget amendments and 2027 proposed budget
teller-county/3.summary: Commissioners held budget work sessions in August and September and a capital plan and budget session on Sept 22. A 2027 proposed budget presentation was set for Oct 8. Resolutions amending the 2026 General, Jail, Road and Bridge, and Social Services budgets were on the Oct 22 agenda.

teller-county/4.title: Changes to Teller County building code and contractor licensing
teller-county/4.summary: A work session on Aug 25 covered proposed changes to the county building code. These include contractor license categories and annual fees, such as $50 for some licenses and $150 for OWTS cleaner and NAWT contractors. Rules for septic (OWTS) contractors are included.

teller-county/5.title: Stage II to Stage I fire ban
teller-county/5.summary: With the fire season and dry conditions, the commissioners considered a resolution on Sept 2 to move from a Stage II to a Stage I fire ban. They were to ratify it on Sept 10.

teller-county/6.title: Jail underground repair contract increase
teller-county/6.summary: A change order for Mid-Colorado Construction raises the not-to-exceed amount for jail underground repair investigation from $40,000 to $100,000 and extends the contract to June 30, 2027.

teller-county/7.title: Road funding and Victor water pipe leak
teller-county/7.summary: Commissioners discussed state Initiative 175 and House Bill 260, which would require highway funds to go to roads, and the effect of state budget cuts. They also reported on the Victor water pipe leak that left the city without water, which has been fixed while Victor seeks grants.

teller-county/8.title: Pinestone Ranch project with Palmer Land Trust
teller-county/8.summary: Palmer Land Trust was scheduled to discuss the Pinestone Ranch project with the commissioners in an Oct 13 work session.

teller-county/9.title: Lot line adjustments in Ranch Resorts and Highland Meadows
teller-county/9.summary: Staff recommended approval of two amended final plats. One adjusts the lot line between Lots 21 and 22 of Ranch Resorts of Colorado Subdivision No. 2 and creates a utility easement for power. The other adjusts the line between Lots 3 and 4 of Highland Meadows Filing 1, on Floresta Drive and Floresta Place, to resolve encroachments.
teller-county/9.where: Ranch Resorts of Colorado No. 2; Highland Meadows 1 (Floresta Drive and Place)

teller-county/10.title: Rosemont Reservoir variance and public health programs
teller-county/10.summary: A board meeting included a discussion of a variance for Rosemont Reservoir. Public health staff reported on a rise in suicides among men aged 45-65, the rural health grant, an emergency oxygen program, and reflective address signs for emergency response. The board also discussed the new Tamale Act and childcare facilities needing special use permits.

telluride/0.title: Carhenge Redevelopment Project design review
telluride/0.summary: The Historic & Architectural Review Commission has three preliminary large-scale applications for the Carhenge redevelopment (Buildings A-C, D1-D2, E1-E3) on Lots 34 and 34B, Backman Village. They were continued from July and August 2026 without discussion and were on the September 30 agenda.

telluride/1.title: Shandoka Lot Redevelopment PUD and large-scale review
telluride/1.summary: The preliminary PUD for redeveloping Lot L (about 4.07 acres) in Backman Village seeks larger dimensional limits in return for public benefits. Planning & Zoning continued it without discussion because of staff capacity, and HARC plans to continue its review to November 18, 2026.

telluride/2.title: Telluride School District employee housing near the middle-high school
telluride/2.summary: Planning & Zoning held a work session on proposed new employee housing at the northwest corner of the Telluride Middle-High School site, under an intergovernmental agreement with the school district. It also continued work on potential Land Use Code amendments.
telluride/2.where: Northwest corner of Telluride Middle-High School site

telluride/3.title: Housing waitlist policies and Telluride Housing Authority actions
telluride/3.summary: The Housing Authority Subcommittee held worksessions on waitlist management and leasing rules (Sections 105 and 106.1) after the waitlist was suspended, and on bedroom size standards. The full Housing Authority took up the waitlist policies on September 22. It also adopted a policy on primary residency for children of multiple custodial parents, set a 20% custodial cutoff and an age limit through 18, and considered amending deed restrictions for town-built units at 215 East Colorado Avenue. The subcommittee also handled owner exception requests.

telluride/4.title: 2027 Town budget workshops
telluride/4.summary: Town Council held a budget workshop on October 13 covering 12 funds requesting $12.11M in revenue and $16.11M in spending. The Open Space set-aside would be drawn down by $4.25M, the Transportation Fund transfer would grow by $290,000, lodgers' tax is projected to rebound, and a Lodgers Tax position would move to full time. Water and sewer rate and fee schedule drafts were also reviewed, with adoption planned for November 17. The Open Space Commission also planned to discuss the budget with the Town Manager.

telluride/5.title: Flock license plate reader cameras
telluride/5.summary: Town Council scheduled a discussion on October 6 about Automated License Plate Reader (Flock) cameras. A written public comment from McKenzie was posted with the agenda.

telluride/6.title: Ethics complaint and Code of Conduct for councilmembers
telluride/6.summary: The Ethics Commission considered a complaint against a councilmember and discussed recommending a Code of Conduct, either folded into the Ethics Code or stand-alone, because its finding hinged on the lack of clear behavioral standards. Town Council set a second reading of an ordinance amending the Ethics Code's general guidelines (Section 2-4-30) for October 6.

telluride/7.title: Town Park Oval improvements
telluride/7.summary: The Parks & Recreation Commission reviewed the Town Park Oval Improvements Project. Members of the public and commissioners discussed goals, design options, facility uses, management and alternative facility options.

telluride/8.title: 2027 campground and shower fees
telluride/8.summary: Staff proposed 2027 Town Park campground fee increases of $2 to $5 per night (about 8%), projecting $203,304 in revenue, up 5% from the 2026 budget. Shower fees are projected to raise $62,500, up 25% from $50,000. The commission also discussed the 5-year capital improvement fund.

telluride/9.title: Pergola built without a permit at Swede Finn Hall
telluride/9.summary: HARC reviewed a pergola on a rated historic structure at Swede Finn Hall, near West Pacific Avenue and Townsend Street, that was built without permits. Staff found insufficient justification for approval and suggested denial or a temporary-structure permit.
telluride/9.where: Swede Finn Hall, West Pacific Avenue and Townsend Street

telluride/10.title: Fuel-burning landscape equipment ban and Climate Action Plan update
telluride/10.summary: The Ecology Commission discussed a draft ordinance banning fuel-burning landscape equipment, a measure called for in the 2022 Climate Action Plan. It is also working on the required 2027 update of the plan and on dark-sky initiatives.

telluride/11.title: 2027 CCAASE grant budget
telluride/11.summary: The Community Assistance, Arts & Special Events commission agreed not to request a budget increase for 2027 grants because of lower projected town revenue. It sent a letter to Town Council and is reviewing 2027 grant applications.

sources.body: Commission for Community Assistance, Arts & Special Events
Commission for Community Assistance, Arts & Special Events
Commission for Community Assistance, Arts & Special Events

telluride/12.title: Telluride Humane Society 5K at Elks Park
telluride/12.summary: The Humane Society requested use of Elks Park and the River Trail for a 5K run of up to 100 registrants, followed by a community celebration. The Parks & Recreation Commission considered the request.

thornton/0.title: Data center moratorium
thornton/0.summary: Council held two discussions in late August and early September on whether to adopt a moratorium on data centers, with a staff presentation on data center impacts.

thornton/1.title: 2027 budget recommendation
thornton/1.summary: Council worked through the city manager's recommended 2027 budget over several planning sessions and meetings this fall.

thornton/2.title: 2027 utility rates
thornton/2.summary: Council reviewed proposed water, sewer and other utility rate changes for 2027.

thornton/3.title: Creekside Gardens annexation at 140th and Washington
thornton/3.summary: Council considered annexing and zoning the Creekside Gardens property near 140th Avenue and Washington Street.

thornton/4.title: Welby Station rezoning at 88th and Welby
thornton/4.summary: Council took up zoning for the Welby Station development near 88th Avenue and Welby Road.

thornton/5.title: Bellflower annexation at 140th and Holly
thornton/5.summary: Council considered the Bellflower annexation and zoning near 140th Avenue and Holly Street.

thornton/6.title: Parks and arts master plans
thornton/6.summary: Council reviewed updates to the parks master plan and the arts and culture master plan.

thornton/7.title: Station area plans for York at 144th and North Thornton
thornton/7.summary: Council looked at station area plans around future transit stops at York Street and 144th Avenue and at North Thornton near State Highway 7.

thornton/8.title: Thornton Parkway multimodal path
thornton/8.summary: Council took up a multimodal path project along Thornton Parkway.

thornton/9.title: Municipal fine and fee schedule
thornton/9.summary: Council reviewed a new municipal fine and fee schedule, including results of a fee survey and staff recommendations.

thornton/10.title: City code changes after a Supreme Court ruling
thornton/10.summary: Council considered amending city code to bring it in line with a recent U.S. Supreme Court ruling.

thornton/11.title: Liquor license hearings at First Street Plaza
thornton/11.summary: Council held liquor license hearings, including one at First Street Plaza where neighbors filed opposition.

thornton/12.title: Water revenue bonds
thornton/12.summary: Council considered issuing water revenue bonds to fund water system projects.

thornton/13.title: Residential housing design standards
thornton/13.summary: Council reviewed changes to design standards for new residential housing.

timnath/0.title: Timnath Landing GID bond issuance (Series 2026A and 2026B)
timnath/0.summary: The Timnath Landing General Improvement District is authorizing Limited Tax General Obligation Bonds (2026A) and Subordinate bonds (2026B) to fund public improvements, reimburse the developer and cover issuance costs. A December 2025 ordinance is being re-authorized because of the extended timeframe, with first reading on Oct. 13 and a public hearing set for Oct. 27, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. The GID also approved an advance and reimbursement agreement with CAC Timnath, LLC and accepted its 2025 audit.

sources.body: Timnath Landing General Improvement District Board
Timnath Landing General Improvement District Board

timnath/1.title: Peanut Park (Timnath Ranch North Park) master plan and $6 million funding
timnath/1.summary: The PROST Committee reviewed master planning for Peanut Park, including a poll of resident interest in amenities and challenges such as drainage and the park's size. The five-year capital plan includes $6 million for the park next year, but funding is not guaranteed until the budget is approved, so the work will be phased. Ayres and Associates presented a draft master plan in October.
timnath/1.where: Peanut Park / Timnath Ranch North Park

timnath/2.title: 2027 budget and five-year capital improvement plan
timnath/2.summary: The Town Council held a work session on the 2027 draft budget, which includes a five-year capital plan, cash flow projections and allocations tied to the Strategic Plan. Capital projects listed include a parks maintenance facility, police department parking lot and network upgrades, and security cameras at Timnath Community Park.

timnath/3.title: Town purchase of 4809 S. County Road 3F and 4104 Main Street
timnath/3.summary: Council is considering resolutions approving contracts to buy a residential property at 4809 S. County Road 3F, with a post-closing occupancy agreement, and a commercial property at 4104 Main Street. The Council also scheduled closed-door talks on real estate purchases or sales.
timnath/3.where: 4809 S. County Road 3F and 4104 Main Street

timnath/4.title: Ban on new on-site wastewater and graywater systems
timnath/4.summary: Council held first reading of Ordinance 16, which would amend the municipal code to prohibit new on-site wastewater treatment systems and graywater treatment works. A public hearing is set for Oct. 27, 2026 at 6:00 p.m.

timnath/5.title: Land Use Code amendments 25 and 26, including flood maps
timnath/5.summary: Council took first reading of Ordinances 17 and 18 adopting Amendments 25 and 26 to the Land Use Code. Amendment 25 relates to the updated Larimer County Flood Insurance Rate Maps and Flood Insurance Study. Public hearings are set for Oct. 27, 2026.

timnath/6.title: Recreation Center design and construction manager contract
timnath/6.summary: The Rec Center project has finished schematic design, and the Town is working with Adolfson & Peterson Construction and a third-party architect to confirm it is within the expected cost range before moving into design development. Council also considered Amendment 1 to the construction manager/general contractor agreement with AP Mountain States LLC.

timnath/7.title: Town employee compensation study
timnath/7.summary: A Council work session was set to review a compensation study of the Town's defined labor market. Staff plan to build the recommendations into the budget to support the goal of attracting and retaining staff.

timnath/8.title: Timnath Community Park entrance improvements
timnath/8.summary: The entrance project at Timnath Community Park is nearly complete, with a few trees still to be planted. Much flood irrigation was removed, making the area more water-efficient.

washington-county/0.title: Wind energy moratorium extension
washington-county/0.summary: The county board took up Resolution 49-2026 to extend its moratorium on wind projects on the September 29, 2026 agenda. The documents do not state the outcome or the new end date.

washington-county/1.title: Landfill resolution and capital purchases
washington-county/1.summary: The board handled Resolution 34-2026 on the landfill over several meetings, including a dedicated 2:30 landfill resolution item on August 18 and the resolution again on September 1. Landfill capital purchases also appeared on the agendas.

washington-county/2.title: RAISE grant request for proposals and bids
washington-county/2.summary: The county drafted an RFP for a RAISE grant in August and September, then opened and discussed bids on October 6 and October 20. The documents do not say what project the grant covers or who bid.

washington-county/3.title: Comprehensive Plan RFP
washington-county/3.summary: A draft request for proposals for a county comprehensive plan came up repeatedly from August through late September 2026. The documents do not say whether it was issued.

washington-county/4.title: Clinic roof and clinic bids
washington-county/4.summary: The board approved a clinic capital purchase on August 4, considered an APEX agreement for the clinic roof on August 25, and opened and discussed RFP clinic bids on October 6 and October 20.

washington-county/5.title: Courthouse and EMS building surveillance system
washington-county/5.summary: On August 18 the board was set to discuss and decide on proposals for a surveillance system for the courthouse and the EMS building. A CamNet service contract appeared on the September 8 agenda.

washington-county/6.title: 2027 employee health benefits and health pool rates
washington-county/6.summary: The board reviewed 2027 health pool rates on September 22 and took up Resolution 50-2026 on 2027 health benefits at several meetings from September 29 through October 20.

washington-county/7.title: Payment in lieu of taxes (PILT) agreement and conflict waiver
washington-county/7.summary: The board discussed a conflict of interest waiver and a PILT agreement on October 13, and a PILT agreement again on October 20. The documents give no details of the parties or amounts.

washington-county/8.title: Railroad letter
washington-county/8.summary: A letter about the railroad was on the consent agenda at the July 28, August 4 and August 18 meetings. The documents do not say what it concerns.

washington-county/9.title: Human services (DHS) agreements and contracts
washington-county/9.summary: The board considered several county Department of Human Services items: a coverage agreement, a core service plan, and contracts and amendments including child care assistance.

washington-county/10.title: Nursing home and housing authority board vacancies and purchases
washington-county/10.summary: The board took letters of interest for the Nursing Home Board and Housing Authority Board on October 13 and 20. It also considered nursing home purchases, including a dishwasher, landscaping and a vehicle.

washington-county/11.title: Fiber and telecom utility easements (Level 3 and Williams Communications)
washington-county/11.summary: On October 20 the board took up resolutions 52-2026 and 53-2026 for Level 3 Communications and Williams Communications. Earlier, a Resolution 40-2026 with Xcel Energy was on the July 28 consent agenda.

weld-county/0.title: Flock license plate reader cameras contract
weld-county/0.summary: The commissioners considered a contract (ID #11010) for purchase, installation and maintenance of Flock license plate reader cameras and a safety platform, bought through a cooperative source.

weld-county/1.title: Rule Farm Metropolitan District Nos. 1-3 service plan
weld-county/1.summary: The county accepted the filing of a service plan for the proposed Rule Farm Metropolitan District, referred it and set a hearing. The plan was heard September 23 and approved on September 30. The site is north of County Road 2 and east of County Road 21.
weld-county/1.where: North of County Road 2, east of County Road 21

weld-county/2.title: Weld County Code rewrites: Chapters 2, 21 and 23 and Ordinance 2026-11
weld-county/2.summary: The board moved Code Ordinance #2026-04 (Administration, Areas and Activities of State Interest, and Zoning chapters) through second and final reading. Code Ordinance #2026-11, which rewrites Chapter 2 Administration, passed second reading on July 29 and final reading on August 12.

weld-county/3.title: Cistern permit and right-of-way permit code changes
weld-county/3.summary: Code Ordinances #2026-12 (cistern usage permit criteria) and #2026-13 (right-of-way use permit appendix) were read in September and passed final reading October 26. Ordinance #2026-19 on liquor code updates, dance licenses and fees had first reading October 26.

weld-county/4.title: BURNCO / Tricycle Lane gravel mining permit amendment
weld-county/4.summary: A first major amended Use by Special Review permit for BURNCO Colorado, Tricycle Lane Texas and the Water Activity Enterprise of the Groundwater Management Subdistrict was heard August 19 near County Roads 58 and 49 and Weld County Parkway. It was approved August 24 and certified September 2.
weld-county/4.where: North of County Road 58, west of County Road 49, near Weld County Parkway

weld-county/5.title: Oil and gas leases, road agreements and department dissolution
weld-county/5.summary: The county held oral auctions for large tract oil and gas leases, approved a 40.685-acre lease and extended other leases. It signed road maintenance agreements with Noble Energy for 1041 WOGLA permits. On September 30 it considered dissolving the Weld County Department of Oil and Gas.

weld-county/6.title: Weld County Justice Center and jail projects
weld-county/6.summary: The county approved a construction manager/general contractor bid for the Justice Center and signed with J.E. Dunn on October 19. It also dealt with an interim stormwater agreement for the project and a parking garage plan review. Other bids covered jail pod renovations, North Jail lighting, and shower and air unit work.

weld-county/7.title: Public safety dispatch agreements with fire districts and police
weld-county/7.summary: The board approved a long series of public safety communications and dispatch services agreements with fire districts, police departments and towns including Greeley, Eaton, Johnstown, Mead and Windsor.

weld-county/8.title: Housing Choice Voucher transfer to Greeley Housing Authority
weld-county/8.summary: The commissioners approved a voluntary transfer of the county's Housing Choice Voucher program to the Housing Authority of the City of Greeley. A recognition of service for the Greeley-Weld County Housing Authority followed.

weld-county/9.title: Community Development Block Grant 2026-2030 plan
weld-county/9.summary: A public hearing was held August 10 on the CDBG 2026-2030 Consolidated Plan and 2026 Annual Action Plan for infrastructure, public facilities, services and housing rehabilitation. The plan was approved, and intergovernmental agreements with towns for CDBG work followed.

weld-county/10.title: Solar energy permits and Latham Solar Farm annexation deed
weld-county/10.summary: Hearings were set October 21 for two solar energy Use by Special Review permits, USR26-0007 near County Road 35 and AA Street and USR26-0015 near County Road 46. A quit claim deed for the Latham Solar Farm annexations was also approved.
weld-county/10.where: County Road 35/AA Street and County Road 46

weld-county/11.title: Annexation petitions with Greeley
weld-county/11.summary: The board considered renewing a petition to annex County Road 35 (North 35th Avenue) between F and O streets into Greeley. It also considered a petition for annexation of portions of County Road 18 and approved a deed for the Poudre River Trail from the West Lowell Annexation.
weld-county/11.where: North 35th Avenue, Greeley; County Road 18; Poudre River Trail

weld-county/12.title: Election agreements and voting system
weld-county/12.summary: The board approved coordinated election agreements with towns including Firestone and amended the voting system acquisition agreement. A resolution to support Amendment 83 was also considered.

weld-county/13.title: Tax incentive agreements and economic development
weld-county/13.summary: The commissioners considered tax incentive agreements, the Colliers Hill urban renewal tax revenue sharing agreement, private activity bonds for residential facilities, and a proposed area for state designation.

weld-county/14.title: County road projects and closures
weld-county/14.summary: The board handled the High Plains Boulevard gas line agreement, a roundabout at County Roads 74 and 31, a traffic signal at State Highway 52 and CR 37, and bridge replacements. Many temporary road closures were also approved.

wellington/0.title: Cleveland Avenue downtown reconstruction project
wellington/0.summary: The Town is rebuilding Cleveland Avenue and 5th Street downtown with new lighting, more on-street parking and a new storm drain system. Coulson Excavating was awarded the contract; state and federal grants including $1.8M Revitalizing Main Street and $1.35M MMOF must be spent by 12/31/2026. Staff reported on waterline work and sewer service conflicts at a Sept. 15 work session.
wellington/0.where: Cleveland Avenue and 5th Street, downtown Wellington

wellington/1.title: FY2027 town budget
wellington/1.summary: The Board held a Budget Workday on Oct. 2 and a public Budget Boo-nanza, with the draft 2027 budget presented Oct. 13 for public comment. Plans include capital projects across funds, a proposed delay in a sewer rate adjustment and a $2,000,000 General Fund loan to the Sewer Fund. Adoption is expected Nov. 10.

sources.body: Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board
Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board

wellington/2.title: Flock license plate cameras and Sheriff contract
wellington/2.summary: The Larimer County Sheriff's Office presented on Flock automated license plate reader cameras at locations including Highway 1/CR 9, I-25 Frontage Road/Jefferson and 6th Street/Cleveland. The Town budgeted $17,000 after a grant to offset costs was not awarded, and the Sheriff contract was on the Oct. 2 budget agenda.
wellington/2.where: Highway 1/CR 9, I-25 Frontage Rd/Jefferson Ave, 6th St/Cleveland Ave, CR 7/CR 64

wellington/3.title: Metropolitan district model service plan and review policy
wellington/3.summary: The Board is developing a model service plan and review criteria for metro district proposals, including what public benefit justifies special district financing and possible mill levy limits (a 60 mill combined total was discussed). Work sessions were held Sept. 22 and Oct. 20.

wellington/4.title: Economic development incentive policy
wellington/4.summary: The Board gave direction on a draft incentive framework focused on commercial development and adopted Resolution 36-2026 on Aug. 25. Tap fee incentives would need significant justification and performance metrics, and a Downtown Development Authority was requested for inclusion.

wellington/5.title: Housing affordability, Prop 123 and housing studies
wellington/5.summary: The town is pursuing a Proposition 123 affordable housing commitment, a Colorado Energy Office Local IMPACT Accelerator grant, and a Housing Needs Assessment update leading to a Housing Action Plan expected in 2027. The NoCo Foundation also briefed the Board on regional housing needs.

wellington/6.title: Public safety sales and use tax ballot question
wellington/6.summary: The Board considered Resolution 30-2026 supporting referral of a public safety sales and use tax question to the Nov. 3, 2026 ballot.

wellington/7.title: Sage Meadows Tract D replat and Kerbel Well parcel rezoning
wellington/7.summary: The Board held hearings on plat approvals for Sage Meadows Tract D Replat and Tract D2, which includes an adjacent Colorado State University parcel for the Kerbel Well and a rezone from R-2 Residential Low Density.

wellington/8.title: Parks master plan, community center and park improvements
wellington/8.summary: The PROST board is implementing the new Master Plan and a community center feasibility study, toured east side parks (Sunrise, Park Meadows, Wellville), and discussed signage and ADA accessible playground ideas at Sunrise Park. A Girl Scout Gold Award project proposes accessible playground improvements.
wellington/8.where: Sunrise Park, Park Meadows, Wellville Park, Harvest Park

sources.body: Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board
Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board
Parks, Recreation, Open Space, and Trails Advisory Board

wellington/9.title: Building, fire code and floodplain code updates
wellington/9.summary: The Board adopted Ordinance 11-2026 updating building and fire codes to align with the Wellington Fire Protection District's 2024 fire code, including solar-ready requirements. Floodplain amendments to the Land Use Code (Ordinance 13-2026) were recommended by the Planning Commission to align with FEMA's model ordinance.

wellington/10.title: Water supply concerns and Box Elder Stormwater Authority
wellington/10.summary: A resident repeatedly raised water concerns, asking the Board to look at options beyond reliance on Lake 3 and recommending action on the Box Elder Stormwater Authority.

wellington/11.title: Xcel Energy public safety power shutoffs
wellington/11.summary: Xcel briefed the Board on wildfire risk mapping and power shutoffs, noting undergrounding work and that water and wastewater plants are critical facilities.

westcliffe/0.title: Data center moratorium (Ordinance 2-2026)
westcliffe/0.summary: After a June discussion of data centers straining the electrical grid and water supply, the Town drafted a moratorium. First reading was July 21, and the Council approved Ordinance 2-2026 on Aug. 18 as an emergency ordinance, effective immediately. No one spoke at the public hearing.

westcliffe/1.title: Main Street parking, safety and crosswalk
westcliffe/1.summary: The Mayor raised closing Main Street between 2nd and 3rd in summers because of over-length vehicles and people crossing outside crosswalks. A workshop is planned. The Town bought two signs (up to $1,000) for the Rosita Street lot and approved a temporary painted crosswalk near 104 Main St. A permanent crosswalk is to be budgeted next year. A stop sign at Main and Adams Blvd is also on the October agenda.
westcliffe/1.where: Main Street between 2nd and 3rd Streets; Rosita lot; Main St. and Adams Blvd

westcliffe/2.title: Prop 123 affordable housing, Housing Needs Assessment and IGA with Silver Cliff
westcliffe/2.summary: The Town considered the final Housing Needs Assessment. It approved an intergovernmental agreement with Silver Cliff on Prop 123 so Westcliffe can count some of Silver Cliff's affordable housing numbers, since it missed the three-year requirement. Residents asked numerous questions about the Prop 123 grant in September, and a Custer County workforce housing report is on the October agenda.

westcliffe/3.title: Water/sewer expansion south of town and reservoir project
westcliffe/3.summary: The Council approved a public statement for trustees and staff to use when residents ask about the water/sewer expansion south of town. It says the project improves the chance private lots get built on. In August the reservoir project was awarded to Mountain Valley Excavation, starting in September with completion hoped by May. The wastewater pilot study was 70% complete.

westcliffe/4.title: Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code rejected and wildfire plan adopted
westcliffe/4.summary: The Council adopted the Custer County Community Wildfire Protection Plan in January, replacing a 2007 plan. In March it denied Ordinance 1-2026 adopting the state Wildfire Resiliency Code. The Fire Department, Silver Cliff and the County had not adopted it, and the attorney noted possible insurance and permitting risks.

westcliffe/5.title: Park shade structures instead of tree planting amid drought
westcliffe/5.summary: Because of drought and water shortage concerns, the Council dropped 2026 tree planting. It approved up to $40,000 for shade structures of about $3,000-$4,000 each. Bids for Memorial Park structures were moving forward in August.

westcliffe/6.title: Overnight camping ordinance update
westcliffe/6.summary: A trustee wants to revamp the Town camping ordinance to match Silver Cliff's, citing more overnight camping linked to rising homelessness. The current ordinance refers only to parks.

westcliffe/7.title: Tourism funding: Highway 69 welcome signs and holiday decor
westcliffe/7.summary: The Council gave $5,000 for Highway 69 welcome signs to get travelers to stop in town, with Mr. Shy opposed and approval contingent on the auditor. It also gave $3,500 for the holiday wreath contest and business holiday decor. The attorney said a statutory town cannot donate to the Altitude Fitness pool resurfacing and it must go through the grant process.

westcliffe/8.title: 2026 budget and mill levy
westcliffe/8.summary: After a public hearing with no comment, the Council approved the 2026 budget, appropriation and mill levy ordinances (5, 6 and 7-2025) in one motion on Dec. 9. A 2027 budget workshop was set for Aug. 28.

westcliffe/9.title: Façade Grant program
westcliffe/9.summary: The Council approved 2026 Façade Grant awards, cutting the Wildflower Hotel's award to $3,542. It rewrote application rules: reimbursement only, in-town business license, brick-and-mortar, and signs capped at $1,000. It also let a 2025 recipient finish work past the deadline.

westcliffe/10.title: Street sweeper purchase and town truck replacement
westcliffe/10.summary: The Council approved buying a street sweeper after a trial period, with discussion of renting it to businesses. Earlier the public works lead sought to buy a truck to replace aging Town trucks.

westcliffe/11.title: Farmer's Market at Jess Price Park and Bluff Park observatory hours
westcliffe/11.summary: The Council approved Resolution 4-2025 supporting the Farmer's Market on Town land at Jess Price Park, drafted as a resolution to avoid creating a leasehold. It also approved an MOU for extended Bluff Park hours at the Smokey Jack Observatory.

westminster/0.title: Data center land use and water service to neighboring jurisdictions
westminster/0.summary: After adopting Resolution No. 20 on July 27, 2026 supporting an interpretation that data centers are a prohibited use in Westminster, Council asked for a study session on the October 19 agenda. It covers data centers proposed just outside city limits, concerns about water use and extraterritorial utility service, and new data center language for the Unified Development Code.

westminster/1.title: 2027-2028 water, sewer and stormwater rates
westminster/1.summary: Council reviewed rate recommendations built on the WATER Task Force report, with a follow-up on single-family residential water rates. A public hearing on 2027-2028 stormwater fee changes was set for September 14. Ordinances implementing water, sewer and reclaimed water rates (Bill 40) and stormwater fees (Bill 43) moved through readings from September to October.

westminster/2.title: Proposed 2027 budget
westminster/2.summary: The proposed 2027 budget was presented August 24, had a public hearing September 14, and was reviewed by Council September 21. Council must adopt it by October 26, 2026. Related 2027 budgets for the Westminster Economic Development Authority (about $14.4 million in expenditures) and the city's general improvement districts had hearings October 12.

westminster/3.title: Affordable housing definition, density bonus and down payment assistance
westminster/3.summary: Council took up bills to amend the 2040 Comprehensive Plan with a density bonus and a new affordable housing definition, plus a parking change, passing second reading September 28. Staff also presented a proposed Down Payment Assistance program offering up to 20 percent of the purchase price, with a contractor being selected after the RFP closed September 3. Housing LIFT agreements with Maiker Housing Partners and Foothills Regional Housing were also updated.

westminster/4.title: Event center moratorium and new ordinance
westminster/4.summary: Council enacted a six-month moratorium on new event centers in multi-tenant commercial developments or within 300 feet of residential areas, citing impacts on public safety, water and sewer, parking, and neighboring businesses. Staff returned October 5 with a revised version of Councillor's Bill No. 19 after talking with operators.

westminster/5.title: Regional homelessness agreements and Navigation Center
westminster/5.summary: Council considered intergovernmental agreements with Jefferson County and the cities of Arvada, Edgewater, Golden, Lakewood and Wheat Ridge on homelessness, including a Navigation Center in Lakewood. A resident urged Council to consider a navigation center closer to Westminster. Staff also gave a homelessness prevention and response update.

westminster/6.title: Kaiser North redevelopment
westminster/6.summary: Council held a public hearing and first reading on a Comprehensive Plan amendment and a preliminary development plan amendment for the Kaiser North redevelopment (Councillor's Bill No. 42).

westminster/7.title: Business tax administration modernization
westminster/7.summary: Staff proposed requiring online filing and payment of business tax returns starting January 1, 2027, letting the Finance Director set filing methods and allowing electronic notices. About 94 percent of the 77,424 returns filed in 2025 were already online. Resident taxpayers are not affected, and the ordinance moved through readings in September.

westminster/8.title: Economic development deals: Mi Pueblo, Digantara, Scratch Kitchen
westminster/8.summary: Council approved an economic development agreement with Mi Pueblo Market for adaptive reuse and one with Digantara U.S. over its location in the city. Council also considered an intergovernmental agreement supporting a Scratch Kitchen and food warehouse at 12450 Delaware Street. An executive session covered incentives for a restaurant prospect.

westminster/9.title: Mountain Range High School Nutrition Center appeal
westminster/9.summary: Council held a public hearing on an appeal of the denial of an Official Development Plan for the Mountain Range High School Nutrition Center.

westminster/10.title: Rental housing costs and conditions
westminster/10.summary: A Westminster renter told Council about rising rents and mold and other housing conditions. Council also moved forward on a property maintenance code update (Bill 38).

westminster/11.title: Waste hauler licensing, Skip the Stuff and recycling proposals
westminster/11.summary: Staff presented three possible code changes: hauler licensing amendments, a Skip the Stuff ordinance, and a construction and deconstruction ordinance. They build on a CU Boulder student study and Colorado's packaging recycling program.

westminster/12.title: Automated license plate readers and fire sprinkler rules
westminster/12.summary: The October 5 study session included a Police Department presentation on automated license plate readers and a discussion of residential fire sprinkler requirements.

windsor/0.title: Data center regulation and Weld County data center concerns
windsor/0.summary: No data center is proposed in Windsor, but activity in unincorporated Weld County prompted a Town Board work session on August 3 about land use rules. Concerns are water and power use, noise and utility rates; Weld County requires closed-loop cooling. Written comments were being accepted and a Weld County hearing was expected in a couple of months.

windsor/1.title: Crossroads/Colorado Blvd roundabout construction phasing
windsor/1.summary: Contractor AB Underground asked to fully close Crossroads Boulevard east of Colorado Boulevard during Phase 2, saying two-way traffic is too constrained to build safely. The change could speed the project and allow NISP water casing installation in one operation, but it requires a detour. The Town Board reviewed it September 21.

windsor/2.title: 2027 budget, staffing and revenue decline
windsor/2.summary: Staff are preparing the 2027 budget with falling property tax and oil and gas revenue. Several positions, including Deputy Police Chief, Deputy Town Attorney and Transportation Planner/Engineer, are not recommended. Work sessions covered revenue estimates, staffing, capital projects and operations, with the general fund getting 67% of sales tax and capital 33%.

windsor/3.title: 2027 water, sewer and stormwater rate increases
windsor/3.summary: A Stantec rate study proposes a 20% sewer rate increase in 2027 and steep water increases through 2028. Drivers are the new wastewater treatment plant (about $154M Windsor share) and NISP water project debt. The Water and Sewer Board and Town Board reviewed it in October.

windsor/4.title: Glade Inlet Canal Diversion grant (NISP)
windsor/4.summary: The NISP Enterprise is applying for a $3,000,000 Bureau of Reclamation grant for the Glade Inlet Canal Diversion Improvements. Windsor holds about 15% of the project, so a grant would save the Town an estimated $450,000.

windsor/5.title: Hollister Lake Metropolitan District service plan
windsor/5.summary: The Town Board discussed and scheduled an ordinance to approve the service plan for Hollister Lake Metropolitan District and an intergovernmental agreement for October 26.

windsor/6.title: Windsor Lake Road / Weld County Road 70 extension right-of-way
windsor/6.summary: The Town is acquiring right-of-way and easements for the Windsor Lake Road extension connecting Hollister Lake Road to SH 257, including properties in Windsor Estates. The Board also planned an executive session on negotiations about the road.
windsor/6.where: Windsor Lake Road / Hollister Lake Road to SH 257

windsor/7.title: Proposition 123 affordable housing opt-in
windsor/7.summary: The Town Board discussed and scheduled a resolution expressing intent to commit to Proposition 123 for affordable housing on October 26.

windsor/8.title: Sign code update
windsor/8.summary: Consultants presented a draft overhaul of Windsor's sign code to implement the 2024 Comprehensive Plan. A public hearing draft is expected in September, Planning Commission in October or November, and adoption in early December.

windsor/9.title: Keeping of large animals in Estate Residential zones
windsor/9.summary: Staff proposed amending the code so large domestic animals are allowed on ER lots at one acre per animal. The review followed inquiries and a recent conditional use permit hearing for goats or a horse on a 1.47-acre lot.

windsor/10.title: Timberline Church stealth silo wireless tower
windsor/10.summary: Planning Commission scheduled hearings on a 50-foot stealth silo wireless tower and conditional use permit at Timberline Church.

windsor/11.title: GWIP annexation and Walmart Supercenter concerns
windsor/11.summary: A resident-expressed frustration about lights affected her quality of life, and the Mayor referenced the public hearing on annexing the GWIP property, saying the Board listens to public comment. Earlier notes said the Board approved Walmart Supercenter site plans, which was not well received.
windsor/11.where: Great Western Industrial Park; Main Street/Hwy 392

windsor/12.title: American Legion funding request for ADA improvements
windsor/12.summary: American Legion Post 109 asked the Town for financial help with ADA access to its building, which sits about five feet above grade.

windsor/13.title: Recreation center tax survey and future ballot
windsor/13.summary: A Magellan survey found 48% support for a 0.8% tax for another rec center, and the Town will wait a year or two before returning to voters. The fire department plans a property tax request in November.

winter-park/0.title: Urban Renewal Authority tax increment agreements with Fire District and Cooper Creek Village
winter-park/0.summary: The Winter Park Urban Renewal Authority was set to consider Resolution 25, a tax increment revenue agreement with the East Grand County Fire Protection District No. 4, and Resolution 26, a services agreement with Northland Securities. It also planned a closed session on negotiating a tax increment sharing agreement with the Cooper Creek Village Metro Districts. The documents do not state outcomes.

winter-park/1.title: Downtown Aerial Transit System (ATS) portal design
winter-park/1.summary: The Urban Renewal Authority's August 18 agenda included a presentation on the design of the downtown portal for the Aerial Transit System (gondola).

winter-park/2.title: Downtown Design Guidelines 75% draft
winter-park/2.summary: The Planning Commission was scheduled to review the 75% draft of the Winter Park Downtown Design Guidelines on September 22, along with its 2026 priorities list.

winter-park/3.title: 2027 Transit Operating Budget
winter-park/3.summary: The Transit Advisory Committee took up the 2027 transit operating budget at its September 14 meeting, with a further packet on October 5.

winter-park/4.title: Rendezvous at Winter Park Filing No. 2C final plat
winter-park/4.summary: The Planning Commission held a public hearing on the final plat for Rendezvous at Winter Park Filing No. 2C (PLN26-024) on August 11.

winter-park/5.title: Arrow at Winter Park master sign program
winter-park/5.summary: The Planning Commission was to review a master sign program (PLN26-088) for Arrow at Winter Park, Lot C-1 on US Highway 40.

winter-park/6.title: Setback variance at 23 Maple Road
winter-park/6.summary: The Board of Adjustment was to hold a hearing on a setback variance request (PLN26-076) at 23 Maple Road, with draft resolutions for both approval and denial prepared.

winter-park/7.title: Site plan reviews: Ski Idlewild, Trademark Drive, Bear Trail, Lupine Lane
winter-park/7.summary: The Planning Commission reviewed minor site plans for 40 Ski Idlewild Road (PLN26-046), 100 Trademark Drive including a retaining wall (PLN26-055), 373 Bear Trail (PLN26-064) and 405 Lupine Lane (PLN26-070).
winter-park/7.where: 40 Ski Idlewild Rd; 100 Trademark Dr; 373 Bear Trail; 405 Lupine Ln

winter-park/8.title: Rooted Food Trailer special use permit
winter-park/8.summary: The Planning Commission considered a special use permit (PLN26-048) for the Rooted Food Trailer on July 28.

winter-park/9.title: ROAM Neighborhood Park
winter-park/9.summary: The Planning Commission discussed the ROAM Neighborhood Park and upcoming projects on August 25.

winter-park/10.title: Turkey Trot special event permit
winter-park/10.summary: Town Council was to hold a public hearing on a special event permit for the Turkey Trot on October 20.

woodland-park/0.title: 209 E. Midland (Vos Building) dangerous-building appeal and historic landmark designation
woodland-park/0.summary: Owner Andrew Nguyen appealed a Dangerous Building Notice and Notice to Vacate (issued May 28, 2026) on the vacant building at 209 E. Midland. His representative said the 60-day permit deadline is not feasible and repairs could take up to a year. Separately, the Historical Preservation Committee considered recommending the building as a Local Historic Landmark, with four letters of support and one comment received.

woodland-park/1.title: Eagle Fire Lodge rezone and conditional use permit for multi-dwelling housing
woodland-park/1.summary: The Planning Commission is set to hear a request by Cedarwood Development for Woodland Capital to rezone 777 East US Highway 24 from Planned Unit Development to Multi Dwelling Urban Residential, with a conditional use permit for multi-dwelling use. A City Council hearing would follow.

woodland-park/2.title: New 'Public Safety Facilities' use in the Unified Development Code (Ordinance 1536)
woodland-park/2.summary: The city is amending the Unified Development Code to add Public Safety Facilities as a defined use allowed through the Special Use Permit process. The Planning Commission discussed it, and Council was to consider Ordinance No. 1536 on initial posting on October 15, 2026.

woodland-park/3.title: 2027 budget and DDA spending plans
woodland-park/3.summary: The Downtown Development Authority discussed its 2027 budget, including cutting the flower budget line from $250,000 to about $50,000, a downtown walkability study, and the Baggage building in Bergstrom Park. The 2026 micro-grant program has approved about 40 applications, up from 30 in 2025, with $197,516.87 in total grants. The City Council also had a 2027 budget presentation scheduled for October 15.

woodland-park/4.title: DDA micro-grants for downtown businesses
woodland-park/4.summary: The DDA reviewed final reports and approved reimbursements for 2026 micro-grant recipients including High Folks ($4,731), Mountain View Studio ($5,000), Woodland Capital ($4,785) and Aspen Leaf Enterprises ($5,000). Board members also discussed a TIF reimbursement for Taylor Mountain Enterprises.

woodland-park/5.title: Main Street programs and AARP/DOLA grants
woodland-park/5.summary: Main Street is applying for a $2,500 AARP livability grant (deadline Aug 28), with Antler Alley as a proposed project, and may use DOLA matching mini-grants. It is also planning a Shop & Dine Passport starting Sept 1 and Oktoberfest participation, and will ask to present to City Council on November 5.

woodland-park/6.title: 116 W. Lake Avenue historic landmark request
woodland-park/6.summary: The Historical Preservation Committee held a public hearing September 1 on designating 116 W. Lake Avenue as a Local Historic Landmark, requested by Steve Plutt with owner Murray WP Cabin, LLC. City Council's hearing is set for October 1, 2026.

woodland-park/7.title: Historic preservation projects: Junction House, Templeton Cemetery, Bergstrom Park
woodland-park/7.summary: The Historical Preservation Committee is tracking the Junction House/Roberts House grant (with Brownfields grant funds possible for planning), the Templeton Cemetery restoration plan, the preservation plan and Bergstrom Park Reimagined. A council member said the park design is already agreed upon; the committee asked whether it will be involved once a contractor is chosen.
woodland-park/7.where: Junction House, Templeton Cemetery, Bergstrom Park

woodland-park/8.title: School district funding and Boy Scouts Reservoir presentations
woodland-park/8.summary: The October 15 Council agenda included a Woodland Park School District presentation on funding and how property taxes factor in, and a Boy Scouts Reservoir presentation by the Utilities Director.

wray/0.title: Zoning and subdivision code rewrite (Ordinances 656 and 657)
wray/0.summary: Council gave first reading in May to Ordinances 656 and 657, which amend and repeal parts of the zoning code (Title 18) and subdivision regulations (Title 16). The Planning Commission recommended both, and they grew out of the Innovative Housing Strategies Grant project. A public hearing on the amendments was held April 21, and second readings were on the June 9 agenda.

wray/1.title: Affordable housing planning and DOLA grant for the southern district
wray/1.summary: Council approved a request to amend DOLA Local Planning Capacity Grant #25-085, adding $50,000 to focus on affordable housing plans for the Wray southern area. Council also appointed two members to the Wray Housing Authority Board in February.

wray/2.title: Wray Civic Center construction contract
wray/2.summary: The June 9 agenda included a draft construction contract (guaranteed price) and possible award of RFP 139-2025 for Wray Civic Center construction. Council was also updated in May on a $2.1 million Congressional Directed Spending request tied to the project.

wray/3.title: Amphitheater revitalization
wray/3.summary: The Amphitheater Advisory Board presented a strategic plan for revitalizing the amphitheater, which Council adopted by resolution in January. In April Council approved a memorandum with the University of Colorado Denver and the Colorado Center for Community Development to help design improvements.

wray/4.title: Electric rates and power supply
wray/4.summary: Council received notice of an electric rate increase in January and held a public hearing in March before approving Resolution 15-2026 establishing electric rates. In April it approved a contract amendment with Western Area Power Administration so MEAN can keep handling power purchases, and in February it signed a consent related to the Sandhills Energy solar project.

wray/5.title: South Business and Residential District project and DOLA grant
wray/5.summary: Council accepted a DOLA Energy and Mineral Impact Assistance Fund grant of up to $800,000 with a local match for the South Business and Residential District Project.

wray/6.title: Industrial park lot sales and listings
wray/6.summary: In January Council approved Ordinance 655 selling Lot 10 of the Wray East Industrial Park to PR Transportation, LLC. In June it considered exclusive right-to-sell listing contracts for Lots 2 and 3 of the East Industrial Park and Lots 1-6, Block 1 of the Golf Course Commercial Addition.
wray/6.where: Wray East Industrial Park and Golf Course Commercial Addition

wray/7.title: Traffic code adoption, e-bike enforcement and traffic safety grant
wray/7.summary: Council adopted the 2024 Model Traffic Code through Ordinance 659, with second reading and a public hearing on June 9. Council approved applying for a $9,038 CDOT safety grant for the Power to Be Safe program with local schools, and discussed police enforcement of electric bikes and scooters and possible changes to the UTV ordinance.

wray/8.title: Procurement policy ordinance (Ordinance 658)
wray/8.summary: Council approved Ordinance 658, which codifies the city's current procurement practices into a formal policy and procedure.

wray/9.title: Airport funding transfer
wray/9.summary: Resolution 21-2026 ratified the City Manager's signature on a transfer of $150,000 in Airport Improvement Program entitlement funds.

yuma-county/0.title: Moratorium on data centers through 2026
yuma-county/0.summary: On March 17, 2026 the commissioners approved a resolution placing a moratorium on data centers in the county until 12/31/2026, along with a companion resolution adopting rules. The documents give no further detail on the rules.

yuma-county/1.title: County Road 39 repaving project
yuma-county/1.summary: The commissioners approved Simon Construction's proposal for repairs on County Road 39 in March. Work was expected to start in late July 2026; by mid-August paving was done from County Road G to M, with grinding next from Highway 59 to County Road G.

yuma-county/2.title: County Road M railroad approach and asphalt repairs
yuma-county/2.summary: Repairs on County Road M near the BNSF railroad crossing were delayed while the county sorted out flagger costs and permits, and were tied to the County Road 39 work to avoid doing it twice. In August the commissioners approved a $410,050 Simon Construction estimate to remove and replace asphalt on County Road M.
yuma-county/2.where: County Road M near the BNSF tracks

yuma-county/3.title: December 2025 windstorm and wildfires
yuma-county/3.summary: After a severe windstorm with 60-70 mph gusts and fires that burned over 14,000 acres, the commissioners declared a local disaster emergency on Dec. 19, 2025. Road crews logged overtime fighting the fires, DOLA matching grants for Eckley's generator were discussed, and crews have been clearing blown sand from roads in the burn scar.
yuma-county/3.where: Countywide, burn scar area and Town of Eckley

yuma-county/4.title: Road and Bridge staffing, supervisor hire and blade coverage
yuma-county/4.summary: The county interviewed for a new Road and Bridge Supervisor and offered the job to David Lee at $76,000 a year. The department is short-staffed, so blade operators cover larger areas and roads may be bladed more slowly. Commissioners discussed adding blade operator positions to the 2027 budget and approved several salary authorizations.

yuma-county/5.title: Expedited review for affordable housing projects
yuma-county/5.summary: The commissioners approved Resolution 11-25-2025D establishing expedited review policies for affordable housing projects. Land use code updates and a fire resilience code were also discussed.

yuma-county/6.title: 2026 budget hearing and revised mill levy certification
yuma-county/6.summary: The commissioners held a public hearing in December 2025 on 2026 budgets for the county, landfill and Water Authority. After the Assessor's Office notified local governments of a required change in January, the board approved a revised Certification of Mill Levies and Revenue for tax year 2025 and budget year 2026.

yuma-county/7.title: South Spur Solar Project and utility permits
yuma-county/7.summary: The South Spur Solar Project is expected to begin in early 2027, and the Road and Bridge supervisor plans to work with the company so county roads are restored afterward. A Viaero underground utility permit was moved to the south side of County Road 38, and exposed fiber on County Road 18 needed a utility locate.
yuma-county/7.where: County Roads 38 and 18; South Spur Solar site

yuma-county/8.title: Sale of the Idalia House
yuma-county/8.summary: The county approved a listing contract for the Idalia House in December 2025. In February 2026 an inspection found the water heater only needed lighting, and the board took $2,500 off the purchase price.

yuma-county/9.title: Dreher Pit and gravel supply
yuma-county/9.summary: Staff contacted the Dreher Pit landowners again about the county's gravel supply, and the board approved purchasing a Grizzly rock screen because the current screen is wearing out. A mining reclamation form was also sent to the state.

yuma/0.title: Historic designation of four properties on South Main Street
yuma/0.summary: The City Council scheduled a public hearing and four resolutions (Series 2026) to give historic designation to properties at 300, 301, 113 and 401 South Main Street. A fifth address, 320 S. Main Street, also appears in the agenda. The documents do not state the outcome.
yuma/0.where: South Main Street (300, 301, 113, 401 S. Main St.)

yuma/1.title: Council five-year goals, survey and strategic plan
yuma/1.summary: Council discussed five-year goals, a community survey and a strategic plan guide between April and June 2026. In September, members planned to attend a strategic planning workshop on teamwork, communication and council priorities.

yuma/2.title: 2026 budget proposal
yuma/2.summary: The December 2025 agenda included a proposal for the 2026 budget, along with grants and donations including the Workman Memorial. No figures or decisions appear in the documents.

yuma/3.title: Library 2026 plans and five-year plan
yuma/3.summary: In January 2026 Council scheduled a discussion of the library for 2026, including a five-year plan. Details are not given in the agenda.

yuma/4.title: June 14 event and Old Threshers event planning
yuma/4.summary: Council met in June 2026 to finalize planning for an event on June 14 and to discuss an event during Old Threshers.
